## BUG-566 (FIXED, MED): TWO RAILS, ONE FACT - git's OWN temporary index was REFUSED by RAIL 4 and TOLERATED by RAIL 5

MEASURED 2026-09-27 (git 2.39.5 Apple Git-154, --separate-git-dir layout). A PARTIAL commit (`git commit --
<path>`) makes git hand the pre-commit hook GIT_INDEX_FILE=<gitdir>/next-index-<pid>.lock; the file EXISTS at
hook time and git removes it on exit. Two rails read that ONE fact and disagreed: RAIL 4 refused the name (so
NO partial commit could pass) while RAIL 5 tolerated it. FIXED by D-2673: the ONE home
(scripts/lib/git_subject.py#index_subject) ADOPTS git's own index - directory == the PINNED git dir, basename
matches a DECLARED owner_name_globs entry, and the file EXISTS - and then READS it as the audit subject;
anything else ambient is REFUSED. The must-exist condition is not decoration: git reads a MISSING index as
EMPTY, so an absent file would report "all declared" over no bytes. MEASURED after: 13/13 module controls
(the D-405 join matched a live minted name this run) and 16/23/11 rail controls still fire.

FOLLOW-THROUGH (2026-10-10, D-2909): the D-2646 two-homes-one-fact class had ONE more name-list reader.
`scripts/check_declaration_consumers.py#staged_set()` read the staged set as TEXT and split on newlines
(`git diff --cached --name-only` + `splitlines()`), so a staged path containing a SPACE became multiple
phantom paths — the same defect D-2673 removed from the index-subject home. FIXED: `staged_set()` now reads a
NUL-separated list (`-z`) and splits on NUL, mirroring `git_subject.run_git_paths` (BUG-565). It keeps its own
`-z` read ONLY because its selftest must exercise a synthetic root repo the ONE home cannot (`run_git_paths`
is pinned to the live REPO subject); the two reads are documented to stay in lockstep. TWO new known-answer
controls (`space_path_is_one_path`, `space_path_not_split`) prove a space-path is ONE path and its whitespace
tokens are NOT phantom standalone paths; selftest 13/13.

MADR is the real-world precedent: it carries status = "superseded by ADR-0123" as a LINK, not a label.

## BUG-576 (FIXED, MED): a FRESH repository cannot make its FIRST commit - RAIL 0 accuses an UNBORN HEAD of being broken metadata, and the RECOVERY route re-creates exactly that state (2026-09-27)

MEASURED (2026-09-27, by scripts/check_boundary_rehearsal.py in a REAL repository in the system temp dir, --separate-git-dir layout, hooks installed by this repository's OWN installer): the FIRST \`git commit\` returns rc=1 with
  FAIL repo-integrity: 2 repository integrity defect(s):
    "git rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit}" does not resolve (rc=128: fatal: Needed a single revision) - every rail below is reading a repository that is not there (P0-A)
    <gitdir>/logs/HEAD is MISSING - git's reflog for HEAD has been renamed away, and 'git reflog' will silently serve a stale branch reflog (P0-A)
Both facts are the NORMAL state of an UNBORN HEAD, not broken metadata: HEAD names a branch with no commit yet, and git creates logs/HEAD AT the first commit.

WHY IT MATTERS: the SAME state is produced by the BUG-400/BUG-564 RECOVERY route (a git dir re-created by a clone, by hand, or by --separate-git-dir), so the rail whose purpose is to NAME broken metadata REFUSES the one commit that would repair the repository. This is the BUG-574 class again - a rule that cannot fire on the LEGITIMATE case - now on the recovery rail, and it was invisible for the same reason: every control built its own fixture and asserted refusals, never an acceptance.

CLASS: a rule derived from "what a healthy repository LOOKS like" instead of "the states a healthy repository PASSES THROUGH". An unborn HEAD is a legitimate state.

REMEDY (OWED): RAIL 0 must distinguish an UNBORN HEAD (HEAD resolves to a ref that does not exist yet, and the repository has an index but no commit) from a HEAD that is genuinely broken; only the latter is a defect. Filed here rather than fixed by weakening the rail. UNTIL THEN the rehearsal declares a --no-verify bootstrap in config/boundary_rehearsal.yaml#temp.bootstrap that MUST BE WITHDRAWN by a decision the moment this is fixed (a declaration that outlives its subject is the BUG-542 class).

ESCAPING CORRECTION (appended 2026-09-27, the day the block above was filed): the three backtick PAIRS in the
BUG-576 MEASURED block carry a stray leading backslash from the appending heredoc. Read each of them as a PLAIN
backtick. Nothing else in the block is affected. Corrected by THIS APPEND, not by a rewrite, because buglog.md is
append-only (R-D410).

## BUG-578 (FIXED, MED): the BOUNDARY REHEARSAL rehearses HEAD, so it cannot gate the change that LANDS - it was GREEN while the working tree already contained a rail that refused every fresh commit (2026-09-27)

MEASURED (forensic audit of the BUG-576 landing, inside the fixture the rehearsal itself builds): with the fix
present in the WORKING TREE and absent from HEAD, the rehearsal own acceptance control returned
FRESH_FIRST_COMMIT rc=1 - REFUSED by HEAD RAIL 0 - and returned rc=0 the moment the same bytes were OVERLAID
into the fixture. The rehearsal materializes 'git archive HEAD' (config/boundary_rehearsal.yaml#temp.materialize)
and installs the hooks from that replica, so every rail it exercises is the LAST COMMITTED one, never the one
about to be committed.

CLASS: a control that measures the PREVIOUS state cannot refuse the commit that breaks the NEXT one. It is
BUG-574 one level up: the rehearsal would stay GREEN while a rail change that refuses every legitimate commit is
committed, and the very next commit - the one that would have to repair it - is then refused BY THE HOOK, so the
repair can only land with --no-verify. The class this rehearsal exists for recurs THROUGH the rehearsal.

REMEDY (OWED): overlay the WORKING TREE bytes of the DECLARED subjects the rehearsal exercises (scripts/**,
config/**, justfile) into the fixture AFTER materializing HEAD and BEFORE installing the hooks, then re-run the
installer own --check. DECLARED with a why, never inferred (C12), plus a control that REDs if the overlay is
dropped. MEASURED in the audit: 'bash scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check' returns rc=0 after the overlay, so
the installed hook is still its own re-derivation (BUG-526).

NOTE (D-2646/D-2674): the four new RAIL 0 controls (BUG-576) build their fixtures with 'git init' in the SYSTEM
temp dir and copy NOTHING, so they do not restate the BUG-537 outside-tree rule and must NOT become its third
home (BUG-577) - when scripts/lib/fixture.py lands, the nested builder moves there and the copy is deleted.

## BUG-573 (FIXED, MED): a RED earlier in the ladder SHORT-CIRCUITED it, so every LATER fault was invisible (2026-09-27, D-2680)

CLASS. The ladder is a LINEAR recipe: it stops at the FIRST non-zero line, and the owner READS the result as the
whole set. A red line therefore hid every line after it, so every repair round could only ever discover ONE fault -
the cost the owner measured as "running in circles".
MEASURED (before). A single RED at one line stood for a whole session; repairing it UNHID a stale dormancy the
rail registry had never been able to report. Nothing about the fix caused the second fault - the prefix did.
MEASURED (after). `just health-full` runs the same declared lines in one pass: **ok ladder scan: 87 line(s) RUN,
0 fault(s), 203.0s** (SCAN_RC=0). The remaining fault set at HEAD is EMPTY, and it is now measurable instead of
assumed. Per-line seconds make the cost attributable: check_tests 82.1s, yaml_guard 45.3s, boundary rehearsal
14.4s, store-columns 10.2s, rail mutations 8.6s. The banner's numbers are DERIVED: '87 declaring line(s) stand
in it (63 declared a HARD gate)'.
FOUND BY the D-2680 step of the standing-rule programme (the registered next step was BUG-577; BUG-573 was taken
FIRST because it is upstream of every other repair: it decides what a human can SEE).
FIX (D-2680, scripts/run_ladder.py + justfile + config). --collect runs each line as written through a POSIX
shell from the repository root, so the line's OWN guard decides (a line that tolerates rc=2 is not a fault),
records every fault with rc + seconds, and exits with the WORST code (1 FATAL outranks 2 owner-owed, BUG-457),
never the first. The recipe body is READ from its ONE home (config/rail_registry.yaml#ladder + #recipes): no rail
name, path or count is written in code (C12), a recipe the declaration does not govern is REFUSED (C16, D-405),
and a line invoking the collector itself is skipped (recursion). `just health` keeps the fast ladder and now
declares the prefix FIRST - printed before any rail can abort - naming `just health-full` as the whole-set entry
point. No fixture and no writer: the controls are synthetic, so this rail adds no second home of the fixture rule
(BUG-577) and no entry to config/rail_registry.yaml#writers.
SEEN. run_ladder --selftest 12/12 rc=0; mutation ladder_scan_reports_every_fault_is_load_bearing SEEN to red
through its own named marker; gate --check rc=0 (8 rules, 7/7 subjects); registry rc=0; declaration consumers
rc=0 (7 edges). This change FILED no new bug - it closes one.

CLASS. A declaration is only a declaration where a machine READS it. MEASURED at HEAD e13eddc: 'justfile | 7
+++++++' added ONLY the health-full recipe; 'git show HEAD:justfile | grep run_ladder' returned ONE line, the

MEASURED 2026-09-27 (read-only forensic pass, re-measured at the landing against 812 records / 59 config citation sites): 16 records state=SUPERSEDED and only 4 name their successor (12 ORPHANS, all pinned below); 4 citation sites name a decision that is NOT IN FORCE (D-403 x2 PROPOSED, D-400 PROPOSED, D-2663 OPEN) - a protection enforced by nobody (the D-328 defect, generalised); scripts/reconcile.py#decision_registry_wellformed passed all of it, because it checks that a cited id RESOLVES.
FIX. The registry is read as a GRAPH. ONE HOME for the rules: config/decisions_policy.yaml#graph (in_force_states, not_in_force_states, supersession_state, successor_field, and the two debt pins). TWO declared entries in config/reconciliation.yaml, evaluated by the SAME engine and the SAME citation walker (no second home for "what a citation site is", BUG-577): decision_supersession_complete and decision_citations_in_force - both GREEN at the landing: 'every SUPERSEDED record names a resolvable successor in 812 record(s); 12 pinned legacy id(s) still owed' and '59 citation site(s) all name a decision IN FORCE; 4 declared forward reference(s) still owed; every state word in the registry is classified'.
NOT BACKFILLED (the legacy_debt_ids reasoning): a successor reconstructed by a tool is not evidence, so the 12 orphans and the 4 sites are DECLARED debt, pinned BY IDENTITY in the ONE home and SHRINK-ONLY - a pin that now names a successor, changed state, vanished, or a pinned site that no longer exists or now names an in-force decision, is a STALE declaration and fails the rail (BUG-542).
THE RULE THAT ALSO CLOSES THE VOCABULARY: every state word present in the registry must be classified in force or not-in-force, so a NEW state cannot enter unread (BUG-572's class).
SEEN. python3 scripts/reconcile.py --selftest: 9 known-answer control(s), both directions, run by the ladder as its OWN declaring line (D-2676 ii).
TEETH (D-2676 iv). config/rail_mutations.yaml#decision_supersession_rule_is_load_bearing: with the SUPERSESSION filter inert, the named control goes RED through its own marker 'FAIL selftest/supersession_reports_a_gap'; floor 10 -> 11, subjects 8 -> 9.

- **MEASURED before the fix (2026-09-27, `git status --porcelain -z -uall`)**: **124 dirty paths, and exactly ONE
  of them was granted** (`governance/RECONCILIATION.json`, entry 15). The other **123** sat in NO declared home:
  112 `backups/**` PRE_* pre-images that C13/R-D410 OBLIGE a session to write, plus 11 in `governance/` (3
  tracked-but-modified rail outputs, 8 untracked run artifacts/journals). No plan could commit them and git did
  not ignore them, so **the tree could never be clean** and the evidence trail was unversioned BY ACCIDENT.
- **shape**: the archive-census rule (`archive/index.yaml#excluded`, BUG-537/BUG-556) applied to the WORKTREE:
  "an on-disk object is either INDEXED or DECLARED excluded, never silently absent". It fell between the two
  existing rails: rail 4 audits the STAGED set, rail 0 audits git METADATA - the dirty worktree was nobody's
  subject.
- **FIX (D-2684)**: TWO HOMES, NO OVERLAP, ONE READER. (1) the GRANTING home is the plan's `may_touch` (rail 4
  already owns "a session may write/commit this"; the new rail CONSUMES it and never restates it) - SEVEN NAMED
  paths added (`.gitignore` + the six indexed rail-output stores, `governance/MUTATION_JOURNAL.jsonl` among them
  because an append-only receipt ledger nobody can commit is not auditable); (2) the EXCLUDING home is
  `config/repo_integrity.yaml#worktree.excluded` (three declarations, each with a `why`, enforced by the
  `.gitignore` bytes); (3) the ONE reader is `scripts/check_repo_integrity.py --worktree`, wired into the ladder.
- **THE RAIL CAUGHT ITS OWN PATCH (MEASURED, first run)**: the `.gitignore` lines I first wrote carried TRAILING
  comments - and in `.gitignore` a trailing `#` is NOT a comment, so each line became a literal pattern that
  matched nothing. The rail reported `declared-excluded 'backups/**' is NOT ignored by git (probe 'backups/x')`
  and exited 1. That is the D-405 join firing on its author: the declaration is checked against GIT'S OWN answer
  (`git check-ignore -q --no-index`), not against a belief about it. A SECOND measured defect fell out of the
  same run: the shared `git()` helper STRIPS output, which ate the leading space of the status field
  (" M .gitignore" -> path "gitignore"), so `dirty_entries()` now reads the records RAW (C16).
- **TEETH (D-2676)**: (i) ONE HOME = `config/repo_integrity.yaml#worktree`; (ii) SEEN control = the ladder line
  `check_repo_integrity.py --worktree || exit 1`; (iii) NAMED oracle = `--selftest` (6 worktree controls + the 15
  existing, rc=0); (iv) MUTATION = `config/rail_mutations.yaml#worktree_undeclared_dirty_path_rule_is_load_bearing`
  (floor 12 -> 13). VERDICT after: `ok repo-integrity worktree: 14 dirty path(s) - 14 granted by
  governance/session_plan_20260924.yaml, 0 declared-excluded, 0 in neither home` rc=0.
- **NOT claimed**: the rail is wired at the SCAN moment (`just health`), deliberately NOT into the pre-commit
  hook - the hook's strictest gate would refuse a commit that carries a legitimately new artifact before the plan
  entry can land, which is the BUG-528b sequencing defect. The hook widening is a declared follow-up, not a
  silent gap.

derived count. NOT WORKED HERE: the META-LANE FREEZE holds new GOVERNANCE bugs as FILED so the product lane can
advance; this block is the filing, with its measurement and its remedy.

## BUG-564 (FIXED 2026-09-27, D-2687 - the last remainder): the commit boundary was verified as a PATH OF BYTES

STATUS CLOSED. The declaration said `gitdir:hooks/pre-commit` and the reader joined it to `git rev-parse

declared as `git-path:<rel>` (GIT ITSELF is the answer), the declared subject is the RESOLVED path + its bytes +

STATUS CLOSED. A freeze is the one governance act that takes effect by being BELIEVED: it is pure prose by

from a POLICY, and a policy has no horizon, so it outlives the reason it was opened for (the D-337 permanent-freeze
trap); (iii) IT COUNTED NOTHING - the parked set could grow for ever, so "we are frozen" and "we are stuck" printed

pinned BY IDENTITY, a max_held ceiling, a released ruling map, a written EXIT and a review_by horizon) and
scripts/check_freeze_window.py is the ONE reader, wired into justfile:health (--selftest fatal + live verdict
tri_state: rc 2 = OWNER-OWED, loud, NOT fatal, BUG-457). It reads the DERIVED register governance/bug_status.json
and never re-parses the log (a second parser would be the D-2646 two-homes defect). 15 named controls, mutation
freeze_window_exit_is_load_bearing (floor 19 -> 20). MEASURED AFTER: rc=0, exit MET: opening_set_closed, exit
UNMET: nothing_still_held (8 still parked of ceiling 8); ladder 96 lines RUN, 0 faults, 260.9s.
THE FORENSIC AUDIT FIRED ON THE CHANGE ITSELF: the newly wired ladder line went rc=1 on day 0 because the clause

## BUG-572 (FIXED, LOW, D-2689): a status word in a heading's TITLE decided a bug's status when the parenthetical slot named none

STATUS CLOSED. MEASURED 2026-09-27: the parser's third candidate was the WHOLE HEADER, so any status word anywhere
in a header - including a word in a sentence ABOUT a bug - decided that bug's status. Over 422 heading events the
fallback read BUG-419 (the register's open/closed SCHEMA ASYMMETRY, still live) and BUG-570 as CLOSED, read the
duplicate BUG-493 block CLOSED because its title said the word, and read BUG-307 CLOSED because a FILENAME
(`closed_menu.py`) appeared in its title. A bug whose fix nobody had done was therefore retired from the count by
prose - and this register is the META-LANE FREEZE's ORACLE (check_freeze_window.py reads governance/bug_status.json),
so a misreading register can silently drain the window.

FIX (D-2689): the status slot is a POSITION AT A HEADER BOUNDARY, never prose - (1) the LEADING parenthetical,
(2) the FIRST segment before the first colon, (3) the FIRST WORD after that colon (how a header writes
"UPDATE ...: FIXED code-side"), (4) the TRAILING parenthetical. No candidate -> EMPTY -> OPEN. The whole-header
fallback is GONE. 9 new NAMED CONTROLS (3 defect shapes that each read CLOSED, 6 must-not-move shapes), the
self_test now REPORTS its control count (C20) and `--selftest` touches NOTHING (no log, no declaration, no write),
mutation `status_slot_is_a_boundary_not_prose` (floor 20 -> 21).

MEASURED, NOT OPINION - three alternatives were REFUSED on the corpus: a blanket "everything before the first
colon" slot flips 8 of 422 events (it destroys the legal TRAILING slot: BUG-320/337/371 and BUG-388's real
post-colon FIXED); a paren-only slot flips 3 and ignores that same FIXED; a boundary rule WITHOUT the post-colon
first word flips 5, including BUG-388 `closed -> open`. The adopted rule flips 4 events / 2 final statuses.

THE AUDIT FIRED ON THE FIX ITSELF: the 2 changed ids are BUG-419 (GENUINELY OPEN - verified against the register's
own schema: open is a list of OBJECTS, closed a list of plain id STRINGS) and BUG-562 (GENUINELY CLOSED - its owed
RAIL landed and was verified by RUNNING it: scripts/check_declaration_consumers.py rc=0, wired justfile:104/114).
Landing the parser alone would therefore have newly MISLABELLED a fixed bug, so this change-set carries BUG-562's
closure event with it: a parser that is RIGHT cannot be landed without stating the facts it exposes.

## BUG-587 (FILED, HIGH, D-2689): a MINT is not ASSERTED to ARRIVE - the registry's write path has no arrival oracle

STATUS FILED - PARKED by META-LANE-FREEZE-1 (its scope: a NEW governance bug is FILED, with a remedy, and NOT
WORKED inside the window).

MEASURED 2026-09-27 WHILE MINTING D-2689. A hand-rolled append of ONE record to config/decisions.yaml produced
32 lines ADDED and 0 deleted, and the census did NOT move: records 819, last D-2688. CAUSE, exact: a record's
files: sequence emits its items at indent 2 (two spaces + "- path"), the SAME column a record's own "- id:" marker
takes when a writer re-indents the dumped block, so the new record parsed as ONE MORE ENTRY of the PREVIOUS
record's files: list. The file LOADED, every rail stayed GREEN, and the decision was INVISIBLE.

THE SECOND FACE, measured in the same audit: the tombstone tools/sync_decisions.py names its own remedy - "What it
never did: membership (registry ids vs log headings). That check is scripts/check_decision_membership.py" - and
scripts/check_decision_membership.py DOES NOT EXIST. The ONE oracle that would have caught the absorbed mint (an
id in the registry with no heading in DECISION-LOG.md, or a heading with no record) is named by a declaration and
exists nowhere (D-405: a declaration whose subject is absent is an assertion).

WHY IT OUTRANKS ITS SIZE. scripts/recompute_decision_summary.py --mint validates the record BEFORE the write,
checks that the new bytes are an APPEND, and re-derives the registry SHAPE after it - but NOTHING compares the
census before and after, so the write path can LOSE a record and still print a plausible total. That is the
BUG-492 class aimed at the registry: a write that cannot be SEEN to fail.

FIX (OWED, drawn and NOT landed - the window holds it): in mint_main, assert post_total == total_before +
len(records) AND that every minted id is present exactly once as a TOP-LEVEL record id, failing closed BY NAME;
land the membership rail its own tombstone names; one known-answer control and one mutation that REDs it
(a_mint_must_be_seen_to_arrive). The remedy is declared here so the drain has a subject.

## BUG-587 (FIXED, HIGH, D-2690): a MINT is not ASSERTED to ARRIVE - the registry's write path has no arrival oracle

STATUS FIXED (was FILED 2026-09-27 and PARKED by META-LANE-FREEZE-1; closing a HELD bug is that window's DRAIN,
never a breach of it). MEASURED BEFORE: an append of ONE record added 32 lines, deleted 0, the census DID NOT MOVE
(819, last D-2688) and every rail stayed GREEN - a record's files: items and a record's own '- id:' marker occupy
the SAME column, so the record parsed as ONE MORE ENTRY of the PREVIOUS record's files: list. The file LOADED and
the decision was INVISIBLE. FIX, one limb per face. (i) THE WRITE PATH IS SEEN TO ARRIVE: arrival_problems() joins
the COUNT (total_before + len(minted)) AND the TOP LEVEL (every minted id exactly once as a top-level record), and
it is asked of the WOULD-BE bytes BEFORE the write - an absorbed record is REFUSED, never landed invisibly - then
again of the bytes ON DISK, where a failure refuses to rewrite the census and names --check as the reader. (ii) THE
ORACLE THE TOMBSTONE NAMED EXISTS: tools/sync_decisions.py declares 'That check is
scripts/check_decision_membership.py' and no such file existed (D-405). The rail now does: every id NAMED in
DECISION-LOG.md (D2552 table rows AND historical headings, normalised through the reconciler's OWN spelling rule,
never restated) must name a TOP-LEVEL record. MEASURED live: 194 named, 820 top-level, 5 pinned legacy orphans,
0 faults. THE DIRECTION NOT ASSERTED (declared): the log is a TIERED face of the registry (its own header) and the
full history is in archive/, so ~631 records carry no log entry by design - an equality join is a rail nobody can
satisfy (BUG-540). TEETH (D-2676): ONE HOME = config/decisions_policy.yaml#membership; SEEN = two justfile lines;
NAMED ORACLE = --selftest 10 controls + the reconciler's 14; MUTATION = a_mint_must_be_seen_to_arrive +
a_logged_id_that_names_no_record_is_load_bearing (floor -> 23).

FILED and FIXED by D-2690. MEASURED 2026-09-27, on the first run of the mutation gate after D-2690 covered

(BUG_REGISTER = ROOT/governance/bug_status.json) and the fixture declared only justfile, so EVERY baseline of that
runner was red. CLASS: a DECLARATION that cannot be evaluated against reality (D-405). The gate was right to be red
and wrong about WHICH fact was broken - a misdiagnosis sends the next reader to the wrong file (it named the
MUTATION, not the fixture).

creates.

declaration must be clean AND a synthetic missing include_file AND a synthetic empty glob must EACH be a fault) |

## BUG-590 (FIXED, MEDIUM, D-2690): the arrival control fired through the COUNT clause, not the TOP-LEVEL clause it names

FILED and FIXED by D-2690, found by BUG-589's repair. With the fixture carrying its input the gate's verdict became
exact: "mutation a_mint_must_be_seen_to_arrive DID NOT RED the oracle: rc=0, declared 1". MEASURED by applying the
mutation by hand to a copy and running its --selftest: 14/14 controls still fired, including "  ok  a mint whose id
is ABSENT from the top level fires (the BUG-587 ABSORBED shape)".

elements, so the COUNT clause fired (expected len(live)+1, measured len(live)) and the control passed for a reason
other than the one it NAMES. With the mutation applied the count clause still spoke, so the arrival rule could be
neutered with EVERY control green - a control whose name and reason disagree is not a control (D-2676 iv, one level
down: the exact class the mutation gate exists to see).
FIX: the count is landed EXACTLY (len(live) - 1 before + 1 minted == len(absorbed_after)), so the control can only
pass or fail through the top-level clause it names. MEASURED after the fix: the mutant prints "  !!  a mint whose id
is ABSENT from the top level fires (the BUG-587 ABSORBED shape)" and exits 1, and the live gate reads "ok rail
mutations: 23 declared rule(s) SEEN to red through their own control ... 1 negative control(s) stayed green, 17/13
declared subject(s) covered (4 derived from the commit boundary, D-2679)".

(a_duplicated_declaring_line_is_refused; floor 24 -> 25, SEEN to red through the control's own name).

## BUG-569 (CLOSED, LOW, D-2695): the adoption NOTE has no RAIL-LEVEL control at a real partial commit
MEASURED 2026-09-27: the rule's controls lived in scripts/lib/git_subject.py --selftest (13/13, both directions,

red and the adoption itself untouched (a mutation that removed the adoption would red the BUG-527 refusal
control as well, and a differential that moves two controls proves neither). INSTRUMENTATION (temp/b569_probe.py,
run before the control was written): an index built from `read-tree --empty` makes the rail refuse at the
BUG-528 family check (rc=2 over 1314 deletions) and NEVER name the probe path, so the audited-bytes limb can
only be satisfied by the `read-tree HEAD` + one-added-path shape - the earlier attempt that used --empty failed
its own baseline for exactly that reason. The probe is SYNTHETIC-plan and SYNTHETIC-index: rc=1 is a fact about

anti-vacuity guard (a harness that cannot mint a name, or a blob that does not resolve, FAILS the control rather

## BUG-592 (CLOSED, MED, D-2698 - FILED by D-2698): the BUG-568 pin control RECURSES through its own --selftest

STATUS: CLOSED. Found while draining BUG-591/D-2697: not a defect of the pin RULE (the pin is correct) but of its CONTROL, which was unbounded.

MEASURED 2026-09-27 (temp/d2697_diag.py, then temp/d2698_mutcheck.py): with the pin mutated as the standing rule requires (config/rail_mutations.yaml#the_rail0_subject_pin_is_load_bearing sets subj, note = None, "") `scripts/check_repo_integrity.py --selftest` did NOT red - it HUNG: rc=124 in 600.0s at the 120s runner ceiling, the DID-NOT-RED the gate reports as "the rule is DECLARED but not READ" (class iii of D-2665, BUG-457 owner-owed). Stack: check_repo_integrity.py:773 in _rail <- :778 in selftest <- :844 in main.

ROOT CAUSE: the pin control proves the decoy is refused by RE-ENTERING the rail with --selftest. With the pin intact the child refuses the decoy in subject_bits() and returns fast; with the pin MUTATED the child tolerates the decoy, runs the WHOLE selftest, reaches the same control and nests for ever. The old fixture BUILDER - which handed its child git the ambient environment (BUG-591) - was the ACCIDENTAL BOUND: under a decoy it returned None and failed the child fast. D-2697 removed that accident and EXPOSED this pre-existing defect. Nothing regressed; a hidden dependency was deleted.

FIX (D-2698): the probe is extracted into the module-level `pin_controls(cfg, ok, n)` and the nested run is given `--no-pin-probe`, which skips the PROBE and never the RULE - the decoy is still refused BEFORE any mode runs (subject_bits() is main() first act), so the bound costs the control nothing.

TEETH (D-2676 iv): BASELINE `--selftest` rc=0 with 17 control(s) and rc=0 with 17 AFTER (the count does not move); MUTATED rc=1 in 4.4s with EXACTLY ONE red line, the declared marker `FAIL repo-integrity selftest/rail0_pins_its_own_subject`, restored byte-identical. Gate: `ok rail mutations: 31 declared rule(s) SEEN to red through their own control` rc=0 over 32 entries = floor 32, with BOTH the D-2696 pin entry and the D-2697 fixture entry in the SEEN list. BUG-592 is CLOSED.

## BUG-593 (OPEN, MED - the MUTATION GATE's fixture carries ONE commit, so a rule whose oracle joins GIT HISTORY cannot satisfy limb (iv) - FILED 2026-09-27 while attempting the BUG-559 drain, D-2699)
FOUND BY: the BUG-559 drain. The owed remedy was the standing rule's limb (iv) (D-2676): the receipt-provenance join (D-2670) had NO mutation entry, so the rule was verified by its own known-answer controls only. An entry was written exactly to the declared schema (`the_receipt_provenance_join_is_load_bearing`, subject/runner scripts/verify_handoffs.py, `--selftest`, marker 'a receipt over a FOREIGN body is REFUSED').
MEASURED, BOTH HALVES: (1) OUTSIDE the fixture the entry is SOUND - the fall-through of receipt_provenance() reduced to 'declared' makes the rail's own selftest rc=1 with EXACTLY TWO declared red lines ('a receipt over a SAME-LENGTH live copy is REFUSED (the BUG-559 shape)' and 'a receipt over a FOREIGN body is REFUSED') while the digestless limb keeps its own early return and stays GREEN, so the differential isolates the fall-through and not a crash; restored byte-identical. (2) INSIDE the fixture the ORACLE's BASELINE IS RED: `FAIL verify_handoffs selftest: revision bc1cc956cbd07fd7 does not re-derive from git:65a13c3cff5b89f584f6411c65082e2e479434cb` (and be1a39e04c378af9 from git:075ae65, f2778a488610cbf1 from git:44c249b). REPRODUCED OUTSIDE THE GATE in a hand-built fixture (scripts+config+justfile+governance/bug_status.json+governance/HANDOFFS.jsonl, `git init/add/commit`): the same three FAIL lines, rc=1.
MECHANISM: the gate's fixture is built from `git: [init, add, commit]` - it carries ONE synthetic commit and NO history. This rail's oracle joins the declared revision LOCATORS, which name git refs of the LIVE repository, so in any fresh fixture those bytes cannot exist. The fixture therefore cannot make this oracle green, and the gate (correctly, per BUG-589) REFUSED to blame the mutation: 'the oracle's BASELINE is not green (rc=1) ... its red after one proves nothing'.
WHY THIS IS A GAP IN THE STANDING RULE AND NOT A DEFECT OF THE ENTRY: (iv) is satisfiable only where the oracle is FIXTURE-PORTABLE, and NOTHING declares that condition - so the next agent walks into the same wall. Two remedies, both explicit: (a) the fixture owes a DECLARED HISTORY - a list of {path, blob or bytes, message} applied as successive commits under `fixture.history`, so a history-reading oracle has a green baseline BY CONSTRUCTION (the preferred remedy: it strengthens every future rail of this class); (b) declare the rule UNCOVERABLE-BY-MUTATION with its reason, joined in both directions (D-405) so a rule that cannot be covered is named rather than silently absent. The third option - weakening the oracle (dropping the revision controls from --selftest) - is REFUSED: it would trade a real control for a green gate.
STATUS: the entry was WITHDRAWN and the floor returned to 32 (D-2699); the receipt-provenance rule keeps its own 7-case known-answer control and the live join (6/6 re-derivable, rc=0). BUG-559 stays OPEN.

**BUG-559 STATUS (2026-09-27, the DRAIN was ATTEMPTED and its blocker is MEASURED - D-2699).** The owed fix LANDED on 2026-09-26: D-2670 joined every receipt to a store that re-derives its bytes (head/prefix/revision/declared, live rc=0, 6/6 re-derivable) and D-2671 promoted the one unjoined object. What was OWED SINCE is the STANDING RULE's limb (iv) - a MUTATION that REDs the join's oracle - because D-2676 was adopted the day AFTER D-2670, so the rule was covered by its own controls only. The entry was written, pre-measured green outside the fixture (rc=1 with EXACTLY TWO declared red lines, restored byte-identical) and then WITHDRAWN, because inside the gate's fixture the ORACLE'S BASELINE is red for a reason that is the FIXTURE'S: the revision controls re-derive locators from git refs the fixture cannot carry (BUG-593, filed and parked). NOT WEAKENED: the rule keeps its 7-case control; nothing in the rail changed.
REMAINING, unchanged and NARROWED: (1) the STORE-LEVEL half - a receipt over an EARLIER COMMITTED revision is reported unrevisioned (remedy: a declared revision locator), and the two run-root escapes are held by census, declared with reasons and SHRINK-ONLY; (2) the PROSE half - the SECOND INSTANCE named at filing, a digest quoted with an ELLIPSIS (governance/ANCHOR_ADJUDICATION_NORMALIZATION_20260925.md line 9, `f2778a488610cbf1...`), is OUTSIDE the hash-claim ruler (which joins 64-HEX digests), so it is not refused - it is not even a SUBJECT. Remedy (owed, small): teach the digest-claim domain to join a truncated hex prefix against the same stores, so a truncation RESOLVES or is DRIFT.
THEREFORE the freeze window reads nothing_still_held = 2 still parked (BUG-559 and the newly parked BUG-593, ceiling 11 -> 12) and this id is NOT released: the drain's remaining work is the PROSE join plus the fixture HISTORY that lets limb (iv) cover the store-level rule.

## BUG-604 (OPEN, 2026-09-30) — stage0_5 metadata extractor mis-splits "liber3.md" filenames, leaking title words into the author field (split book identities)

SCOPE: pipeline/book_metadata.py parse_filename_metadata() / stage0_5_extract_metadata.py; knowledge pipeline/checkpoints/book_metadata.jsonl.
FINDING (2026-09-30 forensic audit, D-2736): the source_book filenames from the "liber3" corpus are formatted
"<title words> <author name> liber3.md", and the author/title split boundary is mis-detected: trailing title words
leak into `author` while the title is truncated. Verified examples (author | title | source_book):
  - 'Contextual Perspective Alan Male' | 'Illustration A Theoretical and' | 'Illustration A Theoretical and Contextual Perspective Alan Male liber3.md'
  - 'Services Jon Yablonski' | 'Laws of UX Using Psychology to Design Better Products &' | '...Better Products & Services Jon Yablonski liber3.md'
  - 'Totalitarianism Mattias Desmet' | 'The Psychology of' | 'The Psychology of Totalitarianism Mattias Desmet liber3.md'
  - 'Basics Daniel Chandler' | 'Semiotics The' | 'Semiotics The Basics Daniel Chandler liber3.md'
  - 'Research Project Zina O'Leary' | 'The Essential Guide to Doing Your' | 'The Essential Guide to Doing Your Research Project Zina O'Leary liber3.md'
EFFECT: each mis-split book produces a DIFFERENT canonical source_id than its correctly-split edition, so the same
work counts as two distinct sources (BUG-289 tail). The new detector scripts/detect_title_renames.py surfaces 45
candidate near-duplicate pairs (jaccard >= 0.60) of which ~40 are this class; the remainder are genuine series
volumes ("The Great Mental Models" Vol 1-4) that MUST NOT be merged (false-positive proof that auto-merge corrupts).
FIX (post-run, D-2736): repair parse_filename_metadata to strip the "liber3.md" suffix BEFORE splitting and to
recognize the trailing-author-name boundary, then re-resolve the affected source_ids — POST RATIFY-2, because
changing source_ids mid-run would change the live embedding fingerprint b9e924d5.

## BUG-607 (CLOSED, 2026-09-30, D-2745) — Stage 2 ModuleNotFoundError: datasketch — bare "python3" in runner drifted across FOUR Python envs (root cause, NOT transient)
SCOPE: pipeline/runner.py run_stage() — `subprocess.run(["python3", script])` (line 374) and the preflight
`["python3", watchdog, "--pre-stage"]` (line 402) resolve "python3" via the LAUNCHER's PATH, not a pinned interpreter.
SYMPTOM (recurring 3x, misdiagnosed "transient" in D-2742/D-2743): S2 fails with
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'datasketch'` at stage2_extract.py:1396 (init_minhash_lsh) → exit 1.
FORENSIC ROOT CAUSE (2026-09-30): the machine has FOUR Python interpreters with DIVERGENT dependency sets:
  - /Users/barn/miniforge3/bin/python3 (conda base, 3.13.12) — the USER's login-zsh `python3` (conda init in .zshrc);
    has numpy/scipy/yaml/pandas/faiss/pyarrow/transformers/torch, NO datasketch (until this fix).
  - /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.12/bin/python3 (Python.org 3.12) — the ONLY env that had
    datasketch 2.0.0, because a prior assistant ran `pip install datasketch` in a NON-login shell (does NOT source
    .zshrc), so bare `python3` resolved to /usr/local/bin/python3 → framework 3.12.
  - /Users/barn/miniforge3/envs/knowledge-pipeline (3.11.15) — named for the project but INCOMPLETE: no
    pandas/pyarrow/datasketch.
  - /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (3.14.6) — reserved for S6 vec0 (stage6.vec_python); no datasketch.
BLINDSPOT: "datasketch installed / transient" tests ran in a non-login shell → framework 3.12 → false PASS, while
the user's actual launch env (login zsh → conda base) had no datasketch. The assistant tested the WRONG interpreter.
FIX (D-2745): (1) `pip install datasketch` into conda base (the user's `python3`); (2) add run.python_bin to
config/pipeline_config.yaml (C12) + _get_python_bin() in runner.py, used for BOTH the stage subprocess and the
preflight, so stages can never drift to a different interpreter than the pinned full-dep-chain env.
VERIFIED: init_minhash_lsh → MinHashLSH ok=True; MinHashLSH insert/query/jaccard round-trip passes under
/Users/barn/miniforge3/bin/python3; `--dry-run --resume-from 2` previews stages 2,4,5,6,6b,6c.
FOLLOW-UP: consolidate the 4-Python drift — either fully-provision knowledge-pipeline (3.11) or delete it and declare
conda base canonical; remove the stray framework-3.12 datasketch install.

## BUG-608 (CLOSED, 2026-09-30) — runner preflight treated watchdog rc==1 (restarted/recovered) as "OMLX DOWN"
SCOPE: pipeline/runner.py preflight + pipeline/omlx_watchdog.py check_and_restart() return-code contract.
ROOT CAUSE: check_and_restart() returns 0=OK, 1=restarted(recovered), 2=error, but the runner's preflight treated ANY
non-zero as "OMLX DOWN" and aborted S2. The orphaned omlx-server (D-2743) was unhealthy → the watchdog restarted it
(rc=1) → the runner aborted with "❌ OMLX DOWN". Compounded by the BUG-017 trend detector false-positives on the
0→8.6GB model-load spike (delta 8.5GB > 2GB trend threshold), which triggered the spurious restart in the first place.
FIX: (1) runner.py treats rc==1 as RECOVERED — re-verifies health once, only aborts on rc==2 or a repeated rc==1.
(2) omlx_watchdog.py adds RSS_TREND_MIN_GB (default 10.0) so a trend restart only fires above 10GB (a genuine leak),
never on the initial model-load spike. Verified: preflight rc=0, "OMLX OK: RSS 4.4GB (restarts: 1)".

## BUG-609 (CLOSED, 2026-10-02) — S2 CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS (exit 2) never advances → deterministic schema failures loop forever
SCOPE: pipeline/stage2_extract.py CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS exit path + config stage2.accept_conditional_within_tolerance.
ROOT CAUSE: A handful of clusters (2–5 of 12,607) emit schema-invalid FBs at temp=0.0 (empty definition, 2-char
  name, missing mechanism/boundary/consequence). At temp=0.0 the failure is DETERMINISTIC — re-running can never
  clear it — yet the exit-2 "Re-run to retry failed clusters" path was the only route to advance, so S2 looped
  forever (first run: 5 failed clusters, exit 2 at 110,814s; every retry hit the same clusters, same failures).
FIX: C12 config stage2.accept_conditional_within_tolerance: true + S2_ACCEPT_CONDITIONAL in pipeline_paths.py.
  When failed/total ≤ max_failed_ratio, CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS now exits 0 (advance to S4) instead of 2.
  NOTE: BUG-609 alone did NOT end the loop — see BUG-610 (the denominator bug that masked this path).

## BUG-610 (CLOSED, 2026-10-02) — S2 fail-closed ratio used the post-resume subset as denominator → hard-fail exit 1 masked the within-tolerance path
SCOPE: pipeline/stage2_extract.py terminal failure-ratio logic (total_attempted).
ROOT CAUSE: The fail-closed check ran BEFORE the CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS branch and computed
  failure_ratio = failed_clusters / len(target_clusters), but on a resume target_clusters is already SHRUNK to only
  the 2–5 unprocessed clusters. With 2–3 deterministic schema failures among 3–5 remaining, the ratio was 60–67% —
  far over max_failed_ratio (0.01) — so it hard-failed exit 1 before ever reaching the within-tolerance branch that
  BUG-609's flag gates. The denominator was "remaining subset", not "total corpus".
FIX: capture total_corpus_targets = len(target_clusters) BEFORE the resume filter; compute
  failure_ratio = failed_clusters / total_corpus_targets (12,607). Verified: S2 exits 0 — 2/12,607 clusters dropped
  (0.016% ≤ 0.01), 8,217 FBs final, pipeline advances to S4.

## BUG-612 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-03) — principle-purity drift: deterministic triage flags 2.1% of 7,151 principle records as definitional non-rules

RESOLUTION (D-2748/D-2750, 2026-10-02): principle-purity audit + adjudication APPLIED. The 527 flagged principles
(152 definitional_no_prescriptive + 238 definitional_with_prescriptive + 144 open_tension + 1 procedure + 5 exact_dup)
were deterministically seeded into governance/content_type_adjudication.json (now 573 rows) via the D-2750 tier-2
fail-closed FORM invariant (_principle_form_violation). No auto-DROP — noise_drop stays owner-gated via tier-1.
Smoke tests green, 0 invalid proposed values.

SCOPE: the SAME rechunk-v4-20260929 checkpoint (8,217 FBs), but the PRINCIPLE bin (7,151 = 87.0%) — which D-2747 /
BUG-611 did NOT audit (that audit covered only the 4 non-principle bins). This is the blindspot the user asked about:
"are all principles 100% transferable rules?" — NO, deterministically ~2.1% are not.
FINDING (scripts/audit_principle_purity.py — pure deterministic rules, D-343 no LLM → temp/principle_purity_triage.json):
527 principles (7.4%) fire a structural signal:
  - definitional_no_prescriptive 152 (2.1%) — the definition asserts "X is / describes / involves" a concept AND no
    prescriptive verb anywhere in the body → a descriptive fact, NOT a transferable rule (D275b: KNOW/APPLY). e.g.
    "A knowledge graph is a data structure...", "The concept of childhood as a distinct developmental stage...".
    HIGH-PRECISION candidate set → noise_drop / descriptive_model.
  - definitional_with_prescriptive 238 (3.3%) — definitional framing BUT a prescriptive verb is present → AMBIGUOUS
    (owner review: many are legitimate despite the framing, e.g. "Natural curiosity is a more reliable predictor...").
  - open_tension 144 (2.0%) — articulates a contested/unverified correlation → growth_edge candidate per D275b/BUG-230
    (mixed precision; false positives like "speaker's message contradicts their nonverbal behavior" are real principles).
  - procedure 1 (false positive — "third rewrite... fourth rewrite" is NOT a step sequence; CONFIRMS D275b: step-count
    is never the discriminator).
  - exact_dup 5 (one definition string × 5 records — a SHA-256 dedup leak).
CONSEQUENCE: the principle bin was ASSUMED 100% pure. ~2.1% are deterministically non-rules and would commit to S6
mis-binned, plus a larger semantic-boundary set (~390) needs owner adjudication before the axis can be called clean.
ROOT CAUSE: S4's classify prompt is principle-only (BUG-170), and _resolve_content_type() is a principle-only safety
net — principles pass through reroute_content_type() as a NO-OP (only non-principle tiers exist). Nothing verifies a
principle's OWN purity before S6.
FIX (owner-gated, do NOT auto-flip — a 2% knowledge-base drop cascades): extend the D-2747 3-tier gate to principles
with a structural invariant (definitional + no prescriptive → disposition), seeded by owner adjudication of
temp/principle_purity_triage.json; then re-run the audit. See D-2748.

## BUG-613 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-03) — extraction_type (FORM) axis is unverified + cross-contaminated; D2417 default `principle → descriptive_model` is a latent inversion

RESOLUTION (D-2749/D-2750, 2026-10-02): D2417 flip RATIFIED — config/content_types.yaml
content_to_extraction_type.principle = normative_heuristic (was descriptive_model; a principle is a transferable RULE).
FORM declared best-effort metadata, never a routing/verification input. Tier-2 FORM invariant wired into
reroute_content_type() (_principle_form_violation): principle whose FORM is not a rule reroutes fail-closed to a
RETAINED disposition only (never auto-noise_drop).

SCOPE: rechunk-v4-20260929 checkpoint (8,217 FBs), the extraction_type (epistemic FORM) axis — the "does content_type rely
on FORM, and is FORM accurate" question.
DEPENDENCY DIRECTION (verified in code): content_type (ROLE) does NOT depend on extraction_type (FORM) — D2323 decouples
them and _resolve_content_type()/reroute_content_type() never read extraction_type. The REAL dependency is the REVERSE:
D2417 CONTENT_TO_EXTRACTION_TYPE defaults extraction_type FROM content_type when S2 omits it. So FORM inherits ROLE's
errors, not vice-versa.
FINDING (scripts/audit_form_axis.py — deterministic signal lexicons, D-343 no LLM → temp/form_axis_audit.json):
  (1) FORM signal agreement is LOW: causal_mechanism 19.5%, descriptive_model 37.3%, normative_heuristic 35.1%,
      empirical_pattern 34.1%; high no-signal (up to 1,127) → the axis is largely UNVERIFIABLE by structure.
  (2) systematic cross-contamination: causal_mechanism records fire a normative signal 726×; descriptive_model fires
      normative 179× / causal 76×; empirical_pattern fires descriptive 387×.
  (3) LATENT INVERSION: CONTENT_TO_EXTRACTION_TYPE['principle'] = 'descriptive_model' — a principle is a transferable RULE
      (normative), so defaulting it to the "describes" FORM bakes in the descriptive leak. In THIS checkpoint 0 records were
      defaulted (_extraction_type_defaulted == 0), so it is LATENT not ACTIVE — but any future batch where S2 omits
      extraction_type silently stamps every principle as descriptive_model.
ROOT CAUSE: the FORM axis has no downstream verifier (S4 classify is principle-only for content_type; nothing checks
extraction_type before S6). Same class of drift as BUG-170 / BUG-611 / BUG-612 — an LLM-assigned label never re-verified.
IMPACT: extraction_type feeds serving_gate epistemic_status derivation and downstream depth/verification consumers; an
unverified FORM axis is a hidden-failure surface. Present-day blast radius is low (0 defaulted, axis is best-effort).
FIX (owner-gated): (a) flip D2417 default principle → normative_heuristic (semantic correctness, needs owner ratification);
(b) make explicit that extraction_type is BEST-EFFORT metadata, never a routing/verification input; (c) if FORM is ever
relied upon, add a cross-contamination canary (D2376 _warn_extraction_type_dominance is the existing pattern).

## BUG-614 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-03) — live S4 process executed PRE-REROUTE code for ~5.5h; 418-record partial checkpoint contaminated (50 provably mis-routed)
RESOLUTION (D-2806): the stage-code fingerprint is now shipped to EVERY checkpoint-writing stage — a config-owned
stage_code_fingerprint() + sidecar write/read/fail-closed-resume in pipeline/stamp.py wired into stage0/0_5/1/1_3/1_5/2/6
(joining the existing stage4 inline + stage5 config-owned fingerprints). A long-running subprocess can no longer silently
resume (or emit) against a stage module edited mid-run: any committed-or-uncommitted code drift invalidates the checkpoint.

SCOPE: rechunk-v4-20260929 S4 (stage4_merge.py), live process PID 60590 started 05:55:45, running when the D-2747/D-2748/
D-2749/D-2750 reroute was wired into pipeline/stage4_merge.py (mtime 10:41:29) and pipeline/content_types.py (mtime 11:11:18).
FINDING (forensic audit): Python loads modules at process start, so the live S4 process had the OLD _resolve_content_type()
that returned `ct` verbatim (no reroute_content_type call). The reroute is wired at stage4_merge.py:273 but the running
process never saw it. Proof: 50 of the 418 already-written partial-checkpoint records have fb_ids present in
governance/content_type_adjudication.json (28→quarantine, 17→noise_drop, 5→growth_edge) yet were committed as `principle`.
Dry-run of reroute_content_type() over the full S2 checkpoint (8,217 FBs) confirms the NEW code corrects 627 records
(principle→quarantine 231, principle→growth_edge 183, principle→noise_drop 151, TI→PT 34, TI→principle 14, principle→PT 9,
TI→quarantine 3, TI→PI 1, GE→noise_drop 1).
IMPACT: the partial checkpoint is a STALE artifact — it does not reflect the adjudicated ontology. If it were resumed or
committed to S6, up to 50 (so far) records would reach SQLite under the wrong ROLE, silently re-opening BUG-611/BUG-612.
ACTION TAKEN: SIGTERM/SIGINT sent to runner PID 60572 and stage4 PID 60590 (both now exited). Checkpoint frozen at 418
records / state.json record_count 418. Remediation (owner-gated, long-running): back up the stale partial checkpoint, then
restart S4 fresh so all 8,217 FBs pass through reroute_content_type() at the now-wired choke point.
ROOT CAUSE (class): a hot-reload gap — a long-running subprocess is not invalidated when a stage module it imported is
edited mid-run. The BUG-183 stale-resume guard only detects S2-input fingerprint drift, NOT code drift of stage4_merge.py
itself. RECOMMENDATION: a cheap pipeline_commit / module-mtime guard in stage4_merge.py __main__ that aborts (or warns) when
its own source mtime is newer than process start (same pattern as the existing s2_input_fingerprint guard).

## BUG-615 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-03) — cross-cluster fb_id dedup leak: 5 identical FBs emitted as separate records (name-disambiguated)

SCOPE: rechunk-v4-20260929 S2 checkpoint (8,217 lines) and S4 partial checkpoint (418 records).
FINDING (forensic audit): the S2 checkpoint has 8,212 unique fb_ids over 8,217 lines — 5 duplicate records. One fb_id
(334554e0…) appears 5× ("Value-first Demonstration"), another (f8b4e061…) appears 2×. All copies are BYTE-IDENTICAL
(same definition, mechanism, source_segments, source_principle_ids). The S4 partial checkpoint already materialised 3 of
them as "Value-first Demonstration", "(2)", "(3)" — the name-disambiguation suffix (D2069/D2350) fixes the NAME collision
but NOT the fb_id identity collision.
ROOT CAUSE: cluster-before-extract placed the SAME source segments into 5 distinct clusters, so S2 extracted the identical
principle 5× under the same content-hash fb_id (fb_id is identity-fixed at S2, D2350). dedup_fbs_by_cosine (D2120) only
dedups WITHIN a cluster — it never fires under the 1-principle-per-cluster invariant — so cross-cluster duplicates leak
through S4 and would reach S5/S6 as N distinct rows with the same fb_id (violates DB unique constraint, inflates counts).
IMPACT: 5 spurious records; a silent bloat + identity-collision surface at S6. The 5× case is the "5-record dedup leak"
observed in the partial checkpoint state.
FIX: cross-run fb_id dedup guard in stage4_merge.py — a seen_fb_ids set (rebuilt from resumed fbs) that skips a duplicate
fb_id and merges its source_clusters/source_segments provenance into the kept record (fail-closed, deterministic). Upstream
S1.5 cluster-assignment root cause (same segment → 5 clusters) is a SEPARATE investigation.

RESOLUTION (D-2807): the cross-cluster seen_fb_ids dedup guard is implemented in the stage4_merge.py
main classify loop — a duplicate fb_id is skipped and its source_clusters/source_segments provenance
merged into the kept record (fail-closed, deterministic). 5 spurious records prevented at S4; the S6
unique-constraint surface is closed.

## BUG-616 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-03) — BUG-183 S2-input-drift guard deletes depth.json; a code-drift guard must PRESERVE it

SCOPE: stage4_merge.py resume block (BUG-183 guard ~lines 1430-1490).
FINDING: depth.json (checkpoint.jsonl.depth.json) is a content-derived sidecar — cluster_id → depth value, computed by
batch_depth_classify from the principle's discipline/domains/mechanism. It is INDEPENDENT of content_type routing (the
D-2747 reroute changes routing, not depth). It has 7,149 entries (~1-2h of compute) that are still valid after the reroute.
The existing BUG-183 guard (and its D2487/format-guard siblings) DELETE depth.json (and .cribs.json) whenever it discards a
stale checkpoint — correct for S2-INPUT drift (cluster_ids change), but WRONG for CODE drift (reroute changes routing only,
depth values are unchanged).
IMPACT: if the BUG-614 fix (stage-code drift guard) reuses the existing discard path, a code-only change would destroy the
reusable depth.json sidecar, wasting ~1-2h of depth classification on every code edit.
FIX: the new stage-code drift guard must discard ONLY fbs + processed_ids + scalar_state, and PRESERVE depth.json/.cribs.json
(content-derived, code-independent). S2-input drift continues to delete them (cluster_ids are input-bound).


RESOLUTION (D-2807): the stage-code drift guard (BUG-614) discards ONLY fbs+processed_ids+scalar_state
and PRESERVES depth.json/.cribs.json (content-derived, code-independent); S2-input drift still deletes
them. depth.json (~7,149 entries, ~1-2h compute) now survives code-only edits.

## BUG-621 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-03) — S4 classifier (gpt-oss-20b) has no head-to-head fit evidence against faster/more-accurate alternatives; Pareto status unverified
FINDING (market research 2026-10-02): gpt-oss-20b (3.6B-active MoE) was chosen for S4 classification without a
head-to-head "fit" eval against alternatives on Maxwell's own human gold (149 depth + 204 discipline). Its
"faster AND more accurate" Pareto position is therefore UNVERIFIED — a hidden blindspot of the same epistemic class
the project otherwise rejects (bare accuracy over kappa, LLM-vs-LLM circular conformance). IMPACT: we cannot claim
the S4 classifier is optimal; any future swap is arbitrary without a measurement. FIX: a gated head-to-head FIT eval
(Cohen's kappa + tok/s vs gold) before ANY classifier change (D-2767). Shortlist: Mistral-Small-3.1-24B (primary),
Gemma-3-12b-it (secondary). Qwen3-* excluded by R5 (generator-family independence).

RESOLUTION (D-2788/D-2789 + D-2808, 2026-10-03): the head-to-head FIT eval BUG-621 demanded is DONE and NEGATIVE-on-swap — the Pareto status is now VERIFIED, not assumed. D-2788 measured gemma-4-12B-it-qat-OptiQ-4bit SLOWER than gpt-oss-20b on BOTH axes (S4 + depth); D-2789 exhausted the swap path 5/5 (all candidates rejected/parked); D-2792/D-2793 proved the remaining gap is measurement-bound (human 3-way discipline ceiling 0.766 < 0.8 operative floor). Conclusion: gpt-oss-20b STAYS the S4 classifier — no swap, no re-fit (ratified in D-2808). BUG-621 CLOSED — the "no fit evidence" blindspot is now measured evidence.

## BUG-622 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-03) — S4 discipline classifier (gpt-oss-20b) FAILS human-gold conformance: kappa ~0.45 << 0.8 operative floor (first live measurement)
FINDING (forensic audit, first live conformance run): the production S4 discipline classifier of record
(merged_cribs_classify -> map_to_canonical_with_fallback, gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8) scores Cohen's kappa ~0.45 against
the 204-row human-owner discipline anchor (discipline_anchor_conformance_20261002.json, D-2766). Sample N=30:
agreement 46.7%, kappa 0.452; N=12: 0.234. FAR below the 0.800 operative floor AND the 0.667 reporting floor
(D-2611: never bare accuracy on a 49-class skewed prior). 27% of predictions remap to 'emerging' (off-menu /
opposite-axis guard). Two-layer root cause: (1) the D-2769 gate itself mis-measured — it invoked
slim_batch_discipline_classify (the BUG-197/D2532 *emerging-row* re-classifier, NOT the main S4 classifier) and
compared RAW free-form strings WITHOUT the production remap: raw kappa 0.060 vs remapped-slim 0.268 vs correct
merged+remap 0.452. (2) Even the correct classifier free-generates adjacent-but-wrong disciplines (e.g.
'psychology' for 'neuroscience', 'information science' for 'computer graphics', 'economics' for 'privacy &
surveillance', 'artificial intelligence' for 'information retrieval').
IMPACT: the S4 discipline axis is NON-CONFORMANT to human ground truth. Committing discipline labels as-is would
inject a ~55% wrong discipline signal into the knowledge store. This also strengthens BUG-621 (gpt-oss fit was
never verified — and now it demonstrably fails the discipline sub-task).
FIX: (a) D-2770 corrected the gate to mirror production (merged_cribs_classify + remap). (b) Root-cause the low
kappa BEFORE any S4 discipline commit — candidates: inline label-list erosion in the merged prompt, absent
negative-exemplar disambiguation, 49-class prior. (c) Do NOT commit discipline labels or swap the classifier until
kappa >= 0.800 (D-2767 gate). NEXT: full 204-row run for a definitive kappa with proper CI (N=30/12 samples above
are indicative, not final).
UPDATE (D-2774, 2026-10-02): the D-2773 closed-menu fix was IMPLEMENTED behind stage4.discipline_closed_menu_enabled
(default false) and live A/B'd on N=30 — menu ON kappa 0.344 vs menu OFF baseline 0.452 (net -0.11). The closed menu
did NOT help; flag reverted to false. This REFINES the root cause: the binding constraint is gpt-oss-20b's
discrimination QUALITY across the 62-label space, NOT the open-vocabulary generation. PIVOT to classifier FIT eval /
swap (D-2767) rather than further prompt engineering on gpt-oss.

UPDATE (D-2797, 2026-10-03): OWNER RATIFIED the 3-way macro re-scope as PRIMARY routing facet + human-parity gate
(~0.73-0.77). CONDITION A (collapse of committed fbs.discipline -> 3-way, ZERO inference): kappa 0.5534 (raw 0.7255,
N=204) — BELOW 0.65 ship threshold; 16 off-menu 'emerging' abstentions (7.8%) ALL WRONG (fine-axis remap failure).
CONDITION C (dedicated 3-way classifier) BUILT (scripts/discipline_macro_classify.py, selftest + dry-run GREEN).

UPDATE (D-2798, 2026-10-03): CONDITION C MEASURED — kappa 0.6066 (raw 0.7696, N=204), BELOW the 0.65 ship threshold
AND below the 0.73 human-parity floor (human 3-way ceiling 0.766). 3-way macro NOT shipped as a routing facet;
discipline is ADVISORY-ONLY (fine-62 -> advisory multi-label tags, soft facet; routing does not gate on discipline).
Condition C beats Condition A (0.6066 vs 0.5534) by eliminating the 16 off-menu abstentions (now 1); residual error =

=256 was too small for the Harmony reasoning CoT (billed against max_tokens) -> finish_reason='length' before content;

RESOLUTION (D-2808, 2026-10-03): owner ratified the D-2798/D-2799 advisory-only BUG-622 contract as FINAL. The

## BUG-632 (OPEN, 2026-10-04) — the D2496 "authoritative expected FB count" gate CANNOT DISTINGUISH a DECLARED failure from a SILENT drop, so S5 and S6 are UNREACHABLE on any S4 run with >=1 failed cluster (the BUG-609 class, applied to S2 only)

**MEASURED** (run `rechunk-v4-20260929`, S4 complete 2026-10-04 18:22):
- `checkpoint.jsonl` on disk = **6,587** records (verified `wc -l`).
- `checkpoint.jsonl.expected_count.json` = `expected_fb_count: **6591**`.
- `expected_fb_count` (`pipeline/stage4_merge.py:~1398`) counts every single-principle DEFAULT-content-type cluster — every cluster S4 *should* turn into an FB — and does **NOT** subtract the `failed` counter.
- 4 clusters were QUARANTINED fail-closed by D2371 (empty/short application, 0 chars): `cluster_6030`, `cluster_26828`, `cluster_28517`, `cluster_40300` — **all `GEN skipped (single-FB)`**.
- 6591 - 4 = 6587 exactly. The shortfall is entirely **declared**, recorded, and intentional.

**CONSEQUENCE — a hard deadlock with two independent locks:**
1. `pipeline/stage4_merge.py:2506` `sys.exit(2)` on CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS -> the runner does NOT advance (deliberate, documented).
2. Even if the owner forces `--resume-from 5`: `stage5_verify._preflight_gate` -> `scripts/preflight_checkpoint_check.py --check <ckpt> --expect-count 6591` -> `AUTHORITATIVE COUNT MISMATCH: on-disk 6587 vs --expect-count 6591` -> **exit 1** -> `sys.exit(1)`. **REPRODUCED LIVE this session.**
3. `scripts/pre_s6_gate.py:_expected_count()` reads the **same** sidecar -> S6 is blocked by the same defect.
A re-run cannot clear it: the 4 failures are deterministic (`GEN skipped (single-FB)` + S2-extracted empty application), so re-running reproduces the identical state. S4 has **NO** `accept_conditional_within_tolerance` equivalent — only `stage2` has it (`config/pipeline_config.yaml:302`), because BUG-609 fixed S2 and S4 never got the same treatment.

**WHY IT MATTERS:** D2496 added the sidecar to catch a SILENT S4-side record drop (BUG-188 class). Failing on `on_disk < expected` is correct. Failing when the entire shortfall is the stage's own declared, fail-closed `failed` count is wrong. The sidecar is **UNDER-SPECIFIED**: it persists `expected_fb_count` but not `failed_clusters`, so the gate cannot tell "4 declared failures" from "4 silently dropped records". The fix must **ADD** the declared number — never relax the inequality (relaxing to `<=` would re-open BUG-188).

**SECONDARY FINDING** (same run, recorded, not a blocker): S4 exited 2, so `runner._write_resume_marker(4)` / `_write_checkpoint_manifest(4)` never ran -> the run dir has **NO** `pipeline_resume.json` and **NO** `.s4.manifest.json`. S5's preflight therefore degrades to "No manifest - boundary verified but content hash not pinned", i.e. the **D2487 SHA-256 pin is absent for this entire 77 MB checkpoint**. `safe_write` (os.replace) makes mid-record cuts unobservable, so this is a WEAKENED-but-not-broken control; reported because the fail-closed exit-2 path silently costs the manifest.

**FIX (D-2817):** persist `failed_clusters` + `failed_cluster_ids` in the sidecar; teach the checker `--declared-failed N` so it passes only when `on_disk + N == expected` and still fails for any undeclared shortfall; forward it in S5 and S6. Preserve `exit 2` as the deliberate human gate — the fix makes the owner's **decided** advance work, it does not remove the decision. Also: the exit-2 path must write the manifest so a conditional success keeps its SHA-256 pin.

## BUG-633 (CLOSED, 2026-10-04) — bug_status.status_slot() let PROSE decide the status: a header explicitly labelled "(OPEN, ...)" retired a LIVE bug because its trailing prose held a status word (third occurrence of the BUG-572 class)

**RESOLUTION (D-2818, 2026-10-04):** the LEADING parenthetical is now AUTHORITATIVE — an explicit "(OPEN, ...)" binds as OPEN and blocks prose fall-through (OPEN_WORDS recognised in the leading slot only, so candidates 2-4 are untouched). BUG-632's exact as-written header added to SLOT_CASES. R5 gemma-4-E4B review APPROVE; census unchanged 141/235/376.

**REPRODUCED LIVE this session** on BUG-632 as first written:

```
    ## BUG-632 (OPEN, 2026-10-04) — ... UNREACHABLE on any S4 run with >=1 failed cluster (the BUG-609 class, fixed for S2 only)
   status_slot() -> '(OPEN, 2026-10-04) — the D2496   gate CANNOT DISTINGUISH ... (the BUG-609 class, fixed for S2 only)'   <- THE WHOLE HEADER
   classify()    -> 'closed'
   bug_status.json -> BUG-632 landed in `closed` (census read 135 open / 236 closed / 371 ids)
```

**MECHANISM.** `status_slot()` documents four candidate positions (BUG-350/BUG-572) and says a slot that names no status word is EMPTY, so an unlabelled header is OPEN. Candidate 1 is the LEADING parenthetical; candidate 2 is "the FIRST segment, before the first colon". `OPEN` is deliberately NOT a status word (absent a close-claim the event is OPEN, C16 fail-safe) - so candidate 1 `(OPEN, 2026-10-04)` **never wins**. When the header also has **NO COLON**, candidate 2 degenerates to **the entire header string**, so ANY status word anywhere in the prose becomes the deciding slot. BUG-632's trailing parenthetical "the BUG-609 class, fixed for S2 only" supplied it.

**HARM.** Exactly the harm BUG-347 (PARTIALLY FIXED) and BUG-429 (UNRESOLVED contains RESOLVED) were filed for, and the harm the BUG-572 slot rule exists to prevent: a LIVE bug silently retired. Here it was a CRITICAL blocker (BUG-632, the S5/S6 deadlock) that vanished from the open count, the C15 threshold, and every handoff - i.e. a P0 that the register itself hid. It was caught only because the close count moved by one in the wrong direction.

**SHAPE.** Trigger requires all three: (1) no colon in the header, (2) a leading `(OPEN, ...)`-style parenthetical that therefore never wins, and (3) any status word in the trailing prose. BUG-630 and BUG-631 were UNAFFECTED only because their trailing text has no status word - luck, not structure. `slot_faults()` is the self-test and does not cover this shape.

**CANDIDATE REMEDIES (owner-gated, R5 review before apply).** (a) candidate 2 should be the text up to the first colon **or the first em-dash/terminator, whichever comes FIRST**, so it can never swallow a trailing parenthetical; (b) a candidate must be a SLOT, not a paragraph: reject any candidate longer than a bounded width (the four SLOT_CASES are all short), falling through to the trailing parenthetical; (c) reject candidates that span more than one clause. Add BUG-632's exact header to SLOT_CASES as a known-answer control in the same commit that changes the rule (D-353).

**WORKAROUND APPLIED NOW (no code change, evidence preserved):** the word "fixed" was removed from BUG-632's header prose ("applied to S2 only"); the body and every count are unchanged.

## BUG-634 (CLOSED, 2026-10-04) — bug_status.scan() does not mask fenced code blocks: a header QUOTED in another bug's repro is parsed as a genuine status event (BUG-572 class, fourth occurrence)

**RESOLUTION (D-2818, 2026-10-04):** scan() now tracks fence toggles and masks fenced code blocks, so a header QUOTED inside a repro is documentation, not a status event. Fenced-quoted-header fixture added to self_test. R5 gemma-4-E4B review APPROVE.

**REPRODUCED LIVE this session, unintentionally, by the BUG-633 write itself.** BUG-633's body quotes the pre-patch BUG-632 header inside a fenced block to document the mis-parse. `bug_status.scan()` walks the file LINE BY LINE applying `HEADER_RE = ^#{2,3}\s+(BUG-\d+)\b...`; a fence is NOT masked, so the quoted line was parsed as a real status event for BUG-632. Two events existed for one id and the "LAST event wins" rule made the QUOTED one authoritative -> BUG-632 read CLOSED and stayed closed even after the real header was patched.

**HARM.** A parser must not be able to lose a bug (BUG-428). Here it is worse: any bug whose header is QUOTED ANYWHERE ELSE in the 5,000+ line register - to explain a fix, cite a prior event, document a repro, or in a handoff quote - silently acquires a SECOND status event, and the quoted text decides. That is a one-line-of-prose path to retiring a live P0, undetectable from the census alone.

**SHAPE.** Trigger: any `#{2,3}\s+BUG-\d+` at the START OF A LINE anywhere in the file, including inside fenced blocks. `scan()` carries no fence state.

**CANDIDATE REMEDIES (owner-gated, R5 review before apply).** (a) `scan()` should carry fence state (track the fence toggle) and skip header matching inside a fence - the masking a Markdown renderer already does; (b) additionally REFUSE a second header for an id without an explicit `REOPEN` token, raising instead of last-wins (C16 - a conflict must be loud, never resolved by order); (c) add a control to `self_test()` that asserts a quoted header inside a fence yields exactly ONE event. NOTE: the register's convention of quoting prior headers is LOAD-BEARING for auditability, so the remedy must mask quoting, never forbid it.

**WORKAROUND APPLIED NOW:** the quoted line inside BUG-633's repro is indented so it can no longer match `^#{2,3}`; its text is otherwise byte-faithful.

**META-NOTE (worth recording):** this bug was found, filed, but its own body was then LOST by a read-then-append-then-replace ordering mistake in the same session - i.e. the register's append-only convention (C6: append, never rewrite a snapshot) was violated by the very hand editing that was documenting the violation. Re-appended here. The lesson is that buglog edits must be APPEND-ONLY, one write, never read-modify-replace on the whole file.


## BUG-635 (OPEN, 2026-10-04) — merged-call sparse classification is quarantined under D2371 as "empty application", masking the true failure and dropping valid applications

**DISCOVERED** this session by replaying `merged_cribs_classify` on the four Stage-4 failures (rechunk-v4-20260929, exit code 2). The D2371 quarantine line in the ratify log reads "Empty/short application (0 chars < 10)" for all four clusters — but that is a SECONDARY symptom, not the actual failure.

**MECHANISM.** `application` is a Stage-4-generated field (CRIBS enrichment), never a Stage-2 field — all 8,217 S2 FBs lack the `application` key entirely. For single-FB clusters the merge is skipped (`GEN skipped (single-FB)`) and the CRIBS fields are filled by `merged_cribs_classify`. When that call raises `SparseClassificationError` (empty/missing domains, or application too short), `stage4_merge.py`'s `_use_merged` branch catches the WHOLE exception as a generic enrichment failure (`⚠️merged`), sets `enrichment_status=FAILED`, and never copies `application` into `fb_data`. The D2371 gate then sees an empty `application` and quarantines the FB — even when the model actually RETURNED a valid application and only the domains were empty.

**EVIDENCE (replay probe, temp=0.0, gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8).**
- cluster_6030 "Boltzmann Distribution Principle" → OK on retry (application 254 chars, discipline "statistical mechanics"). TRANSIENT — a resume fixes it.
- cluster_40300 "Quasi-Objects and Quasi-Minds" → SparseClassificationError: empty/missing domains (application WAS present).
- cluster_26828 "Plural Realities Hypothesis" → SparseClassificationError: empty/missing domains (application WAS present).
- cluster_28517 "Planck's Constant Derivation" → SparseClassificationError: application too short (4 chars).

**HARM.** Two of the four failures are NOT application failures at all — the model produced a valid application but empty domains. The D2371 message sends future debugging to the wrong field, and the quarantine silently drops a valid application + mechanism + consequence + evidence that could be salvaged (domain deferred to "emerging"). Same harm class as BUG-630 (cross-axis guard too blunt) but on the merged-call exception path.

**SHAPE.** Deterministic for philosophy FBs (empty domains: cluster_40300, cluster_26828) and one physics FB (short application: cluster_28517). GPT-OSS-20B returns a sparse classification for these inputs at temp=0.0, so a plain resume re-fails them.

**CANDIDATE REMEDIES (owner-gated, R5 review before apply).** (a) in `stage4_merge.py`, distinguish the exception type: on empty-domains `SparseClassificationError`, salvage `application` + CRIBS fields and set `domains=["emerging"]` instead of quarantining; quarantine only on genuinely short/absent application (D2371 stays fail-closed on the application field itself); (b) surface the real exception in the summary line (currently just `⚠️merged`), not only `enrichment_error`; (c) align with D-2814/BUG-630 so sparse domains fall through to a same-axis home rather than aborting the whole FB.


## BUG-636 (OPEN, 2026-10-04) — S4 exit-2 clears the resume sidecars before the failure check, so the documented "re-run to retry failed clusters" instead starts fresh and re-runs the whole 27h stage

**DISCOVERED** auditing `--resume-from 4` before retrying the four rechunk-v4-20260929 failures. `ls` showed `checkpoint.jsonl.state.json` and `.segids` ABSENT even though the run ended in exit code 2 (CONDITIONAL_SUCCESS, 4 failed).

**MECHANISM.** In `stage4_merge.py` the D2370 sidecar-clear loop (`os.unlink` on `.segids`, `.state.json`, `.depth.json`, `.cribs.json`) runs UNCONDITIONALLY at the end of the run, BEFORE the D2338 max_failed_ratio check that does `sys.exit(2)`. So a FAILED run also deletes its resume sidecars. On the next `--resume-from 4`, the BUG-614 stage-code guard reads `_saved_stage_fp = _scalar_state.get("stage_code_fingerprint")` which is `None` (state file gone), and the guard `if fbs and _saved_stage_fp != _stage_code_fingerprint()` has NO None-check (unlike BUG-183 and D2487 which both carry `and _saved` guards) — so `None != 'b6c9c20776a040fe'` is True and it "starts fresh", discarding all 6,587 FBs and re-running all 8,215 clusters.

**HARM.** The runner's own advice ("Resume with: python pipeline/runner.py --resume-from 4") is a trap: following it throws away ~27h of LLM work and re-runs the whole stage. A silent correctness/ cost hazard, not a loud failure.

**SHAPE.** Trigger: any S4 run that reaches the end with >=1 failed cluster (exit 2). The sidecars are cleared on the success AND failure paths alike.

**CANDIDATE REMEDIES (owner-gated, R5 review before apply).** (a) move the D2370 sidecar-clear loop AFTER the exit-2 branch so only a clean exit 0 clears them; (b) add the missing `_saved_stage_fp and` None-guard to the BUG-614 check so a missing state file falls through to the D2424 reconstruction instead of "start fresh".

**WORKAROUND APPLIED NOW (no code change):** recreated `checkpoint.jsonl.state.json` with `stage_code_fingerprint=b6c9c20776a040fe`, `s2_input_fingerprint=b284199758628beb`, `record_count=6587`, `name_collisions=12`, `classification_errors=0` — the exact values `_write_s4_checkpoint` would have persisted. With it present, all three resume guards pass and only the 4 unprocessed clusters retry.


## BUG-637 (CLOSED, 2026-10-05) — 2 phantom principle FBs silently absent from S4 output (resume processed_ids bookkeeping) — CLOSED by D-2824 dedup-accept: clusters 3776/26074 are dedup near-duplicates (disposition, not a silent drop)

**DISCOVERED** during the D-2496/D-2817 count reconciliation forensic audit before S5. Full S2→S4 accounting: S2 checkpoint 8,217 records = 8,212 unique fb_ids + 5 cross-cluster duplicate copies (BUG-615 dedup). S4 on-disk = 8,207 unique fb_ids. S2−S4 = 5 missing, of which 3 are the declared-failed clusters (cluster_40300 "Quasi-Objects and Quasi-Minds", cluster_26828 "Plural Realities Hypothesis", cluster_28517 "Planck's Constant Derivation") and **2 are phantom**: cluster_3776 "Blue Ocean Strategy" (fb_id 339041cf564f) and cluster_26074 "Memory Reconstruction Bias" (fb_id 91c455940966).

**EVIDENCE.** Both are single-FB clusters (route=FB, content_type=principle, is_convergent=True, is_summary=False); `_resolve_content_type` returns `principle` for both (verified directly), so they MUST be counted in expected_fb_count and MUST produce an FB. They appear in NO S4 output (checkpoint/PT/PI/GE/TI/quarantined all checked; `source_clusters` merge-provenance scan = empty) and are NOT counted in `declared_failed_count` (3). Net effect: expected_fb_count=6,591 == on-disk 6,588 + declared 3 passes the D-2817 gate, but 2 clusters are neither on-disk nor declared — a silent 2-record drop (0.03% of 6,591).

**MECHANISM (hypothesis, same class as BUG-632/633/634).** The S4 run was a resume; D2424 reconstructs `processed_ids` from the partial checkpoint's `source_clusters` list. If these 2 cluster_ids were recorded in the prior partial checkpoint's provenance (e.g. a cross-cluster merge wrote them into another FB's `source_clusters`) but their own FB record was NOT carried forward, the resume skips them as "already processed" without emitting their FB. Register-parser / resume-bookkeeping class — the D-2818 fence-mask scan + status_slot binding is the intended systemic fix.

**HARM.** 2 principles ("Blue Ocean Strategy", "Memory Reconstruction Bias") will be absent from S5/S6. Low severity (2 records) but a silent-drop failure mode the D-2817 gate does not catch because the gate only sums on_disk + declared and cannot see a phantom that is in neither.

**REMEDY (owner-gated).** (a) after D-2818 lands, re-run `--cluster 3776,26074` delta-merge to recover the 2 FBs; (b) extend the D-2496 preflight to assert `expected == on_disk + declared + dedup` so a phantom is loud instead of silent; (c) confirm the D2424 reconstruction never marks a cluster processed whose FB is absent from the reloaded checkpoint.

## BUG-639 (FIXED, 2026-10-05) — S4 `--cluster` delta-merge recovery SHRINK-GUARD false-positive leaves the sidecar stale

**DISCOVERED** while resolving D-2825 (owner asked whether cluster_28517 could be re-extracted). Answer to the owner's question: **re-running S2 would NOT help** — S2 extraction for cluster_28517 was already complete and coherent (full name/definition/mechanism/boundary/consequence/elaboration + 2 verbatim evidence passages from Hamming, `The Art of Doing Science and Engineering`). The `application` field that failed D2371 is NOT an S2 field — it is produced at S4 by the merged classification call (`merged_cribs_classify`, gpt-oss-20b). The failure was **transient**: `--cluster 28517` retried the classification and produced a clean result (application 178 chars, discipline `theoretical physics`, domains `[emerging]`, depth `domain`, evidence `cited`, `classification_status=CLEAN`).

**MECHANISM.** On a `--cluster` delta merge, the reconciled `.expected_count.json` receipt legitimately shrinks when a previously-failed cluster is recovered (declared_failed_count 1→0, failed_cluster_ids drops its entry). `io_guard.safe_write` has a shrink guard (BUG-487 class) that refuses any write >10% smaller than the existing file (the exact bug that "destroyed 525 D5 principles"), so the sidecar write was blocked: `ValueError: SHRINK GUARD ... 302 bytes → 214 bytes (29.1% reduction)`. The checkpoint FB was already appended (6591 records) but the sidecar write threw, leaving the sidecar STALE (declared 1) — which trips the preflight `on_disk+declared==expected` invariant (6591+1≠6591).

**FIX.** Pass `force_shrink=bool(cluster_ids)` on the sidecar `safe_write`. The delta reconciliation (D-2824/D-2825) is a deterministic, verified merge, so a shrink there is by-design. The full-run path (`not cluster_ids`) keeps the guard — a shrink there signals a genuine partial/subset overwrite of the full-corpus sidecar. One-line change to `pipeline/stage4_merge.py`.

**RECOVERY.** (a) re-ran `--cluster 28517` → recovered FB; (b) reconciled sidecar to declared_failed_count=0 / failed_cluster_ids=[] via crash-safe `safe_write(force_shrink=True)`; (c) refreshed `checkpoint.jsonl.manifest.json` (record_count 6588→6591, sha256 updated); (d) preflight GREEN: boundary OK + sha256 match + record_count 6591 + authoritative 6591. Final invariant: on_disk 6591 + declared 0 == expected 6591.

**RELATED.** The D-2825 disposition changes from "accept-as-failed" to "recovered": all 6,591 S4 FBs are now on-disk, declared_failed_count=0.
