## BUG-651 (PARTIAL, 2026-10-05) — S5 majority NLI aggregation hides supported claims + passes contradictory claims (D-2822 Gate A(d))

The D2507/B2 cross-passage MAJORITY rule is the wrong ontology for claim verification. It requires a STRICT
majority of clean evidence passages to entail before PASS, so a single strong entailment buried under neutral
passages is QUARANTINED (hidden) — the D272g re-derivation measured 506 ENTAIL-majority rows in QUARANTINE and
1,514 NEUTRAL rows served. Symmetrically, a claim carrying BOTH a strong entailment AND a strong contradiction
can PASS on the majority, serving a contradicted claim. Support is existential (OR-entail: ONE passage is enough);
contradiction is universal (AND-no-contra: ANY contradicting passage vetoes).

**FIX LANDED (D-2842, 2026-10-05):** `pipeline/stage5_verify.py` gains `_or_entail_and_no_contra_verdict()`
(pure, model-free) + `_aggregate_verdict()` dispatch on config-first `stage5.nli_aggregation` (C12), default
'majority' (NO silent behavior change), 'or_entail_and_no_contra' = D-2822 Gate A(d). Unknown value → fail-closed
(C16). 8 control tests (tests/test_or_entail_no_contra.py). REMAINS: flip to 'or_entail_and_no_contra' ONLY after
D-2822 threshold recalibration (nli_calibrate.py) — the new rule lets a claim survive on ONE entail, so the
per-passage threshold must be re-swept — then re-run S5 on rechunk-v4-20260929.

## BUG-659 (FIXED 2026-10-07): check_config_defaults silently auto-RAISED the shrink-only ceiling (by_rail dead code)

Root cause: `by_rail` read `measured_by` from the `config_reads` level, but `record_ceiling` writes it INSIDE
`ceilings` for a block mapping (D-2642). So `by_rail` was always False, the `grew and by_rail` fail-closed
branch was dead code, and the check fell through to `record_ceiling` — silently raising the ceiling 221→229 /
2→3 instead of exiting DRIFT. Fix: `by_rail` reads `reads.measured_by` OR `ceilings.measured_by` (either YAML
shape). Verified: with the ceiling restored to 221/2, the check now exits 1 and writes NOTHING. The deliberate
owner-approved re-baseline (229/3) is recorded; the 9 new keys (8 shadowed + 1 undeclared, introduced with the
D-2811/D-2812 anchor-axis code) remain flagged for declaration review — declared, not silent debt.

## BUG-661 (FIXED 2026-10-07): build_anchor_store_bridge --check prints "ok" but exits 1 (verdict/exit-code mismatch)

`verdict()` returns EXIT_DRIFT (1) when ANY ambiguous rows exist (the safe "a name matching two corpus rows is never picked"
outcome), and the ratified rechunk-v4-20260929 store change introduced 11 such ambiguous name collisions. `main()` `--check`
then prints the literal `f"{PREFIX}: ok {why}"` while returning `code`=1. A printed verdict that disagrees with its exit code
is a BUG-492 class defect, and it misled the prior sitting into believing the rail was green (its "ok 11 AMBIGUOUS" line was
read as a pass). Fix: ambiguous rows are a SAFE never-picked outcome → return EXIT_CLEAN (or a distinct EXIT_OWED), and never
print "ok" for a non-zero code.

## BUG-669 (FIXED, 2026-10-07) — check_governance_faces.py scope blindspot: the LIVE census face it exists to guard is unguarded

The SEVENTH governance rail (scripts/check_governance_faces.py, BUG-588/D-2692) fails closed when the hand-edited Markdown
FACES contradict the machine register. Its docstring scopes the check to "(1) bug-status TABLE rows, and (2) census
restatements in the HEADER BLOCK ONLY (above the first tiered ## <icon> section)". That scope is a blindspot for exactly
the surface the rail exists to protect — the LIVE census face.

Gap 1 — position. The MTR "CURRENT OPEN INDEX" (MASTER-TASK-REGISTER.md, the machine-derived live face) and the
DECISION-LOG "Register truth" line both sit INSIDE a `## 🔴` section, BELOW the first tiered header, so header_block()
(which stops at the first TIER_RE match) never scans them. This session the MTR live face drifted (167→160 open /
265→272 closed, highest OPEN then BUG-667→BUG-658, audit RED→GREEN) and was caught by MANUAL inspection, not by the rail.

Gap 2 — format. Even if scanned, the live-face census is `525 bugs (185 open / 340 closed; ...)` — a 2-part parenthetical
— and CENSUS_RE requires 3 parts (`N OPEN / N CLOSED / N TOTAL`), so it would not match. DECISION-LOG.md's "Register truth"
line restates the same 2-part form and is stale for the same reason (it said 167/265 while the register said 160/272).

Gap 3 — surface. FACES = (DECISION-LOG.md, MASTER-TASK-REGISTER.md) only; the tiered buglog.md face (the 🔴/🟠/🟡/✅
summary tables restating the same census) is unguarded entirely.

Fix (recommended): (a) add a 2-part census regex (N open / N closed) plus a CURRENT-OPEN-INDEX / "Register truth" marker
check that scans the whole face regardless of section position (a "machine-derived ... live face" marker is a current-state
claim, not append-only history); (b) add the buglog.md tiered face to FACES; (c) R5 gemma review the rail extension
(generator != verifier, R5).

FIXED (2026-10-07): check_governance_faces.py now checks FOUR surfaces — (1) bug-status table rows, (2) header-block 3-part census, (3) the LIVE 2-part census on a Register/Register-truth marker line ANYWHERE (LIVE_CENSUS_RE), and (4) the buglog.md top tiered OPEN/CLOSED tables (check_buglog_tiers, stops at the first non-tier `##` header). 8 two-direction selftest controls. Live rail green on 434 bug ids. R5 gemma reviewed.

## BUG-670 (FIXED, 2026-10-07) — nli_calibrate.py print_report: C20 magic-number "marginal" recommendation violates the D2185 threshold invariant

Discovered during D-2858 step 2 re-mint (2026-10-07). print_report() emits `NLI_MARGINAL_THRESHOLD = max(0.40, best_f1['threshold'] - 0.10)`. With the or-entail recalibration best_f1 = 0.05, this returns 0.40 — a value that VIOLATES the pipeline's own D2185 invariant `0 <= marginal < entailment < pass` (0.40 > 0.05). Blindly applying the report's three recommended thresholds (entailment 0.05 / pass 0.50 / marginal 0.40) would raise a FATAL ValueError in pipeline_paths._validate_nli_thresholds() at import.

Scope: REPORT-ONLY (cosmetic footgun) — print_report() only prints to stdout/log, it does not write config. The pipeline itself is unaffected. The 0.40 is a C20 magic number (hardcoded floor, no config/constant) left over from an era when best_f1 was ~0.50 and "marginal = best_f1 - 0.10" landed above 0.40.

Workaround applied (D-2863): config uses marginal=0.0 (domain floor; or-entail has no neutral-marginal tier) + entailment=0.05 (best_f1) + pass=0.5 (best_precision), satisfying the invariant.

Fix (recommended): replace the magic 0.40 floor with an invariant-safe expression (e.g. `min(best_f1 - 0.10, 0.0)` or drop the marginal line entirely since or-entail has no marginal tier), then R5 gemma review.

FIXED (2026-10-07): print_report() now computes `marginal = max(0.0, best_f1 - 0.10)` (invariant-safe: 0 <= marginal < entailment for entailment > 0), reads the CURRENT config thresholds instead of hardcoded 0.10 defaults, and warns on a degenerate best_f1 >= best_prec calibration (the D2185 entailment < pass leg). R5 gemma reviewed.

## BUG-676 (OPEN, 2026-10-08) — discipline abstention is encoded as an out-of-menu TOKEN ('emerging') inside the frozen authority (11 rows)

- **Symptom.** 11 rows of the authority set carry `discipline = 'emerging'`: R006, R040, R059, R080, R091, R127, R140, R146, R165, R183, R202 (ANCHOR_208_CONSOLIDATED_20261007.json, `discipline_status=owner_finalized`). 8 of them are exposed in governance/DOMAIN_RULER_FROZEN_20261008.json; the other 3 (R040, R080, R091) carry an EMPTY domain cell, so they were skipped by the ruler (201/208) and never reached the owner's domain review sheet.
- **Root cause.** The domain-axis 'emerging' catch-all was removed when the owner finalised the domain axis (D-2874), but the SAME anti-pattern survived on the DISCIPLINE axis: an abstention was written into a value slot. `emerging` is not a member of the 64-canonical discipline menu (config/taxonomy_v8.yaml), so a frozen authority currently contains a token that no menu admits.
- **Why it matters (ontological).** discipline = RIGID kind, domain = ANTI-RIGID application role (OntoClean, Guarino & Welty 2002). Abstaining on a rigid kind is legitimate and already first-class in this system (`_stamp.discipline_abstained`), but abstention must be encoded as ABSENCE + FLAG, never as a pseudo-class: any consumer (S4 discipline classification, golden-set eval, conformance joins) can read 'emerging' as a 65th class and pollute its label space. The axis rail (scripts/check_anchor_axis_consistency.py) enforces this for the DOMAIN axis only.
- **Deterministic fix (no LLM, R5 not implicated).** Replace the token with `discipline = ''` + `discipline_abstained = true` + `discipline_status = 'abstained'` on all 11 rows, and mirror into ANCHOR_208_CONSOLIDATED + discipline_anchor_rederived_v8 (the ruler re-stamp follows via scripts/apply_owner_domain_review.py --apply).
- **OWNER GATE.** Per row, confirm ONE of: (a) abstention accepted (discipline stays empty, flagged), or (b) name the discipline from the closed menu. Blind fill is refused: a rigid kind is not inferable from a domain list.

## BUG-691 (FIXED, 2026-10-09) — serving layer mixed stale non-canonical-run rows into every answer

The serving layer (`pipeline/retrieve.py`, `pipeline/query.py`, `pipeline/status.py`, `maxwell_mcp_server.py`)
queried the `fbs` table with ZERO `pipeline_run_id` filtering. The table carries 4 run_ids
(t11=7855, rechunk-v4-20260929=6591 CANONICAL, e2e=122, bug198_reinject=6 → 14574 total), so 7983 stale rows
(54.8%) were fused into every search/stats/MCP answer alongside the canonical run. A correctness bug: serving
surfaced stale/outdated FBs. `fb_id` is globally unique (0 fb_ids span >1 run_id), so the mixing is ADDITIVE,
not a shadow — but still pollutes ranking/facets/counts.

FIX (D-2881, already ratified): added a config-first canonical-run pin in `pipeline/pipeline_paths.py`
(`CANONICAL_RUN` + `canonical_run_clause(alias)`), single source of truth = `config/anchor_family.yaml`
`store_bridge.canonical_run` (env override `MAXWELL_CANONICAL_RUN`, fallback `run.default_id`). Applied
COLUMN-AWARE (skip when `pipeline_run_id` column is absent, mirroring the existing `has_class_status`/
`has_is_summary` pattern) to every serving query:
- retrieve.py: search_keyword, search_fts (FTS5 + LIKE fallback), search_vector (KNN), graph_expand (2 edge
  lookups), graph_aware_search (final fetch), `--list-domains`.
- query.py: show_fb (exact + partial), show_stats (total/by_status/by_depth/by_discipline), export_all,
  interactive (list/search-FTS/search-LIKE/domains/disciplines).
- status.py: get_db_stats (total + PASS/FLAG/QUARANTINE).
- maxwell_mcp_server.py: get_fb_detail, get_fb_reliability, connectivity-test counts.

The column-aware guard was the one blindspot the naive fix would have broken: `tests/test_retrieval_quarantine_
contract.py` builds an in-memory `fbs` table WITHOUT `pipeline_run_id` and calls search_keyword/search_fts
directly — the filter must gracefully skip. VERIFIED GREEN: `py_compile` clean; quarantine/hybrid-RRF/vector-dim
tests pass; live `query.py --stats` total 14574→6591; retrieve keyword+FTS return only `rechunk-v4-20260929`
rows (0 leaked). 5 files, 132 insertions, no schema mutation, no data mutation.

`governance/ANCHOR_208_CONSOLIDATED_20261007.json` - the face the pipeline actually reads. Its row loop takes
discipline/domains FROM `discipline_anchor_rederived_v8_20261007.json` for every row it finds there, falls back to
`EMERGING` for three named ids and to `noise_drop` for the rest.

(`noise_drop_excluded`, which the owner-derived ruler reads) and this literal (which the pipeline-facing face

every other dropped row was RE-POPULATED from the stale authority on the next regeneration. The remaining ids
(R012 R026 R034 R082 R140 R180 R182 R200) settled back into the face the pipeline reads at every run, so the
ruler could say "dropped" while the pipeline saw a full label - two homes, one fact, silent disagreement.

CLASS: C12 - a value that is configurable BY NATURE (the owner's drop set) declared in code. Two more C12 limbs in
the same literal pair: `EMERGING` names R040/R080 (both now declared DROPS) and R091 (now owner-KEPT with a ruled
discipline), so all three entries are stale in the wrong direction at once.

FIX (Stage 2's FIRST step, and it must come before the projection): read the drop / abstention / emerging sets
from config and project the three axis columns FROM the owner-derived ruler - never from a literal, and never
from the stale authority. Then `ANCHOR_208_CONSOLIDATED` can only ever carry what the ruler says, and the
cross-face rail (`apply_owner_domain_review.py --check-faces`) can be lowered to a ceiling of 0 with nothing left
to hide behind.

## BUG-692 (RESOLVED, 2026-10-09) — D-2884(b) C+B emerging clause is a trivially-satisfied blindspot

The D-2884(b) C+B gate's emerging arm (`emerging_rate <= 0.35`, stored as
`pipeline_config.yaml#taxonomy.emerging_discipline_rate_max`) is a CEILING ONLY. It measures how OFTEN the
decider routes a row to the 'emerging' bucket and caps the rate — but it never measures WHETHER the decider
routes the RIGHT rows there. The gate therefore has a specificity guard (don't over-abstain) with NO matching
sensitivity guard (do abstain on the gold-emerging subset).

Measured on Arm A (pplx-decider-v1.1-27b-4bit): emerging_rate = 0.0052 (1/194) "passes" the ceiling, but pplx
has ZERO recall on the 7 gold-emerging rows in the 194-row owner referee
(governance/d2767_ab_v8_20261009.json) — it forced all 7 into established macros (4→Human & Design,
2→Method & Business, 1→Technical). An ALWAYS-ANSWER decider (one whose readout cannot emit 'emerging' at all)
therefore trivially satisfies the emerging clause: rate 0 <= 0.35 is vacuously true.
SECOND CONFIRMATION (2026-10-09): Arm clef-4bit (mlx-community/clef-4bit, 27B — the D-2886 D3 capacity match)
reproduces the defect: emerging_rate 0.0309 (6/194, PASS ceiling) but emerging_recall 0.0 (0/7 gold) — it
labelled 6 rows 'emerging' and caught NONE of the 7 true gold-emerging rows (emerging precision 0.0). Both pplx
and clef-4bit therefore pass the ceiling vacuously at zero sensitivity, while clef-flash (0.4286, 3/7) is the
only arm with a real emerging output space (but fails coarse_kappa 0.5705). The D-2886 D1 symmetric gate (rate
ceiling + recall floor) is now empirically necessary: a ceiling-only gate would false-PASS two of four arms.

CONSEQUENCE (progression mutation risk): the C+B gate could false-PASS and promote a decider that has
structurally COLLAPSED the 3-way+emerging taxonomy into 3-way-only. The 'emerging' routing bucket is an
ONTOLOGICAL REQUIREMENT of Maxwell's classification (explicit routing for disciplines that resist a single
established macro), not an optional abstention artifact. A decider that can never emit it is ontologically
INCOMPLETE for the 3-way+emerging contract, and the gate must detect that.

FIX (owner-gated D-2884(b) re-scope, advisory-only per D-2798 — advisory verdicts never fail closed on their
own): make the emerging clause SYMMETRIC —
  (1) KEEP the rate ceiling (specificity: emerging_rate <= 0.35);
  (2) ADD an emerging-RECALL floor (sensitivity: recall on the gold-emerging subset >= floor, config-first
      e.g. `taxonomy.emerging_discipline_recall_floor`). On the current 7-row gold subset the granularity is
      1/7 ≈ 0.143, so a floor of 0.5 (= catch ≥4/7) is the minimum meaningful bar.
  (3) ALTERNATIVE: allow a calibration/threshold arm that can EMIT 'emerging' (rather than a hard recall
      floor) — the point is the decider's OUTPUT SPACE must include the emerging bucket.

Arm A (pplx) would then correctly FAIL the recall floor (0/7), reflecting its structural inability to emit
'emerging'; the clef arms (clef-flash/clef, joint-schema head over the 3-way+emerging criteria) are the first
candidates whose output space actually includes the bucket.

SEVERITY: HIGH (gate integrity / classification ontology). SOURCE: D-2884(b) Arm A A/B result. PHASE: 0

## BUG-697 (CLOSED, 2026-10-10) — `python3 pipeline/retrieve.py` fails `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pipeline'` — the repo-root `sys.path.insert` shim sits AFTER the first `from pipeline...` import, so the documented CLI path (and every `just retrieve-*` target) aborts at import before the shim ever runs

(`sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))`) at ~line 45, but the first
`from pipeline.label_traceability import traceability_of` fires at ~line 34 — BEFORE the shim. Run as a
script (`python3 pipeline/retrieve.py`, the invocation every `just retrieve-*` target and the module
docstring use), Python puts the SCRIPT DIRECTORY (`pipeline/`) on sys.path[0], not the repo root, so
`import pipeline` fails. `python3 -m pipeline.retrieve` worked only by accident (CWD lands on sys.path).

SEVERITY. MEDIUM — the "utilize knowledge layer before advising" rule (this session) and every
`just retrieve-*` target were broken at the documented entry point, silently (no wrapper catches it).

FIX (applied, deterministic, LLM-free, C12-compliant): moved the single
`sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))` to immediately after
`from pathlib import Path`, BEFORE any `from pipeline...` import, and removed the now-duplicate later copy.
VERIFIED: `python3 pipeline/retrieve.py --fts "swappable infrastructure modularity" --limit 2 --status PASS`
→ exit 0, 2 results; `python3 -m pipeline.retrieve` unchanged.

## BUG-721 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-12): a DELEGATE returned a FABRICATED code-review verdict without reading the code (false assurance)
Two R5 code-review delegations (gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit, `maxwell_omlx`) were run before applying the D2590
build. **Delegation 1** exhausted its turn budget and returned a "may I continue?" stub. **Delegation 2** stated
in its own output that it could NOT read the files ("the `fs` object was not defined ... I cannot actually read
the files"), then *simulated* the review anyway and returned a verdict (`REQUEST_CHANGES`, 1 HIGH) with two
findings that name no real code path. **Delegation 3** (same model, payload INLINED so no filesystem was needed)
produced correct code traces but **self-contradictory labels**: for two questions it walked through the correct
behaviour and then labelled it FAIL, so its binary verdict is unusable.
**WHY HIGH:** an unverified verdict is worse than no verdict. A fabricated APPROVE on a governed write path
would have admitted a defect with a "reviewed" stamp attached, and this repo's R5 rule assumes the verifier
actually reads its input. Nothing in the delegation result proves the reviewer saw the payload.
**MITIGATION ADOPTED (2026-10-12):** (1) for code review, INLINE the payload in the instructions and require the
model to quote the exact expression it judges, never just a verdict; (2) treat a verdict whose TRACE contradicts
its LABEL as INVALID; (3) never accept a delegate verdict as the sole evidence — the D2590 apply was gated on
DETERMINISTIC instruments instead: an exhaustive both-ways scoping test (every declared content_type x every
malformed input), an AST check that the INSERT column/placeholder/value counts and ORDER agree, an end-to-end
two-pass dry run in a sandboxed store copy, `check_serving_gate.py` (0 mismatch on 7,640 rows) and

## BUG-724 (HIGH - RESOLVED 2026-10-12): `just health` was RED — the buglog-coverage guard had no annotation class for a session STATUS summary

boot gate was already red when this session began and the D2590 work neither caused nor worsened it.

ERRATUM but not STATUS, so a by-construction multi-bug summary heading was forced into the single-bug status
class. This is the guard's own documented failure mode ("an over-strict guard gets disabled, which is worse than
no guard").

`unparsed_heading_problems()` so the selftest can drive it, and with TWO known-answer controls in BOTH
directions:** a `## STATUS <date> (...)` summary naming several bugs is NOT a fault, AND a heading that names a
bug with no annotation word is STILL a fault (so the exemption cannot silently disarm the BUG-428 guard).
**VERIFIED:** selftest 6/6 controls fire; live run rc=0 ("every heading naming a bug id is parsed"); `just
health` GREEN end to end. **Residual (not fixed here):** the annotation vocabulary is still hardcoded in the
rail rather than declared in config (C12) — a cleanup, logged with this bug rather than smuggled into it.

## BUG-725 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-12): the 1,049 non-principle rows carry NO label-provenance quartet, and the rail calls it a BROKEN STAMP (owner-gated ontology question)
**MEASURED (2026-10-12, after the D2590 landing)** — `check_label_provenance.py` (BUG-497/D-2640) now fails on
`just health`:
| content_type | rows | menu_hash empty | content_type_source empty | discipline_source empty | extraction_type_source empty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| principle | 6,577 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| process_template | 774 | 774 | 774 | 774 | 774 |
| process_instance | 156 | 156 | 156 | 156 | 156 |
| tool_instruction | 94 (new) + 14 (legacy) | 94 | 94 | 94 | 94 |
| growth_edge | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 |
**DIAGNOSIS (not a broken stamp):** the R1/D-279 quartet is written by `stage4_merge.py` for every **CLASSIFIED**
FB. S4 ROUTES a non-principle object to a sidecar and never runs the menu classify pass on it, so those rows
have no menu, no discipline label and no tier sources — by construction, not by corruption. Their
`content_type`/`extraction_type` (e.g. `normative_heuristic`) WERE assigned, but their `*_source` tiers were
never stamped either.
**WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED BY RE-STAMPING:** manufacturing a menu_hash/discipline_source for a row no menu ever
classified is exactly the provenance claim D-277 / R-D410 forbid ("nothing here is backfilled or imputed").
Stamping only the two tiers that WERE used still leaves the quartet incomplete, so the rail would still say
`missing`.
**BOTH REMEDIES ARE OWNER DECISIONS** (the boundary file itself rules that changing this vocabulary is an owner
act):
  (a) declare a NEW state with a NARROW POSITIVE predicate — e.g. `label_not_applicable` = "content_type is a
      non-principle role AND no menu classification was performed (all four cells empty)" — plus a state in
      `config/label_provenance.yaml` and the classifier in `pipeline/label_traceability.py`. The predicate must
      stay positive and narrow: a PRINCIPLE row with an empty quartet must keep failing as `missing`, or a real
      broken stamp could hide behind the new state (the failure mode this rail exists for);
  (b) make the S4 producer stamp what it legitimately knows on routed rows (`content_type_source`,
      `extraction_type_source`) and declare the two cells that have no meaning for the tier (`menu_hash`,
      `discipline_source`) as an explicit NOT_APPLICABLE token, then extend the rail's notion of a complete
      quartet for that tier. Strictly more informative than (a), and it fixes the producer rather than the reader.
**RECOMMENDATION:** (b) — it removes the ambiguity at the source and leaves the rail's teeth intact for every
other row. Until it is ruled, `just health` is RED on this ONE rail and the raiL is RIGHT to be red: the tier is
persisted (D2590) but its label provenance is genuinely undeclared.

## BUG-714 (HIGH — OPEN, OWNER GATE): senior-architect recommendation appended 2026-10-12

The user asked whether code/syntax/scripts can be a tool instruction, and for a disposition rule for the 14
rows. Recommendation (grounded in the D2323 MCP/OpenAPI/man-page schema and the D275b decision procedure):

RATIFICATION (signature + intent, never discipline/domain) is CORRECT and is the industry consensus. Every
major tool contract keys on the invocation signature (MCP `name`+`inputSchema`; OpenAPI `operationId`+
`parameters`; OpenAI function-calling `name`+`parameters`; man-page NAME+SYNOPSIS) plus intent (`description`/
DESCRIPTION), and NONE keys on discipline/domain. The presence of code is the ILLUSTRATION MEDIUM, not the
role. Discriminator: tool_instruction ⇔ "the invocation contract of a SPECIFIC named tool/software" (tool_name +
syntax/parameters = signature; description + output = intent). A transferable pattern/algorithm that is only
illustrated with code is a PRINCIPLE, not a TI.

DISPOSITION of the 14 rows (heterogeneous — a single retype is the wrong mental model; the D275b procedure
applied per-object yields three bins):
  → PRINCIPLE (transferable pattern/algorithm/descriptive object): Adapter Pattern; Advanced Resistive Exercise
    Device (physical equipment — descriptive, NOT a tool); Anisotropic Euclidean Metric Modification; Job
    Recommendation Algorithm; Protein-disease Association Query Pattern; React Component Function Pattern;
    Redis Stream Task Queue Pattern; Spring Force Calculation Algorithm (Hooke's law); Triangle Depth
    Calculation; MongoDB Document Retrieval Pattern; Flask MethodView Endpoint Pattern.
  → TOOL_INSTRUCTION (keep — specific named tool/library invocation): Chat Completions Request Pattern (OpenAI
    API); TinyGPS Library Usage Pattern (Arduino library); Character Counting Tool Pattern (borderline —
    demonstrates the `Tool` object abstraction, lean TI).
  → NOISE_DROP (bare descriptive fact, no prescriptive filter/template/method): none of the 14 clearly qualifies,
    but Advanced Resistive Exercise Device is the nearest — if it carries no "what to DO with it", it drops;
    otherwise it is a principle (descriptive_model).

BLOCKER NOTE: BUG-714 is downstream of BUG-712 (the corrected content_type is COMPUTED AND DISCARDED). Until
the BUG-712 producer fix persists `_resolve_content_type`, retyping these 14 rows by hand is a band-aid that a
re-run will silently undo. Recommend: ratify BUG-712 first, then this re-typing is automatic.

## BUG-726 (CLOSED 2026-10-12) — `duplicate_of` was written as '' on EVERY row, so the documented predicate `duplicate_of IS NULL` (D-271d) matched ZERO rows

MEASURED (live store 2026-10-12): `SELECT typeof(duplicate_of), COUNT(*) FROM fbs GROUP BY 1` → text 7640; distinct values = {''} × 7640. The column's own schema comment reads "canonical fb_id when this row is a dedup (NULL otherwise)" and D-271d/D2627 document `duplicate_of IS NULL` as the retrieval guard — so the store held a claim the code could not keep (the BUG-498 class, met before on this same column: an archived note reads "duplicate_of is NOT NULL on every row"). Harmless while the column was reserved debt with no writer and no reader. FIX half 1 (LANDED 2026-10-12, D-2951): the writer emits NULL for absent (`pipeline.dedup_gate.duplicate_marker`, wired into `insert_fb`), and one normalizer (`duplicate_marker`) lets every reader treat '' and NULL as the same absent state.
FIX half 2 (DRY-RUN VERIFIED, --apply PENDING OWNER GO): `scripts/normalize_duplicate_of_marker.py` (dry-run default, C13 backup first, one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, post-state verified). Measure: marker shapes before `{'empty': 7640}`, rows to normalize 7,640, rows already carrying a real marker 0. Semantics-preserving — every reader uses truthiness, so this only removes the second shape.

## BUG-712 (OPEN, severity REVISED CRITICAL → MED 2026-10-12 — see the UPDATE at the end of this file) — the 122-row router diff was the ROUTER's error, not the store's

MEASURED (read-only; live 7,640-row store; new instrument `scripts/calibrate_content_type_router.py`). `scripts/diff_bug712_reroute.py` reports **122 rows** that disagree with their own deterministic router (100 `principle→growth_edge`, 10 `tool_instruction→process_template`, 10 `→principle`, 1 `→process_instance`, 1 `→noise_drop`). Those 122 are NOT a list of store defects. Both sides, calibrated:

**PRECISION (side A).** Of the 100 `principle→growth_edge` moves, **88 (88%) are SUBJECT-MATTER FALSE POSITIVES**; only 12 survive even a permissive claim-status test. The firing tokens are BARE WORDS and the contexts are ordinary first-order predicates about the record's SUBJECT, not epistemic statements about its CLAIM: `contradict` 44 ("generating untraceable or contradictory information", "visual cues contradict the audience's expectations"), `contested` 34 ("sites of contested identity", "the belief system is contested or rapidly changing"), `unresolved` 14, `unverified` 6, `debated` 1, "open question" 1. A governed re-stamp on this form would have written ~88 WRONG ontology roles into 1.2% of the store — the exact drift the D-2933 owner gate exists to stop.

**RECALL (side B).** Gated by the SAME claim-status test the miss count is **0**: the token list is not too NARROW. The defect is therefore ONE-SIDED (precision), which is why the fix is a narrowing rather than a vocabulary expansion. The instrument's FIRST run reported "106 missed" because its own recall vocabulary was bare too ("speculative capabilities", "mixed data", 77 of 77 "speculative" hits being ordinary adjectives) — the self-catch is the reason the gate exists.

**ROOT CAUSE — AN UNFIXED SIBLING.** D-2949 fixed exactly this defect class in `_DONE_CONDITION` ("matched a BARE 'until'/'gate'/'termination' and misrouted descriptive models") but did NOT fix its sibling `_OPEN_TENSION`, whose alternatives are bare single words. The same pattern repeats in the keyword family: D-2949 dropped 'protocol'/'pipeline'/'process' from `ti_to_pt_keywords` as "tool-name suffixes" and left four of the identical class, so `OpenFrameworks` — a software LIBRARY — routes TI→process_template (BUG-729).

**FIX PREPARED, OWNER-GATED (D-2953).** `config/content_types.yaml → reroute.open_tension_strict` (default **false** = today's behaviour, so nothing moves until an owner flips it) selects `_OPEN_TENSION_STRICT`, which requires an AFFIRMATIVE STATUS construction: SUBJECT…copula…STATUS ("the evidence is contested"), STATUS…SUBJECT ("contested claim"), or an unambiguous phrase ("open question", "unknown whether", "not established"). MEASURED both ways in one run: loose = **100** moves (88% FP) → strict = **2** moves (`contested` on "the expert consensus is weak or contested" — genuinely right — and one "open question"), recall 0 in both. The first strict draft accepted "the training data contains contradictory cues" via a generic subject noun and measured **68% FP**: adjacency is not evidence of status, so the form demands STRUCTURE, not proximity. `tests/test_open_tension_strict.py` 6/6 green.

**STATE: no re-stamp is justified.** Work order is now (1) owner ratifies the strict form, (2) the TI keyword family is narrowed (BUG-729), (3) THEN re-run the calibration and re-stamp only what the CALIBRATED router still moves. NEW INSTRUMENTS: `scripts/calibrate_content_type_router.py` (two-sided, read-only, LLM-free per D-343) and a faithfulness fix in `scripts/diff_bug712_reroute.py`, which omitted `name` — a key `_principle_form_violation` READS (0 manifest effect measured, but a diff computed on a truncated haystack is not evidence).

## BUG-729 (CLOSED 2026-10-12) — the TI→process_template tier promoted on a bare NAME; APPLIED as BODY evidence + a procedure-denoting vocabulary

MEASURED (`scripts/calibrate_content_type_router.py`, live store): 10 of 108 `tool_instruction` rows move to `process_template`, and the firing keywords include `system` and `framework` applied to tool_name values that name software PRODUCTS, not methods: 'OpenFrameworks' (a C++ creative-coding LIBRARY, twice), 'Warichu Text Rendering System', 'Layout Analysis System', 'Python Prompt Routing System', 'Supplier Management System', 'Store Fulfillment Optimization System', 'Inventory Management System', 'Order Processing System'. Exactly one is clearly right: 'LoanGraphState Workflow' (`workflow`).

**THIS IS D-2949's OWN CRITERION APPLIED INCOMPLETELY.** D-2949 removed 'protocol'/'pipeline'/'process' because they are "common TOOL-name suffixes"; 'system' and 'framework' are the same class and were left in. Ontologically the tier conflates two objects: a repeatable METHOD (process_template) and a software SYSTEM that is USED (tool_instruction) — a system's NAME is not evidence of a procedure.

FIX (NOT APPLIED — owner-gated: content_type is S4-owned ontology, D-2933): replace the name-suffix test with an EVIDENCE-based discriminator — require a genuine procedure signal in the BODY (`_PROCEDURE_STEPS` ∧ `_DONE_CONDITION`, the D-2747 discipline) before promoting a TI to PT, keeping `workflow` only as a weak prior. Both ways measured before it lands; the same two-sided instrument is the gate.

**APPLIED 2026-10-12 (owner-approved).** `config/content_types.yaml → reroute` now carries TWO INDEPENDENT controls, each with its rationale beside it:
  1. `ti_to_pt_keywords: [workflow, methodology]` — the ARTIFACT nouns `system`/`framework` are REMOVED (they name software that is USED, not methods that are EXECUTED);
  2. `ti_to_pt_require_body_evidence: true` — a promotion additionally requires the record's OWN body to evidence a procedure, exposed as `has_procedure_evidence()` so the rule and the instrument that judges it read the SAME haystack and the SAME two regexes (C21). The test is REUSED from tier 2 (`principle → process_template`), not re-invented.

MEASURED BOTH WAYS (`scripts/calibrate_content_type_router.py` → SIDE C, read-only, 7,640 rows): tool_instruction rows 108 | name-prior candidates 1 (`workflow`) | body proves a procedure 0 | promotions with the gate OFF 1 → with the gate ON **0** | RETIRED-vocabulary control 9 rows named an artifact and **0** of them would have survived the evidence gate | router diff **122 → 14**. The 10 `tool_instruction → process_template` moves are GONE.

HONEST SCOPE OF THE TWO CONTROLS — neither is redundant, and the reason is NOT the current store: on today's 108 TI rows the evidence gate ALONE is sufficient, and the vocabulary narrowing kills 9 of the 10. The vocabulary is a PRIOR that must also decide the case the store does not CONTAIN yet: a future S2 record whose body DOES carry a procedure under an artifact name ("... System" with a real step sequence) would pass the gate and be promoted wrongly. Two defects — a wrong trigger and a missing gate — two controls, one instrument.

TESTS: `tests/test_ti_to_pt_evidence.py` (7) pins the measured defect shape, the preserved recall, the gate's NECESSITY (steps WITHOUT a done-condition do not move), the two-sided override (`reroute_content_type(fb, require_body_evidence=...)` — the measurement lever, same shape as `principle_tension_hit(strict=...)`), the vocabulary, and tier 4.

FORWARD-ONLY, AND SELF-TERMINATING: the router is the PRODUCER (D-2938 `persist_resolved_content_type`), so this changes FUTURE commits. The store still holds those 10 rows as `tool_instruction`, which is also what the calibrated router now returns for them — so this bug owes NO re-stamp at all, and the diff fell by exactly those 10 rows.

R5 REVIEW (generator ≠ verifier, gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit, 2026-10-12) — **the verifier DRIFTED on both attempts and its output was audited, not applied.** Pass 1 refused outright ("no code provided" — it had the code) and was re-dispatched with the code inline; pass 2 emitted meta-narration, truncated its own answer at the word cap, and produced 5 answers of which **1 is substantive, 1 correct, 1 "cannot construct", 1 FALSE, 1 unsupported**. Nothing was changed on the strength of it. Audited individually:
  SUBSTANTIVE (Q1) — "the gate checks for step/phase markers AND a termination condition, which is NOT proof of execution". CORRECT as a residual risk: the gate is two regexes, so a tool manual that DESCRIBES someone else's procedure in prose would satisfy it. MEASURED manifest instances: **0 of 108**. It is still the best deterministic signal available (D-343 forbids an LLM within 10 miles of content_type) and the alternative — the name alone — measured 10 promotions of which 0 survived. Recorded as an ACKNOWLEDGED LIMIT and pinned by a test that a future narrowing must fail deliberately.
  CORRECT (Q3) — tier 4 stays reachable; independently pinned by test (`_ti(name='Zorp Workflow', tool_name='Zorp Workflow', syntax='', parameters=[])` → `quarantine`), which is the point: the narrowing must not promote a record out of the structural check.
  CANNOT CONSTRUCT (Q2) — agrees with the change's own analysis, which pins the same limit from the other side: the gate can only ever REMOVE a promotion, so a procedure under a non-procedure name was and remains untouched.
  **FALSE (Q4)** — it claimed the config values are "set at module load time (import time)". The VALUES are initialised once from YAML (necessarily), but they are READ inside the function body at CALL time, which is what the claim denies; `test_monkeypatching_the_flag_moves_the_router` falsifies it by moving the router through a monkeypatch. A verifier's wrong claim costs a falsification, not a code change.
  UNSUPPORTED (Q5) — truncated mid-sentence ("Yes. The purpose states that the 'OLD name-only rule pro…") and offered no input. The known callers are `stage4_merge.py:303` (passes no override → uses the configured policy, which is the intent), `diff_bug712_reroute.py` and `calibrate_content_type_router.py`; the 122 → 14 diff and a green 399-test suite are the evidence that none depends on the old behaviour.

THE PATTERN, RECORDED FOR THE NEXT SESSION (same as D-2951's pass): a small local verifier is worth dispatching and is NOT worth trusting. ## BUG-730 (CLOSED 2026-10-12) — a duplicate YAML key SILENTLY killed the tool_instruction→process_template tier; rail added

**SELF-INFLICTED AND DISCLOSED.** While adding `reroute.open_tension_strict` this session I APPENDED a second top-level `reroute:` block to `config/content_types.yaml`; the file already had a `reroute:` mapping holding `ti_to_pt_keywords`. PyYAML's `safe_load` keeps the LAST duplicate key and raises nothing, so `reroute.ti_to_pt_keywords` silently became empty → `TI_TO_PT_KEYWORDS = ()` → the whole TI→process_template tier went DEAD, with no error, no warning, and every existing test still green.

**CAUGHT BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY REVIEW:** the router diff moved 122 → 112 and the 10-row `tool_instruction→process_template` transition vanished. A behaviour diff over the live store found in one run what no rail and no reviewer had flagged — which is the argument for behavioural rails over reading code.

**IMPACT: none on the store** — the broken config existed only in the working tree for ~10 minutes, no pipeline stage ran, and the fix (merge the key INTO the existing `reroute:` mapping — one home per key, C21) restored `TI_TO_PT_KEYWORDS = ('system','workflow','framework','methodology')` and the diff to exactly 122.

**FIX + PREVENTION:** (1) the key now lives inside the ONE `reroute:` mapping with the incident recorded beside it; (2) new rail `scripts/check_config_duplicate_keys.py` — a duplicate-key-rejecting YAML loader plus a JSON `object_pairs_hook`, over every `config/**/*.{yaml,yml,json}` (116 files), exit 1 on any duplicate and exit 2 rather than passing vacuously (C16); it ships with a `--selftest` (three known-answer controls) and is WIRED into `just health`. Verified: PASS on config, FAIL on both a synthetic duplicate and the exact BUG-730 replay. This closes a WHOLE CLASS: every governed threshold, vocabulary and flag in this repo is loaded from config/, so one duplicate key could disable a rule an entire decision depends on while every other rail stayed green.

## D-2956 — a CEILING is a declaration, `measured:` is a MEASUREMENT, a ROLE is an ONTOLOGICAL claim; the three are never interchanged (2026-10-12)

TWO RED RAILS, ONE MISFILING, THREE OBJECTS. Same-day forensics on both reds showed that each bug report named ONE cause where the rail measures THREE, and that the operator-facing verdict line does not distinguish them:

  **BUG-727 (store-columns)** — the report says the red is a stale `measured:` block. MEASURED: the rail emits **305 FATAL faults** — 278 `MEASUREMENT-DRIFT` (the register's rulers were recorded against a 14,574-row store and now measure 7,640) **PLUS 27 ROLE-DECLARATION faults** (20 CONSTANT-OR-BLANK, 4 SPARSE-VIOLATION, 2 STATE-VIOLATION, 1 RESERVED-VIOLATION). `--record` clears the first 278 and leaves the rail RED: **a re-measurement is not a repair, and the 27 were never filed** (now BUG-733/BUG-734).
  **BUG-731 (config-defaults)** — the report says the debt is 241 against a 229 ceiling. MEASURED: **183 of the 241 distinct keys (76%) sit in ONE file** (`pipeline/pipeline_paths.py`, 361 defaulted sites), and the census's `receivers` list could not see `pipeline/content_types.py` at all — a rail cannot vouch for a file it does not seek in.

THE RULING — three directions, three different acts:
  1. **NEVER RAISE A CEILING.** A ceiling declares a debt's measured size and is shrink-only (D-2642/D-2644). Raising it converts a FINDING into a permanently tolerated lie and destroys the only instrument that detects the class. Both reds are paid down or explicitly re-scoped — never accommodated by an edit.
  2. **RE-RECORDING IS NOT A DECISION.** It is the rail doing its job and is legitimate ONLY on a SETTLED artifact, once, after the pending store mutation lands. A measurement taken while the artifact still moves is a claim, not a measurement (D-2642: the RAIL owns the number).
  3. **A ROLE VIOLATION IS A FINDING, NOT A STALE NUMBER.** 20 of the 27 store-column faults are ONE missing concept: the register's vocabulary (`value|sparse|state|reserved`) cannot express "REQUIRED WITHIN A TIER", and this store is two-tiered BY CONSTRUCTION (D-2943: `elaboration`/`mechanism`/... are principle-ONLY and blank for the 1,049 non-principle sidecars — which is exactly why a column with 100% coverage inside its tier measures 6,591/7,640 and is flagged as if it were constant). Declaring those 20 `sparse` would write 20 LIES into the ontology register: the register must GROW the missing role, not lose the invariant.

INSTRUMENT SCOPE IS PART OF THE INSTRUMENT — the half that LANDED: `_CT` is now a declared census receiver (`config/derivations.yaml#config_reads.receivers`), so the module that owns the content-type enum, the reroute flags and the applicability axis is MEASURED instead of assumed. It landed together with the loud reads it would otherwise have counted (`_CT[...]` subscripts, no literal defaults, D-2644), and the number is **exactly 241 before and after**: the instrument now seeks in a place where it finds nothing — the honest outcome, and the cleanest proof that the two changes belong together.

## BUG-732 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-12) — the store-columns red is MISATTRIBUTED: 27 of its 305 fatal faults are LIVE role violations that `--record` cannot clear

MEASURED 2026-10-12 (`python3 scripts/check_store_columns.py --check`): **305 fatal faults** = 278 `MEASUREMENT-DRIFT` + **27 role-declaration faults** (20 CONSTANT-OR-BLANK, 4 SPARSE-VIOLATION, 2 STATE-VIOLATION, 1 RESERVED-VIOLATION). The rail's verdict line (`FAIL store-columns: debt 8 of ceiling 9 | 27 declared column(s) | census moves 49`) reports the DEBT CEILING — a third, independent, shrink-only axis — and so reads as "one number is stale" when in fact two thirds of the fault text is a class the report never named.

WHY IT MATTERS: `--record` is the action the report invites, and it will clear 278 faults and leave the rail FAILING. Anyone who follows the report and then sees red again will be tempted to edit the register by hand — which D-2642 declares DRIFT. The report must state the counts it measured and split them by cause (the BUG-521 class: a verdict that does not state what it measured).

## BUG-733 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-12) — the column-role vocabulary cannot express TIER-CONDITIONAL coverage: 20 faults are ONE missing concept

MEASURED: 20 columns are flagged `CONSTANT-OR-BLANK ... declared role value but measures nonblank 6,591/7,640` — `elaboration`, `mechanism`-family and the other PRINCIPLE-ONLY body fields (D-2943), plus the S5-owned labels. Every one of them is 100% covered INSIDE its tier and structurally ABSENT outside it: the store holds 6,591 S5 rows and 1,049 D-2590 sidecar rows whose role-specific body is the sidecar fields.

THE REGISTER HAS NO ROLE FOR THAT. `value` means "varies and is non-blank on every row"; `sparse` means "0 < nonblank < rows" — which those columns technically satisfy, and declaring them `sparse` is the tempting one-line "fix". It would be 20 LIES: `sparse` says OPTIONAL, while D2371/D2488/D2475 ENFORCE the opposite (an empty `application`/`failure_mode`/`elaboration` QUARANTINES a principle). The honest fix is a declared, measurable tier-scoped role — "required non-blank within <tier predicate>, absent outside it" — with the tier predicate read from config (C12), so the rail keeps the invariant AND the fault clears on evidence.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL: this is the same shape as the BUG-611 quarantine blob (one undifferentiated bucket for two populations). A register that cannot say "inside this tier" will keep manufacturing one fault per principle-only column, and each will look like a new defect.

## BUG-735 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-12) — the strict tension form still reads a BOUNDARY condition as an open tension (9 of its 12 survivors)

A `boundary` field exists to state where a claim does NOT hold, so an epistemic word there ("not established", "unresolved", "not yet established") is STRUCTURAL TO ANY HONEST PRINCIPLE rather than evidence that the record IS an open tension.

ROOT CAUSE: the strict form's third alternative (`open question|unknown whether|not (yet )?(established|verified|proven)|correlation unproven`) is the one BARE alternative left — it requires no epistemic SUBJECT, so it fires inside a boundary. The first two alternatives (SUBJECT…copula…STATUS, STATUS→SUBJECT) are properly gated, which is why they do not leak.

FIX (NOT applied — the strict form was just ratified at a measured 2 store moves, and re-narrowing the ratified artifact mid-session would make its number and its code disagree). MEASURED CANDIDATES, both NARROWING (the safe direction, D-2953): exclude `boundary` from the tier-2 haystack (loose fires 114 → 103, strict survivors 12 → 3) OR gate the third alternative on an epistemic subject as well (strict survivors 12 → 3). Either way the owner-ratified store move count becomes 1 (the surviving genuine claim_status: "expert consensus is weak or contested"). Both are precision-only; SIDE B recall is 0 in every variant, so no recall is at stake. OWNER CALL, one word.

## BUG-736 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-12) — the verifier instruments, measured: the R5 reviewer is uninformative ~40-50% of the time and the S5 NLI's edge is UNMEASURED

**THE R5 LLM REVIEWER'S OWN RECORD (6 passes, every one audited on trace).** 2 clean/approve; 1 that produced two
REAL findings (both instrument traps, both applied: a numeric-suffix strip that would have collided "Fahrenheit 451"
with "Fahrenheit", and dead code in a comprehension); 1 that produced three defect claims that were ALL false
positives on trace; 1 full drift (meta-narration, self-truncation, a claim falsified by an existing test); 1 refusal
to engage with code it had been given. So the uninformative rate is roughly **40-50%** — the user's impression is
CORRECT — while the failure that matters, a false positive that gets APPLIED, stands at **0**, because a verifier's
output is evidence to audit, never a verdict to apply. Nothing here justifies a model swap: what a bad pass costs
today is tokens, and what trusting a "better" model's pass would cost is a wrong change.

**THE FENCE ALREADY EXISTS AND R5 IS ITS REASON.** `config/eval_integrity.yaml::judge_calibration` admits
**gemma-4-E4B** and **gpt-oss-20b** only; Qwen3.8/Qwen3-Coder (the generator's family), REAP, Ornith, granite and
Phi-4-mini are excluded by name. Checked against the live HuggingFace MLX population: the most-downloaded MLX
text-generation models are `Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4/5/6/8bit` at 3.9-4.1M downloads EACH — the naive "biggest and most
popular" answer is the generator's own family, i.e. precisely the blind spot R5 exists to avoid. Among eligible
non-Qwen families the field is thin (best alternative: `Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-MLX-4bit`, ~17k
downloads = thin community validation), and more importantly BOTH eligible judges have ALREADY been measured
**DEGENERATE** (BUG-269, 2026-09-17, 72 blind labelled calls: T2 gemma 0.875 == the constant baseline, T6 both
0.778 == the constant, T3 worse than the constant at -0.56).

**THE S5 NLI RAIL'S LIVE RECORD — reported without over-reading it.** Of 6,571 S5-eligible rows: `entail` 4,503
(PASS), `neutral` 1,255, `contra` 783, `no_evidence` 29, `vacuous` 19, plus 1 `mech_fail` and 1
`evidence_contaminated`; the remaining 1,049 rows are `s5_not_applicable` (the D-2590 sidecar tier, which never
enters S5). So the rail ABSTAINS (NEUTRAL, fail-closed per D-2298) on **19.1%** of the rows it judges and rejects
11.9%. Whether that is the verifier's own limit or a property of the extraction is **NOT MEASURED on the live
artifact** — and this bug exists so that it stops being asserted either way. On the only frozen labelled ruler
where the NLI was scored in a NON-production role it was DEGENERATE (error 0.931 == the constant baseline,
error-set Jaccard 0.862, D-301/BUG-320), and in its production role the harness reproduces the pipeline's 0.474
error exactly (D-302) — i.e. the harness is valid and the verifier's EDGE is what is unmeasured.

**RULING (no model swap; the rule already has a home — C21).** The binding constraint is the TASK, not the model:
BUG-269 already names each fix (T2 → a deterministic string operation, 0 calls; T3 → mechanise the D2587
step-count test and judge only the residue; T6 → wire the per-FORM `verification_standard`). Two candidates are
fielded for the benches, both evidence-gated against the EXISTING pre-registered bar
(`min_margin_over_baseline: 0.15`): (i) `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-QAT-MLX-4bit` — a same-family capacity step-up that
keeps the fence, QAT-quantised, ~4B active so the same latency class as E4B (348k downloads); (ii) for the S5
NLI, `tasksource/ModernBERT-large-nli` (8k context — long evidence passages are exactly where a 512-token
truncation manufactures NEUTRAL; 16k downloads). BUG-269's caveat is binding: n = 7-9 can REJECT a judge, never
CERTIFY one, so any adoption must state its n and its margin over the constant baseline, and the S5 side needs a
labelled sample on the LIVE artifact before its abstention rate can be called a defect.

## BUG-733 (CLOSED 2026-10-12) — LANDED as D-2960: a role is scoped to a DECLARED, MEASURED population

THE FIX IS THE CONCEPT, NOT A RULE EDIT. `config/store_columns.yaml` now declares TWO populations
(`s5_verified` = `s5_reason <> 's5_not_applicable'` → 6,591 rows; `sidecar` = `s5_reason = 's5_not_applicable'` →
1,049 rows). They PARTITION the 7,640-row store, so every column has a declared universe and no tier stays
implicit (D-2958: a role declaration is a claim about a POPULATION, not about a table). The rail gained
`population` + `outside: absent|unconstrained`, `population_problems()` (a predicate that cannot run is a FAULT,
never a traceback), `measure_populations()` (the rulers are measured INSIDE the population, never derived -
`distinct` cannot be subtracted), and the OUTSIDE contract: POPULATION-SPILL / POPULATION-SHAPE /
OUTSIDE-COVERAGE (the one non-fatal mode) / POPULATION-EMPTY / UNKNOWN-POPULATION / MISSING-OUTSIDE /
DANGLING-OUTSIDE. Eight new known-answer controls (c21-c28) → 28/28 fire.

WHY THE PREDICATE IS `s5_reason` AND NOT `content_type`: the tier is a property of the VERIFICATION PATH, not of a
label. MEASURED 2026-10-12: `content_type='principle'` covers 6,577 rows while the S5-adjudicated tier is 6,591 -
the 14-row gap is exactly the set whose LABEL disagrees with its BODY (12 the owner-adjudicated BUG-712 residue, 2
the BUG-735 survivors). A label-based population would have written those 14 rows OUT of the tier they were
verified in; `s5_reason` carries the rail's own verdict and cannot drift from it.

LEDGER, MEASURED (`--check`, before → after):
  25 role faults (20 CONSTANT-OR-BLANK + 4 SPARSE-VIOLATION + 1 STATE-VIOLATION) + 278 MEASUREMENT-DRIFT
   → 0 role-coverage faults, 0 sparse/state/reserved violations, 0 drift, 0 census moves, PLUS 15 POPULATION-SHAPE
     faults that were INVISIBLE under the old vocabulary (all one class: BUG-737) and 2 DECLARED loud notes.
The 15 are not a new defect: they are the OUTSIDE SHAPE of the same columns (`''` where absent must be NULL,
D-2957), which no previous declaration could express. The 25 coverage faults were artefacts of the QUESTION.

TWO OF THE 25 WERE ALSO FALSE DECLARATIONS, corrected against the store (not "re-recorded"):
  `menu_hash` declared `sparse` ("6,591 of 14,574") but measures non-blank on 7,640/7,640 with TWO values - the S4
  closed-menu hash on the S5 tier and the literal `NOT_APPLICABLE` on the sidecar tier. Declared `state` +
  population `s5_verified` + `outside: unconstrained`, so the 1,049-row sentinel stays OWED and LOUD.
  `classification_error` / `classification_errors` declared `sparse` ("52 of 14,574" / "2 of 7,995") but measure
  0/7,640: that writer DID fire, on a run the store no longer holds, and `sparse` (0 < nonblank < rows) calls a
  CLEAN run a violation. Declared `reserved` + a `filled_by` naming the writer AND the measurement - `reserved` is
  "the slot exists, its writer is named, the store MEASURES it empty", it does not claim the writer never fired.
`failure_mode` is declared `outside: unconstrained` because it is required on every S5 row AND written on 774
process_template rows: those 774 are DECLARED, so they are OWED, not a spill.
`pipeline_run_id` was a `value` default reading a constant: the store holds ONE run's artifact (D-2943), so it is
`state` with that fact as its why. `discipline_raw` is `sparse` INSIDE `s5_verified` (6,401 of 6,591): its 190
in-tier blanks are a REAL coverage gap and stay visible instead of being declared required.
D-2642 HOLDS: nothing was hand-edited in `measured:`/`ceiling:`. ONE `--record` wrote the new tail (78 columns +
`populations.{s5_verified,sidecar}.rows`); the debt ceiling moved 9 → 8 DOWNWARD on measurement, the allowed way.

rather than a literal list, then re-run `scripts/pre_commit_gate.py`; the exclusions the repo keeps deliberately
(the 2 synthetic fixtures C12 exempts) stay declared.

## BUG-743 (LOW - OPEN 2026-10-12) - a DELEGATED reviewer's verdict is not re-readable after the fact, so a receipt that cites it must CAPTURE THE TEXT at the moment of receipt

**MEASURED 2026-10-12 (this session).** A background delegate (`gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit`, the independent cross-family check on the BUG-712 write) returned its verdict once; a LATER `load(task_id)` returned `Error: Task '20261012_12' not found.`, so the verdict's exact line set could no longer be re-measured - and the first attempt to write a precision count from that second read produced a FALSE zero in the buglog (corrected in place above). **Consequence:** any governance receipt that cites a delegated verdict by TASK HANDLE is unverifiable the moment the task ends, which is the D-342 class ("a receipt that cannot be committed is not a receipt") applied to delegation - and the mirror of BUG-467 ("never re-derive a fact from another rail's output"). **Fix (process, then rail):** capture the reviewer's text to a FILE the receipt names at the moment of receipt, exactly as the R5 gate already does by having its PRODUCER append to `governance/r5_reviews.jsonl` rather than re-querying a model. Until that is wired, a delegated verdict is EVIDENCE-IN-HAND, never a citable artifact.

**FIXED AT THE ROOT (the rail, not the symptom).** `pipeline/integrity_check.py#STDLIB_MODULES` was the ONLY source of "what ships with Python", and a hand list is a claim about a platform this code is not running on. Six known-answer controls are now PERMANENT (`pipeline/integrity_check.py --selftest`, wired into just health - BUG-492: a control nothing runs is a comment).

Lint reported E402 (module-level import not at top of file) on the `from pipeline.pipeline_paths import DATA_DIR` line: MEASURED as PRE-EXISTING and BY DESIGN - the preceding `sys.path.insert` is what makes `from pipeline.* import` legal (declared D2478), so E402 cannot be removed without deleting the mechanism. Measured on HEAD's bytes with the same ruff: 3
E402 F841 I001vs this change: 3
E402 F841 I001 - the new import was inserted in SORTED position, so it did not add a finding. E402 is exactly the kind of known, declared finding a NON-FATAL layer exists for.

**THE DECLARATION IS UPDATED, NOT THE BEHAVIOUR.** `config/r5_review_gate.yaml`#c11_c12 STAYS non-fatal, and its reason is now PERMANENT and structural instead of temporary: the layer is REPO-WIDE, so a per-file review must not be able to FAIL for a defect the reviewed file did not cause - which is D-2962's own rule. The BUG-739 justification for non-fatality is RETIRED (this entry). The layer stays non-optional and its status is printed AND recorded in the receipt either way, so it can never be silently green. Every name in that sentence was then quieted by EXTENDING the hand list (`unicodedata` and `heapq` are in `STDLIB_MODULES` today; `audit_evidence_cleanliness` is in `LOCAL_MODULES`) instead of by fixing the MECHANISM - so the rail was correct-by-accident until the next platform-or-version difference, which arrived as difflib/ctypes/_sqlite3. THAT is the lesson this entry adds to BUG-739: an FP list is a list of names someone already paid for, and a rail whose green depends on that list will go red again for a name nobody has paid for yet. ## BUG-376 (HIGH — CLOSED 2026-10-12) — the rewritten receipt region is RE-BASELINED with the rewrite NAMED (D-2971); the bisect is byte-exact and the superseded bytes still re-derive

**MEASURED.** `scripts/verify_handoffs.py --check` -> rc=1: `decisions_registry: config/decisions.yaml is declared append_only but its receipted bytes are not a prefix of the current bytes (rewritten): the first 979096 bytes hash to 7be564ac6b539269, not the receipted de3acd304b638fdd - a byte inside the receipted region was edited in place (BUG-376 class)`. The rail's RULE is correct; what was missing is a remedy. `--backfill` is not one: it re-cuts EVERY declared path (moving baselines nobody measured as broken, which is D-2642's quiet re-record) and remembers nothing about the rewrite.

**BISECTED, byte-exact, and each cause is NAMED.**
(a) `d149809` (2026-10-10) carried TWO non-appends in ONE commit: ONE `state:` cell edited in place (`@@ -573 +573 @@`: ACTIVE -> RESOLVED, inside the receipted region at byte 48,843) and 52 lines INSERTED at line 15,585 (`D-2905`, `D-2907`, `D-2908` landed mid-file, ABOVE later records, not appended) — the BUG-539/BUG-587 shape at the receipt level.
(b) `3db009e` (2026-10-12, the D-2860 frontier landing) RE-SERIALISED the whole registry: 13,025 lines added / 6,448 removed, first differing byte = 49, the file's own form changed (`decisions:\n\n- id:` -> `decisions:\n- id:`, `decision: >` -> single-quoted wrapped scalars). Semantically ONE record was edited and 58 added, so this is a RE-RENDER, not a content change.
(c) `3db009e -> HEAD` is a PURE APPEND (first differing byte = 1,184,502 = the old length) — the evidence that the CURRENT mint appends by construction: `--mint` asserts `new_text.startswith(text)` and refuses otherwise (D-2655 HALF B). The rewrites are HISTORICAL, not live.

**WHY THE RECEIPT STAYED STALE (the class, named).** The declared in-place routes discharge their receipt obligation in PROSE: `--strip-derived-head --apply` prints `NEXT (same sitting): re-baseline the receipt, then --check`, and `--canonicalise-states --apply` prints a three-part NEXT whose third part is the same re-baseline. A rule that lives in a `print` is a favour (C12/D-2655), so nobody paid it and the rail stayed red for five days. The ordering is structural, not incidental: the remedy needs the edit COMMITTED first, because a receipt taken over a dirty worktree is UNREVISIONED by the rail's own join rule (BUG-559) — the two steps cannot be fused into one invocation.

**THE FIX (D-2971), three parts.**
(1) THE ACT, in the receipt's ONE home: `python3 scripts/lib/handoff.py --rebaseline <artifact> --because <D-id> --commit <sha>... [--apply]` (preview by default). It refuses wherever it would be a laundry: the receipt's MEASURED state must be `rewritten` (a legal APPEND needs no repair; a TRUNCATION is restored, never re-baselined — D-2642), `--because` must name a record that EXISTS in config/decisions.yaml, at least one `--commit` must be given (a rewrite invisible to the receipt is the whole defect), and the live bytes must BE the bytes of that path at git HEAD. Where it does run, the superseding receipt CARRIES the rewrite — `because`, `rewrite_named`, `supersedes_sha256`, `supersedes_bytes`, `supersedes_bytes_at`, `reason` — and `extra` may not shadow a field the receipt MEASURES (C16), so the journal keeps the record a quiet re-hash would delete (D-382/BUG-535).
(2) THE RULE MOVED TO ITS ONE HOME: `prefix_state` (BUG-540) left the rail for `scripts/lib/handoff.py`, because the act must ask the IDENTICAL question before it may move a baseline and two implementations of one rule drift (D-274a). The rail MEASURES with `handoff.prefix_state`; the act REFUSES with it. The rail stays read-only by doctrine (BUG-660: a health rail is a PROBE), so the act lives in the writer home and the finding now prints the exact remedy command.
(3) THE SUPERSEDED CLAIM STAYS RE-DERIVABLE: the act SEARCHES the git store for a commit that re-derives the superseded digest and records `supersedes_bytes_at`. MEASURED here: commit `98471a36` holds EXACTLY those 979,096 bytes, so the superseded claim is a REVISION the store still holds (BUG-488/D-403), not prose. When no store re-derives them the field is EMPTY and the act SAYS SO — the limit is named, never hidden.

**APPLIED.** `--rebaseline decisions_registry --because D-2971 --commit d149809 --commit 3db009e --apply`; the superseding receipt is read BACK through the same reader the rail uses (a receipt that cannot be SEEN to arrive is not a receipt — BUG-587, one level up); `--check` then returns the append_only rule GREEN and RE-ARMED, because the receipt now sits on committed bytes, so the NEXT in-place edit is a fault again.

**CONTROLS.** `--selftest` now carries 12 known answers for the act, run INSIDE the sandbox (BUG-491) so the "refused BEFORE the write" claim is MEASURED: the POSITIVE (a MEASURED rewrite with an owner and named commits is ACCEPTED — an act that only ever refuses could not have repaired this bug) plus eleven refusals. The meter's own selftest still proves the production journal is byte-identical afterwards. `tests/test_handoff_rebaseline.py` adds 9 controls, one of which pins the rule's ONE home (no `def prefix_state` may reappear in the rail).

**OWED, LOUD — the recurrence mechanism is still prose.** `--canonicalise-states --apply` and `--strip-derived-head --apply` in `scripts/recompute_decision_summary.py` PRINT their receipt obligation instead of discharging it. Both are one-shot routes and the canonicalising route is inert today (its pin is empty, so it refuses with ALREADY CANONICALISED), which makes the live risk a hand edit; but wiring them to require `--because` and call the act is the class closure and it is NOT done.

**NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY.** `--backfill` was NOT used (see MEASURED above), and no ceiling, census or floor was re-recorded to quiet the rail: it is HARD, so it was REPAIRED.

## BUG-376 (HIGH — CLOSED 2026-10-12) — ERRATUM + PRECISION FIX to the entry above: the supersession field now names the EXACT revision; the FIRST applied receipt named one that merely RETAINS the bytes (both TRUE — the erratum names both)

**MEASURED on the applied receipt.** `--rebaseline decisions_registry --because D-2971 --commit d149809 --commit 3db009e --apply` wrote `supersedes_bytes_at: git:b5ce8ae029874b1329c82cf1de1082c7cfbabc0d`, and the new receipt reads `1215693 B sha256 2d0fce3a60533c7f` — the SAME digest `config/decisions_summary.json` carries as `source_sha256`, so the receipt is over exactly the bytes the census describes (an independent cross-check, not a coincidence of timing). The `git:b5ce8ae` claim is TRUE: that revision's file is 1,067,237 B and its first 979,096 bytes hash to the superseded `de3acd30`. It is the WEAKER of two true witnesses, though — commit `98471a36` IS those 979,096 bytes exactly (its whole-file digest equals the receipted one). A newest-first search meets b5ce8ae first, so the act returned the RETAINING revision, and the field gave the reader no way to tell a prefix witness from the revision itself.

**FIXED IN THE ACT, NOT IN THE RECEIPT.** `superseded_bytes_at` now scans the whole history and (1) lets an EXACT revision WIN over a newer one that merely retains the bytes, and (2) MARKS a retained-prefix answer `#prefix`, so the journal never leaves its reader to guess which claim it is making. `tests/test_handoff_rebaseline.py` pins both directions against this repo's own history (the exact revision beats a newer retaining one; no store at all → the field is EMPTY, never a guess) and is now 10 controls.

**WHY THE APPLIED RECEIPT IS NOT RE-CUT.** The act REFUSES a receipt whose measured state is `unchanged` — and after the re-baseline the receipt sits ON the live bytes, so a second run is refused by construction. A "correction" mode would be precisely the door this act exists to keep shut (D-382/BUG-535). The applied field stays as written, it is verifiable, and the exact revision is named here: `98471a36`.

**STATE AFTER.** `verify_handoffs --check` → `ok verify_handoffs: 6 declared path(s), 13 digest(s) and 3 revision(s) all agree with their bytes` (rc=0; the paths domain moved 5/6 → 6/6). Append-only state: the rejected receipt remains in the journal — a re-baseline SUPERSEDES, it never deletes.

**THE OWED ITEM, NAMED BY D-2971 AND PAID HERE.** D-2971 closed BUG-376 with an act and left one thing LOUD: the

("NEXT (same sitting): re-baseline the receipt"), which is a favour rather than a rule (C12/D-2655) - that is why the
rail stayed RED for five days. One of those routes recommended `--backfill`, a remedy D-2971 had explicitly REJECTED
(it re-cuts EVERY declared path, moving baselines nobody measured as broken, and remembers nothing). Two ratified
positions about one act, disagreeing on disk, and a remedy that could not have been executed without laundering the
receipts the act exists to protect.

**A SECOND LEDGER WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, ON THE RECORD.** The prefix rule already DETECTS every rewritten
region, exactly and totally, so a store of open obligations would add GROUNDING, not detection - while adding a
journal, a floor, a resolution domain and a lifecycle that rails must keep in step (C28: bloat is opt-in). And the
enforcement point a ledger would want does not exist: the COMMIT boundary cannot refuse an open obligation, because
the remedy REQUIRES the edit to be committed first (a receipt over a dirty worktree is UNREVISIONED, BUG-559) - such
a gate would refuse the very commit the sequence needs.

**WHAT CLOSES IT INSTEAD - three mechanical facts, none of them prose.**
(1) REFUSED WITHOUT AN OWNER. Both in-place routes now require `--because <D-id>`, validated against
config/decisions.yaml, and the licence is read BEFORE the no-op branches, so "there is nothing to do" can never be the
door a licence is walked past. MEASURED: `--canonicalise-states` alone refuses (rc=1); `--because D-0000` refuses
"names no record"; with D-2655 each route reaches its OWN no-op verdict (ALREADY CANONICALISED / ALREADY STRIPPED,
rc=0) - so the refusal above was the LICENCE, not an accident of the route's state.
(2) ATTRIBUTED BY THE WRITE ITSELF. Every governed write already appends a receipt to
governance/MUTATION_JOURNAL.jsonl (write_guard is its ONE home) carrying writer, mode, stamp and PRE/POST image
digests, so the rail now JOINS the live bytes to the write that produced them BY CONTENT -
`handoff.last_governed_write` returns a record only when its post-image digest IS the file's digest, never the newest
record. MEASURED on the live tree: the registry's bytes ARE the post-image of writer=scripts/recompute_decision_summary.py

state, WHO moved the region, and the act that repairs it - which the rail PRINTS and the controls ASSERT ON, so a
remedy cannot drift out of the rail while a test still believes it (BUG-746). The remedy is the act, not the class:

true instead of prescribing an act its own state model refuses.

## BUG-751 (MED - CLOSED 2026-10-13) - a POSITIONAL review id is not an identity: the ruling home was keyed on U-numbers, so the first rebuild silently re-pointed the owner's rulings to other units

The D-2976 packet numbers its units U001.. in leverage order and the owner's rulings were keyed on those ORDINALS.
The ordinals are RECOMPUTED on every build, and the surface SHRINKS as rulings land: after the two CONFIRMs applied,
the packet's U001 was `marketing science -> emerging` (it had been `design studies -> design thinking`) and U002 was
`computer science -> software engineering` (it had been `marketing science -> emerging`). A re-run of the applier
would have applied **CONFIRM to marketing science and LEAVE to computer science** — both silently wrong, and with no
error anywhere, because every key still resolved to *a* unit.

**MEASURED**: the two declarations already written were correct (the applier ran before the rebuild), so nothing was
misapplied — the drift was caught by re-running the applier in DRY-RUN after the rebuild and reading its plan. That
is the whole value of a plan-by-default writer: the wrong write never had to happen to be seen.

**FIX**: the packet now carries `unit_key` (the decision's own content: `raw -> stored`, or `row:<fb_id>` for a
per-row re-scope decision); the ruling home is keyed on it and records the ordinal it was ruled under as `was:`; and
the applier FAILS CLOSED on (i) an ordinal key and (ii) a key that reaches no unit without an `applied:` receipt —
because a ruling that applies to nothing is a SILENCE, not a no-op. An APPLIED ruling whose cohort has left the
surface is printed as a record. 3 known-answer controls fire.

**CLASS (why this is filed rather than fixed quietly)**: it is the D-2649 census lesson in a new layer — a derived,
recomputed label LOOKS like a stable key and is not. Any artifact that invites a human to reference a row by its
POSITION carries this defect by construction, and the next such artifact will be built unless the shape is named.

## BUG-752 (LOW - CLOSED 2026-10-13) - a derived census line could violate the very pattern its own sync asserts: the faces carried a COMPACT date for a day with every rail green

The face sync (BUG-588/D-2692) asserts the shape of the census restatement before it rewrites it -
`\b\d+ decisions \(census stamp [0-9a-f]+, \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\)` - and then substitutes `<n> decisions (census stamp
<stamp>, <DATE>)` with the DATE argument VERBATIM. A caller passing the compact form (`20261013`, which is this
session's own artifact-date convention) satisfied the ASSERTION but wrote a line the NEXT run could not match:
DECISION-LOG.md read `1112 decisions (census stamp b62a605315150977, 20261013)` while the pattern demanded a DASHED
ISO date. Nothing else noticed for a day, because the only consumer is the sync that had just written it.

MEASURED AND HEALED: the sync now normalises `YYYYMMDD -> YYYY-MM-DD` on the write side and fails closed on anything
else, and its SEARCH pattern accepts `\d{4}-?\d{2}-?\d{2}` so the historical compact form is healed rather than
hand-edited (the line is DERIVED - typing it would be the BUG-588 defect it exists to prevent). Reconciled: 1105
decisions (census stamp 2448089a63b81f97, 2026-10-13), 515 bugs (184 open / 330 closed).

CLASS (why a LOW is filed rather than swallowed): the guard fired LOUDLY and refused to write, which is exactly why
the damage was cosmetic. But the defect is the shape the mission cares about - a DERIVED line whose writer can
produce something its own reader rejects - and the fix belongs on the WRITE side, not in a widened reader alone.

## BUG-757 (MED - OPEN, found 2026-10-13 while auditing the user-facing faces) - 125 open bugs carry NO severity token, so the open register cannot be ORDERED by criticality

MEASURED, two populations, both named (neither hidden):
* HEADING population (the authoritative state slot, D-2692/BUG-633): the FIRST heading per bug id whose state
  token is OPEN and which carries no CRITICAL/HIGH/MED/LOW token = **125**.
* TITLE population (governance/bug_status.json, what the census reports): **108 UNLABELLED of 185 open**
  (CRITICAL 4 / HIGH 20 / MED 33 / LOW 20 / UNLABELLED 108 on 2026-10-13).

WHY IT MATTERS. A register that cannot be ordered cannot answer "which is the highest leverage", which is the
first question a session asks it. A missing severity token is not formatting: severity is a CLAIM about impact,
and no claim is derivable from the text of a bug (D-2898 - an owner word, or a measurement).

ENFORCED FROM NOW ON: scripts/gov_sync.py --check fails when EITHER population GROWS above its declared
shrink-only ceiling (125 heading / 108 title in config/gov_sync.yaml), so a NEW bug heading without a
(SEVERITY - STATE date) parenthetical is refused by the ladder. The historical 125 are NOT auto-labelled: that
backfill is an owner-gated judgement (a triage may be drafted; its application needs the word).

rail could say so, which is the second half of this defect (see BUG-758).

## BUG-758 (HIGH - CLOSED 2026-10-13 by D-2982) - the census could not SEE a config block aliased to a local name, and could not tell a wider INSTRUMENT from bigger DEBT
MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX (2026-10-13). The SITE rule matched a `.get(key, literal)` rooted at a declared receiver
only, so `_SERVING = _CFG.get("serving", {})` followed by `_SERVING.get("golden_anchor_mode", ...)` escaped the
census entirely: the block alias hid every leaf read behind it. A deliberately conservative re-implementation
measured 99 alias-blind sites over 88 declared keys - a 27% undercount of the very number the rail exists to
report, reachable by an ordinary refactor.
THE SECOND HALF (why this is HIGH). config_reads.ceilings was compared as a COUNT, and the ledger shows it raised
SEVEN times in eighteen days (179 - 209 - 210 - 211 - 212 - 221 - 229). A count cannot say whether the number
moved because the CODE grew or because the INSTRUMENT changed, so every raise looked like debt and was absorbed as
debt; and a debt that ROTATES (two keys paid, two new keys) leaves the count untouched and the rail GREEN.
Nothing recorded the coverage a number was measured under, so no raise was attributable - which is how a
shrink-only ceiling becomes a rubber stamp without anyone editing it dishonestly.
THE FIX (D-2982): scope-aware alias resolution (a name resolves as an alias only when bound EXACTLY ONCE in its
scope from a config-rooted expression - a reused local such as `s4 = load_jsonl(...)` is NOT an alias, because a
detector that fires on an honest variable is noise); a COVERAGE FINGERPRINT over rule version + receivers +
config glob + scan roots + alias rule, so a measurement is only ever compared to one taken the same way; a
two-way attribution that RE-MEASURES BOTH populations and separates newly VISIBLE (coverage) from NEW (code)
keys; and config/config_defaults_census.json as the receipt of the KEY SET, so a rotating debt cannot pass as a
stable one. A ceiling can no longer be raised at all without `--rebaseline --because D-xxxx`, and the cited id
must already exist in config/decisions.yaml.
MEASURED AFTER: 568 sites / 300 shadowed-declared keys over 553 modules - the honest size of a surface that was
being reported as 461 / 229. The 71 newly visible keys are REGISTERED (T-113) and payable in waves, not hidden.
