## BUG-760 (HIGH - FIXED 2026-10-13 by D-2984) — the register lied through the FACES: DECISION-LOG listed two RESOLVED decisions as pending, and the rail that owns the faces had no decision-row join at all

**Discovered:** 2026-10-13, by the owner reading DECISION-LOG.md ("seems like the done, fixed, resolved task bugs,
decisions are still on top") and then MEASURED.

**The measurement.** `DECISION-LOG.md:195` read `| D2622 | ACTIVE |`, `:196` read `| D2621 | PROPOSED |`, both
under the heading `## 🔴 OPEN / PENDING — highest priority first` — while `config/decisions.yaml` holds both as
RESOLVED. `:247` cited `D2537`, an id the register does not carry (the record that carries that decision is
D-2979). In MASTER-TASK-REGISTER.md, `:60` and `:77` were headed `CURRENT OPEN INDEX (... the live face ...)` — a
SECOND live face beside the derived one — and `:61` restated the census with a derived field (which bug is
highest-OPEN) stated as a bare value, BUG-750, with no moment at all, while the register's own answer was BUG-757. Measured across the three faces: 8 such lines (5 in DECISION-LOG, 3 in MTR, 0
in buglog). The DERIVED block was right in every case; the hand prose beside it was wrong in every case.

**Why nothing caught it — the rail read tables, never prose.** `scripts/check_governance_faces.py` had four
surfaces: bug-status table rows, the header-block census, the live-census marker, and the buglog tiers. It had NO
`DEC_ROW_RE` at all, so a decision row was unjoined; and the region a face declares "DATED HISTORY: append-only,
NOT a register" was never policed as a claim surface. This is the BUG-759 shape one level up: the artifact the
owner READS said a thing that was false, and the instrument watching it was green. Its predecessor BUG-669 fixed
WHERE the live census marker sits, and made the rail CHECK it — it did not ask whether a live marker belongs in a
region declared not to be a register.

**FIXED by D-2984 (the claim surface).** A claim is either JOINED to the register, or it DECLARES THE MOMENT it
speaks about (D-2660). Four limbs, each with a named repair: (1) a live-claim label may not lead a line below the
marker — no exemption, because a pointer is not a claim about a moment; (2) a live census marker may not stand in
a region declared NOT a register; (3) a decision ROW is joined to config/decisions.yaml unless its SECTION
declares its moment — this is the twin of the ratified bug-row rule (BUG-669) that was simply never written; (4) a
present-tense "BUG-N is OPEN" assertion is joined unless its ENTRY declares its moment. Plus the derived
A derived field — which bug is highest-OPEN — must state its moment on its own line (one home, D-2642).

**SEEN.** `check_governance_faces --selftest` 22/22 known answers in both directions (11 new, including a
4-column transition row, a discussion of the label that must NOT fire, and an append-only claim that must stay
quiet); the rail rc=1 on the 8 measured faults and rc=0 after the repairs; the paired contract
`tests/test_governance_faces_spec.py` 10/10 (D-2978, spec `specs/governance_faces.spec.md`); the mutation
`a_decision_row_that_contradicts_the_register_is_load_bearing` SEEN to red the control that names the rule
(floor 33 → 34); a declared guard (`fatal`) in config/rail_registry.yaml.

**The repairs were 8 lines, and NO history was rewritten.** buglog.md needed ZERO edits: all nine of its
present-tense "still OPEN" claims sit under entries that already carry a date, so the rule reports zero faults
there — the append-only file stays append-only. In MTR/DECISION-LOG the repairs were the 8 claims that
contradicted the register: two snapshots relabelled (they were calling themselves the live face), one census
marker demoted to a dated snapshot, one section heading given the moment it was written (2026-10-03, from git
blame of its own rows) plus an appended CORRECTION naming the two decisions the register has since moved to
RESOLVED, one row re-cited to the id that carries it (D-2979), and three derived fields given the word "then"
(`highest OPEN then BUG-622`, `then BUG-667`).

**RESIDUAL:** BUG-761 — the hand tier sections still live INSIDE the region the faces declare to be history.

## BUG-762 (HIGH - FIXED 2026-10-13 by D-2985) - the LIVE region was never policed: the part the OWNER actually opens

**MEASURED 2026-10-13, one day after D-2984 closed the mirror hole.** D-2984 policed everything BELOW the
`GOV-HISTORY:START` marker. The region ABOVE it - the one the owner opens the file on - had no join at all, and

   my instruction hasn't delivered."

**WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT.** The rail's five surfaces read tables, marker lines and the history region; nothing
read the live region's prose, its citations, or the register's own axes. A face nobody derives drifts (D-2981);
a face whose LIVE region is nobody's claim surface lies (this bug).
**FIXED BY D-2985:** the LIVE region is a claim surface - a hand line may not claim to BE the live index, a
citation in it must resolve, and the face LEADS with the declared OWNER LANE; the register now declares a
`mover` on every entry, an `R-` id is `state: rule` and is never counted as open work, and `state: gate` is
retired (gatehood is `mover: owner` + the gate text).

## BUG-763 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-13 by D-2985) - one question had THREE answers: the severity line did not join the census

**MEASURED 2026-10-13.** The register-truth line the owner reads first said
`CRITICAL 7 · HIGH 36 · MED 57 · LOW 30 · UNLABELLED 125 ... of 185 open` - parts summing to **255** for a

   **18 open ids** were missing from the denominator. The buglog itself already records this class for

   lesson was written down and never propagated to this reader.
**THREE ANSWERS, ONE QUESTION:** 125 (heading population), 108 (the census's own title population, quoted in
T-104's title), 101 (the truth against the census's open set). The face printed the wrong one twice and the
task title printed the third - while T-104's whole remedy depends on which population is meant.
**FIXED BY D-2985:** the population IS the census's open ids and the severity is read from the id's FIRST
heading at ANY depth; the parts now partition the open count exactly (CRITICAL 4 · HIGH 22 · MED 39 · LOW 19 ·
UNLABELLED 101 = 185); the ceiling LOWERED 125 -> 101 (D-2644); the retired second number

## BUG-765 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-13 by D-2987) - the ONE authority did not account for 133 `ratified` decisions (12% of the register), and the state they sit in was declared NOWHERE

**FOUND BY THE RAIL, NOT BY READING.** D-2987's second limb (PRESENCE: a declared sign nothing renders is a
comment) was written to answer a different question - "does the authority actually RENDER the signs it declares?"
Its first run reddened all three faces, as expected, and then the COMPLETENESS limb reddened on six census keys
the new map did not cover. Five were not states at all (`total`, `by_category` - a fault of the RULE, the
D-2986 lesson, repaired by making the required set come from the DECLARED axes instead of the census's keys).
**The sixth was `ratified`, and it was not a fault of the rule.**

**THE MEASUREMENT.** The census counts fourteen decision states. The DERIVED decisions line rendered:

    NEEDING ACTION 67 (open 32 + proposed 14 + draft 1 + deferred 14 + planned 6)
    in effect (active) 565
    closed: resolved 314, superseded 16, archived 8, rejected 11

    = **981 of 1114.** The 133 decisions it never accounted for are exactly those in state `ratified`
      (D300, D315, D316, D-2884, D-2953, D-2959 ... - real, load-bearing decisions, not junk rows).

**WHY IT IS A DEFECT, NOT A COSMETIC GAP.** (1) The line prints its OWN total two words earlier and does not
sum to it - an authority whose arithmetic does not close is not an authority. (2) `ratified` is a state of the
DECISION LIFECYCLE that no file under governance declared: not in `open_decision_states`, not in
`state_tokens`, not in the convention line at the head of DECISION-LOG.md, not in any spec, not in the glyph
map. A reader asking "what is the difference between `active` and `ratified`?" had no artifact to consult -
the same class as BUG-761's twelve undeclared index headings and BUG-757's 101 untokened bugs: **a state with no
sign is a state the face does not show.** (3) It is the THIRD time in four acts that the front-facing surfaces
were found under-reporting: D-2986 policed twelve HEADINGS, D-2985 the LIVE region, and now the state AXIS.

**FIXED 2026-10-13 by D-2987 — "every declared state carries a SIGN and is ACCOUNTED FOR":**
1. the decision-state axis is a **DECLARED PARTITION** in config/gov_sync.yaml: `open_decision_states` (needs
   action) + `decision_in_effect_states` + `decision_closed_states` + `decision_void_states`;
2. the renderer prints **every** declared bucket, so the counts account for the whole register
   (67 + 698 + 349 + 0 = 1114 - exact BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why the invariant is the PARTITION and not a
   separate sum comparison);
3. **NEW RAIL LIMB** `scripts/check_governance_faces.py#partition_faults`: the four buckets must be pairwise
   DISJOINT and their union must EQUAL the states the census counts. **SEEN to red** on the pre-D-2987 config -
   "the census counts ['abandoned','active','archived','ratified','rejected','resolved','revoked','stale',
   'superseded'] (1047 decision(s)) but NO declared bucket holds them" - and green on the repair;
4. `ratified` carries its own sign (⚖) and its own bucket membership, so it is VISIBLE and distinct.

**RESIDUAL - AN OWNER ONTOLOGICAL QUESTION, DECLARED NOT DECIDED.** `ratified` is now *visible* and its
grouping is *declared* (in effect, with its own sign) - but whether it is a genuinely distinct live state or a
SYNONYM of `active` is an ontology question for the owner, not a rendering question. This act did NOT merge
them: merging two states is a claim about the domain, and the honest minimum was to stop pretending 133
decisions did not exist. If the owner rules they collapse, the change is ONE line in config/gov_sync.yaml.

**NOT FIXED HERE:** the same partition question has NOT been asked of the BUG axes (state_tokens and
severity_tokens are declared but their buckets are not), and the census still carries three states that are
declared with a value of 0 (`stale`, `revoked`, `abandoned`) whose WRITERS are not named - a state that no
writer can produce is a declaration without a producer (C19's shape one layer up).

## BUG-767 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-13) - the RETIRED trust metric still leaves the machine, published to agents and written into two exports

FOUND WHILE ANSWERING THE OWNER'S T-107 CHALLENGE ("what were the original concept behind BORP and lead for drop
besides there are no current infrastructure/logic behind it?") - the archaeology, the measurement and the
recommendation are `governance/BORP_FEEDBACK_ASSESSMENT_20261013.md`.

THE DEFECT, three layers deep. (1) `fbs.borp_score` is **non-null `0.0` on every row and NOTHING writes it**:
`pipeline/stage6_commit.py:910` default-injects `fb.get("borp_score", 0.0)` for every row, so the column holds a
value that no producer ever computed (the BUG-511 family: a value nothing writes, presented as a measurement).
(2) Its producer was DELETED - `pipeline/stage5_verify.py:20` records *"DELETED (dead checks): BORP (S1.5
guarantees >=2 sources)"* - and the formula it inherited was DEGENERATE ON THE ADMITTED POPULATION: the v2
`check_borp` (git `c95f7ff:pipeline/stage5_verify.py:105-115`) computed `min(distinct / BORP_MIN_SOURCES, 1.0)`
with the pass bar AT that minimum, so every admitted FB scores exactly 1.0. It was never a score - a boolean
wearing a ratio's name. (3) The stored `0.0` is a FALSE ABSENCE with TWO READINGS inside ONE function:
`pipeline/retrieve.py` reads it as a VALUE in SQL (`COALESCE(borp_score, 0.5)` -> 0.0, which is why any
`ORDER BY borp_score` degenerates to rowid order - the F-40/BUG-710/INV-3 defect) and as ABSENT in Python
(`fb.get("borp_score", 0.5) or 0.5` -> 0.5). MEASURED 2026-10-13 on the live store: `sqlite3 -> 0.0 | 0.5`,
`python -> 0.5 | 0.5`.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS (the outward harm). The value LEAVES the machine as a trust metric:
`pipeline/stage6_okf_export.py:128-130` emits `borp_score: 0.0` as an OKF line,
`pipeline/stage6b_anytype_push.py:336,466` pushes it into the external Anytype store, `pipeline/run_monitor.py:162`
averages it into run metrics (`avg_borp_score`), and `maxwell_mcp_server.py:136,:195,:246` publishes it to agents
in three payloads (`query_knowledge`, `get_fb`, the trust-metrics block). A reader therefore learns "no
corroboration" about rows the same store measures as `strong` with up to 21 source works.

FIX: retire `borp_score` from every served surface in ONE change-set (the payload, the OKF export, the Anytype
push, the diagnostics), make the retired column SQL NULL so the absence is TRUE (D-2957), and PROMOTE the real
signal `isor` (D2284/D2309) under the name `corroboration`. OWNER-GATED: T-107 carries the word; the rail
`scripts/check_served_fields.py` (D-2989) reports the field as declared-absent-advertised at rc 2 until the
change-set lands, and REFUSES a half-move (a declaration without the code edit, or a code edit without the
declaration - BUG-548).

## BUG-768 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-13) - BORP is satisfied by a MINORITY of the served corpus: the deleted per-row check left the SINGLETON route unguarded

THE MEASUREMENT (store `knowledge pipeline/maxwell.db`, the only committed run `rechunk-v4-20260929`, 2026-10-13):

```
status        is_convergent    rows     of which >=2 canonical source works
PASS               0           3,565            0
PASS               1             938          938
QUARANTINE         0           2,682            0
QUARANTINE         1             455          455
```

`is_convergent = 1` is EXACTLY the set with `json_array_length(source_ids) >= 2` (1,393 rows - an identity, not a
correlation). So the SERVED population (`status='PASS'`) satisfies the Book of Record Principle on 938 of 4,503
rows = **20.8%**, and 5,198 of the 6,591 verified rows carry ONE source work. The secondary signal agrees: the
persisted ISOR ratings are weak 5,212 / medium 969 / strong 410 (NULL 1,049 = the D-2590 sidecar tier).

ROOT CAUSE. `check_borp` was deleted at S5 on the argument that "the guarantee moved to S1.5". It did - for the
CLUSTER route only (`S15_MIN_SOURCE_DIVERSITY = 2`). The SINGLETON route (35,239 singletons at S1.5, by
construction one source) never passes through that gate, and once the per-row check was gone nothing re-asserted
the principle: the rows that could never satisfy it were the exact rows the deleted check existed to flag. This is
the BUG-511/BUG-492 class one level up - a guard removed because "the property is structural now", where the
structure covers only one of two admission routes.

CONSEQUENCE. The pipeline's own stated key principle ("BORP: >=2 independent sources for convergence") is TRUE of
the corpus it was built on and TRUE of only a fifth of what it SERVES, while the payload advertises a metric named
after that principle whose value is a dead constant (BUG-767). Neither the pipeline nor the owner could see this:
the metric that would have shown it was the one that died.

FIX (two acts, one owner word). (1) T-107 puts the REAL measurement on the wire (`corroboration` from `isor`:
sources / convergent / independence / independence_score), so the gap is visible to every consumer of the store.
(2) T-118 asks the OWNER the policy question no agent may answer (D-2898): may a single-source row be served as if
corroborated, must it carry a declared tier on every answer, or must it stay out of the default answer path? A
repair that silently re-generated or re-gated those rows would change what the corpus SAYS, which is a ruling.

## BUG-769 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-13 by D-2989) - a MEASURED receipt field the paired contract compares had no re-record act

FOUND BY FIXING SOMETHING ELSE (the honest cascade of adding two modules under the census scan roots, not a side
effect: the new files moved a number the receipt declares).

THE DEFECT. `config/config_defaults_census.json` records `counts.modules`, and
`tests/test_config_defaults_census_spec.py::test_the_receipt_equals_the_measurement` asserts that the receipt EQUALS
a fresh measurement. But `scripts/check_config_defaults.py` rewrote the receipt only on a CEILING change
(`if changed or paid:`), and a coverage change goes through `--rebaseline`. MEASURED 2026-10-13: adding two
`scripts/*.py` moved the count 553 -> 556 while every key, site and ceiling stayed put - so the rail reported `ok`
and the CONTRACT failed, with no act able to refresh the receipt: a hand edit is forbidden (D-2642) and a rebaseline
is not a coverage change. That is the D-2981 shape one field over: **a measurement with no writer.**

FIXED IN THE SAME ACT. `receipt_module_drift(receipt, files)` (a pure helper) + a `--record` path that re-records
the receipt when the module count is stale (the ceilings are untouched, and the print names both numbers), one new
known-answer control (the rail is now 15/15) and one mutation lock (`the_receipt_module_count_rerecord_is_load_bearing`,
floor 46 -> 47, SEEN to red). MEASURED after the fix: `--record` re-recorded `counts.modules` 553 -> 556 with the
ceilings unchanged at `{shadowed_declared: 300, undeclared: 3}`, and the paired contract is 10/10 green.

## BUG-770 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-13 by D-2991) - the reviewed-sheet JUDGMENT existed TWICE, so the pre-flight could pass a sheet the writer refuses

**CLASS.** One rule, two implementations. `scripts/reanchor_retrieval_goldens.py` carried the verdict logic in
`_check_reviewed` AND `_apply_reviewed`: the "exactly ONE anchor" refusal, the owner-signature refusal, the
unreviewed-query refusal and the drop/ADD reporting were each written out twice, in slightly different words
(`rows marked 'anchor' — exactly one is required` vs `rows marked 'anchor' - exactly one is required`).

**WHY IT MATTERS.** `--check` exists to tell the owner what the writer will do BEFORE a 150-cell sitting. A
pre-flight that is a COPY drifts from the writer silently, and it drifts in the one direction that costs real work:
it can report a sheet as appliable that the writer then refuses (or, worse, the reverse — a refusal nobody can see
until the end). This is the D-2642 class (one derived value, two homes) applied to a CONTROL.

**MEASURED.** The owner's sheet was refused with 48 faults by BOTH paths, but the two paths agreed only because
both had been edited in the same act; the vocabulary literal, the multiplicity rule and the signature rule were
each hardcoded in both. The fourth defect was invisible: **neither path could express the SET semantics the harness
already had** (`_recall_at_k` is micro over `expected`; `expected_names` is a list) - the limit was the tool's,
not the format's.

**FIXED IN THE SAME ACT.** `judge_review(rows, queries, mode, signature_required, live)` is now the ONE pure,
store-free judgment; `--check` and `--apply` both call it and neither restates a rule (asserted by
`tests/test_retrieval_goldens_spec.py::test_inv6_check_and_apply_call_the_one_judgment`); the mode, the vocabulary,
the signature requirement and the multiplicity rule all live in `config/pipeline_config.yaml` and are read
FAIL-CLOSED; 11 known-answer controls (`--selftest`) prove the guards can FAIL, and `specs/retrieval_goldens.spec.md`
(INV-1..INV-10) is the paired contract for a surface that had NONE.

## BUG-771 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-13) - the review sheet compared every candidate against a golden state that no longer existed

**THE DEFECT.** `scripts/reanchor_retrieval_goldens.py` fills `old_name`/`old_fb_id`/`old_status` from the LIVE
golden at GENERATION time and nothing records WHICH golden state that was. The sheet the owner reviewed
(`governance/golden_reanchor_candidates_20261011.csv`, generated 2026-10-11 20:44Z) was generated BEFORE the
`20261011T221956Z` apply that re-anchored the same 30 queries - so every "old" cell described the PRE-apply set.

**MEASURED 2026-10-13 (on the owner's reviewed copy).** `30/30` `old_name` values are ABSENT from their own
candidate list; `30/30` LIVE expectations are PRESENT. The instructions' cheapest, highest-value cell class -
*"if the query is already correct, still write it: anchor the row whose `cand_name` equals `old_name`"* - was
therefore unsatisfiable for EVERY query. The reviewer had no way to see what the system currently expects, which is
precisely the comparison the column exists to make.

**CONSEQUENCE (bounded, but real).** A 30-query owner sitting was run against a ghost. It did not produce a WRONG
anchor (the owner judged the live candidates on their merits), but it removed the cheapest correct answer
("what is already right") from the sheet and made the review slower and harder for no reason.

**FIX (owed).** (i) The generator stamps the golden state it compared against by HASH (`sha256` of
`config/golden/retrieval_queries.yaml` at generation) into the sheet header; (ii) the pre-flight REFUSES a sheet
whose stamped hash no longer matches the live file - a STALE-PREMISE rail, the same discipline as D-2989's
advertised-claim rail one artifact over; (iii) the reviewer is told in the sheet which candidate the system
currently expects. Until then: regenerate the sheet immediately before a review sitting, never re-use one across an
apply.

## BUG-773 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-13) - the declared rule "a commit may never rewrite an existing row's body" is contradicted by the live upsert

**THE DEFECT (a declared rule and a live path that disagree).** `config/dedup_identity.yaml` (`edition_supersession.execution`)
declares `never_at_commit: true  # D-2933 rule V: a commit may never rewrite an existing row's body` and `never_delete: true`.
The live commit path is `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO fbs` on a `fb_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` (`pipeline/stage6_commit.py:764`, 77
columns) whose identity is `SHA-256(name + definition)` (`pipeline/schemas.py:175`) — DEFINITION-SENSITIVE, stated as the
D-2949 root cause in `pipeline/dedup_identity.py`. Two shapes, both wrong: (i) the definition is byte-identical → the SAME
`fb_id` → every column is rewritten from the new checkpoint, so the PRIOR READING IS DESTROYED with no revision and no trace
(C6 forbids exactly this); (ii) the definition moves by one character → a DIFFERENT `fb_id` → a SECOND row is committed, both
survive, and nothing reconciles them (that second shape is BUG-772's case, one step further).

**MEASURED 2026-10-13 (read-only, by reading the write path — nothing was written).** `content_basis` — the column that would
say WHICH text the current body was read from — is declared a RESERVED NAME WITH NO WRITER
(`config/dedup_identity.yaml` → `freshness_pointer`, with its own build order: "record it at EXTRACTION first; a supersession
operation must never act on a fact nobody recorded"). So the corpus cannot answer "is this body's text the one I read last
time?" for ANY row.

**CONSEQUENCE.** A richer source (a newer edition, a cleaner scan, a better extractor, a re-chunk) silently BECOMES the row,
and the previous statement of the claim is unrecoverable — while D-2952's queue for exactly this case
(`supersede_review`, from the dedup gate's `would` vocabulary) cannot be executed safely because there is no basis to compare
against. A knowledge base that cannot retain what it used to say cannot absorb a correction, which is the strongest reason
option (a) "never update anything" was rejected (D-2992 §3).

**FIX (owed, D-2992 R2).** (i) The HEAD may change; the RECORD never does: an append-only revision sidecar (`fb_id`,
`revision_n`, the body fields, `source_ids`, `gen_model`, `pipeline_commit`, `run_id`, `effective_from`/`effective_to`,
`basis`), with the superseded filename APPENDED to `source_ids` (never replacing one). (ii) `content_basis` gets its writer at
EXTRACTION. (iii) The axes are NOT touched by a body revision (D-2992 R3). Precedents, verified before citing (2026-10-13):
Kimball SCD Type 2, Fowler's event sourcing, and PROV-O (`prov:wasRevisionOf` is a subproperty of `prov:wasDerivedFrom`).

## BUG-772 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-13) - corroboration is frozen by ONE run's clustering, so a later independent source can never raise a row's tier

**THE DEFECT.** `is_convergent` is written by S1.5 as "at least two distinct canonical sources **in one cluster of one run**"
(`pipeline/stage1_5_embed_cluster.py`, D2176) and PERSISTED with the row. Nothing recomputes it, and nothing joins a later
work to an existing claim: the dedup instrument built for the same-concept-two-identities collision groups by
`(normalize_name(name), source_id)` — THE SAME WORK — with a body-divergence merge gate and a `would` vocabulary of
`link_duplicate | supersede_review | insert` under `mode: report` (`pipeline/dedup_identity.py`, `pipeline/dedup_gate.py:211`).
A DIFFERENT work asserting the same claim is therefore invisible to it BY CONSTRUCTION (the grouping key differs), and the only
path that sees the case is a FULL re-run whose segment set contains both works.

**CONSEQUENCE (two, and the second is silent).** (i) A row's tier can NEVER RISE: a claim extracted from one work stays
single-source for ever, however many later works assert it. (ii) The first DELTA run — and incremental intake is what the
internet-media plan requires — corroborates NOTHING and reports it indistinguishably from "nothing to corroborate": absence by
blindness, the BUG-487 class relocated onto the quality axis, where the number that would look wrong is the one nobody
recomputes.

**FIX (owed).** T-120: independence becomes a DERIVED value (ONE DERIVED VALUE, ONE HOME, D-2646 — `config/derivations.yaml`,
which already homes `fbs.status` / `fbs.confidence_score` / `fbs.epistemic_status` each with a parity rail), computed from the
row's OWN evidence (`source_segments` → `n_voices` by embedding similarity, NLI-confirmed; `source_ids` → works × authors ×
domains) and only for rows whose tier would MOVE. That is T-119's plan promoted from a measurement to the engine, and its
FALSIFIER travels with it: if P(n_voices >= 2 | is_convergent = 1) is indistinguishable from 1, the count is not contaminated
in this corpus and the hardening is documentation only.

## BUG-774 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-13, PREVENTIVE) - the planned non-book intake has no identity, and the branch it would fall to is the one a closed defect class removed

**THE DEFECT.** Media intake (peer-reviewed articles, journals, video transcripts, social threads, podcasts) is on the
roadmap, but identity is BOOK-SHAPED: `source_id = SHA-256(normalize_author｜normalize_title)` with a FILENAME FALLBACK branch
(`pipeline/book_metadata.py::compute_source_id`), over a converter that accepts only `{.epub, .pdf, .md}`
(`pipeline/stage0_convert.py`). The evaluator's rail asserts fail-closed that the fallback branch is NEVER live —
`config/eval_integrity.yaml` → `source_identity.max_both_unknown_ratio: 0.0`, enforced by
`scripts/verify_source_identity.py`, whose docstring records the ORIGINAL defect this closed: `source_diversity` counted
FILENAMES, so "29.1% of convergence (757/2597 rows) was the same book twice", and 369 work-identities carried >1 filename.

**WHY IT IS SEVERE LATER AND MEDIUM NOW.** Nothing non-book has been ingested, so no row is wrong TODAY. A transcript, a
podcast episode, a journal article or a thread has no author｜title in that shape, so it lands on the fallback branch — and a
work RE-PUBLISHED in another medium (preprint → version of record; the author's book → the author's podcast; a paper → its
blog post) would count as a SECOND `source_id` and certify corroboration between a voice and itself. That is the R3
contaminated-source failure of D-2990, at a scale the corpus has never seen, arriving through the identity layer rather than
through the count.

**FIX (owed, D-2992 R4 + T-121).** In this order: (i) a source-KIND axis with a per-kind identity resolver — the precedent is
already in-repo (`config/references.yaml` resolves bibliographic metadata from OpenAlex BY DOI "rather than letting anyone
type it (so a wrong year, venue or DOI cannot survive a rebuild)"), and OpenAlex's work `type` is a controlled 25-value
vocabulary; (ii) the re-publication collapse rule (a work and its versions are ONE voice — the D-2308 edition collapse,
generalised; the standard vocabulary is NISO RP-8-2008 JAV's seven versions and Crossref's `isVersionOf`/`isPreprintOf`/
`isTranslationOf`/`isCommentOn` relations — note `isRetractedBy` is NOT a Crossref relation type; retraction is Crossmark
update metadata); (iii) `content_basis` + `retrieved_at` + licence recorded at extraction; (iv) only then conversion. A
retraction/update path is part of the same obligation — a corpus that cannot absorb a retraction cannot be trusted
(Crossref Crossmark; COPE).

## BUG-775 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-14) - ONE BIT IN THREE COLUMNS: the corroboration the store advertises is a derivation nothing declares
- **Where.** `fbs.is_convergent`, `fbs.source_diversity` and `fbs.source_ids` (the D2185 canonical works), joined by
  NOTHING. `config/derivations.yaml` declares a home and a parity rail for every other derived column it knows; these
  three rows do not exist, so "which column owns the fact?" cannot be answered from the repo (D-2646).
- **Measured 2026-10-14** (read-only, CANONICAL_RUN `rechunk-v4-20260929`, 7,640 rows): `is_convergent = 1` ⟺
  `source_diversity >= 2` ⟺ `|source_ids| >= 2` on **7,640/7,640 rows, 0 exceptions, 0 NULL source_ids**. Three
  governed columns, one bit. The corroboration count is therefore a PURE PROJECTION of the source set: exact, and
  information-free beyond it — the falsifier D-2992 attached to its own ruling (P(n_voices>=2 | is_convergent=1))
  measured **1.0000** against a counterfactual **0.0000** and FIRED (`governance/T120_S1_RECON_20261014.md`).
- **Why it matters beyond tidiness.** A reader may branch on any of the three columns and no rail reports the
  divergence; a delta run can write one and not the others; and the whole "derived corroboration" plan (T-120) was
  scoped as if the count carried information the row did not already state. The information is on the INDEPENDENCE
  axis (`isor`, D2284/D2309: weak 5,212 / medium 969 / strong 410), where 35 of the 938 served count-corroborated
  rows are WEAK, 148 carry ONE author and 170 ONE domain.

## BUG-776 (CLOSED 2026-10-14) - the RETIRED scalar is gone from the wire but still READ inside the machine
- **Where.** The T-107 change-set (D-2994) removed `borp_score` from all three serving surfaces, and the rail proves
  it from the payload's own AST keys (INV-12). The INTERNAL readers were deliberately NOT touched, because they move
  retrieval behaviour and therefore need their own change-set with its own measurement.
- **Measured 2026-10-14 (read-only).** `pipeline/retrieve.py::_quality_field` returns `"borp_score"` whenever
  `RANKING_QUALITY_SCORE_ENABLED` is OFF, i.e. the degraded path ranks on a constant; `pipeline/retrieve.py:893,913`
  SELECT it into the graph-aware path; `pipeline/query.py:287` prints `BORP Score: 0.0` to the operator;
  `pipeline/run_monitor.py:162-163` reports `avg_borp_score`, which is 0.0 by construction (`borp_score` is 0.0 on
  7,640/7,640 rows) - a monitor metric that can never move; `pipeline/retrieval_evaluator.py:253` formats the dead
  value into an evaluation line; and `pipeline/stage6b_anytype_push.py::ALL_FIELDS` is a list NOTHING reads (a dead
  declaration, C19) that still names the column.
- **Why it matters.** The BUG-511 class: a reader can branch on a value nothing writes, and a MONITOR that reports a
  constant is a control that cannot fire - exactly the shape the register exists to find. A wire-only retirement
  leaves the machine's own view of corroboration still false wherever the degraded path is taken.
- **Fix (declared, owed as ONE change-set).** Point `_quality_field()`'s fallback at the live measure (or make the
  fused ranking unconditional), replace the two SELECT lists, replace the printed line and the monitor metric with
  the graded tuple (or delete the metric), and delete the dead `ALL_FIELDS` list. It must land with a
  retrieval-measurement receipt (golden set) because it changes served ordering; a silent edit inside a contract
  change was refused on purpose.
- **Status.** CLOSED 2026-10-14 by D-2995 (the reader change-set, one commit, with its receipt).

**WHAT LANDED (D-2995).** Every reader named above is gone and the PRODUCER is gone with them:
| site | disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `pipeline/retrieve.py::_quality_field` | the retired-column fallback is DELETED; the measure is now `config/pipeline_config.yaml#ranking.quality_field`, read fail-closed by `pipeline_paths.py::RANKING_QUALITY_FIELD` |
| `pipeline/retrieve.py::_rank_sql` | the off-arm no longer returns a dead `ORDER BY`; with `quality_score_enabled: false` BOTH functions raise (`RuntimeError`), because there is no declared degraded ordering — a dead ordering may not return as a silent fallback (C16) |
| `pipeline/retrieve.py:893,913` (graph SELECTs) | the false scalar is out of the neighbour payload; NO new field was added (that would be its own payload-contract act) |
| `pipeline/query.py:287` | the operator line now prints the graded `corroboration_tuple` (D-2994's replacement), not a fabricated 0.0 |
| `pipeline/run_monitor.py:162-163` | `avg_borp_score` DELETED — a monitor metric that could only read 0.0 is a control that can never fire |
| `pipeline/retrieval_evaluator.py:253` | the `BORP: ?` slot DELETED from the judge prompt. It was information-free by construction (the constant 0.0 failed its own truthiness test, so it always rendered `?`) |
| `pipeline/schemas.py` | `VerifiedFB.borp_score` (default 1.0) DELETED — a pydantic default of 1.0 on a retired measure FABRICATED a trust score for any model built without it |

| `scripts/sync_checkpoint_from_db.py`, `sync_s5_checkpoint_from_db.py` | removed from the DB-only field sets, so the checkpoint round-trip (BUG-376) cannot CARRY the fabricated value back |

was run before and after the change over the 29 golden queries, SERVED path (`search()`, D-2980):

fingerprint `00deeb030657f314` pre == post. The ordering does not move; the bug's risk was measured, not

> the rule does not resolve STAYS `declared_unresolved`, because the COUNT is the debt (fail-closed). Home:
> `config/anchor_family.yaml#store_bridge.resolution`; consumer: `scripts/build_anchor_store_bridge.py`. The mover is
> now the pipeline, and this ruling is what lets BUG-778's 5 hidden rails come back GREEN-or-RED ON THEIR OWN CAUSE
> instead of behind a red line.

## BUG-779 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-14 by the same act) - the SERVED ranking carried TWO homes for ONE policy value: the ORDER BY inlined a literal where the same file used the declared constant

**FOUND** while completing D-2995's own cascade check (the audit was looking for a retired value that left; it found a
DECLARED value that had never fully arrived). `pipeline/retrieve.py::_rank_sql()` - the ONE home of the served
`ORDER BY` (D2537/D-2980) - built its fusion clause as
`COALESCE(confidence_score, 0.5) * {RANKING_CONFIDENCE_WEIGHT}`, **inlining the neutral prior as a literal**, while the
SAME FILE's served SELECT (`:1103`) and its Python re-sort (`:1123`) read the declared
`NEUTRAL_PRIOR = config/feedback.yaml#serving.neutral_prior`. That is precisely the shape
`config/feedback.yaml`'s own header names as the reason the file exists: *"a policy value with TWO homes is the
BUG-499/BUG-502 class"* - and it sat on the ORDER path, where changing the config would have moved the SELECT and left
the ORDER BY behind, silently re-ranking every answer with a prior the register no longer declares.

**WHY IT SURVIVED.** The two values are numerically equal today (0.5), so no measurement could see it; and the
`borp_score` retirement workstream had every reason to look at what LEFT this function and none to look at what it
still INLINED. It is the mirror of BUG-776: that bug was a value nothing writes being read as a measurement; this one
is a value that HAS a home being written a second time inside the same function.

**THE FIX.** One line: `0.5` -> `{NEUTRAL_PRIOR}`; `specs/retrieval_serving.spec.md` INV-3 now names the declared home
instead of quoting the number.

**THE RECEIPT (inertness, proven by construction rather than by benchmark).** The rendered SQL is **byte-identical**
before and after the change: `NEUTRAL_PRIOR` is read from `config/feedback.yaml#serving.neutral_prior` and equals
`0.5`, so the substitution cannot alter a byte of the statement the store executes - verified by rebuilding the
pre-fix string from the post-fix one and comparing (`old == sql` -> True, 2026-10-14). A ranked-identity benchmark run
was attempted as a second receipt and was **abandoned on a 300s cap** (the ladder's whole-set collection was running
concurrently); it is NOT needed here, because a byte-identical statement cannot produce a different order, and
claiming otherwise would be a receipt for a risk this change does not carry. **The lesson is recorded as the receipt's
own limit:** a benchmark is the right instrument when the change can move behaviour, and the wrong instrument when the
change is a substitution of equal value - spending 15 minutes to "prove" inertness by measurement is the mirror of
asserting it.

**WHAT IS *NOT* IN THIS ACT.** (a) The `or NEUTRAL_PRIOR` idiom at `:1123`/`:1124` still conflates a stored `0.0`
with absence (0.0 becomes 0.5) - that is the D-2957/R4 half and it belongs to T-107's declared `keep-and-declare`
limb, not here. (b) A rail that would CATCH this class (a numeric literal on a path whose value has a declared home)
does not exist; the census rails count code defaults READ through `cfg.get(...)`, and an inlined literal inside an
f-string is neither. NAMED, not fixed: it is the natural home of the `check_config_defaults` family's third limb.

Evidence: this entry; `pipeline/retrieve.py::_rank_sql` (the one line) + `:1103`/`:1123` (the declared reads);
`config/feedback.yaml` (the ONE home, and its own header stating the rule);
`specs/retrieval_serving.spec.md` INV-3.

## BUG-783 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-14 by the same act) - THE MUTATION GATE'S FIXTURE WAS UNDER-DECLARED: two guards of the served-fields rail could not be made to red, so the gate blamed the MUTATION for a fixture gap

- **Where.** `config/rail_mutations.yaml#fixture.include_files` against the inputs
  `scripts/check_served_fields.py --selftest` actually reads.
- **The measurement (2026-10-14).** The gate reported two entries as `the oracle's BASELINE is not green (rc=1):
  the runner is already red before any mutation, so its red after one proves nothing` —
  `the_undeclared_advert_guard_is_load_bearing` and `the_owner_word_vocabulary_guard_is_load_bearing`, both
  mutating `scripts/check_served_fields.py`. Reproduced in the kept fixture: the runner failed **1 of 24** controls,
  with `promotions.corroboration.builder 'pipeline/corroboration.py::corroboration_tuple' does not resolve (file +
  symbol)` and `consumers names 'maxwell_mcp_server.py', which does not exist`. The same runner in the live tree is
  green (24/24, rc 0) — so the fault was the FIXTURE, and the gate's message attributed it to the mutation.
- **Why it matters (not cosmetic).** Those two guards are the served-fields rail's advertised-field guard and its
  OWNER-WORD vocabulary guard — kind (iv) teeth of the standing rule (D-2676: a rule that cannot be made to fail is
  not a rule). While the fixture lacked the declaration's builder and consumers, BOTH were un-provable, and the
  ladder reported them as a mutation fault rather than as a missing input: the same false-attribution shape as
  BUG-589, one declaration over.
- **Fix.** `include_files` gains the files the declaration NAMES (`maxwell_mcp_server.py`, `pipeline/
  corroboration.py`, `pipeline/stage6_okf_export.py`, `pipeline/stage6b_anytype_push.py`), with the before/after
  measurement recorded beside the list. VERIFIED: 24/24 in the fixture; `check_rail_mutations.py` 47/47 declared
  rules seen to red, 1 negative control green, 0 baseline faults.
- **What it does NOT claim.** The other mutation-fixture inputs may be under-declared in the same way and are not
  audited here: the gate only measures what its DECLARED entries mutate, so a third guard of another rail could be
  silently un-provable. That audit is T-124's triage (the masked rails) and is NOT closed by this entry.

## BUG-782 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-14, closed with the signer) - THE OWNER LANE HAD NO INTAKE: a machine screen sat in a column NAMED `owner_ruling`, the deterministic tier was off by five, and no reader existed for either

- **Where.** `governance/work_identity_collapse_review_20261014.csv` (the T-129 review sheet) and the absence of a
  consumer for it: no module under `scripts/` or `pipeline/` read the sheet; the only reader was
  `pipeline/ingest_gate.py#collapse_debt`, and it located the ruling column by NAME.
- **The measurement (2026-10-14, read-only).** (a) The sheet's `identical_text` = **42 yes / 42 no** while its own
  source artifact `temp/voice_collapse_pairs_20261014.csv#certain` = **37 yes / 47 no** and
  `config/corroboration_collapse.yaml#lexical_limb.measured.pairs_identical_text` = **37**. Re-measured today
  through the intake (`--render`, 67 s, imports the rail's limb): **37 identical / 47 containment / 84 pairs /
  72 groups** — the rail and the census were right and the sheet was wrong. (b) The sheet's `owner_ruling` column
  held **68 yes / 16 no**, written by no script in this repo, in a claim-shaped name a reader would take for an
  owner's word. (c) Per-pair `rows_affected` summed to **745** against a census of **530** because 117 rows sit in
  more than one pair and rows span groups: the columns are NOT additive and nothing declared it. (d) Σ per-group
  distinct = **717** over a corpus-wide distinct of **530** — the same fact, one level up.
- **Why nothing caught it.** The pair OBJECT had no home: the counts were published (`lexical_limb.measured`) but
  the pairs came from a one-off under `temp/` (auto-purge 7 days), so the sheet was **hand-built** and could not be
  re-derived; the sheet's only reader sniffed a column by name and would have landed on `proposed_ruling` — a
  PROPOSAL — had one existed; and the sheet's own columns were declared nowhere. Same class as BUG-781 (a claim
  with no reader) and the same class as the census cascade (a measured field compared by nothing).
- **The fix.** `config/owner_marks.yaml` (ONE contract: vocabularies, homes, tiers, proposals, derivation,
  coverage, conflict rule) + `scripts/owner_marks.py`:
  `--render` measures the store through the rail's own limb (IMPORTED, D-2646), writes the pair object
  (`governance/corroboration_collapse_pairs.json`, carrying the rule's sha256 so a changed rule makes the object
  STALE), renders the sheet with per-row proposals and provenance, carries every owner word/note already given and
  FAILS CLOSED rather than drop one; `--check` derives the effective word (override > signed tier > none),
  validates the vocabulary, tests the transitivity conflict rule, and binds the sheet to the census by digest;
  `--apply` expands ONLY signed tiers and writes `ruling_source` per row; `--selftest` = **9/9** known-answer
  controls (unknown word, unsigned tier, withheld word, transitivity conflict, stale sheet, dropped word,
  unparseable predicate, stale pair object, signature expansion). `ingest_gate.collapse_debt` now reads the column
  by DECLARATION (`config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml#ledger.collapse_word_column_from` →
  `config/owner_marks.yaml#homes.collapse_sheet.derived_column`).
- **What it does NOT do.** It never chooses a word (a proposal is not a word and the derivation never reads one,
  D-2898), never applies a collapse in the store (the identity repair stays T-129's pipeline act) and never writes
  a home it does not declare (the four other owner lanes are pointers, `other_owner_lanes`).
- **Owner act.** `governance/OWNER_MARKS_20261014.md`: 5 signed tiers (A/B/C/L-A/L-B) + 8 per-row words
  (`hint == review`).

## BUG-781 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-14) - THE IDENTITY MACHINERY HAD NO ENFORCEMENT POINT: the owner ledger sat 59 pairs PENDING for a fortnight while the INGEST path read nothing

- **Where.** The ABSENCE of a reader, not the presence of a defect: `pipeline/stage0_convert.py`, `justfile#triad`,
  `justfile#stage0` — none of them read `governance/duplicate_adjudication.json`. The machinery around it is healthy
  and green in the ladder (`detect_title_renames.py` 45 candidates, `detect_same_work_content.py` 29 candidates,
  `gate_duplicate_candidates.py` 59 ledger pairs, `verify_duplicate_gate.py --selftest` passing).
- **The measurement.** MEASURED 2026-10-14: `candidate_count: 59`, `adjudicated: 0`, verdicts `Counter({'PENDING': 59})`,
  ledger last written 2026-09-30 19:52 — fourteen days in which the corpus kept growing and BUG-780's 84 pairs kept
  certifying 530 rows as corroborated by ONE voice under TWO names (369 of them SERVED).
- **Why it is the BUG-780 shape, one level UP.** BUG-780 is the CORPUS consequence; this is the PIPELINE cause. An
  unresolved identity was not refused at the door, so it was ingested, rowed, and decided by nobody.
- **Why nothing caught it (four reasons, all reusable).** (a) `--gate` is declared POST-RUN; a reader that only runs
  after the batch cannot refuse the batch. (b) The ledger's own `_preserve_verdicts` carries verdicts forward, so a
  never-adjudicated ledger re-renders byte-identically on every run and LOOKS maintained. (c) `verify_duplicate_gate.py`
  was run by the ladder in its STRUCTURAL mode, whose docstring is explicit that "PENDING is a valid state (owner
  gating is a human step)" — TRUE about the structure and SILENT about the door: green rail, open door. (d) No line
  carried a corpus-denominator, so "the corpus grew" had no measurement that could disagree with it.
- **The fix (T-130).** The missing enforcement point and nothing else: `pipeline/ingest_gate.py` (the door) +
  `scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py` (its rail, 8/8 controls) + `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml` (the ONE
  policy home). It re-detects NOTHING (detection has one home, C12/D-2646), merges NOTHING (D-2898: a work-identity
  label is an owner word) and deletes NOTHING (R-D410). It is DELTA-SCOPED — only files absent from the metadata
  cache are candidates — so no ingested file, row, checkpoint or count can move because of it (the cascade rule;
  measured: 0 candidates over the live 940-file corpus). A deferred candidate is skipped IN PLACE, named loudly and
  receipted under declared runtime state. Wired into `stage0` (so no recipe can bypass it) and into the ladder as a
  TRI-STATE line whose rc 2 REFUSES at the ingest step BY DECLARATION (`door.ingest_reading: rc2_refuses`).
- **The two blindspots found while building it (recorded, because both were caught by CONTROLS and not by reading).**
  (1) `compute_source_id`'s filename-fallback branch returns a BARE digest — there is NO `unknown|` prefix to test
  for — so a door that trusted the id's SHAPE admitted a brand-new file as its own duplicate; identity honesty is now
  decided by the SOURCE (a cache record carrying author AND title), never by an id's shape (the BUG-511 class).
  (2) The detector report carries NO `pair_id` while the ledger does, so a coverage check compared two id NAMESPACES
  and reported all 29 content candidates as an uncovered/STALE ledger — a false FATAL. Coverage is now joined on the
  unordered `{a_id,b_id}` pair key, the one key both surfaces carry. A door ships with controls, not with confidence.
- **Status.** OPEN. The DOOR is landed and inert on the existing corpus; what remains is the owner's words on the 59
  ledger pairs + the 84 collapse rows (T-129/T-130), and until they land `--gate` REFUSES BY DESIGN. Evidence:
  `governance/INGEST_IDENTITY_GATE_20261014.md`; `pipeline/ingest_gate.py`; `scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py`;
  `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml`; `config/rail_registry.yaml`.

## BUG-780 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-14) - WORK IDENTITY COLLAPSE: 84 work-pairs are ONE TEXT under TWO NAMES, so 530 "corroborated" rows (369 of them SERVED) are certified by a SINGLE VOICE while `isor` rates 205 of them strong/medium

- **Where.** `fbs.source_ids` / `source_books` / `is_convergent`, one level below the D-2309 identity fix. Measured
  read-only 2026-10-14 over the 1,393 `is_convergent = 1` rows of the canonical run (`rechunk-v4-20260929`, 7,640
  rows): **84 work-pairs collapse at containment ≥ 0.80, 37 of them IDENTICAL normalised text, forming 72
  duplicate-work groups** (largest 3). Those pairs certify **530 rows**, of which **369 are SERVED
  (`status='PASS'`)** and **134 of the store's 257 `epistemic_status='corroborated'` rows** are in the set.
  Threshold-free class: **184 rows** are identical text, no similarity judgement involved.
- **Measured (rail + rule, both read-only).** `scripts/check_corroboration_collapse.py --voice` against
  `config/corroboration_collapse.yaml#lexical_limb`; the method and the worked pairs are in
  `governance/WORK_IDENTITY_COLLAPSE_20261014.md`. ZERO store writes; ~1 minute of local CPU; no model.
- **Why it matters.** The store's corroboration claim is FALSE on these rows, and the false half is the half an
  agent reads: `config/served_fields.yaml#tier_policy` (T-118, granted 2026-10-14) publishes
  `{sources, convergent, independence, independence_score}` — on 134 collapsed rows that reads "convergent: true,
  independence: **strong**" about **one voice**. `isor` (author × domain × count) is a METADATA measure, so a book
  ingested twice under two names rates **strong**; a content-level fact cannot be screened by a metadata-level
  measure. Distribution among the 530: PASS/source-supported/medium 220 · PASS/corroborated/**strong** 134 ·
  QUARANTINE/medium 88 · QUARANTINE/**strong** 71 · weak 17.
- **Why the existing fixes do not cover it (nothing regressed, nothing is contradicted).** D-2309 removed FILENAMES
  from identity — these two names resolve to two *different* canonical works, so it was necessary and not
  sufficient. `dedup_identity` groups by `(normalize_name, source_id)` — the SAME WORK — so a second ingest under
  another name is invisible to it **by construction** (the BUG-772 shape), and `duplicate_of` still has no writer.
  `check_corroboration_bit` stays GREEN: `is_convergent == |source_ids| >= 2` on 7,640/7,640 — the count is exactly
  re-derivable AND carries no information about whether the named sources are distinct VOICES. Both facts hold.
- **The blindspot that hid it (recorded, because it is the reusable lesson).** T-119's semantic limb probed for
  persisted EMBEDDINGS (`*.index`, `*.npy`, `embeddings_cache/*`), found none, and reported BLOCKED (correctly —
  absent is not zero, D-2957). The limb needs the segment TEXT, not the vectors, and the S1 chunk store persists it
  (730 MB, `stage1_chunk/rechunk-v4-20260929/checkpoint.jsonl`); all 148,831 referenced segment ids matched. The
  limb was never blocked — it was looking in the wrong place.
- **Fix (declared, owner-gated on the WRITE, D-2898).** Collapse the 84 pairs at the identity layer: 37 are
  DETERMINISTIC (identical text), 47 need one owner word each. Then re-derive `source_ids`/`source_diversity`/
  `is_convergent` for the affected rows and let `check_corroboration_bit` re-prove the whole population against its
  own evidence. Sheet: `governance/work_identity_collapse_review_20261014.csv`; task T-129. Raising
  `stage1_5.min_source_diversity` is explicitly REFUSED (risk R2, gate regression, would suppress real
  corroboration with the fake) and no duplicate-adjusted SCALAR may be minted (C12/C20, D-2646).
- **Scope, stated.** LEXICAL screen: it can CERTIFY a collapse and can never certify independence — paraphrase,
  translation and heavy editing are invisible to it, so 38.05% is a LOWER BOUND and the embedding+NLI limb stays
  declared as the residual (no longer a blocker).
- **Status.** OPEN. Evidence: `governance/WORK_IDENTITY_COLLAPSE_20261014.md`;
  `config/corroboration_collapse.yaml#lexical_limb`; `governance/work_identity_collapse_review_20261014.csv`.

## BUG-784 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-14) - the T-101 pre-flight read the GENERATOR's sheet, so a COMPLETED owner act was recorded as OWED, and the draft `--apply` needs lived in an auto-purging directory

- **Where.** `scripts/reanchor_retrieval_goldens.py` (`CSV_OUT`/`YAML_OUT` used as the defaults of `--check`/`--apply`),
  `config/pipeline_config.yaml#retrieval_benchmark.reanchor` (no reviewed-sheet declaration), and
  `temp/golden_proposed_v5.yaml` (gitignored, purged at 7 days).
- **The measurement (2026-10-14, read-only).** (a) `--check` with its defaults: `rows 150 · queries 30` and
  **30 faults**, every one of the form "query '...': NO row marked 'anchor' and no retire/rewrite verdict — 5
  candidate row(s) to choose from (a guess is not a label)". (b) The SAME judgment over the owner's sheet
  (`--reviewed-csv governance/golden_reanchor_candidates_20261011.reviewed.csv --reviewed-draft
  temp/golden_proposed_v5.yaml`): **rc 0**, `29 / 29` queries with an expected set, **120 anchor names**,
  **19 owner abstentions excluded**, every chosen anchor owner-signed (D-2939). (c) The owner's sheet:
  `decision` non-empty on **150/150** rows (120 `anchor` / 19 `ambiguous` / 11 `rewrite-query`), `owner_signature`
  non-empty on **150/150**, dated 2026-10-13 — the act the register recorded as owed had been complete for a day.
  (d) The misspelled mode token D-2991's note records (19 cells as `ambigouos`) is in NEITHER the packet nor the
  projection today (0 hits): the applier normalises it and its selftest pins that, so the typo never needed a re-fill.
- **Why nothing caught it.** The reader named its input by the GENERATOR's default path; both artifacts are the same
  shape (150 rows × 30 queries); and the pre-flight printed counts WITHOUT printing which file it had read, so its
  faults read exactly like an owner's omission. T-101's `gate:` then recorded the fault verbatim ("`--check` sees 0 of
  30 queries with an anchor row (30 faults, --apply would REFUSE)"), which a later session reads as owed work. This is
  BUG-492's class at the level of a PATH: a rail nobody has seen fail on its own input is a rail whose input nobody
  has checked.
- **The fix.** `reviewed_sheet` + `reviewed_draft` DECLARED in `config/pipeline_config.yaml`;
  `--reviewed-csv`/`--reviewed-draft` resolve from that declaration and `SystemExit(1)` when it is absent (C16: a
  guessed path is how this happened); `--check`/`--apply` read only the declared paths; the pre-flight now prints the
  sheet, the draft, the row count, the marked-decision count and the signature count, and warns in words when NO row
  carries a decision ("this is the GENERATOR's empty sheet, not the REVIEWED one"); the draft moved from `temp/` to
  the durable home `governance/golden_reanchor_proposed_v5.yaml`. 11/11 known-answer controls still fire.
- **Status.** FIXED, verified: `--check` rc 0 on the declared paths; rc 1 + the warning when the empty generator sheet
  is passed explicitly. Evidence: `config/pipeline_config.yaml#retrieval_benchmark.reanchor`;
  `governance/golden_reanchor_candidates_20261011.reviewed.csv`; `governance/golden_reanchor_proposed_v5.yaml`.

- **Where.** `governance/canonical_relabel_review_20261014.csv` (`owner_action`, `owner_canonical`, `owner_comment`),
  `scripts/build_relabel_review_packet.py` (writes them BLANK and is the only file in the repo that names the
  column), `config/relabel_rulings.yaml` (the declared HOME of the words — its header says the OWNER writes it and
  its `packet:` field still names the 2026-10-13 surface), `scripts/apply_relabel_rulings.py` (reads the YAML).
- **The measurement (2026-10-14, read-only).** `owner_action` **72/72** (38 CONFIRM / 17 CORRECT / 14 LEAVE /
  3 ABSTAIN), `owner_canonical` **33**, `owner_comment` **2**, covering all **311** rows of the ESCALATE surface.
  `grep -rn owner_action` over `scripts/`, `pipeline/`, `config/`, `justfile`: the packet builder only (plus prose in
  `config/decisions.yaml`). Two column-level defects: **U022** (`higher education administration` -> stored
  `organizational theory`) is `CORRECT` with an EMPTY `owner_canonical`; and **17** rows carry an `owner_canonical`
  while the action is ABSTAIN (U047, U048) or LEAVE (U059-U072, where the cell restates the stored home) — coherent as
  intent, INERT as data under the declared vocabulary, and a later reader could take the cell for the ruling.
- **Why it matters.** T-117 is MUST and the register reads its gate as owed. The owner's word is on disk and unread:
  the shape BUG-782 retired for the collapse lane (an owner lane with no intake) and BUG-784 one lane over (a reader
  pointed at the wrong artifact). Three surfaces now carry the same act (the packet, the YAML, the plan render) and
  only ONE of them is read.
- **The fix owed.** `scripts/ingest_relabel_rulings.py`: (i) read the returned packet keyed by `unit_key` — NEVER by
