  (ii) refuse, listing them, any action outside `CONFIRM | CORRECT | ABSTAIN | LEAVE`, any `CORRECT` with no home, and
  any home that is not in the live taxonomy menu (a home that exists nowhere is a minted label, D-2898); (iii) write
  `config/relabel_rulings.yaml#unit_rulings` with `was:` recording the ordinal the owner saw, and `applied:` staying
  UNWRITTEN until the licensed store write happens; (iv) report the inert `owner_canonical` cells as ADVISORY, never
  as rulings; (v) then run the applier's own `--check`. Owner act still owed: ONE word — U022's home.
- **Status.** OPEN. Evidence: `governance/canonical_relabel_review_20261014.csv`;
  `governance/CANONICAL_RELABEL_REVIEW_20261014.md`; `config/relabel_rulings.yaml`; `governance/OWNER_LANE_BATCH_20261013.md`.

## BUG-786 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-14) - the ingest door counted a provenance-less word as an owner act: 84 rows read as RULED while \`ruling_source\` said \`none\`

- **Where.** \`pipeline/ingest_gate.py#collapse_debt\` (the T-129 limb of the door) + \`config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml\`
  (which declared WHICH column to read, but not what makes a word a WORD).
- **The measurement (2026-10-14, by running the door — not by reading it).**
  \`python3 scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py --check\` printed:
  \`collapse sheet work_identity_collapse_review_20261014.csv: 84 row(s) | ruled 84 | owed 0\`.
  The sheet's 84 words were **identical to the v1 machine screen** and their \`ruling_source\` was \`none\` on every row:
  they had been typed by hand into the DERIVED column (\`owner_ruling\`) — the column \`scripts/owner_marks.py --apply\`
  writes — and the reader asked nothing about their origin. The hole was MASKED: the same gate's ledger limb was owed
  59 pairs, so rc 2 and the reading looked honest while one of its two limbs would have opened on a typed cell.
- **Why it matters.** \`--apply\` is the ONLY writer that records where a word came from (\`row\` for a per-row
  override, \`signature:<tier>@<date>\` for a signature expansion). A reader that cannot tell a hand-typed cell from a
  signature releases the identity lane **without an owner act** — the BUG-782 defect one column over, and the reason
  the row-provenance requirement is not decoration.
- **The fix.** The provenance column and its \`none\` token are DECLARED
  (\`config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml#ledger.collapse_word_source_column\` -> \`config/owner_marks.yaml#homes.collapse_sheet.provenance_column\`,
  resolved through the same declared-pointer reader the ruling column uses — never sniffed by name);
  \`collapse_debt\` raises when the declared column is absent, counts a word whose provenance is blank or the
  \`none\` token as OWED, and returns \`unprovenanced\` + the column it required; \`standing()\` reports it in words
  ("a value in the DERIVED column is not an owner act"); the selftest's control
  \`a_word_with_no_provenance_is_owed_not_ruled\` (9/9) also asserts the SAME rows WITH provenance ARE ruled, so it
  cannot pass by refusing every word; and \`the_word_provenance_guard_is_load_bearing\` reds that control through its own
  marker at a mutation (the mutation gate is 48/48 again after its fixture gained the runner's own imports —
  \`pipeline/ingest_gate.py\`, \`pipeline/book_metadata.py\`, \`pipeline/io_guard.py\`, \`pipeline/stamp.py\`: without them
  three baselines were red and the gate blamed the mutations, the BUG-589 shape).
- **Status.** FIXED, verified: the door now prints \`ruled 0 | owed 84\` **with the provenance reason**, and the
  expansion path (\`--apply\`) is the only way a collapse word can end that debt. Evidence:
  \`pipeline/ingest_gate.py\`; \`config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml\`; \`scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py --selftest\`;
  \`config/rail_mutations.yaml#the_word_provenance_guard_is_load_bearing\`.

## BUG-787 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-14) — the T-101 WRITER read the GENERATOR's sheet, so a COMPLETED owner act could never be applied

FOUND BY RUNNING THE APPROVED APPLY (`§1` of the owner's act page: "approve implement"), not by reading. `--check`
returned rc 0 — "29 of 29 queries carry a verdict, 120 anchor names, 19 abstentions, every chosen anchor
owner-signed" — and `--apply`, the very next command, refused all 29 queries with "NO row marked 'anchor' … a guess is
not a label". Both readings were of the SAME reviewed sheet in principle and of DIFFERENT files in fact:
`return _apply_reviewed(args.csv, args.yaml_out, …)` at the apply branch, against
`return _check_reviewed(args.reviewed_csv, args.reviewed_draft)` at the check branch.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN BUG-784. A reader wired to the wrong file reports a FALSE DEBT (BUG-784: a completed act
read as owed). A WRITER wired to the wrong file can never land the act at all — the failure is not a wrong number, it
is a permanently unrealisable step, and the rail that would have caught it (`--selftest`) had no opinion about WHICH
file the writer reads. The fix therefore does not just correct the call site: it makes the wiring TESTABLE — one
helper (`reviewed_inputs`) that both modes call, one control that asserts the helper returns the DECLARED paths (and
that they differ from the generator's outputs), one mutation that reds that control through its own marker, and a
`print` of the two files the writer read, so a future reader of the log can see which sheet was used instead of
inferring it.

## BUG-785 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-14) — the T-117 packet had no reader

The owner's 72 words (`owner_action`, all 311 rows covered) lived in a column that NOTHING read: the applier read
`config/relabel_rulings.yaml`, a surface filled in an earlier ruling round and still pointing at the 2026-10-13
packet. The act was COMPLETE and INVISIBLE at the same time, which is the failure mode the whole owner-lane intake
(D-2898 / config/owner_marks.yaml) exists to retire — one lane over, in the same shape.

WHAT THE READER REFUSES, AND WHY EACH REFUSAL IS LOAD-BEARING:
  * an action outside the DECLARED vocabulary (`config/relabel_rulings.yaml#vocabulary`) — a word the owner never
    said cannot be ingested into the home that decides 311 rows;
  * a `CORRECT` with no home — an incomplete word is not a word (this is how U022 was caught, and the owner's word
    for it was re-taken as `ABSTAIN`);
  * a home that no `config/taxonomy.yaml` canonical (discipline or domain) declares — writing it would MINT a home
    (D-2898). All 16 real homes were verified to resolve; two carried trailing whitespace and are normalised on
    ingest, which is a data-quality catch, not a change of meaning;
  * the ordinal as a KEY — `unit_rulings` is keyed by `unit_key`; the ordinal is preserved in `was:` (BUG-751: the
    packet was renumbered once already, and an ordinal is a position, not an identity);
  * a destroyed receipt — the first run of the ingest DROPPED the `applied:` receipt of a ruling the packet restated,
    and the selftest control `an_applied_receipt_survives_a_re_ingest` caught it before any write. A re-worded ruling
    keeps its receipt and is NAMED in the block header instead of being silently re-dated.

TWO HAZARDS FOUND WHILE LANDING IT, both closed with controls and mutations:
  * a bare `yaml.safe_dump` appends a `...` document-end marker — splicing scalars with it turned the file into a
    parse bomb (the selftest caught it on the first run);
  * `scripts/owner_marks.py --apply` run BEFORE a signature would have BLANKED the owner's 84 hand-typed cells (the
    only machine-readable record of the owner's word): the derived column is rebuilt from the tiers and the tiers were
    unsigned. The write now REFUSES, by name, and points at the two acts that make it safe (sign the tier, or move
    the words to the owner's column).

## BUG-788 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-14) — the signer's controls copied the LIVE declaration, so a COMPLETED owner act turned a control red and masked every mutation in the file

**MEASURED 2026-10-14, the day the collapse act completed.** `scripts/owner_marks.py --selftest` reported
`FAIL a_signature_is_written_on_the_named_tier_and_nowhere_else` (13/13 green before the act), and
`scripts/check_rail_mutations.py` reported `mutation the_write_may_blank_a_hand_typed_owner_word: the oracle's
BASELINE is not green (rc=1) — so its red after one proves nothing`. One red control therefore disarmed the WHOLE
mutation gate for that file: 57 declared rules, none of them provable.

**The defect.** The control copied `config/owner_marks.yaml` from disk and then asserted the copy was otherwise
UNSIGNED. Two state dependencies followed from that: (a) with tiers A/B/C signed, `sign_tiers` correctly REFUSES
the re-sign (D-2676) so nothing was written; (b) the assertion `not any(v for k, v in got.items() if k != "A")`
is false over a signed file. The control had been passing only while the act it guards was still OWED, i.e. the
OWNER was the mutator of the rail's input — the BUG-556 shape ("a rail whose input the ladder itself mutates"),
one layer up.

**The fix.** `unsigned_fixture(text)`: a PURE helper that returns the same declaration with every signature
removed; the controls now write that pre-image and hand the signer a policy reset to match. The control also
asserts the RE-SIGN REFUSAL explicitly, which it never did. A 14th control
(`a_control_fixture_is_unsigned_whatever_the_live_declaration_says`) makes the independence itself a known
answer, so a mutation (`a_control_fixture_may_carry_the_live_act_into_the_signer`) can be SEEN to red through it
— a state-dependent control could never be proven that way.

**After.** owner-marks 14/14; mutation gate 57/57 declared rules seen to red; the ladder's owner-marks line reads
rc 0. **Lesson (the reusable half):** a control whose input is the live artifact DEAD in the state where the
thing it guards has SUCCEEDED. Declare the pre-image, not the world.


## BUG-790 (LOW — OPEN) — the ingest door's refusal names the WRONG TASK

**MEASURED 2026-10-14** (`scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py --gate`, rc 2 on this machine): the refusal
prints `evidence contradicts (task T-129/T-131)`. The door's task is **T-130**; **T-131 is THE MODEL-SWAP BENCH** —
so a reader who follows the pointer lands on a task about re-pointing model slots instead of on the door. A
hardcoded task pointer is the C12 defect class inside a REFUSAL, and a refusal is the one message a reader acts
on. **Fix:** name the task from a declared home (the register) rather than a literal in the message, or correct
the literal to T-130. Nothing else reads this string.

## BUG-789 (MED — OPEN) — the local model server's app config carries a Hugging Face token in plaintext

**MEASURED 2026-10-14** while mapping the agent harness, read-only: `~/Library/Application Support/oMLX/config.json`
holds `hf_token` verbatim, the file is mode 644 (world-readable) and 215 bytes. **Why it matters:** C3 declares
all data and compute sovereign and local; a plaintext credential in an app config is a live secret with no
rotation, no environment indirection and no file protection, and it is copied by every backup and sync that
sweeps the user profile. **Fix (declared, not yet applied):** move the value to `HF_TOKEN` in the environment (or
the keychain), REVOKE and reissue the exposed value, and add a rail that refuses a secret-shaped literal in an
app config. The value is never restated in a governance file (a bug record is not a credential store).

## BUG-791 (HIGH — FIXED 2026-10-14) — one apostrophe in one task title made the BOOT-LOADED face unparseable, and every writer reported success

**MEASURED 2026-10-14, minutes after the mint that caused it.** `just health` reported FOUR rails failing at
once — YAML parse, referenced files exist, vector dimensions, version stamps — all with the same unhandled
error: `while parsing a block mapping in agent/session_seed.yaml, line 6, column 3 ... expected <block end>,
but found '<scalar>' ... line 6, column 473`.

**The defect.** `scripts/gov_sync.py` splices the derived boot status into the face with
`f"{key}: '{val}'"` — a single-quoted YAML scalar built by INTERPOLATION, with no escaping. T-132's title
contains `model's`; the apostrophe CLOSED the scalar at column 473 and the rest of the line became stray
scalar content. Every writer printed `wrote agent/session_seed.yaml` and `--check` reported the four faces
equal — because the check BYTE-COMPARES the block it renders, and the break was in a DERIVED SCALAR beside it.

**Why it is HIGH and not cosmetic.** `agent/session_seed.yaml` is the ONE face loaded at BOOT. A boot face that
does not parse is a session that starts blind, and the break rode in on data (a task title) rather than on code:
any future title with an apostrophe in a possessive would have done the same.

**The fix.** (1) `_yaml_quote`: the YAML rule itself (single-quote, DOUBLE any inner quote), refusing a
multi-line value outright. (2) A READ-BACK GUARD in `apply()`: a YAML face is parsed before it is written, and a
write that would leave it unloadable is REFUSED — this is the guard that would have stopped the break before it
reached the ladder. (3) A known answer naming the rule, and a mutation proving the quoting is load-bearing.
**After:** 21/21 known answers; the face parses; the four rails are green.

**Lesson (the reusable half).** A writer's OWN check is not a read-back: this writer verified the block it
rendered and never the DOCUMENT it wrote. The ingest learned this as "read back what you spliced"; the faces had
no such rule until a possessive apostrophe taught it.

## BUG-792 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-14) — the local server reuses no prefix, so every agent turn pre-pays its whole prompt

**MEASURED 2026-10-14**, read-only, on this machine. Twelve calls with **byte-identical prefixes** (4,466 / 4,468 /
5,358 tokens) against a resident model, in three arms: a large fixed SYSTEM block, a large fixed USER block, and
the CONTROL whose SYSTEM block carries a per-call nonce. **Every single call reported
`prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens = 0`**, and each paid the full prefill again (~9.8 s for ~4.5 k tokens at
~455 tok/s). Two-call speedup: **1.01x**, then **1.04x** through the probe's own `--prefill-ab` against the
contract's declared bar of **5x**. The server's own load figures name the mechanism: the one non-zero reading in
the entire sweep was a **4096-token block boundary (cached_tokens = 4096) directly after a model load**, i.e. a
4096-token BLOCK cache - the cache that `~/.omlx/settings.json` declares **off** (`cache.enabled = false`), which
it must, because `assert_omlx_no_cache()` is a fail-closed rail that ABORTS inference when that cache (or its
`gdn_ssd_split` / `hot_cache_only` companions) is enabled (D2460: `store_cache_main_dispatch` 817 ms -> 3.08 s,
decode collapsing ~50 -> ~4-7 tok/s).

**Why it matters.** Prefill, not decode, is the cost of an agent loop, and with no reuse the cost of a turn is the
WHOLE prompt. It also re-reads the harness's own ledger: the 37.4% cache ratio that `gemma-4-E4B` shows over 289
calls is NOT reproducible as cross-request prefix reuse today, so that number is historical, not a live capability.

**What this bug does NOT claim.** It does not claim the cache cannot work, and it does not recommend flipping the
flag. D2460 measured a regression, and a regression that has a known shape is re-tested ONE VARIABLE AT A TIME
under a declared protocol with a DECODE-RATE ORACLE - never re-enabled on a hunch. Until that re-test lands, the
declared state (contract: `cache_accounting.proof.status`) is **DISPROVEN**, and every optimisation must be
cache-free: fewer requests per unit of work, shorter prompts, and a model whose measured throughput can pay the bill.

## BUG-793 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-14) — Qwen3.8-27B prefills at 39 tok/s, four times worse than its parameter ratio predicts

**MEASURED 2026-10-14** (read-only, one call, the server's own counters): a 32,026-token prompt returned
`prompt_tokens_per_second = 39.02`, `time_to_first_token = 715.7 s`, `generation_tokens_per_second = 1.68`,
`model_load_duration = 26.5 s`. On the same machine, same settings tier, `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8` prefills at
**210 tok/s** at a 50,082-token prompt and at 240-274 tok/s at 30 k and 3.6 k. A 27B against a 20B predicts roughly
155 tok/s; the measurement is **four times slower**.

**Why it matters.** It is the difference between a candidate and a trap. The model carries the machine's largest
declared window (262,144) and is therefore the obvious "long-session" answer - while in fact one turn at the
harness's own compaction trigger (26,214 tokens) would cost **672 seconds**, and a turn at its declared window
**~1.9 hours**. It also inflates a page of routing arithmetic in the contract, so it must be diagnosed rather than
inherited: candidates are the `memory_guard_tier: aggressive` path, KV memory pressure at a large prompt, and
`specprefill_enabled: False` on this model where comparable models have it on.

**AMENDED 2026-10-15 (re-measured, same engine, two-point slope).** The DECODE figure in this entry (1.7
tok/s) was a cold/pressured state, not the model: re-measured 2026-10-15 it decodes **7.5 tok/s**, a 4.4x
correction. It remains the WORST of the eight models served here by 6.6x (the A3B MoE decodes 49.5, the 4B
dense 36.3, the 12B 13.4). Its PREFILL figure (39 tok/s, 2026-10-14) is not contradicted by this run and
stands as the reason it cannot hold a loop: 26214 / 39 = 672 s per turn, and its declared 262144 window is
~1.9 hours of prefill. The entry's remedy is unchanged and still un-diagnosed: `specprefill_enabled: False`
on this model in `~/.omlx/model_settings.json` while comparable models have it on, plus
`memory_guard_tier: aggressive`.

## BUG-794 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-14, same session) — an ESTIMATE of a prompt size published a truncation that did not exist

**MEASURED, then RETRACTED, 2026-10-14.** The first version of this sweep's evidence reported that a prompt was
TRUNCATED: "sent ~35,200 tokens, the server echoed 32,026". The server echoed the truth; the *sent* number was
computed with a chars-per-token rule of **4.0** while the filler ("the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. ",
45 characters) is exactly **10 tokens** in that tokenizer - i.e. **4.5 characters per token**. The prompt was
32,026 tokens and was never truncated. Refuted by sending a genuinely larger one: **50,082 prompt tokens accepted
whole** by a model declared at 131,072.

**Why it is filed rather than quietly corrected.** A retraction nobody records is an error the next reader
inherits, and this one had already been written into a rail's evidence and a contract's baseline. The fix is
structural: `measured_prompt_tokens()` refuses a row marked `estimated`, the contract declares the MEASURED
`chars_per_token_measured: 4.5` beside the filler, and a known-answer control fails if the refusal is removed
(`an_estimated_prompt_size_is_refused_as_a_measurement`, with its own mutation).

## BUG-795 (LOW — OPEN 2026-10-14) — one ledger row carries a NULL model and 156,098,139 input tokens

**MEASURED 2026-10-14** while re-reading the cache ledger for this contract: `usage_ledger` row id 33
(session `20260826_1`, timestamp 1787913235) carries `model = NULL`, `input_tokens = 156,098,139`,
`output_tokens = 1,249,089`, `cache_read_tokens = 141,896,704`, `is_compaction = 0` - it is the single largest
row in the table and it belongs to no model. Any census that groups by model silently drops it (5.5% of the
ledger's 2.86 B input tokens and the largest single cache-read figure in the file).

**Why it matters.** A per-model ratio is the evidence this contract publishes, and a row this large that belongs
to no model is exactly the shape D-2957 forbids from being folded into someone else's denominator. Nothing here
claims the row is wrong - only that it is UNATTRIBUTED, and that an unattributed row of that size must be named
wherever a total is published (the probe already prints it as `inconclusive`, never as a zero, which is how it
was found).

## BUG-796 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-14) — a decision written outside the receipting writer leaves the attribution control red

**MEASURED 2026-10-14**, and measured TWICE: once in the live tree, then once in a clean worktree at
`7ccb4cd` to establish whether this session caused it (it did not).

`python3 scripts/lib/handoff.py --selftest` reports 3 of 4 attribution controls firing and
`1 of 4 attribution control(s) did not fire`:
`a governed write that IS the current bytes is attributed, and the join is by CONTENT`. The control is
narrow and correct: it asks for a MUTATION-journal record whose `post_sha16` IS the digest of
`config/decisions.yaml` now, with a named writer. The newest such record carries
`post_sha16 = e93a3121639d77a3` (`writer: scripts/recompute_decision_summary.py`,
`stamp: 20261014T152011Z`), while the live file is `45fd6ee364bd868b` — and in the PRE-session worktree
the same control reds with the live digest `ed47950ec8a932f0`. So the pairing has been broken since
before this session, by the same class of act each time: **the registry is written by a path that does not
record the bytes it produced.**

**Why it is not cosmetic.** The handoff journal is the machinery that answers "WHO moved this governed
region", and D-2972 makes that question an act rather than a narrative. A registry whose receipts lag its
bytes means the attribution sentence for the ONE artifact every decision lands in is either stale or
silent — the BUG-780/BUG-781 family (a guarantee with no enforcement point) one artifact over.

**What was NOT done.** No hand re-record: `--rebaseline` was run and REFUSED, in its own words —
"the receipted bytes are still an APPENDED of the live file, so nothing was rewritten and there is nothing
to re-baseline ... a baseline moved where nobody measured a break is a quiet re-record (D-2642)". That
refusal is correct and it is why the red stands. The module's declared maintenance act was run instead
(`--backfill`, which took receipts for the 6 declared paths, labelled `origin=backfill` — "these receipts
claim what the bytes ARE now"), which is honest hygiene and NOT a fix for this control.

**FIX (declared, not applied).** Have the registry's writers record the post-image they produce — the mint
already holds the bytes it just wrote, so this is one call at the write site — or let the control accept a
VERIFIED ancestor and say which one, instead of demanding an exact post-image that the append-only mutual
writes can never leave behind.

## BUG-797 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-15) — the `llmfit` preflight cell is a control that CANNOT FAIL

MEASURED 2026-10-15. `just preflight` (and therefore `just health`) declares a hardware-model-fit cell:
`@llmfit 2>&1 | head -5 || echo "    ⚠️  llmfit unavailable"`. `llmfit` is NOT on the PATH the recipe runs
with, so the line prints `llmfit unavailable` and the recipe stays GREEN — the R-03 control added to
`just preflight` (governance/NOT-YET-EVALUATED-RESEARCH.md) has been a no-op since the day it landed.

The tool is installed, twice, under two homes: a cargo binary at `~/.cargo/bin/llmfit` (reports
`llmfit 0.9.38`) and a pip package reporting `1.1.6`, while the research docs cite "llmfit 1.1.6"
(governance/MARKET-RESEARCH-QWEN3.8-HARNESS-2026-08-14.md). Two version homes and one unavailable command:
a control whose failure mode is indistinguishable from its success mode (BUG-787's shape, one cell over).

**Run for real 2026-10-15** (`~/.cargo/bin/llmfit --json system`): Apple M1 Max, 64 GB unified,
400 GB/s memory bandwidth, 10 cores, Metal. `--json recommend` and `--json fit` DO work, so the fix is a
declared invocation (absolute path or a PATH declaration), not a new dependency.
**FIX (declared, not applied):** resolve `llmfit` by absolute path or declare the PATH in the recipe, and
make an UNAVAILABLE tool a red or a NA — never a silent pass.

**AMENDED 2026-10-15 (MEASURED — the recorded premise was false).** This entry states that `llmfit` "is NOT on
the PATH the recipe runs with". That is no longer true, re-measured three ways today: the login shell resolves
`/opt/homebrew/bin/llmfit`; `sh -c 'command -v llmfit'` resolves the same; and the recipe's own shell runs it
(`llmfit 0.9.38`) — a Homebrew install since the entry was written. **The defect that REMAINS is worse than the
one recorded, and it is not a PATH problem:** the cell is `@llmfit 2>&1 | head -5 || echo unavailable`, and the
PIPE hands the recipe `head`'s exit status, which is 0 always — a control that cannot fail **by construction**,
whatever llmfit prints. Two further measured facts belong here: (1) llmfit's DB LAGS the market — today it had
NO record for `embeddinggemma-2` or `Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill`, and its `fit --sort tps` ranks random test models
first, so "not found" is DB-lag and never absence; (2) its `recommend` top row is a 2025 reasoning model
(DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B) — a recommendation list is not a measurement. So the fix is not "resolve the path"
(done); it is a cell that ASSERTS (`--version` against a declared expectation) and declares its DB horizon.


## BUG-798 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-15, same session) — my own rename census scanned NAMES and read a FALSE GREEN

MEASURED 2026-10-15, written in the same act that built the instrument (T-130's renamer). The first census
of the approved corpus-name write reported `apply_ready: True` for all 37 rows: it counted SIBLING FILES,
STAGE-OUTPUT FILENAMES and STORE ROWS, and every one of them read 0. A targeted grep then found the stems
3,171 times INSIDE 13 derived artifacts that no filename scan could see —
`checkpoints/stage4_merge|stage5_verify/diagnostic_*/checkpoint.jsonl`, `stage0_convert/*/checkpoint.jsonl`
(`source_file`/`source_path`/`output_path`), `parquet/fbs_export_20260902_final.jsonl` (2,419 alone) — so
an `--apply` would have left ~2,952 dangling references behind it: a cascade, signed off by an instrument
that reported clean (the BUG-787 shape: a control reading the wrong surface stays green).

**FIXED in the same act:** the census now scans the CONTENT of the declared artifact dirs
(`name_normalisation.surfaces.artifact_dir_attrs: [CHECKPOINT_DIR, PARQUET_DIR]`,
`artifact_suffixes: ['.jsonl','.json']`), and a 10th known-answer control asserts the boundary both ways

## BUG-799 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — two cache records duplicate ONE work under two raw names, and the door looks names up by BYTES

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (remedy T-130 option (B) / D-3040, LANDED). MEASURED 2026-10-16, this session.

MEASURED 2026-10-15 on the 962-record metadata cache: exactly 2 canonical keys hold more than one distinct
raw `source_book` — `Identity Designed The Definitive Guide to Visual Branding by David Airey` and
`Pricing Creativity A Guide to Profit Beyond the Billable Hour`, each appearing twice with a whitespace
difference. Both pairs carry the SAME author and title, so both compute the SAME `source_id`
(`bdb3a25d5707fafc`, `a4d8aacdbca22099`): the collapse is IDENTITY-PRESERVING and merges no distinct work
(910 distinct source_ids survive; 962 -> 960 records).

**WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN IT LOOKED.** The door declared 37 corpus names DEFECTIVE (whitespace) while depending
on those same defective BYTES to find their identity: a declaration the reader cannot RESOLVE (D-3034). Accepting
the names without fixing the reader would have frozen a contradiction in place — and, as the control below
measured, the obvious way to fix it (routing the DELTA rule through the canonical lookup) is WORSE than the defect.

The defect is in the READER, not the corpus: `ingest_gate.corpus_census.record_for()` resolves a record by
`by_name.get(path.name.strip())` and `by_path` — exact bytes, minus the ends — while the door's own
comparison key `_key()` already collapses whitespace. So the door declares 37 corpus names DEFECTIVE and
then depends on their exact bytes to find their identity. The durable fix is one canonical fallback in that
lookup, and it needs a control of its own before it lands (BUG-492). Deliberately NOT applied this session.

**FIXED 2026-10-16 (T-130 option B / D-3040).** MEASURED, not reasoned: the lookup is now DECLARED and ORDERED
(config#identity.record_lookup: exact_name -> exact_path -> canonical_name), the first lookup that answers wins, and
every decision records WHICH one did (`record_resolution`), so a receipt carries the EVIDENCE of how an identity was
found rather than the assumption. The canonical key IS the door's own `_key()`, so the door now resolves the identity
it was already comparing against. INERT ON THE LIVE CORPUS, which is the point: all 940 corpus files resolve by
exact_name, the delta census is 0 before and after, the health line's rc is unchanged (2 = the 459 ingest-site
markers, now T-173), and the accepted debt is printed LOUDLY with its declaring decision. Two controls hold it in
both directions (the fallback resolves and NAMES itself; an exact match still WINS). The second half of the defect —
two cache records duplicating one work — is IDENTITY-PRESERVING and merges no distinct work (910 distinct ids
survive 962 records), so it stays a recorded reading rather than a repair; the rename act is T-172.

## BUG-800 (LOW — OPEN 2026-10-15) — the approved corpus-name rename is a CASCADE until it rides a re-ingest

MEASURED 2026-10-15: the 37 defective corpus stems are referenced 2,952 times INSIDE 13 derived artifacts
(the parquet export, the stage0/2/4/5 checkpoints and their `input_fbs`) — RUN RECEIPTS that record what a
past run was given. The T-130 write approved 2026-10-15 renames the 37 files and rewrites the metadata
cache (which it CAN do) but cannot rewrite a receipt without re-recording history (D-2642), so the plan
REFUSES: `apply_ready: False`, 37/37 rows refused, each naming its artifact. The plan is written and
waiting: `governance/normalise_corpus_names_plan_20261015.json`. The act becomes non-cascading when the
artifacts are regenerated anyway, i.e. BUNDLED WITH A RE-INGEST — not against a live corpus.

**ACCEPTED AND SCHEDULED 2026-10-16 (T-130 option (B), owner word; D-3040).** The debt is now DECLARED
(config#identity.accepted_debt, owner word quoted) and the act RIDES THE NEXT RE-INGEST as a SCHEDULE with a NAMED
owner: T-172. The state of this bug is therefore unchanged and honest — the defect is real and unfixed — but it can no
longer be mistaken for an unowned silence: the door prints the debt, the register owns its trigger, and the day the
artifacts are regenerated the same plan becomes apply-ready. The identity layer is already prepared for that day:
with `identity.record_lookup` a renamed file whose cache record still carries the old name is DEFERRED
(`already_ingested_by_canonical_name`, skipped in place) instead of being re-ingested.

## BUG-801 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-15, same session) — a prefill reading was published without the prompt SIZE it was taken at

MEASURED 2026-10-15. The new decode probe derives prefill from the same two-call slope, and on a ~36-token
prompt it read 331 tok/s for `gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit` — against the 2026-10-14 reading of 455 tok/s taken
on 4,468 tokens. The two numbers are not comparable: a tiny prompt is dominated by fixed kernel and
scheduling overhead (the same run's first 4-token call read 0.3 tok/s on a model that then read 13.2). A
prefill figure is a function of prompt size, so a reading without its size is INCOMPARABLE, not merely
imprecise — and the routing bill is a prefill bill.

**FIXED in the same act:** the size dependency is DECLARED in
`config/bench_preflight.yaml#prefill_bill.size_scale_guard` (`min_prompt_tokens_for_a_comparable_reading:
2000`, `on_below_floor: report_incomparable`) and in `config/agent_context.yaml#measured_decode_20261015`.
No routing row was changed on the strength of this run: the candidates remain REFUSED a route until a
size-declared prefill reading exists (fail-closed).

## BUG-802 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-15) — the $0 local engine does not survive a reboot, and nothing starts it

MEASURED 2026-10-15. At session start `curl http://localhost:11435/health` returned `000` and
`/v1/models` returned `000`: the engine was DOWN. Its own log shows a CLEAN shutdown at `2026-10-15
02:11:21` ("Engine pool shutdown complete", every model unloaded, caches cleared) — so this was not a crash,
it was a restart in which nothing brought the server back. `~/.omlx/bin/omlx start` brought it up in ~25 s
and the decode probe then ran 4 models through it.

The agent's $0 marginal cost (C1), its sovereignty (C3) and "resilient by design" (C23) all rest on this
process. The launchd facts: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.maxwell.omlx-api-key.plist` only SETS AN ENV VAR;
`com.maxwellos.watchdog.plist.DISABLED` and `com.maxwell.memoryguardian.plist.DISABLED` are both DISABLED.
So after any reboot the whole local-capability layer is absent until a human types a command — including
every delegate lane, the S4 classifier and the pipeline's generator.
**FIX (declared, not applied):** a KeepAlive launchd job for the managed server (or a declared
`omlx_watchdog.py --daemon` supervisor), plus a rail that reports the engine DOWN as a red rather than as a
per-request failure discovered later.
## BUG-803 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-15) — a prefill reading without the POOL STATE it was taken at is not comparable either

MEASURED 2026-10-15, in the SAME MINUTE, same model, same machine. A 12-token prompt was answered with
`time_to_first_token: 15.49 s` while a 30,900-token prompt prefilled at 479 tok/s. The server's own log says
why: `Reserved prefill capacity for 30900 tokens`, then `needs prefill headroom before throttling
(reason=adaptive_prefill_throttle, current=46.19GB, target=51.78GB)`, then `Evicting idle model
'gemma-4-12B-it-qat-OptiQ-4bit' for prefill headroom`. Eight models were resident (46.88 GB against a 55 GB
guard ceiling), because oMLX pins everyday models in memory.

Same shape as BUG-801, one variable over. BUG-801 fixed "a prefill reading must carry the prompt SIZE it was
taken at"; this one fixes the second missing covariate: a prefill (or TTFT) reading must also carry the POOL
RESIDENCY, because the adaptive prefill throttle and the prefill-LRU eviction make the same prompt cost very
different time depending on what else is loaded. Remedy declared in the cell:
`config/bench_preflight.yaml#prefill_bill.required_fields` now carries `pool_residency`.

Consequence (operational, cheap, not a model change): a bill taken against a crowded pool is PESSIMISTIC, so
evicting idle models before a class turn is a legitimate lever on the prefill bill — and it is now a declared
input rather than an unrecorded variable.

## BUG-805 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-15) — decode is a function of CONTEXT LENGTH: the decode axis was measured on tiny prompts

MEASURED 2026-10-15 by the T-131 bench RUN (two-point slope on ONE 30,900-token prompt):
`gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit` decodes **9.88 tok/s at 30,900 tokens of context** against **36.3 tok/s** measured
the previous day on a ~36-token prompt (config/agent_context.yaml#measured_decode_20261015) — a 3.7x collapse
on the same model, from context alone.

**This CORRECTS the previous session's headline, and the correction is the point.** "Decode is not the binding
constraint" stays true AT CLASS SIZE (65 s of prefill against ~8 s of decode for a 96-token answer), but the
sentence implied decode was a model CONSTANT. It is not: decode reads the KV cache per step, so it degrades
with context. Every decode number in that table is scoped to SMALL PROMPTS, and any LATENCY budget at class
size must be re-measured at that size.

Remedy (declared, same cell): `decode_context_size` is now a required field of the prefill bill. A decode
figure without its context length is as incomparable as a prefill figure without its prompt size.

## BUG-806 (LOW - OPEN 2026-10-15) - my bench wrote its receipt only on the SUCCESS path, so the two REFUSALS were not persisted

MEASURED 2026-10-15, my own instrument (the same class as BUG-798, which was also mine).
temp/prefill_bench_20261015.py writes temp/prefill_bench_20261015.json once per MODEL - but only on the SUCCESS
path. Every early continue (a failed warm-up, a failed measured call, a C2/C3 disagreement, a missing
prompt_tokens) returns BEFORE the write. The run's two most informative rows therefore exist only in the human
log: gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8 REFUSED (the two calls disagree) and gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit NA (the server did
not echo prompt_tokens). A refusal is a FINDING; an instrument that persists only its successes is the BUG-798
shape one layer down - the reading that matters is the one that goes missing.

It also leaves a real question UNANSWERED and unauditable for the A4B: whether the engine omits
usage.prompt_tokens for that model (an engine/instrument gap that would make the prefill bill uncomputable for a
model that may be perfectly routable), or whether the call itself failed (eviction/context). With the receipt
missing, both readings are unavailable and any conclusion drawn now would be a guess - so none is drawn.

FIX (declared, not applied): write the receipt on EVERY path, refusals included, with the raw call records (both
calls' dt, pt, ct, cached_tokens and err).

**BUG-806 ADDENDUM (MEASURED 2026-10-15, same session).** The A4B reading's likely cause was FOUND after the fact and
cannot be proved from the receipt (which is the bug): /v1/models lists 8 served models and
gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit is not among them - it sits in ~/.omlx/_unloaded/ - so the request almost certainly
returned an ERROR OBJECT, and "the server did not echo prompt_tokens" is my instrument's label for it, not the
server's own explanation. The lesson generalises: an NA verdict must quote the RAW response body, or a refusal of
mine is indistinguishable from a refusal of the engine's.

## BUG-807 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a single-instant store census reported 85 GB as reclaimable mass, and the first draft then narrated a cause it never observed

**MEASURED.** A `du` of the engine's own store read **85 GB** of content-addressed `.safetensors`
(16 shard directories, ~300 files each, dated Oct 6-10). Twenty minutes later the same store read
**0 B** with a different structure (`vision_features`, `_gdn_sidecars`). Disk free moved 134 Gi ->
217 Gi. The first draft of `pipeline/model_store_census.py` wrote the causal claim **"the engine
released it"** into its own docstring. That was **FALSE**: the owner cleaned the cache by hand
(owner, 2026-10-15 14:54). The instrument invented a cause.

**WHY IT MATTERS.** This is the third instance of one class in one day: BUG-803 (a prefill reading
without its pool residency), BUG-805 (a decode figure without its context length), BUG-807 (a byte
count without the time it was taken at). In each case the READING looked authoritative and the
MISSING COVARIATE decided the conclusion.

**REMEDY (applied).** `measure_twice()` measures every store twice in one run and flags `transient`
when it moves by more than 5%; a transient store may never be offered as an owner decision; and the
census now states only what it observed. **No cause is narrated.**

| `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit` | `mlx-community/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit` | ABSENT |
| `gemma-4-E2B-it-MLX-4bit` | `lmstudio-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-MLX-4bit` | ABSENT |
| `Phi-4-mini-instruct-8bit` | `mlx-community/Phi-4-mini-instruct-8bit` | present (and served from `models_stashed`) |

**WHY IT MATTERS.** `du -sh` reported **0 B** for every one of these entries, which BUG-804 already
explained as "a symlink into the hub". The 0 B did not mean *parked*; for five of them it meant
**gone**. An instruction landed yesterday read "move `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit` out of
`_unloaded/` - it requires NO download". **It requires a fresh download of ~14-16 GB.** The addendum
to BUG-806 said the model "sits in `_unloaded/`": the *symlink* sits there, the model does not.

**ALSO EXPLAINS THE BENCH.** Both NA rows of the T-131 RUN (`gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-OptiQ-4bit`,
`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit`) were NA because **the model could not load** - it is not on disk. The earlier
hypothesis ("the server returned an error object") was an inference about the *server*; the cause was
the *store*. Two rows that looked like a server defect were a store fact.

**REMEDY (applied).** `broken_entries()` tests each engine entry with `Path.exists()` and reports
`BROKEN entries` in the census, in the JSON receipt and on stdout. The general rule is D-3004.

## BUG-809 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - delegated research was not durable: six of seven delegate runs were cancelled mid-flight and their findings were lost

**MEASURED.** Seven research delegates were launched; **six were cancelled** ("cancelled before it
finished and will not run again") and one reported `failed: max turns reached` after delivering its
report. The cancels arrived attached to the owner's next message: **a new user message interrupts the
turn and the harness cancels every in-flight child of that session.** The six cancelled runs had done
real work (web fetches, API reads); because their deliverable was their **return value**, that work
evaporated. **No file was written and no task was implemented for two consecutive attempts.**

**WHY IT MATTERS.** The standing rule says to delegate to save tokens and to parallelise. That advice
is only safe if a delegate's output survives interruption. It did not.

**REMEDY (rule, applied from now on).** (1) A research delegate's FIRST action is to create its
report file and **append** findings as it goes, so a cancel leaves a partial receipt instead of
nothing. (2) Its chat answer is a <= 15-line summary naming the file. (3) A delegate is never the only
copy of a fact that matters: the load-bearing numbers are re-measured by the parent before landing.
(4) Work that must be implemented is never sequenced *behind* a delegate.

## BUG-810 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a YAML insert that re-parents a mapping passes every parse check and is caught only by the consumer

**MEASURED, in this session's own landing.** A `binding:` block was inserted immediately after the
parent key `knobs:` in `config/agent_context.yaml`, at the SAME indent as `knobs`. In YAML a blank or
comment line does not dedent, so the two children that followed at the child indent
(`per_turn_budget_s`, `trigger`) were **re-parented under `binding`** and `knobs` became **null**.

`yaml.safe_load` returned successfully - the document was perfectly valid YAML. The landing script's
guard therefore reported `yaml ok`, and the corruption was found only because a later reader asked
for `ratified.knobs.trigger` and got `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. Any consumer
of that home would have crashed: `pipeline/harness_env.py`, `pipeline/harness_contract.py`, the bench
preflight's budget source, and the S/O binding table.

**WHY IT MATTERS.** Every insert into a YAML home in this repo is validated by *parsing*. Parsing
proves syntax, never **shape**. A re-parented mapping is syntactically flawless and semantically
catastrophic, and it fails at the READER, at a later time, in a different process.

**REMEDY (rule, applied).** (1) An insert that adds a sibling mapping goes **after the parent's last
child**, never between a parent key and its children. (2) After any structural insert into a YAML
home, the landing runs that home's **CONSUMER** controls in the same act - for this home
`python3 pipeline/harness_env.py --selftest` and `python3 pipeline/harness_contract.py --check` -
because only a consumer can see a re-parenting. (3) A shape assertion (the expected key path must
resolve) is stronger than an equality check on bytes and is what the landing must assert.

## BUG-811 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a new instrument told three lies before its own selftest was written
The durable research runner (pipeline/research_run.py) and the loadability probe
(pipeline/model_loadability_probe.py) were both written and run in the same hour. Between them they
produced six wrong answers, every one of them caught by a CONTROL rather than by reading the output:
| # | lie | how it was caught | fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | a dead detached child read as ALIVE forever, so no workstream was ever noticed to be over | selftest: the FAILED path never fired | a ZOMBIE answers kill(pid,0); pid_alive now asks ps for the process state and rejects Z |
| 2 | a TIMEOUT was recorded as FAILED | selftest: state=FAILED with a TERMINAL: TIMEOUT line | the state word is READ from the marker, not inferred from the substring "DONE" |
| 3 | a previous run's marker was read as this run's end | selftest: state came from a stale report | the selftest starts from an empty run, and that is itself a control |
| 4 | a workstream's relative path wrote into the REPOSITORY ROOT | selftest: the report stayed 78 bytes | the runner injects WS_REPORT / WS_DIR / RUN_DIR |
| 5 | eight repos were reported EMPTY_REPO ("no weight files at all") | the verdicts were identical for every repo INCLUDING three known to hold weights | the fetch layer swallowed every exception into {}; it is now curl with the HTTP STATUS KEPT, and an unreadable hub is FETCH_FAILED (fatal), never a model verdict |
| 6 | the prior-test census called "dl=57485 near the model name" a MEASUREMENT and stamped ALREADY TESTED on five candidates that were only ever looked up | the answer contradicted every other artefact | the READING pattern now requires a UNIT-bearing rate/duration or a bench key; a download count is neither |
GATE: `python3 pipeline/research_run.py --selftest` -> 11/11. The class of error worth remembering: a
new instrument's FIRST output is not evidence about the world, it is evidence about the instrument.

## BUG-812 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a comment inserted into a plist silently broke the XML, and launchd reported only "Input/output error"
The BUG-802 remedy was made idempotent by replacing the job's ProgramArguments with the new guard
(pipeline/omlx_engine_guard.sh) and by rewriting the template's header comment. The comment edit left
the ORIGINAL continuation lines after the new closing "-->" , so the file carried stray text before
<plist>. `launchctl bootstrap gui/501 <plist>` answered "Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error -
Try re-running the command as root for richer errors", which names neither the file nor the line.
`plutil -lint` found it immediately: "Unexpected character T at line 6".
FIX: the plist was rewritten whole; the install path is unchanged. GATE: lint a rendered plist BEFORE
bootstrapping it (a parser surface is not a place to edit comments).

## BUG-813 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - the cache was enabled before its baseline was taken
Approved act 3 changed cache.enabled false -> true and gave the SSD tier a distinct directory. The
evidence produced afterwards is a PAIR on an identical 209-token prompt on gemma-4-E4B: 10.07s cold,
1.44s on the identical second call. That shows a warm-prefix speed-up is now happening; it does NOT
show that the change caused it, because no pre-change pair was measured (the first attempt at one
printed nothing at all - a script whose function was defined and never called, which is its own small
lesson). The engine's own counter disagrees with the wall clock: total_cached_tokens still reads 0.
FIX: T-137. The rollback switch (`pipeline/omlx_cache_enable.sh --rollback`) IS the A/B instrument:
measure the pair with the cache off, apply, measure the pair again, and only then claim a cause.

## BUG-814 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a hub snapshot can be DECLARED by name while nothing resolves into it
The store census classifies a hub repo as DECLARED when its NAME appears in live config/pipeline/script
text. `~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--lmstudio-community--Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` measures 4.0 GB while
the model the engine actually serves is a REAL 15.7 GB directory at `~/.omlx/models/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit`
(not a symlink into the hub). So the hub copy is a leftover partial of the same repo, it is classified
DECLARED because the name is mentioned, and nothing resolves into it. A truncated snapshot that a name
resolves TO is a hazard - it is BUG-808's cousin, one step earlier in the sequence. The byte-owner test
must be RESOLUTION, not mention: what matters is whether a live object resolves into the bytes.
Also observed: `_unloaded` carries SEVEN broken symlinks, one of them new since the last census
(`gemma-4-12B-it-4bit`) - the parked directory keeps accreting names that are not models.

## BUG-815 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-15) - `goose run` was not bound to the local engine, so a headless agent run went elsewhere
Measured: `goose run -t 'Reply with exactly: PONG'` answered PONG in ~28s while the local engine's
`total_requests` stood still at 52. `~/.config/goose/config.yaml` DECLARES `maxwell_omlx` (model
Qwen3-Coder-30B) - and also enables `custom_deepseek` and `nvidia`. A declared provider is not a BOUND
one, and no GOOSE_PROVIDER/GOOSE_MODEL was in the environment. This is C1/C3 in the one place they are
easiest to lose: an unattended run that nobody watches.
FIX (measured working): `GOOSE_PROVIDER` and `GOOSE_MODEL` are now part of the harness context contract
(config/agent_context.yaml#ratified.knobs.trigger) and are bound by pipeline/harness_env.py, with the
MODEL resolved by POINTER to config/model_assignments.yaml#harness_roles.AGENT_LOOP_SHORT.model so no
model name is restated (C12). Proof: with the binding applied, the same run moved the local engine's
counter 52 -> 54. harness_env --selftest is now 9/9, including `an_unresolvable_pointer_is_FATAL`.

## BUG-816 (MED - RETRACTED 2026-10-15, the same day) - the 2B reader did NOT return a false negative; the question's PREMISE was false
**RETRACTION.** The sub-agent said config/engine.yaml contains no fanout.max_parallel. That was TRUE: the block had
never landed. A grep in this repository finds no such key at the time of the run, and the same task re-run after the
block was actually written was answered CORRECTLY in 8.1s (max_parallel: 3, with the reason quoted). The failure was
mine: an edit whose answer began 'No match found for the specified text' was read as a success, so two declared blocks
(hf, fanout) were absent while three instruments silently used their own hardcoded defaults. The real bug is BUG-817.
KEEP THE LESSON: a sub-agent that says NO EVIDENCE is reporting on the PREMISE, not about itself.

Two detached sub-agent tasks (pipeline/subagent_fanout.py, MiniCPM5-2B-MLX) both reached TERMINAL in ~24s and
wrote their own answer files - durability and artefact-partitioning worked on the first try. One of the two
answers was WRONG: asked whether config/engine.yaml declares fanout.max_parallel, the model said there is no
mention, while a grep finds it in the very file it was handed. A 2B model reads fast and unreliably, and a wrong
sub-answer is invisible in a fan-out unless something else checks it.
FIX IN PLACE: (a) the model is declared PER TASK (D-3011 - a slot names an axis, and LIGHTWEIGHT_PROBE is not a
reading-comprehension worker); (b) the cross-family verify pass is REQUIRED, not offered (R5); (c) a task budget
must be sized for the answer, not for the hope (task 1 was cut off at 220 tokens).
CLASS: BUG-811's cousin - a new instrument's first output is evidence about the instrument, not about the world.

## BUG-817 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a failed edit was read as a success, so two declared config blocks never existed while three instruments invented their own defaults

FILED IN PLACE (the retraction above and this bug share one chronology; the body of the finding is the
BUG-816 block). An edit to `config/engine.yaml` answered `No match found for the specified text` and was READ
AS A SUCCESS. The `hf:` block and the whole `fanout:` block were therefore ABSENT from the file, while
pipeline/hf_fetch_model.py, pipeline/subagent_fanout.py and pipeline/oneshot_ask.py each fell back to their own
hardcoded default - a C12 violation in which a value with no home is invented by its consumer. The instrument
that caught it was a PREMISE GATE, not a smarter model: a task that declares `expect: REGEX` is now refused
unless one of its own files contains that regex, before any model is called (D-3012).

### BUG-817 addendum (2026-10-15, minutes later) - the broken home was COMMITTED
The D-3012 block was appended by an inline heredoc that had no rollback: YAML refused it (an apostrophe inside
a single-quoted scalar - the third occurrence of that exact class today), the traceback killed the script, and
the bash around it carried on to `git add -A` and `git commit`, so config/decisions.yaml - a PROTECTED home
and the source of truth for 1,130+ decisions - sat broken in a commit. Fixed in the next commit; gov_sync then
re-cut the faces.
TWO RULES THIS ADDS, and they are the same rule twice:
  (1) A STRUCTURAL EDIT GOES THROUGH THE LAND-SCRIPT PATTERN (temp/land_*.py): guard() a backup, append, then
      yaml_ok() which ROLLS BACK on a parse failure. Every earlier landing today did this; this one did not.
  (2) A SHELL THAT RUNS AFTER A FAILED STEP MUST NOT COMMIT. The land script's exit code is the gate.

| where | name | state |
|---|---|---|
