## BUG-814 (CLOSED 2026-10-15) - 4.0 GB of hub bytes that can never become a model, named as a model that already is one

MEASURED, and the answer to "can we not just resume it?" is NO, twice over.

(a) `models--lmstudio-community--Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` = 4.0 GB and ALL of it is `.incomplete` fragments:
319 MB + 0.24 MB + 1459 MB + 1657 MB + 293 MB + 513 MB. Three target hashes appear TWICE with different
random suffixes (`471a9a...55035491.incomplete` AND `471a9a...f6248dc7.incomplete`; `0e1038989...fc41e56b`
AND `ff5c14eb`; `e7474b8f...c30174f6` AND `ce03d157`) - the fingerprint of two overlapping or aborted
attempts. huggingface_hub does not resume a foreign fragment: there is nothing here to resume FROM.
(b) The snapshot directory holds METADATA ONLY (config.json, tokenizer.json, index.json, README, processor
configs) and NOT ONE shard symlink: the index names three shards; the snapshot names none.
(c) The model is NOT missing. The served `~/.omlx/models/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` is a REAL 15 GB directory,
3 complete shards (5.34 + 5.35 + 5.36 GB), and its quantization block is IDENTICAL to the hub fragments
(`qwen3_5`, 4-bit, affine, group_size 64). Resuming would rebuild something that already exists, next to it.
(d) It was classified DECLARED only because its name appears in two governance documents. RESOLUTION, not
mention, is the byte-owner test (D-3010) - the same test that keeps the three 12-24 KB metadata stubs and
the `pplx-decider`/`clef` trio in T-142 rather than in a delete list.

## BUG-818 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - the retire tool's dry run promises a park and its code performs a delete; and safe_delete would copy model weights into a Dropbox-synced repo

Three self-inflicted traps found while executing the owners deletion order (D-3013).

(a) `pipeline/omlx_retire_model.sh` dry run prints "would move the ENTRY (not the bytes) to
`models_stashed/NAME`" while the apply branch does `rm "$ENTRY"` for a symlink and only MOVES a real
directory. Two behaviours, one sentence: an operator who reads the dry run believes the entry is
recoverable from the stash and it is not.
(b) A park followed by a byte deletion produces a parked symlink pointing at nothing - recreating BUG-808
inside the tool that exists to prevent it.
(c) `pipeline/safe_delete.py` copies its target to `backup/deletions/` before deleting. For model weights that
copies 8.4 GB INTO THE REPOSITORY, which is a Dropbox-synced folder: the bytes would leave the machine
(C3) and the gain would be nil. The tool already prints the right instruction for weights ("delete directly
with rm -rf") - the trap is that its own default contradicts it.
FIX RULE (now part of D-3013): model weights are deleted directly, with a receipt naming path, measured
bytes, reason and decision id; the engine entry is removed FIRST so no name can outlive its target.

## BUG-819 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a face that says "generated from the live oMLX registry" was hand-copied and had drifted

`governance/eval_models.txt` opens with `# generated from live oMLX registry` and is cited by
`config/r5_review_gate.yaml` as the evidence for what is live. Measured: it lists seven models including
`Ornith-1.5-9B-OptiQ-4bit` (the engine now serves `Ornith-1.5-9B-MLX-8bit`) and it does not list
`MiniCPM5-2B-MLX` (adopted 2026-10-15). Nothing writes it. A count or a list with no generator is a claim,
not a face: regenerate it from `/v1/models/status` or delete the "generated" line.

## BUG-820 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - a guard artifact rewritten by a generic YAML dumper loses the comments that ARE the guard

`governance/session_plan_20260924.yaml` is read by `scripts/check_session_plan.py`, and its `may_touch` list carries
per-entry NAMED comments (which decision or bug earned each grant) so that a later agent can tell an earned grant from a
blanket one. Granting five new paths with `yaml.safe_load` + `yaml.safe_dump` rewrote the file: 618 insertions /
666 deletions, 34 comment lines gone, folded scalars re-flowed, and 78 duplicate entries silently collapsed - the data
survived and the PROVENANCE did not. MEASURED, then REVERTED (`git checkout HEAD --`) and redone as a TEXTUAL
insertion that preserves every comment.

RULE: a governed YAML file whose comments carry provenance is edited by INSERTION, never by load-dump. A dumper is
safe for a file whose meaning is entirely in its keys; it is destructive for a file whose meaning is partly in its
comments (the same distinction BUG-810 made for shell-quoted arguments).

## BUG-821 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - the census could not count 16 records because the mint path was bypassed, so four faces quoted a stale total for two sessions

MEASURED then FIXED. `config/decisions_summary.json` declared **1128 decisions** while `config/decisions.yaml` held
**1144**. The recompute tool refused to repair it, and its refusal names the reason: `FAIL-CLOSED (BUG-483):
decision D-3005 carries no canonical state: key (legacy keys present: [status]) - it would be silently counted as
ACTIVE.` Twelve records minted by appending text in a land script carried no canonical keys at all - eight had
`status:` instead of `state:`, four had `class:` instead of `category:` - so the census stopped advancing and
DECISION-LOG.md, MASTER-TASK-REGISTER.md, buglog.md and agent/session_seed.yaml all quoted 1128 for two sessions.

(a) THE MINT PATH IS THE ONE HOME. A decision is added by `--mint`, which validates the record, joins its own
fields to reality (the cited bugs, the cited files, D-2660) and REWRITES THE CENSUS IN THE SAME INVOCATION.
Appending text to the register is a path that can mint a record nothing can count.
(b) The normalisation exposed a second defect: `scripts/recompute_decision_summary.py` declares
`written_by: temp/mut_recompute.py` and the tool in `temp/` declares `written_by: scripts/recompute_decision_summary.py`.
Each therefore reports exactly one drift - the other - and `--check` becomes a false witness depending on which ran
last. ONE artifact, ONE writer: the declared writer should be the one in `scripts/`, and the tool in `temp/` should
either move there or be deleted.
(c) The first repair attempt fixed ONE record of the twelve: it collected block indices once and then INSERTED a
line per record, so every later index pointed one line off (the loop had to run in reverse). BUG-811 cousin -
an instrument mutating the list it is iterating indexes into.
(d) AFTER THE FIX: 1144 decisions, stamp `81ac953af5bd0eda`, source_sha256 `414ccaa436aeecdf`, and both gates pass
(`records-only` and `describes those exact bytes`).

## BUG-809 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-15) - delegated research was not durable; the fix is now INFRASTRUCTURE, not a rule

**RE-MEASURED, and it failed again first.** On 2026-10-15 the owner's own delegate calls failed twice in one
session (one subagent returned an empty response, one was cancelled) while "running for so long without any
result". The 2026-10-15 remedy in this register was a RULE applied by hand (write the report first, summarise in
chat, re-measure the load-bearing numbers, never sequence implementation behind a delegate). A rule that a human
must remember is not a fix: the same two failures happened again.

**THE FIX (three layers, all landed).** (1) DURABILITY: a task runs as a DETACHED workstream
(pipeline/research_run.py, own session, own process group) so no harness event can cancel it, and it writes its
answer to a file - the deliverable is never a return value. (2) GUARDS: pipeline/subagent_fanout.py#run plans,
launches under the declared pool cap, watches to a declared deadline, reaps a task past its budget, and writes a
receipt naming every task's state. (3) HONESTY: the terminal word is DERIVED from the answer the task actually
got (see BUG-824 - the old command asserted `TERMINAL: DONE` unconditionally).

**EVIDENCE.** `python3 pipeline/subagent_fanout.py --selftest` -> 20/20; `doctor` -> 8/8;
`run --tasks temp/fanout_20261015h.yaml --run fanout_20261015i` -> 3/3 DONE, rc=0, one task deliberately given
a 1 s budget: it was reaped at 2.2 s, retried on a DIFFERENT model, and the receipt shows both attempts
(temp/runs/fanout_20261015i/98_receipt.json). `pipeline/research_run.py --selftest` -> 18/18.


## BUG-822 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-15) - a land script wrote three config blocks TWICE, and every parse check passed

**MEASURED.** Landing the 2026-10-15 ancestors decision inserted `harnesses.jobs`, `hf.lock_dir`/`lock_suffix`/
`duplicate_fragments` and the whole `model_store` block into config/engine.yaml, and the anchor-based insert ran
twice. Result: **16 duplicate scopes** (`model_store` at lines 106 and 112, `harnesses.jobs` at 52 and 68,
`hf.lock_dir` at 83 and 88, and 13 more). PyYAML does not refuse a duplicate key - it keeps the LAST one - so the
file parsed, every rail stayed green, and the second copy silently shadowed the first.

**HOW IT WAS CAUGHT.** Not by a rail: by a hand-written duplicate-key detector, after the fact. The detector that
already existed (`scripts/check_config_duplicate_keys.py`, BUG-730) found it in one second when run by hand.

**REMEDY.** The three duplicate blocks are deleted (verified: the checker reports 0 of 135 files);
`fanout.guards` was landed as a single insert. The systemic half is T-149: an instrument that is never CALLED is
not a guard, so this checker goes into `just preflight`.


## BUG-823 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-15) - a governed config file did not parse, and nothing read it

**MEASURED.** `config/intake_sources.yaml` failed to load: `mapping values are not allowed here` at line 34.
Twelve rows were written as `- class: video   {mechanic: ...}` - a flow mapping cannot follow a plain scalar.
No file under pipeline/, scripts/ or tools/ reads `intake_sources`, so the defect could not surface as an error
anywhere: the intake declaration was unreadable AND unread, which is the worst of both.

**REMEDY.** The rows are repaired into flow mappings (`- {class: video, mechanic: ...}`) and the file parses.
T-152 records the governance half: a declaration with no reader cannot fail loudly, so it must either get its
reader or be marked proposal-only.


## BUG-824 (HIGH - FIXED 2026-10-15) - the fan-out executor told four lies, and the first one was a false success

**ALL FOUR MEASURED on 2026-10-15, three of them by the executor's own acceptance run.**
1. **A FALSE SUCCESS (the BUG-817 class, inside the instrument that reports delegation health).** Every planned
   command ended with `echo "TERMINAL: DONE - oneshot rc=$?"`, so a oneshot that exited 1 - engine refused, no
   content - was recorded as **DONE**. The `$?` was captured and then ignored. The terminal word is now computed
   by a grader that reads the answer file and the rc (`_grade`), so EMPTY, FAILED and DONE are earned.
2. **NO REAPER.** `timeout_s` was consulted only when somebody happened to call `status()`. A run nobody polled
   stayed RUNNING forever - the owner's exact words, "it runs so long without any result, it seems stuck". There
   is now a `watch` loop, and `run` attaches one, so a budget is enforced without a human polling.
3. **NO LIVENESS.** A hung child and a working child read identically. `idle_s` is now measured against a
   declared `stall_s` and published; only a task declared `kill_on_stall` is killed on suspicion, but silence is
   never a secret.
4. **THE CAP DOUBLE-BOOKED A LAUNCH, STRANDING A TASK.** `started + _running(run_id) >= cap` counted the same
   launch twice, so the third of three tasks was never started: measured live as `started 2 (cap 3)` with one
   task left PENDING and the receipt reporting `2/4 usable` for a run that had answered every question. The
   receipt now rolls attempts up to the TASK.

**A FIFTH, found in the same run:** a TIMEOUT/STALLED record never stamped `t1`, so its `elapsed_s` kept growing
after it had died - `55.1 s` reported for a task that stopped at 2.2 s. Every terminal transition now stamps it.

**EVIDENCE.** `--selftest` 20/20 including the controls that would have caught all five; `research_run.py
--selftest` 18/18 including `a_TIMEOUT_record_stops_growing_its_elapsed_time`. The live proof run is cited under
BUG-809.


## BUG-825 (HIGH - FIXED 2026-10-15) - a deletion receipt overstated the reclaimed space 2.07x, and the batch exited 0 while its census face never moved

**MEASURED, in the sweep that ran minutes after the delegation fix.** Two defects in one receipt.
1. **THE RECLAIM FIGURE WAS MINE, NOT THE DISK'S.** Each repo's bytes were summed with
   `sum(p.stat().st_size for p in rglob)` - which counts a hub **blob** and the **snapshot hardlink** that points
   at it as two files. The receipt claimed **30.66 GB freed**; `du -sk` on the same directory showed
   **14.83 GiB** (153.50 -> 138.67 GiB). Calibration on the repos that still exist: the overstatement factor is
   **exactly 2.000** on every one of them. This is the BUG-807 class - a reclaim figure nobody can act on - and
   it was caught only by measuring the disk on both sides.
2. **A FAILED WITNESS WAS READ AS A WARNING.** The census exits **2 when orphan proposals exist** (a
   measurement, not a failure). The batch read `rc != 0` as "the census did not re-run", printed a warning, and
   **exited 0** - while `governance/model_store_census_20261015.json` did not move AT ALL (byte-identical to
   HEAD, `hub_bytes` 0.15 GiB, buckets unchanged) despite 14.83 GiB having been deleted. That is exactly the
   BUG-819 class the warning itself names: a face describing bytes that are gone.

**REMEDY.** The receipt carries a `measurement` block with the disk's own before/after, the original claim kept
visible, and the defect proved by live calibration (temp/land_20261015g.py --phase c). Phase b now measures each
repo ONCE PER PHYSICAL BLOCK (`physical_bytes`), records the census total BEFORE the sweep, treats rc=2 as a
measurement, and **raises** if the census did not move - a batch that deletes without moving its face may not
exit 0 (T-147). The stale face itself is T-151.

## BUG-826 (HIGH - FIXED 2026-10-15) - the delegation doctor failed against the LEDGER OF EVERY RUN EVER, and the check beside it passed having checked nothing

**MEASURED, minutes before T-149 was to wire this doctor into `just preflight`.** `python3
pipeline/subagent_fanout.py doctor` returned `doctor: 7/8` with
`[FAIL] the retry model is not a task model (R5: a retry may not repeat the failing model) fallback=gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit`
and, next to it, `[ok] every task model is served by the engine  2 distinct model(s) checked`. Those two models
were read from `temp/runs/*/fan_*/task.json` - **the ledger of delegations that already finished**. R5's retry
question ("is the retry target the model that failed?") is a property of a **PLAN**; asked of history it answers a
question nobody asked, and it answers it WRONG in the direction that matters: a fallback model that was some task's
model yesterday fails a doctor run for a plan that does not exist yet. The check beside it reported `ok` having
checked nothing about the plan in hand.

**WHY IT IS HIGH.** T-149 exists to CALL this guard from preflight. Wiring a guard that is red on history makes
preflight permanently red - and a permanently red guard is a guard an operator learns to ignore. The instrument
had to be honest BEFORE it was obeyed.

**REMEDY (tri-state verdicts).** A check that had nothing to decide now prints `[undecided]` and is counted as
neither a pass nor a failure - D-3015 ("an instrument that cannot decide says so and stops") applied to the
per-check verdict, not only to the whole tool. Models are read from the PLAN (`--tasks`) or not at all; history is
never a plan. `doctor: 6/6 decided, 2 undecided (nothing to decide)`, rc 0. **The FAIL path is proven live, not
assumed:** a synthetic plan naming `gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit` as a task model returns rc 1 with the R5 line FAIL.
`--selftest` 26/26, with five new controls including `a_doctor_with_no_plan_reads_UNDECIDED_not_FAIL` and
`a_plan_whose_task_model_IS_the_retry_model_reads_FAIL`.


## BUG-827 (HIGH - FIXED 2026-10-15) - nothing in the guard chain reads the file an answer cites, so a fabricated review was graded DONE (BUG-721, reproduced live)

**MEASURED on the FIRST harness job (T-144, run `harness_20261015a`).** Asked to find every place where a terminal
state can be recorded without a derived proof, the declared agent_loop model (`gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit`, driving
`pi` through `omlx launch pi`) returned **eight `file:line` citations and every one of them pointed at unrelated
code**. It "quoted" `word = "DONE"` at `pipeline/subagent_fanout.py:111`, which reads `if len(text) < min_chars:`;
it cited `pipeline/research_run.py:149` for `rc == 0`, which reads `if not pid_alive(pid):`. The answer was
**1,737 chars, exited 0**, cleared the 80-char floor and was recorded `TERMINAL: DONE - rc=0, ok, 1737 chars`.

**ROOT.** Every guard in the chain judged the answer's **FORM** - not a stub, long enough, sane rc, bounded wall.
Not one of them read the file the answer made a claim about. `answer_verdict()` cannot see a fabrication: a
fabrication is long, exits 0 and does not carry the stub prefix. This is BUG-721 (a delegate returned a fabricated
verdict without reading the code) measured again, five sessions later, with the same result.

**REMEDY: the R5 duty made MECHANICAL.** `citation_defects()` (`pipeline/subagent_fanout.py`), exposed as
`python3 pipeline/subagent_fanout.py citations --answer F`, reads **both shapes models actually write** -
`path.py:111` inline and a `path.py` heading followed by `Line 111:` bullets - and refutes (a) a quoted fragment
that is not on the cited line, (b) a line past the end of the file, (c) a file that does not exist. A prose
reference (no punctuation, like `the grader`) is never read as a quote, so a loose answer is not failed for being
**loose** - only for being **false**. The receipt now carries `citations_checked` / `citations_refuted` per attempt
and returns exit 1 when any deliverable's citation is refuted.

**EVIDENCE.** On the real answer (the one graded DONE): **8 citations checked, 13 refuted claims**, rc 1 -
`temp/runs/harness_20261015a/ws_guard_review/40_citation_check.txt`. `--selftest` 32/32 with six controls
including `a_fabricated_citation_is_refuted` and `a_prose_reference_is_never_read_as_a_quote`.
**The lesson generalises:** a claim about a file is not judged, it is READ BACK - the verifier of a citation need
not be a smarter model, it must be a reader (D-3022).


## BUG-828 (MED - CLOSED 2026-10-15) - the deployed harness is not bounded by the declared budgets: the liveness signal cannot see it, and one turn outlasts the stall threshold

Three measured parts, all from the same T-144 run.

1. **THE LIVENESS SIGNAL DOES NOT SEE THE HARNESS.** `research_run` counts progress as
   `10_report.md|20_answer.md|run.log`. A harness writes its transcript to `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl`
   continuously and its answer only at the END. Measured live at 17:46: `state=RUNNING idle_s=66.6 stalled=True`
   **while pi was mid-loop and healthy** (the next engine line 12 s later was `finish_reason=stop`). A stall flag
   that fires on a working run is the BUG-824 family again: the instrument asserting something it has not measured.
2. **ONE TURN IS LONGER THAN THE DECLARED STALL THRESHOLD.** The final turn measured **45.58 s** (521 tokens at
   27.4 tok/s, prompt 12,438) against `config/engine.yaml#fanout.guards.stall_s=45`. The threshold is BELOW the
   longest single measured turn of the deployed class, so the flag trips by construction rather than by defect.
3. **THE TURN'S TOKEN CEILING IS THE ENGINE'S GLOBAL CAP, NOT THE CLASS BUDGET.** pi sends no `max_tokens`
   (`request_max_tokens=None` in the engine log) and the per-model entry caps at **32,768** - inherited from
   `~/.omlx/settings.json#sampling.max_tokens` - which at 27.4 tok/s is **~20 minutes** against the owner's
   declared **90 s** per-turn knob. The bound that actually bites is the workstream wall (300 s declared for this
   job, reaped by `research_run watch`), which is why that wall is load-bearing rather than decorative.

**REMEDY (T-154):** a harness workstream declares its transcript INSIDE the workstream
(`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$WS_DIR/agent`, a knob the engine's own pi integration already honours), progress becomes a
recursive count of the workstream directory, and the per-turn token ceiling is declared per class instead of being
inherited from a global number that was never about the class.

**CLOSED 2026-10-15 (T-154).** All three parts are fixed, each with a control that can fail:

1. **The liveness signal now sees the harness, and this was PROVEN LIVE, not argued.** The workstream class
   declares its env (`config/agent_context.yaml#classes.agent_loop.env: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR: '{ws}/agent'`, applied
   by `pipeline/research_run.py::class_env`) and progress is a RECURSIVE walk of the workstream dir minus the
   runner's own `state.json`/`.tmp_*` (a counter that counted its own writes would pin idle at 0 and make the stall
   flag UNREACHABLE - the opposite silent failure, and there is a control for that too). Measured on
   `temp/runs/harness_20261015c/fan_h1`, sampled every 8 s while pi worked:
   `idle=9.5/17.7/7.2/15.4/0.9/9.1 s, stalled=False`, with `progress_newest` naming
   `agent/sessions/--Users-...--/2026-10-15T19-50-31-290Z_*.jsonl` as the transcript grew 113,306 -> 114,750 B
   **inside the workstream**. The 45 s threshold that fired on a healthy loop is gone: the class declares 120 s
   (longest measured turn 45.58 s x declared margin 2.0) and the class - not the caller - owns it.
2. **The threshold is now a DERIVED floor with a checker.** `pipeline/subagent_fanout.py doctor` and
   `python3 pipeline/research_run.py --check` (wired into `just preflight`) recompute every class bound from
   declared sources: stall floor from the class's longest MEASURED turn x `turn_budget.stall_margin`, the wall from
   the owner's `per_turn_budget_s` x the class's declared `max_turns` against the guard the class names, and the
   ceiling from `per_turn_budget_s` x the MEASURED decode rate. Known-answer controls prove each assertion CAN
   fail, including the exact 45 s threshold this bug measured.
3. **The ceiling is declared per class, and where it cannot be declared it is DERIVED - with the residual named.**
   A one-shot passes its own `--max-tokens` and is checked against the derived ceiling (512 <= 3150). A harness
   sends NO `max_tokens` (83 of 83 gemma calls in the engine log carried `request_max_tokens=None`), so its ceiling
   is what the SERVER falls back to: the derived ceiling is **3,266 tokens** (90 s x 36.3 tok/s) and the checker
   reads `~/.omlx/model_settings.json` for it. That file's `models` map is EMPTY, so the checker reports
   **OWNER-OWED (rc 2)** - loud, never a pass - because binding it edits the LIVE SERVER's own home. That is the
   remaining act, and it is the owner's: T-161.

**A DERIVATION WAS DRAFTED AND RETRACTED IN THIS SAME SESSION, and the retraction is part of the record.** The
first wall formula added the class's `working_set / prefill_tps` term. Computed, it turned a 15-second one-shot
class into a 690 s wall and contradicted a guard that is measurably right - because `working_set` is the prompt a
class must be able to PAY FOR (a routing gate the prefill bill already owns), not the prompt it sends. An estimate
dressed as a derivation is BUG-794's defect, so the shipped derivation keeps only terms that are declared facts.


## BUG-829 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - the review surface's own agent panel defaults to a CLOUD provider

**MEASURED while executing T-146.** `~/.config/zed/settings.json` declares
`agent.default_model = deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` (provider `deepseek`, effort high, thinking on) - and the SAME
file already declares `agent_servers: {pi-acp: {type: registry}, deepagents: {type: registry}}`. So the surface
being adopted as the REVIEW surface carries a native agent that leaves the machine by default, while its
ACP-hosted agents can be wired to the sovereign engine (pi's config already points at
`http://127.0.0.1:11435/v1` with the local token).

**WHY IT IS FILED AND NOT LEFT AS A NOTE.** No rail in this repository can see this file - it lives outside the
repo - so an implicit cloud default in a surface used to review governed work is exactly the C3/C22 drift the
constitution names, and it is invisible to `just preflight`. **Options, in order:** (i) bind
`agent.default_model` to the local engine (provider `omlx`), so the panel is sovereign like the harness is; or
(ii) record the cloud default as an explicit owner OPT-IN, because C22 permits API use that is *explicit*, not API
use that is *ambient*.

## BUG-830 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-15) - preflight had been RED since the delegation session, because the delegation code kept a SECOND copy of two declared values

**MEASURED 2026-10-15, by running `just preflight` after wiring T-149's two guards into it.** The recipe failed
**before** either new guard, at `pipeline/config_audit.py --check-unchecked --strict`:
`UNCHECKED - 5 hardcoded values not in audit registry: model_store_census.py:39 MOVE = 0.05,
oneshot_ask.py:25 TEMPERATURE = 0.0, research_run.py:60 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 1800, research_run.py:61
DEFAULT_STALL_S = 600, research_run.py:65 POLL_S = 2.0`. Two of those five are the sharpest kind of defect C12
names: `config/engine.yaml#fanout.guards` **already declared** `default_timeout_s` and `stall_s`, so the module
held a **second home for values that had one** - and it held the WRONG one (1800 s and 600 s against the declared
120 s and 45 s). A workstream that inherits 1800 s while the executor budgets 120 s is exactly the silence
BUG-809 exists to prevent, and it was written by the fix for BUG-809.

**WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, and this is the point.** The fix was verified with `--selftest` (18/18), doctor runs and
live runs - every instrument EXCEPT the one recipe that gates everything. Preflight was red for a day and no one
asked it, which is the same lesson T-149 was filed for one day earlier: **an instrument nobody calls is not a
guard**. T-149's wiring is what made this visible: the guard rails went in ABOVE the failure and immediately
reported it.

**REMEDY.** (1) `pipeline/research_run.py` now READS `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S` / `DEFAULT_STALL_S` from
`config/engine.yaml#fanout.guards` at import, failing closed if the home or the block is absent - so the executor
and the runner can no longer disagree about a budget. (2) `pipeline/model_store_census.py` reads its movement
tolerance from the new declared `model_store.census_move_ratio` (0.05) instead of carrying a literal - the ratio
decides whether a re-measure counts as movement, which is a POLICY value, not an implementation detail.
(3) `POLL_S` (a 2 s watch cadence) and `TEMPERATURE` (R7 mandates 0.0 on every generation script - a
constitutional constant, and making it configurable would make R7 violable) are REGISTERED as acknowledged
literals with the reason stated, in `pipeline/config_audit.py#ACKNOWLEDGED_HARDCODED`.

**AND THE AUDIT ITSELF WAS TOO WEAK TO CHECK THE FIX.** Its registry resolves dotted paths against
`config/pipeline_config.yaml` only, so an engine.yaml value could not be registered at all - which is WHY the
authors left literals instead of linking them. Registering them made the audit report `CODE-ONLY` instead of
clean. The resolver now accepts `FILE#dotted.path` (`engine.yaml#fanout.guards.stall_s`), so the audit VERIFIES
that the code equals the declared value across files rather than merely knowing the name. Audit rc 0.

## BUG-831 (HIGH - FIXED 2026-10-15) - the citation checker certified a LINE without reading its labelled quote, and a real fabrication walked through the gap in the same hour it was written

**MEASURED, on the R5 review of the checker itself (run `harness_20261015b`, 2026-10-15).** A different family was
asked for one concrete way each of two new guards could produce a wrong verdict. Its answer cited two lines. One of
them read:

```
*   **File:line:** `pipeline/config_audit.py` (line 110)
*   **Exact Code:** `if not path.exists(): raise SystemExit(...)` (This line is *not* the issue, ...)
```

`pipeline/config_audit.py:110` actually reads `ACKNOWLEDGED_HARDCODED: set[str] = {`. The "Exact Code" was
invented - and the checker reported **`2 citation(s) checked, 0 refuted claim(s)`** on that answer, because its
quote window was the SAME line as the citation and the quote sat on the next one. The guard certified the line
number it could read and never read the sentence it was shown.

**A SECOND DEFECT, found by writing the control for the first:** the `path.py (line N)` shape resolved against the
file named in the nearest preceding HEADING, so a heading over file A followed by a citation to file B was checked
against **file A** - a false refutation, which is the failure mode that disables a guard (D-3022's own boundary).

**REMEDY.** (1) A quote on the NEXT line is now tied to the citation when that line LABELS itself as code
(`**Exact Code:**`, `Code:`, `Quoted:`, `Reads:`, `Says:`) and carries no citation of its own - the label is
required so that a merely nearby fragment is never guessed at, and an unlabelled next line is still not read.
(2) A line that names its own file on the same line is now checked against THAT file, with the heading as a
fallback only. `--selftest` 37/37, six of the controls being this bug's.

**EVIDENCE, both directions.** The fabricated `config_audit.py:110` quote is now REFUTED BY NAME; the honest
citation beside it (`subagent_fanout.py:171`, `if quote and quote not in actual:`) is **no longer refuted** by the
new lookahead, and is only reported now because the file MOVED (the fix added lines above it) - so the limit is
declared rather than hidden: **the check is against the file AS IT IS NOW**, and a refutation of an answer written
before an edit means the file moved. A receipt is written minutes after its answer, where the two coincide; a
re-check of an old answer is archaeology and must be read as such.

**D-3022 is unchanged in rule and extended in shape:** the rule is "a citation is read back"; BUG-831 is the
measurement that "both shapes" was one shape too few, and that the reader has to be told where the quote lives.

## BUG-832 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) — the session brain is the provider a CLOSED bug banned, and nothing in the repo can see it change

MEASURED 2026-10-15, read-only:
- ~/.config/goose/config.yaml:311 reads `active_provider: custom_deepseek`, and providers.custom_deepseek
  (lines 273-276) is enabled with model: deepseek-v4-pro.
- BUG-243 (CLOSED 2026-10-09) closed on the rationale "active_provider=maxwell_omlx; delegate-safe guard +
  delegate_rules ban (DELEGATE-001). No active config references custom_deepseek." That rationale is FALSE
  today: the active provider IS custom_deepseek.
- DECISION-LOG.md D-295 (RESOLVED) records the same remedy — "the bug is active_provider: custom_deepseek.
  Switch to maxwell_omlx".
- The economy of the current arrangement, measured by the new instrument:
  python3 pipeline/delegation_economy.py -> cloud 32,851 calls / 3,981,322,921 input tokens / $105.42
  (estimated) against local 379 calls / 3,667,410 input tokens / $0.00, i.e. the local fleet carried
  0.09% of the load.

ROOT — two defects stacked, and neither of them is the owner's taste in models:
(a) ONTOLOGICAL: the rule's SUBJECT is mistyped. DELEGATE-001 is a defect of the DELEGATE PASSTHROUGH PATH
    (a reasoning model returns finish_reason=stop with an empty final content under json_object), not of a
    provider NAME. The ban names the provider, so it is at once too broad (an interactive session on the
    same provider is not that bug) and too narrow (no path is guarded but the delegate path — tools/
    delegate_safe.py validates a DELEGATE's provider, so the SESSION's own provider is unchecked). A rule
    whose subject is a name rather than a MECHANISM cannot be enforced anywhere.
(b) STRUCTURAL: a home-directory setting that a decision NAMES has no reader in the repo, so a reversal of
    a ruled remedy is invisible — no census, no rail, no face. The repo measures config/*.yaml to the key;
    it does not measure the harness homes that config/agent_context.yaml#homes itself declares.

REMEDY (owner-gated: the setting is the owner's and the choice of brain is theirs).
1. CENSUS the harness homes a decision names, so a change is a READING and not a discovery (T-157).
2. DECIDE the brain explicitly (C22: local-first, API opt-in EXPLICIT): either execute D-295 literally, or
   AMEND D-295 — the session brain is a measured, ceilinged opt-in. The measurement makes the second the
   honest option today: no served model passes agent_loop long-context reasoning
   (config/harness_policy.yaml#capability_axes.long_context_reasoning_16k: gemma-4-E4B 0.0, Qwen3-Coder 0.0;
   only Qwen3.8-27B at 1.0, and at 39 tok/s prefill a 26214-token turn costs 672 s). The local route is
   therefore REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT for this class, which is exactly the declared escalation reason
   'local_route_refuted' in config/delegation_economy.yaml.
3. RESTATE the ban with its real subject (the delegate passthrough path), not a provider name.

EVIDENCE: ~/.config/goose/config.yaml:311 and :273-276 | governance/buglog.md BUG-243 close rationale |
DECISION-LOG.md D-295 | python3 pipeline/delegation_economy.py --check (rc 0, within ceiling) |
config/harness_policy.yaml#capability_axes.long_context_reasoning_16k.

OWNER WORD 2026-10-18 (D-3038 accepted negative — the ceiling is NOT raised): the breach re-read 2026-10-18 is
cloud input tokens 4,638,632,408 > ceiling 4,600,000,000 and cloud calls 38,690 > 37,000 (cost $120.56 < $130.00,
NOT breached). The owner ruled: do NOT raise the ceiling — a SHRINK-ONLY ceiling must never be raised to chase

## BUG-833 (MED - CLOSED 2026-10-15) — a workstream started with an ABSENT prompt ran to completion, called NO model at all, and exited 0

CLOSED 2026-10-15 (T-160): research_run start now materialises the run brief into the workstream prompt and
REFUSES a mandate-less workstream (EMPTY state, no command, no process, non-zero rc). Proven by the runner's own
selftest (20/20) and a live reproduction of this exact shape, which now refuses with rc 1.

MEASURED 2026-10-15, live (temp/runs/r5_economy_20261015/ws_r5_economy):
- python3 pipeline/research_run.py new --run r5_economy_20261015 --brief temp/_r5_economy_prompt.txt wrote the
  RUN-level 00_brief.md (904 B) and NO workstream prompt.
- ... start --ws ws_r5_economy --cmd-file temp/_r5_economy_cmd.sh created the ws dir (00_prompt.txt ABSENT)
  and ran the command ANYWAY.
- The shipped cmd idiom reads the prompt as -p "$(cat "$WS_DIR/00_prompt.txt")"; a missing file expands to an
  EMPTY STRING, so pi was launched with an empty -p ("Executing 'node' command with arguments: ... -p",
  30_pi.err line 25).
- pi exited 0, wrote 0 bytes, and THE ENGINE WAS NEVER CALLED: ENGINE_WITNESS chat_completions 232 -> 232
  (the two prior jobs moved the counter 223 -> 226 and 226 -> 232). 16.5 s of a 300 s budget produced nothing.
- The grader called it "TERMINAL: EMPTY - rc=0, the answer is empty" - an honest VERDICT, but rc=0 is a lie: a
  run that did nothing returns the exit code of a run that answered. A chain that keys on rc cannot see this.

ROOT: the two halves disagree about who owns the prompt. pipeline/subagent_fanout.py writes 00_prompt.txt for
the FAN-OUT path (line 308) and copies it on the retry path (line 449); the DURABLE RUNNER writes only the
run-level 00_brief.md. A caller following the documented shape (new --brief, then start --cmd-file) therefore
starts a workstream with an empty prompt, and NOTHING refuses it: start validates neither the prompt's
existence nor its size, and "$(cat missing)" is silent by design - the shell defect BUG-817 already named.

REMEDY (all three; the third is what makes the first two durable):
1. research_run start REFUSES before it invokes anything when the ws prompt file is absent or 0 bytes
   (fail closed, C16) - the shape the engine contract's own readers already use.
2. new --brief MATERIALISES the brief into the workstream (or start copies 00_brief.md -> ws/00_prompt.txt
   and reports the byte count).
3. an EMPTY terminal must not carry rc 0: the state vocabulary already separates EMPTY from DONE, so the rc
   must follow the STATE, not the child process.

EVIDENCE: temp/runs/r5_economy_20261015/ws_r5_economy/10_report.md (ENGINE_WITNESS + TERMINAL), 30_pi.err,
state.json | pipeline/subagent_fanout.py:308 and :449 | the two prior jobs' engine counters (223 -> 226,
226 -> 232).


## BUG-834 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) — a delegate's handle did not resolve, so the deliverable of an in-process delegation was unretrievable in the same turn

MEASURED 2026-10-15, in-session: the delegate surface (Summon.delegate, extensions: [developer], max_turns 6)
returned the string "Delegated to foreground subagent 20261015_13" and nothing else - no answer, no artifact path.
load(source: "20261015_13") returned "Error: Task '20261015_13' not found.". The prompt asked for three
file:line citations that a deterministic reader could have checked (D-3022), so the delegation was built to be
verifiable; it produced nothing verifiable.

ROOT (bounded claim, not a diagnosis): the handle returned to the CALLER does not name an object the caller can
load. Whether the answer arrives later in the parent transcript is UNTESTED - the honest statement is that the
caller cannot retrieve it at the moment it needs it, and that is enough to make the in-process delegate
unsuitable for any work whose loss costs something.

## BUG-835 (HIGH - CLOSED 2026-10-15) - the engine's chunk-shaped SSE keepalive is read as the model's FINAL answer, so a harness turn ends empty while the loop is healthy

MEASURED 2026-10-15 21:51:29, live, in the T-154 harness proof
(`temp/runs/harness_20261015c/fan_h1`): pi ran a healthy four-turn tool loop (read -> grep -> assistant), the

    {"role": "assistant", "content": [], "output": 0, "stopReason": "stop",
     "provider": "omlx", "model": "gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit", "responseModel": "keepalive"}

    finish_reason=stop, max_tokens=32768, request_max_tokens=None, stream_model_ttft=unavailable

ROOT (read from the engine's own source, not inferred): `~/.omlx/settings.json#server.sse_keepalive_mode` is
`"chunk"`, and `omlx/server.py::_resolve_keepalive` returns `_KEEPALIVE_CHAT_CHUNK` for that mode - a
wire-level frame shaped EXACTLY like a real completion chunk
(`{"id":"chatcmpl-keepalive","model":"keepalive",...}`), emitted during a long prefill. `responseModel:
"keepalive"` in pi's transcript is the frame's own `model` field arriving as the turn's final response. The
engine documents the hazard in the same function: "Some clients (e.g. OpenClaw / WorkBuddy) cannot parse" it, and
the alternative `comment` mode returns `_KEEPALIVE_COMMENT`, which is a true no-op for any compliant client.
**pi is such a client.** The other two modes it declares are `comment` and `off`.

WHY THIS IS HIGH: the harness class is the deployment T-137 measures and the flip to `active_provider:
maxwell_omlx` depends on. An agent loop that loses its last turn cannot be trusted as the primary provider, and
the failure is silent in the worst way - the process exits 0, the transcript looks busy and healthy, and only the
EMPTY terminal (BUG-833's discipline, working as designed) says anything is wrong. It also inflates the measured
loop cost: the run spent ~60 s and three model calls to produce nothing.

DO NOT CONFUSE THIS WITH THE LIVENESS FIX (BUG-828): BUG-828 was the runner being blind to a working loop, and it
is fixed. Here the loop was SEEN perfectly and still produced nothing - a different layer, a different remedy.

REMEDY (owner act on the LIVE server's home, then a re-run): set
`~/.omlx/settings.json#server.sse_keepalive_mode` to `comment` (the engine's own no-op frame) or `off`, and re-run
the T-154 proof - which then also becomes the T-137 preflight. Declared as a PRECONDITION of the T-137 A/B gate
(`config/ab_harness_t137.yaml#preconditions`): both arms drive the same harness class, so an A/B run in this
environment measures the keepalive, not the model.

EVIDENCE: the transcript record and the engine log line above; `omlx/server.py:2494-2545` (`_resolve_keepalive`,
`_chat_keepalive_chunk`); `~/.omlx/settings.json#server.sse_keepalive_mode = "chunk"`;
`30_harness.err` shows the loop ran to completion with the wrapper's node/hermit banner on stderr.

CLOSED 2026-10-15 22:09 (T-162 done): `~/.omlx/settings.json#server.sse_keepalive_mode` set `chunk` -> `comment`
(backup `settings.json.bak-20261015220705`), the engine server was restarted (new pid 46950), and the proof re-run

## BUG-836 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-15) - the R5 cross-family review route produced NO usable review from either local verifier, and one of the two failures was graded as an ANSWER

MEASURED 2026-10-15, reviewing this session's own T-154 diff (R5: the generator may not verify itself, so a
different family was asked):

1. **gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit returned a DEGENERATE answer that was accepted.** Given a 22 KB diff and a
   four-defect checklist, it answered 2,294 characters containing nothing but a sequential `file:line` list
   (`pipeline/research_run.py:16`, `:17`, ... `:9`) - no finding, no claim, no defect. `oneshot_ask.py` wrote it
   as a normal answer (`ok: ... answered 2294 chars in 40.55s`) because the only gate on an answer is
   `min_answer_chars = 80`. A citation list is not a review; a length floor cannot tell the two apart.
2. **gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8 returned NO content at all, twice.** Both `max_tokens=700` and `max_tokens=2500`
   produced `message.content` EMPTY with the whole response in `message.reasoning_content`; `oneshot_ask.py`
   correctly refused it ("returned no content"). The 700-token attempt is the informative one: the reasoning
   stream consumed the entire budget, so a ceiling that does not cover reasoning buys an empty answer - which is
   D-3027's point measured rather than argued, and it means the strongest local reasoning model is NOT today a
   usable verifier through this path.

CONSEQUENCE FOR T-156 (the capability registry): a route is only legal if the instrument has a MEASURED usable
output on the class of work, and "a 4B model reviewed a 22 KB diff" is now a measurement that says NO. Two
instruments failing in two different shapes (degenerate-but-accepted, empty-and-refused) is exactly the pair a
registry must encode - and it must name the checker that can tell an answer from a non-answer, because today
nothing does.

REMEDY (T-163): an answer's SHAPE is checked, not only its length - a delegated REVIEW must carry at least one
finding citing a location in the artifact it was given, and a citation-only listing must read as NOT AN ANSWER
(the fan-out receipt already knows this shape: `an_answer_with_no_citation_checks_nothing_not_passing`).
Then re-route: a review whose prompt exceeds a measured size is refused by the registry rather than sent to a 4B.

EVIDENCE: `temp/t154_r5_review.md` (the 2,294-char degenerate answer), `temp/t154_r5_review2.md` (the "no
content" stub) and the two prompts `temp/t154_review_prompt.md` (22 KB) / `temp/t154_review2_prompt.md` (8.9 KB).

**REMEDY LIMB 1 LANDED (T-163, same day, 2026-10-15) - THE SHAPE IS NOW READ.** `answer_verdict()` takes the
task's declared `shape` and the artefact it was given; `shape_defects()` counts FINDINGS - a citation INTO the
artefact under review that RESOLVES (through `resolve_location()`, the ONE reader extracted from the quote refuter
of D-3022, so the two cannot drift) AND carries at least 40 characters of reasoning beside it that states a defect
from a DECLARED vocabulary (`config/engine.yaml#fanout.answer_shapes.review`, 65 markers). The requirement is
DISCLOSED to the model (`shape_instruction()`, appended to the prompt by the same declaration that grades it), the
artefact coordinates are FROZEN into task.json so the grader, the retry, the receipt and the verifier all judge by
the shape the task was ASKED for, and a task that declares a shape nobody declared is FATAL at plan, before any
model is called.

**MEASURED ON THE EXACT BYTES OF LIMB 1, and the pair IS the point:**
`python3 pipeline/subagent_fanout.py citations --answer temp/t154_r5_review.md` -> **82 citations checked, 0
refuted, rc=0** - D-3022 CANNOT refuse this answer, because every location it names exists. Then
`python3 pipeline/subagent_fanout.py shape --answer temp/t154_r5_review.md --shape review --artifact
pipeline/research_run.py` -> **rc=1: "the answer carries 0 finding(s) stating a defect about
pipeline/research_run.py - a review must carry 1 - across 82 citation(s) into the artefact and 82 in total; every
citation RESOLVED, so this is a LISTING of true locations and not a review"**. The limiting case is now decided:
the answer was never FALSE, it was EMPTY OF ANY CLAIM, and a length floor cannot tell a review from a table of

The bytes are a DECLARED FROZEN CONTROL (`governance/evidence/BUG836_gemma_citation_list.md`, verbatim, 2,294 B,

**MEASURED 2026-10-15**, while landing T-163 (a new ladder line for `pipeline/subagent_fanout.py --selftest`, whose
declaration was appended after the existing 2026-10-15 fan-out declarations). `yaml.safe_load` of
`config/rail_registry.yaml` returns EIGHTEEN top-level keys where the file visibly declares NINE:

    schema_version, authority, ladder, recipes, ladder_receipt, dormant, writers, guards, commit_boundary
    + 'pipeline/research_run.py --selftest',          'pipeline/research_run.py status',
      'pipeline/model_loadability_probe.py',          'pipeline/hf_fetch_model.py --verify-only',
      'pipeline/omlx_engine_guard.sh',                'pipeline/oneshot_ask.py',
      'pipeline/subagent_fanout.py status',           'pipeline/omlx_retire_model.sh --model'

**ROOT.** `commit_boundary:` opens a block at line 242 whose keys are 2-space indented, and the 2026-10-15
declarations that follow it were appended at COLUMN 0. In YAML a mapping at column 0 after an indented block is
not a member of that block: it is a SIBLING of `commit_boundary` - and of `guards`. So those declarations sit in
the registry as keys no reader reads, which is the D-2649 shape exactly: a declaration with the wrong home.

**CONSEQUENCE.** `scripts/check_rail_registry.py#audit` iterates `cfg['guards']` ONLY, so its verdict - printed on
every `just health` - is a claim about 35 of the 43 declared guard classes. MEASURED: it printed "no declared guard
disagrees with the ladder" while EIGHT declarations (19%) were never compared with the ladder at all, four of them
`tri_state` classes on live instruments (`research_run.py status`, `oneshot_ask.py`,
`model_loadability_probe.py`, `subagent_fanout.py status`). This is BUG-826's class one layer down - an instrument
reporting a coverage it does not have - and it is the SAME structural defect BUG-832 filed against the session
provider: a home a decision names, with no reader in the repo. A misindented declaration is INERT, and inert is
indistinguishable from green.

**REMEDY (two limbs, and the second cannot land alone):**
 (a) THE HOME. The eight declarations name invocations that live in recipes this registry does not govern
     (`recipes: [health, health-deep]`, while `pipeline/research_run.py --selftest` is a line of
     `just research-selftest`). They therefore cannot be honoured as declared: either WIDEN `recipes:` to the
     recipes that run rails (research-selftest, model-loadability, engine-guard, cache-dry, status ...) or REMOVE
     the declarations and let those recipes own their own guards. Both are governance acts, so this is ONE
     decision and it is OWED.
 (b) THE LIMB THAT PREVENTS RECURRENCE. `check_rail_registry.py` must FAIL CLOSED on an unknown top-level key in
     its own registry (a registry whose schema is unchecked is a registry where a typo is a silent disarm, C16),
     proved by a known-answer control in its `--selftest`. Adding (b) alone would make `just health` RED, which is
     why it is registered WITH (a) as T-164 rather than half-landed here.

**EVIDENCE:** `python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('config/rail_registry.yaml')); print(len(d['guards']),
[k for k in d if '/' in k])"` -> `35` and the eight keys above. The T-163 line was moved INSIDE the mapping and
that entry IS pinned (`just health` runs it, the class matches, rc=0); the stray set is the eight pre-existing
declarations, untouched by this landing.

**R5 REVIEW OF THIS LANDING, BY A DIFFERENT FAMILY, THROUGH THE NEW PATH - AND THE FALSE NEGATIVE IT FOUND
(2026-10-15).** The generator may not verify itself (R5), so this module's own shape reader was reviewed by
`gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit` through the fan-out's front door, with a task that declared `shape: review` over
`pipeline/subagent_fanout.py` (task file `temp/t163_r5_review.yaml`). It was run as a MEASUREMENT of the whole new
path - plan, shape validation, prompt disclosure, the `--shape/--artifact` command, the grader, the receipt - and
not as a courtesy.

1. **THE GATE REFUSED A REAL FINDING (run `t163_r5b`, rc measured without a pipe).** The model answered 1,615 chars
   of genuine PROSE that stated a defect and named its location as a RANGE: "the most critical line ... is
   **338-342**" and "(lines 349-351)". The reader returned `0 finding(s) ... across 0 citation(s) into the artefact
   and 0 in total`, `citations` returned "none to check", and the workstream's terminal word was
   `TERMINAL: FAILED - rc=0, not a review: ...`. A grammar that reads only `path.py:111` had refused a located,
   predicated finding as if no location had been given - a FALSE NEGATIVE, which is the costly direction (D-3022:
   an over-strict guard is a disabled guard), and it was found by delegating the review rather than by reasoning
   about the code.
   **FIXED, and the fix is bounded by measurement.** `citation_sites()` learned the LINE RANGE (`lines N-M`, and a
   BOLDED `**N-M**`), attributed to the file the answer was TOLD it is about - a parameter the SHAPE reader passes
   and the quote refuter never does, so `citation_defects` is untouched: on the BUG-836 bytes it still returns
   **82 checked / 0 refuted**. A bare reference is attributed ONLY when exactly ONE artefact is declared (with two,
   `338-342` is ambiguous and is not counted); a range is read by its FIRST line, which must EXIST; and a bare line
   with no prose beside it is still not a finding. The answer is frozen as a second declared control
   (`governance/evidence/BUG836_gemma_prose_review.md`, `expect: an_answer`), so the gate's proof is now TWO-SIDED
   ON REAL MODEL BYTES: the listing must stay refused, this must stay accepted.

2. **THE WHOLE PATH, END TO END, AFTER THE FIX (run `t163_r5c`, exit 0).**
   `TERMINAL: DONE - rc=0, ok, 981 chars, 1 finding(s) for the declared review shape`; the receipt carries
   `shape: review`, `shape_findings: 1`, `answer_usable: true`, and the run reports `1/1 task(s) DONE`. The receipt,
   the task.json coordinates and the grader's own verdict agree, which is what "the shape is read" has to mean in
   practice and not only in a unit control.

3. **THE RESIDUAL THE REVIEWER POINTED AT IS REAL, AND IT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN PATCHED.** Both replies (1,615
   and 981 chars) argue that a listing could pass because `min_findings: 1` is satisfied by ONE good line inside an
   otherwise-degenerate answer. Its FACTS are wrong - it reads the docstring, and the measured listing IS refused -
   but the shape of the worry is right. Disposition, deliberately: **the shape gate is a FLOOR, not a quality
   bar.** `min_findings` is a DECLARED per-task number that any task may raise, and it is DISCLOSED to the model
   (`shape_instruction`), so a review that needs three findings declares three; adding a proportion limb now would
   be speculative machinery with exactly the false-negative risk just measured. Quality is the VERIFIER's job
   (R5/D-3022), and that is the boundary D-3029 draws. The knob is named here so the next session finds it instead
   of re-deriving it.

4. **ONE WORD CORRECTED IN THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN VOICE (error leak).** `retry()` printed `FATAL: the retry model ...
   IS the model that failed` and then `return 0` - a verdict the code never carried (the run's honest exit is
   decided by the receipt). It now reads `retry refused: ...`, same behaviour, no false FATAL. MEASURED in
   `t163_r5b`, where a task whose model IS the declared fallback hits this line by construction.

## BUG-837 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-15) - eight guard declarations in the rail registry were TOP-LEVEL keys, so the rail that reports "no declared guard disagrees with the ladder" never read them

**REMEDY (T-164/D-3030, landed 2026-10-15).** Three acts, each measured, none of them a comment:

1. **THE REGISTRY'S OWN SCHEMA IS CLOSED.** config/rail_registry.yaml now declares `schema: {keys: [...], required: [...]}`,
   and scripts/check_rail_registry.py reports class (iv) for any top-level key `schema.keys` does not list - and refuses a
   key shaped like a COMMAND LINE outright, which is this bug's shape exactly: eight command lines were read as sections.
   `schema` must list ITSELF (a closure that exempts its own description is not a closure), and `required` is now READ
   from the file (the hardcoded tuple is gone, C12) and includes `dormant`, `writers` and `guards`, because the rail's own
   closing sentence asserts something about each: an omitted section made that sentence VACUOUSLY true.
   MEASURED: 10 top-level keys, 0 strays; the rail now reads 36 declared guards (it covered 35 of the 43 declarations).
2. **THE EIGHT ARE DISPOSITIONED, NOT DELETED.** Two of them were also claims the ladder cannot support:
   `pipeline/hf_fetch_model.py --verify-only` is carried by NO justfile recipe, and `pipeline/subagent_fanout.py status`
   is written `|| true`, so its exit code is DISCARDED and no class can be pinned. They could not move inside `guards:`
   because a guard class is a claim a CHAINED ladder consumes, `recipes:` is [health, health-deep], and WIDENING it is not
   an option - scripts/run_ladder.py COLLECTS cfg["recipes"], so widening would make `just health-full` RUN the engine
   guard and the retirement script. Their fact - which operator lane carries which command, and whether that command is
   still there - is declared in config/capability_registry.yaml#lanes, whose reader checks all three limbs: the recipe
   exists, the command is in THAT recipe's body, and the command is in NO governed recipe.
   MEASURED, and this is the argument for a CHECKED declaration over a remembered one: the reader caught a real defect in
   the FIRST draft of that declaration - a lane was declared against a recipe named `task`, and the ladder carries `ask`
   (a numbered listing had been misread).
3. **THE PARSER'S SUBJECT WAS TOO NARROW.** `ladder_invocations` admitted only `python3`/`python` lines, so a FATAL rail
   written `bash ...` could not be declared AT ALL: the reader would answer a TRUE declaration with a FALSE fault ("an
   invocation the ladder does not contain"), which reads as "this class cannot be pinned" rather than "this class is
   unpinned". It now takes every DECLARING line except a bare echo, and justfile:136
   (`bash scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check || exit 1`) is pinned fatal so the widening is LOAD-BEARING.
   MEASURED: 160 invocations parsed (was 158), the `invoked` set unchanged (99), and the census lists
   `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check` for the first time.

**CONTROLS.** `python3 scripts/check_rail_registry.py --selftest` is now 19 known answers (5 new: an unknown top-level
section; the command-line-as-a-key shape; a closure that omits itself; a bash lane that IS nameable; a bash lane whose
declared guard disagrees), and the LADDER runs it (`just health`), because a control nothing runs is a comment (BUG-492).

## BUG-838 (HIGH - OPEN 2026-10-16) - the store census partitioned the hub DIRECTORY and called the result a set of models, so the store's own machinery entered the only class a deletion may come from

**MEASURED 2026-10-16** by reading the instrument against the store it measures. `pipeline/model_store_census.py`
measured EVERY entry of `~/.cache/huggingface/hub` and called the result "repos", so the partition's DOMAIN was a
directory listing rather than the model repos it holds. Three limbs, one class.

**(1) UNSOUND.** `.locks` (the hub's lock directory) and `version.txt` (its cache-format version) were counted as
"repo(s)" and fell into ORPHAN, because no engine entry resolves to them and no file under config/, pipeline/ or
scripts/ spells their names. ORPHAN is the only class a deletion may ever be proposed from (D-3004(3)) and
pipeline/safe_delete.py is the only deleter (R-D410), so a class that admits a non-member is not untidiness - it is
a deletion candidate that is not a model. The census's own line read "ORPHAN 8 repo(s)" where 6 were repos.

**(2) SELF-REFERENCE.** `blobs` - the hub's own blob-store root, 1118.7 MB - read DECLARED, because classify() asks
whether the repo's STEM appears in the text under config/, pipeline/ and scripts/, and THIS FILE spells "blobs" at
its own line 113. The instrument's vocabulary was acting as a declaration.

**(3) PROTECTION BY ACCIDENT.** The seven eval datasets were DECLARED - not protected - because config text happens
to mention their names. D-3014(2) states the rule ("a dataset is not a model and is never swept with model bytes")
and the DELETION_RECEIPT_20261015 names them "the eval instrument", but NOTHING ENFORCED IT: the recorded face
still lists datasets--TIGER-Lab--MMLU-Pro, datasets--HuggingFaceH4--MATH-500 and datasets--openai--openai_humaneval
as ORPHAN deletion candidates. Remove one citation and the eval instrument joins the candidate class.
`datasets--hotpotqa--hotpot_qa` alone is 359.2 MB - larger than the entire ORPHAN set (267.9 MB).

**CLASS.** The instrument's vocabulary outran its observations: BUG-804 (measured symlinks, called it bytes),
BUG-808 (a name that reads as on-disk, resolving to nothing), BUG-814 (a snapshot the census calls DECLARED on a
mention). What is new here is that the defect sat UPSTREAM OF EVERY COUNT - the partition had no declared domain, so
its membership was whatever the directory happened to hold, and the safety property D-3004(3) asserts could not
hold because the class it names had no membership rule.

## BUG-838 (CLOSED 2026-10-16) - the partition's DOMAIN is DECLARED and read, and the eval instrument is protected by a rule instead of by a citation

**REMEDY (T-136/D-3033).** `config/engine.yaml#model_store.census_domain` now DECLARES what the partition is a
partition OF (C12/D-402): `member_prefixes: [models--]` is the ONLY candidate class; `non_member_repo_prefixes:
[datasets--, spaces--]` are repos that are NEVER candidates (D-3014(2); `spaces--` is declared with zero members
rather than implied, the D-3031 practice); `store_metadata: [.locks, version.txt, CACHEDIR.TAG, blobs]` are not

inverse of the green-by-vacancy disease (BUG-487).

movement check reads (T-147/T-151) - of which model repos 123351.8 MB over 33 repo(s); LIVE 7 / PARKED 0 /

controls, where before it had NONE, among them that a dataset and the store machinery can never reach ORPHAN, that

## BUG-839 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-16) - a citation reader matched a path SEGMENT, so a harness home that exists was reported as a missing repo file

**MEASURED 2026-10-16, exposed by a face that had been RE-CUT rather than by a search.** Each face's LIVE region
carries the open-MUST task table, and T-157's row cites the goose harness home -
`~/.config/goose/config.yaml:311 reads active_provider: custom_deepseek`. `LIVE_PATH_RE` matched with `\b`, so
it returned `config/goose/config.yaml` - the segment that follows the dot - and `live_faults()` then demanded that
`REPO/config/goose/config.yaml` exist. It does not, so three faces were reported as "cites config/goose/config.yaml,
which does not exist - a citation whose subject is absent is an assertion (D-405)". The subject was NOT absent:
`~/.config/goose/config.yaml` exists (7,849 B, and its line 311 reads `active_provider: custom_deepseek`, which is
T-157's own evidence). The rail was reporting a claim the face never made - the false-fault direction of BUG-454
("a rail that cannot express a state is not a rail for that state").

**WHY IT SURFACED NOW - the fault was not new, its VISIBILITY was.** The T-157 row entered the derived block only
when `gov_sync --apply` re-cut the faces, so this rail had never read that row. A face nobody re-cuts is a checker
with nothing to check: the stale face had been HIDING a red rail, which is the BUG-819/T-151 family ("a face that
says measured and is stale") sitting on top of a false fault.

**REMEDY.** A citation must START a token - `(?<![\w./~-])` replaces `\b`, so `.config/...` is not a citation
while a line-initial, space-preceded, `(`-preceded or quote-preceded `config/...` still is. Two known-answer
controls land in the rail's own selftest, in BOTH directions: a home-relative citation makes no problem, AND a
genuinely dangling repo citation still FIRES beside the same home path, so the fix cannot blind the rule it
repairs. Measured after - `check_governance_faces.py --selftest` 46/46 and the live check rc 0.

**THE CLASS, KEPT.** A reader that infers "this is a claim about THIS repository" from a path-shaped substring will
meet a home-relative path eventually; the durable fix is T-157's - CENSUS the harness homes a decision names, so an
out-of-repo home is a DECLARED join instead of an inference from prose.

## BUG-840 (MED - OPEN 2026-10-16) - the DECLARED class is a MENTION INDEX, so a GOVERNANCE WRITE reclassified 267.9 MB with no byte moving

**MEASURED 2026-10-16, twice, in the same session.** `classify()` decides DECLARED by asking whether a repo's stem
or its last path segment appears ANYWHERE in the joined text of config/, pipeline/ and scripts/. At 01:01 the census
read **ORPHAN 6 repo(s) / 267.9 MB**, whose only member with bytes was a 267.8 MB encoder. Minutes later, after this
session's own landing wrote that repo's stem into T-136's evidence in `config/task_register.yaml`, the SAME census
read **ORPHAN 5 repo(s) / 0.0 MB, DECLARED 21 / 56700.7 MB**. Nothing left the disk. Verified rather than asserted -
the only new occurrence of the stem under the reference roots is the added evidence line, and the pre-existing
mentions in config/decisions.yaml name a DIFFERENT, superseded stem.

**WHY IT MATTERS, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Write a repo's name into the register and it LEAVES the candidate class;
delete or rename the mention and it ENTERS it. The first direction is fail-safe for a deletion, and it is how a
record protects a dependency by accident. The second is the hazard, and T-130 is the standing example - a
corpus-name RENAME touching roughly eighty references per stem. So the class an owner is shown as "declared" is not
a resolution, and any count taken from it is invalidated by the next prose edit: the D-2941 corollary firing on the
instrument's own INPUTS.

**THIS IS NOT THE DOMAIN DEFECT (BUG-838) AGAIN.** BUG-838 was WHAT may be counted, and it is fixed - the partition
now has a declared domain, so the hub's own machinery can never be a member. BUG-840 is HOW membership of DECLARED
is decided, and it is still a substring test. D-3018 already ruled the remedy for a SWEEP ("the byte-owner test is
RESOLUTION, not MENTION"); that ruling now has to reach the CLASSIFIER that feeds the sweep, because a sweep can
only be as honest as the classes it is handed.

**NOT FIXED HERE, AND SAID SO.** The resolution test is T-142's gate, which already asks for exactly it - "re-run
the census with a RESOLUTION test (does a served entry, config value or script resolve into these bytes?) and report
per repo: resolution, bytes, re-acquirability". Leaving the class as a text index while T-142 lands is a DECLARED
limit rather than a silent one: this entry is the declaration.

## BUG-840 - EFFECT (MEASURED, and the record CORRECTED rather than edited)

This landing's own prose quotes "ORPHAN 6 repo(s) / 267.9 MB". That was a true reading at 01:01 and it does NOT

was empty before this reclassification and is empty after it.

## BUG-840 (CLOSED 2026-10-16) - the DECLARED class was a MENTION INDEX; a RESOLUTION test replaces it, and the control that refuses a SENTENCE is named

**Status:** CLOSED (T-142/D-3034). The remedy is the same instrument, one rule deeper: pipeline/model_store_census.py#classify confers DECLARED only on a RESOLUTION, and what counts as one is DECLARED in config/engine.yaml#model_store.resolution_domain and READ from there (FATAL when absent or empty - BUG-487).

MEASURED 2026-10-16, same machine, same hour, by the owner's read-only probe (temp/t142_probe.py) and by the census: before - LIVE 7 / PARKED 0 / DECLARED 20-21 / ORPHAN 5-6, owner-owed 0, hub total 124837.5 MB; after - LIVE 6 / PARKED 1 / DECLARED 13 (56023.9 MB) / ORPHAN 13 (676.8 MB), owner-owed 0, hub total 124837.5 MB unchanged. THE DOMINANT DECLARING HOMES WERE THE REGISTERS THEMSELVES: in the probe, config/decisions.yaml and config/task_register.yaml carried most of the strings that declared the bucket, and the values of both registers are SENTENCES. A decision that mentions a model is a RECORD of a decision, not an owner of its bytes.

The three forms a resolution may take (D-3018: the byte-owner test is RESOLUTION, not MENTION): an ENGINE ENTRY whose realpath lies inside the repo dir; a VALUE that IS the reference (the full org/name or the bare name - a sentence is never equal to a model id); or a PATH that EXISTS and lies inside it (a citation whose subject is absent is an assertion, D-405). A string that merely CONTAINS a reference is recorded as a MENTION: reported in the audit, and it confers nothing.

CONTROL (BUG-492: a remedy whose control nothing runs is a comment): a_SENTENCE_that_mentions_a_model_does_NOT_declare_it; a_value_that_IS_the_reference_DOES_declare_it_full_id_and_bare_name; a_bare_name_belonging_to_ANOTHER_org_does_not_declare_THESE_bytes_but_is_still_a_mention; a_PATH_that_RESOLVES_inside_the_repo_declares_it_and_one_that_does_NOT_does_not; the_INSTRUMENT_own_vocabulary_cannot_declare_a_repo (the reader's own file is EXCLUDED by a declared list - BUG-838 limb 3, generalised); and an_EMPTY_exclude_list_is_FATAL_because_the_reader_would_declare_itself. 24/24 known-answer controls fire where the instrument had 13.

WHAT THE AUDIT NOW REPORTS (T-142's gate): per repo, the resolution evidence with its home and key path or line number, the bytes, the mentions it did NOT count, and whether the bytes can come back (FETCHABLE-BY-ID when the cache entry carries the declared refs/ marker - it was fetched by repo id and can be fetched again; LOCAL-ONLY otherwise). The mention-only remainder is 13 repos / 676.8 MB and every one of them is below config/engine.yaml#model_store.deletion_floor_bytes (268435456 B); the largest is typeform/distilbert-base-uncased-mnli at 267836416 B. So the owner-owed set is 0 by RESOLUTION as well as by the floor - a STRONGER statement than the floor alone, because it also NAMES the five repos the floor was protecting without saying why: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, Qdrant/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx, cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, minishlab/potion-base-32M, google/flan-t5-base.

## BUG-841 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-16) - LIVE was decided by NAME ACROSS STORES, so a cache copy read as if the engine were serving it

**Status:** FIXED (T-142/D-3034). classify() asked whether an entry NAME existed in the serving store, so a repo whose entry was PARKED read LIVE whenever the same name was also served from somewhere else.

MEASURED 2026-10-16, verbatim: ~/.omlx/_unloaded/Phi-4-mini-instruct-8bit resolves to hub/models--mlx-community--Phi-4-mini-instruct-8bit/snapshots/93b273a5497a4fcdcfb7ac00143565506b4f72e4 (5774.6 MB of blobs; 27 files) while the SAME NAME is served from ~/.omlx/models_stashed/Phi-4-mini-instruct-8bit (4098.0 MB; 14 files). The hub copy therefore read LIVE and its bytes sat inside the LIVE bucket (66651.0 MB) although the engine serves a DIFFERENT directory under that name - a claim about bytes that were not its subject.

REMEDY: serving_owners() - an entry is SERVED only when the serving store holds the NAME AND its TARGET lies inside these bytes. LIVE 7 -> 6, and the collision is REPORTED rather than resolved by taste: the face prints SAME NAME, DIFFERENT BYTES with both paths and the fact that the inventories differ. This is also why a duplicate is never offered by NAME (T-142): because the inventories are NOT equal, the hub copy is the only pristine copy of that fetch and NOTHING is offered for it. Had a same-name test alone been promoted to an offer, the census would have proposed deleting a unique fetch.

CONTROL: an_engine_entry_in_ANOTHER_repo_does_not_claim_this_one, plus the two same-name-copy controls, which fire in BOTH directions (redundant when the inventories are equal, PARKED and not offered when they differ).

**Status:** FIXED (T-146). The owner typed `pipeline/hf_fetch_model.py` and read "zsh: permission denied".

MEASURED 2026-10-16: pipeline/hf_fetch_model.py was -rw-r--r-- and carries #!/usr/bin/env python3 on its first line.
