## BUG-843 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-16) - the instrument PROSE contradicted the DIGEST it printed: a same-name copy read as unique because two file LISTS could never be equal

**Status:** FIXED (T-167/D-3035). The owner read his own store and asked whether the Phi-4 pair is a duplicate; the census said no, and the census was wrong.

MEASURED 2026-10-16, read-only, by this session: `~/.omlx/models_stashed/Phi-4-mini-instruct-8bit/model.safetensors` hashes to `84bcf5553d78094fd6fbe8d7b547a94c6b21996c4066a7a1e89ee4d347a50a24` at 4,076,012,072 B, and the CACHE copy's `model.safetensors` symlink resolves to `blobs/84bcf555...a24` - the same digest at the same size, so the two weight files are ONE set of bytes. The only names that differ are `.gitattributes` and `README.md` (present in the repacked directory, absent from the snapshot; 4,097,978,555 - 4,097,975,786 = 2,769 B, exactly those two files). Yet `pipeline/model_store_census.py` printed "they are NOT the same bytes", "the parked hub copy is therefore the only pristine copy of that fetch", and `same_weights: false` - one line away from the digest that disproves it.

ROOT CAUSE, two limbs. (1) Redundancy was asked of FILE INVENTORY EQUALITY (`held_inv == served_inv`, a frozenset of (name, size)), and a hub SNAPSHOT can never equal a REPACKED DIRECTORY: it is a subset by construction, so equality was unreachable and the copy could never be offered - the conservative direction, but reported as a FACT about the bytes rather than as the limit of the comparison. (2) The figure that made the sentence look measured - "27 files, 9872601143 B" - was a DOUBLE COUNT: `file_inventory` walks with `os.walk(followlinks=True)`, so a snapshot's symlinks resolve into the very blobs the same walk already counted, and 9,872,601,143 B is the repository (5,774,623,426 B of blobs) ADDED to the served directory (4,097,978,555 B) it holds a copy of. A walk that follows symlinks measured a content-addressed store twice - the very class this census exists to catch (BUG-804 failure 1) inside the census itself.

REMEDY: `config/engine.yaml#model_store.redundancy` DECLARES what a weight file IS (`weight_suffixes`), the proof (`digest: sha256`), the partial marker (`.incomplete`) and the bound (`max_weight_files: 64`), and it is read at import (FATAL when absent, empty, or a digest this reader does not implement). `weight_proof()` re-hashes EVERY weight file of the served twin from the bytes on disk and calls a copy redundant only when each matches by name, size and digest; the files that differ are NAMED beside it and a PARTIAL download is named too - MEASURED: 1,676,647,640 B of the same model sat in that repository under a `.incomplete` name, so the cache held a complete copy AND a half-download of the same file. The face now reads "REDUNDANT BY CONTENT - the weights are the same bytes ... these bytes may leave, and the name still resolves from the served copy", and the census offers 5,774.6 MB for the first time (rc 2, owner-owed).

CONTROL (BUG-492): 12 new known-answer controls over synthetic directories - the digest path is EXERCISED, not mocked. They hold both directions (the same content under different listings IS redundant; the same NAME and SIZE with different content is NOT, and the digest mismatch is named), a missing weight file, a served twin with no weight file at all, the declared bound, the `.incomplete` naming, an undeclared digest algorithm refusing BY NAME, and the fail-closed reads of an absent / empty / unimplemented redundancy rule. `model-store-census: 36/36 known-answer control(s) fire` (was 24).

## BUG-844 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-16) - pipeline/subagent_fanout.py can show a FAN-OUT while no delegated run leaves a trace: an async delegate has no declared budget and no start or end record, so a stalled, a finished and a cancelled subagent are ONE state to every later reader

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (remedy T-168, LANDED). MEASURED 2026-10-16, this session.

SYMPTOM (the owner's words): "how the fuck do I know if they progressing or not and timed out?" Three delegates were launched for independent read-only work. The harness then reported "cancelled before it finished" for all three. ONE had already written its artifact (`temp/draft_diagnose_skill_20261016.md`, 6,573 B) and was still in its closing turns; the other two had written nothing. NOTHING ON DISK DISTINGUISHED THOSE THREE STATES - there is no start record, no artifact claim, no budget, no timeout and no end record anywhere in this repository, so the only witness was the session transcript, which no later reader can join.

ROOT CAUSE: the delegation ECONOMY is measured (`config/delegation_economy.yaml`, cost tiers, the D2549 routing map) while the delegation ACT is not. `pipeline/omlx_delegate.py` and `scripts/delegation_economy.py` count what a call COSTS; nothing records that a call was MADE, what it was allowed to write, how long it had, whether the file it claimed to write exists, or whether the harness killed it. The peek surface reports activity (turn count, idle time, recent tool calls) but it is SESSION-SCOPED: it dies with the session and it is invisible to `just health`, to a handoff and to the next agent.

PROPOSED FIX (T-168): a declared delegate journal - a START row (task id, purpose, model, the exact files it MAY write, its wall budget) written BEFORE the call, an END row (outcome, artifacts VERIFIED ON DISK, wall time) written after - plus a `--status` reader that lists OPEN rows past their budget, wired as a rail, so a silent stall becomes a RED line instead of a shrug. Files it may write must be declared because two delegates on one file is a conflict nobody sees (C21/C23).

LANDED 2026-10-16 (T-168/D-3039). The trace EXISTS and is a RAIL. `scripts/delegate_journal.py` writes a START row BEFORE the call (purpose, model, the exact files the run MAY write, its wall budget) and an END row after it (state, a wall time MEASURED from the journal's own two rows, and artifacts VERIFIED ON DISK with their byte count and content stamp), and its `status` verb is wired into `just health` as a tri_state rail: 0 nothing is open | 1 a JOURNAL FAULT | 2 an OPEN run past its declared budget. The four states the old absence made indistinguishable are now four READINGS: working reads OPEN inside its budget, stalled reads OVERDUE, killed reads OPEN past its budget until an end row arrives, and succeeded reads ENDED with its artifacts' digests. THREE REFUSALS make the trace un-fakeable rather than merely available: a `done` whose artifact is ABSENT is REFUSED and the row STAYS OPEN, so a false success has no home in the file (the honest alternative, `--state failed`, is always available); a claim that resolves OUTSIDE this repository is refused (BUG-818c - work that leaves the tree leaves its receipts behind); and a file another OPEN run already holds - by equality or by CONTAINMENT - is refused BEFORE either runs (C21/C23: two delegates on one file is interleaving, and the loser is whoever wrote first). 37 known-answer controls, one per limb, run in the ladder (a control nothing runs is a comment, BUG-492), and the journal's own home, vocabulary and budget rule are read from ONE declaration (`config/agent_surface.yaml#logging`, every key REQUIRED and absent-is-FATAL) with the join registered in `pipeline/config_audit.py`. The DURABLE reading is the digest: run 1 approved the bytes before the lint fixes, run 2 the final bytes, and each end row records the artifacts and their stamps rather than a verdict - a verdict is evidence only for the digest it names (R5). THE DECLARED LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: this repository cannot INTERCEPT the harness's own `delegate` call, so the trace is a discipline the caller keeps - what changed is that keeping it is now ONE COMMAND, that the writer's first live start (which crashed on a virgin tree with FileNotFoundError, because a suffix proof needs a pre-image) is fixed and controlled, and that omitting it is visible to every later reader rather than being indistinguishable from a kill.

## BUG-845 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-16) - the CORE is harness-agnostic while the BINDING is scattered across five homes and config/decisions.yaml names none of them, so a harness swap is archaeology

**Status:** OPEN (remedy T-169). MEASURED 2026-10-16, read-only.

SYMPTOM: nothing in this repository says where the agent harness is bound. The core is genuinely agnostic - oMLX owns the models at 127.0.0.1:11435, the pipeline is deterministic Python, the registers are files, the rails read files, and MCP is the declared agent interface (C21/C25) - but the BINDING an agent needs sits in at least five places: `agent/skills/maxwell-os-SKILL.md`, `~/.config/goose/skills/maxwell-efficiency-goose.md`, `~/.config/goose/config.yaml` + `custom_providers/maxwell_omlx.json`, `AGENTS.md#delegate_rules` + `#models` (prose), and `config/agent_context.yaml` / `config/harness_policy.yaml`.

ROOT CAUSE: C21/C25 are enforced for INFRASTRUCTURE (every component behind a protocol) and for the AGENT INTERFACE (MCP, no agent-specific coupling in the engine), but nothing declared where the CLIENT of that interface is configured. So each harness addition appends another coupling that no file enumerates, and a swap cannot be checked - only attempted.

REMEDY (T-169): `config/agent_surface.yaml` DECLARES the core, the ONE adapter root, the external roots a swap re-points, the AGENTS.md sections that are adapter-owned text, and the rule that a PORTABLE artifact (a SKILL.md, a task, a decision) may not name a harness or a provider. The reader is `scripts/check_agent_surface.py` (a rail, still to be written - which is why this bug is OPEN and not FIXED): a forbidden name in a portable artifact, or a harness-specific path outside the declared roots, is a fault.

**FIXED 2026-10-16 (T-169/D-3042).** The remedy is LANDED, not promised: `scripts/check_agent_surface.py`
reads `config/agent_surface.yaml` and REFUSES - 19/19 known-answer controls in both directions, wired into
`just health` as two lines (selftest fatal, reading tri_state).

WHAT THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE DECLARATION GOT WRONG, and this is the part worth keeping: it put `agent/skills/**/SKILL.md`,
`config/task_register.yaml`, `config/decisions.yaml` and `governance/**` in ONE `portable_artifacts` list, so a reader
enforcing "a portable artifact may not name a harness" would have had to fault a decision that legitimately NAMES a
client (the T-138 row, D-3041) - or stay silent. Both directions were wrong, so the classes were SPLIT: a **portable**
artifact (a skill) may not NAME a client, while a **record** artifact (a register, a decision, a governance document)
may name one and may not BIND one. And the binding rule is enforced where a swap actually BREAKS - CODE - through a
declared register rather than through prose.

WHAT IT FOUND ON ITS FIRST LIVE RUN (the reason the rail is worth its controls): EIGHT sites name a client binding in
code, and THREE of them BIND rather than cite - `pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py` constructs the client home that
`config/agent_context.yaml#homes.harness_config` already declares, `pipeline/parallel.py` pops two client knobs by
their literal names that `config/agent_context.yaml#ratified.knobs` declares, and `pipeline/subagent_fanout.py` writes
a client binary path into generated shell inside the deterministic core. Registered as BUG-850, remedy T-175, reported
loudly (rc 2) with the row named - a debt that is counted AND declared, never a discovery (D-3040).

## BUG-846 (LOW - OPEN 2026-10-16) - governance/buglog.md is a REGISTER while the intake assessment is only a DOCUMENT: a rejected research finding has no register, so it can be re-proposed by the next reader as if it were new

**Status:** OPEN (remedy: D-3038 and the registry it declares). MEASURED 2026-10-16.

SYMPTOM: the 2026-10-14 intake (`governance/INTAKE_ASSESSMENT_20261014.md`) screened two external repositories and produced verdicts - MUST for tester-army's "the assertion decides, the agent only drives", SHOULD for a portable model-agnostic skill shape, WORTH for diagnosing-bugs / code-review / tdd as named procedures, for `.out-of-scope/` as a first-class negative, and for calibration (ECE) as a rail. SIXTEEN days later none of those verdicts had a home in `config/decisions.yaml` or `config/task_register.yaml`: the assessment is a DOCUMENT, and a document is not a register. The same failure direction already broke the other way once - a rejected idea re-proposed as new, which is what `.out-of-scope/` exists to prevent upstream.

ROOT CAUSE: verdicts are recorded where they were FORMED (a report) rather than where they are USED (the registers), so a future reader must find and trust the report. No artifact enumerated the accepted negatives.

REMEDY: D-3038 registers the intake as a REGISTER - each revelation gets a verdict in a decision, the accepted NEGATIVE (M3: no repo-wide shebang-equals-exec-bit invariant; the FORM rule stays, BUG-842) is recorded as a first-class decision rather than a silence, and the two adoptions that need building become T-169/T-170.

## BUG-847 (MED - FIXED 2026-10-16) - C11 read a SIBLING import as an undeclared third-party dependency, and the finding sat in the tree for a sitting because the only rail that reads it is a review

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (found by the R5 review of scripts/delegate_journal.py; declared by D-3039's measurement). MEASURED 2026-10-16.

SYMPTOM: `python3 scripts/r5_review_gate.py --file scripts/delegate_journal.py` reported the C11 layer RED - "Undeclared imports: model_store_sweep.py: imports `model_store_census` - not in stdlib, local, or known deps" - naming a file nobody was reviewing. The finding belonged to `pipeline/model_store_sweep.py`, which landed the day before, and no earlier rail had reported it.

ROOT CAUSE: the sweep reached its sibling through `import model_store_census`, made importable by a late `sys.path.insert(0, ROOT / "pipeline")`. To a static reader a BARE module name reached that way is indistinguishable from a package nobody declared, so C11 was RIGHT to refuse it: the defect was the FORM of the import, not the gate. The repository already declares the package form (`pipeline/stage0_convert.py`: `from pipeline import ingest_gate`) and the sweep did not use it.

REMEDY: `from pipeline import model_store_census as census` with the repository root on the path, and the two import statements ordered and separated as ruff's I001 requires; C11 now reads 123 files with every import declared. THE SECOND LIMB IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING: a C11 finding on a NEW file is only ever caught when that file is next reviewed or staged, so it can sit in the tree for a sitting - it was found here by a review of an unrelated file. The commit-boundary gate and the R5 review gate both read it for anything that touches the file again, so the remedy is recorded as a discipline (review a new file before it lands, not only before it is edited) rather than as a new rail.


## BUG-848 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the obvious way to fix the reader WOULD HAVE CONVERTED DUPLICATE WORKS: routing the DELTA rule through the canonical lookup makes a file the gate never decides, never records and never skips

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (same session, found by a PRE-EXISTING control, mechanised so it cannot return). MEASURED 2026-10-16.

SYMPTOM: the first landing of T-130 option (B) routed CANDIDACY through the same canonical lookup the decision uses,
which looked like consistency ("one rule, both readers"). The pre-existing control
`a_noise_suffixed_candidate_collapses_to_its_corpus_stem_and_is_deferred` went RED: `corpus name defects` counts
unchanged, delta still 0, but a noise-suffixed duplicate of an ingested work was no longer a candidate AT ALL.

ROOT CAUSE (MEASURED in `pipeline/stage0_convert.py:202`): stage0 computes the books it converts as the corpus MINUS
`report["deferrals"]` — the set this door NAMES. A file the delta rule absorbs is therefore never decided, never named
in the deferral receipt and never skipped: it is CONVERTED, i.e. ingested as a second work under a second name — the
outcome BUG-780 measured 530 rows of — while the door's own reading still said `0 candidates`. The delta rule is about
VISIBILITY; the canonical lookup is about IDENTITY. Sharing one implementation is right; sharing one RULE is a hole.

WHY NO RAIL CAUGHT IT: every READING stayed green (0 candidates, rc unchanged, counts unchanged). The only thing that
moved was a CONTROL, and only because the control asserted a REASON and not a count — the same shape as BUG-787/798
(a reading on the wrong surface stays green).

FIX (three parts, none of them documentation): (1) candidacy is its own DECLARED key
(`config#identity.candidate_lookup`: exact_name, exact_path) and `candidate_lookup()` REFUSES a list that is not a
SUBSET of `record_lookup` — so the only way back into the trap is a config edit that fails closed; (2) the same edit
exposed a THIRD DEFERRAL STATE the pre-B door could not reach: a candidate whose record is found ONLY by a non-exact
lookup is a work the store ALREADY HOLDS (the corpus holds it under a variant name, or the file IS the record's file
renamed, its recorded `source_path` gone) — it is now DEFERRED (`already_ingested_by_canonical_name`, naming the record
it matched) rather than admitted, which is what makes T-172's rename safe; (3) the weaker path stays ALIVE by control:
a record with no author|title still defers on its sanitized stem (a control that proves only the new path can pass
while the old one dies silently is not a control, BUG-492).

ACKNOWLEDGED LIMIT: the four deferral REASONS (`same_work_identity`, `same_sanitized_stem`, `byte_identical`,
`already_ingested_by_canonical_name`) are code-level tokens, not a declared vocabulary; a future hardening could
declare them, and this entry records that they are not declared rather than implying that they are.


## BUG-849 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — pipeline/harness_contract.py reads the DEFAULT client's declared provider as UNBOUND, but nothing reads the CONSEQUENCE (the engine's own request counter), so the everyday path can leave the machine while every declaration looks correct

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (T-174, owner word "T-174 bound"; its census is T-157, landed in the same act).

FIX (measured, on the DECLARED path only — no hand edit of the owner's file):
`python3 pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py --apply-flip` bound the harness home to the declared provider and the
declared agent-loop model — backups beside the home, the written file READ BACK, and both values resolved by
POINTER from config/engine.yaml#harnesses.goose_provider_id and
config/model_assignments.yaml#harness_roles.AGENT_LOOP_SHORT.model. MEASURED BEFORE: a DIRECT headless run (the
everyday path, no wrapper) answered `PONG` with the engine's own counter standing still at 594833. MEASURED
AFTER: the same run moved it 594833 -> 594835. The counter now has a READER
(scripts/check_harness_homes.py prints it from the DECLARED home config/agent_context.yaml#homes.engine_stats),
so the witness is a line in `just health` rather than a probe somebody remembers to run — and the rail that
reads the home reports every fact BOUND at rc 0 where it reported TWO CONFLICTS (this one and the model pin)
minutes earlier. Revert is one command: `python3 pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py --rollback`.


SYMPTOM (read, not inferred): `config/engine.yaml#harnesses.goose_provider_id` declares `maxwell_omlx` and
`~/.config/goose/config.yaml` has that provider `enabled: true` — while the SAME file sets
`active_provider: custom_deepseek`, `GOOSE_PROVIDER`/`GOOSE_MODEL` are ABSENT from the environment this session
runs in, and `DELEGATE-001` already records `custom_deepseek` as unusable (a `reasoning_content` passthrough bug).
So the everyday driver of this repository can be answering from a cloud provider that the repo's own routing map
forbids and that C1/C3 (sovereign, no marginal cost) do not allow as a default.

MEASURED 2026-10-16 BY THE REPOSITORY'S OWN RAIL (this is the part I first got wrong, corrected before commit):
`python3 pipeline/harness_contract.py` reads **rc 2 (OWNER-OWED)** with `GOOSE_PROVIDER`, `GOOSE_MODEL` and
`GOOSE_CONTEXT_LIMIT` all **UNBOUND**, and it states the consequence itself — *"the harness will use its OWN
defaults for the names above (C1/C22: those defaults are a cloud price tier, not a local budget)"*. So the UNBOUND
state IS registered (T-132/D-3000 owns the BINDING and `config/agent_context.yaml#ratified.knobs.trigger` is the
one home) and IS visible in the ladder. THIS ENTRY DOES NOT RESTATE THAT FACT (C12): it records the two things
that rail cannot say.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (2026-10-15, governance/HARNESS_UTILIZATION_20261015.md §6): a headless run answered PONG,
rc 0, while the LOCAL engine's request counter did not move — i.e. the traffic left the machine. The counter, not
the config, is the witness.

ROOT CAUSE: the D-3034 shape one layer out — a DECLARATION that nothing RESOLVES in the process that acts on it. A
provider id in a policy file is not an environment; an enabled provider is not a bound provider. T-132/D-3003 hit
the same wall for the CONTEXT CONTRACT and the repo's answer was to bind the environment from ONE home
(`pipeline/harness_env.py --exec`, `scripts/bind_harness_env.sh`), whose own header names this exact case: a
harness started OUTSIDE a shell, including the desktop app.

WHAT THE RAIL CANNOT SAY, and why this is still a bug rather than a duplicate of T-132:
  (i) it measures the ENVIRONMENT, not the CONSEQUENCE. Nothing in the ladder reads the engine's own request
      counter, so the day a binding is dropped — or bypassed — the contract line goes back to rc 2 while nobody
      learns whether the traffic left. Same family as BUG-787/798: a reading taken on the wrong surface stays
      green, and here the wrong surface is a config the RIGHT surface (a counter) disagrees with.
  (ii) THE EVERYDAY PATH IS AN APP LAUNCH, which does not pass through the wrapper at all: the binding is a
      CHILD-process contract (`pipeline/harness_env.py --exec`) plus a shell helper
      (`scripts/bind_harness_env.sh`), and the desktop driver starts outside both. A contract that only holds for
      the launches that remember it is exactly what T-132 was ratified to end.

REMEDY (T-174, owner-visible): launch the default client through the DECLARED binding — `python3
pipeline/harness_env.py --exec /Applications/Goose.app/Contents/Resources/bin/goose run -t "<text>"` — or bind the
app's own environment the same way, then RE-MEASURE the engine counter instead of trusting the declaration. Making
`active_provider` itself local is a ONE-LINE change to the owner's harness home and is deliberately NOT taken by a
session: the provider in effect is the one serving the session that would be editing it.

ACKNOWLEDGED LIMIT: nothing in the ladder reads the engine counter today, so this fault can recur silently the
moment a binding is dropped. THE WITNESS'S HOME, MEASURED 2026-10-16: the counter is `total_requests` in the
engine's own stats file under the app-support directory (~/.omlx/stats.json) - a file, on disk, that NO script in
this repository reads (the repo has the ENGINE's health endpoint and the CLIENT's ledger, and neither carries a
request count). So the probe below is a hand measurement, and the reader belongs to this row: the check is
`python3 -c "import json,os;print(json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.omlx/stats.json')))[\"total_requests\"])"`
before and after ONE headless run through the declared path - a RISE is the proof, a still number means the run
left the machine (the agreed form of the command is in agent/adapters/goose/wiring.md#run-it). MEASURED 2026-10-16, 12:44: through the DECLARED path the counter ROSE 594825 -> 594828 and the run answered in 19.0s on the declared LOCAL model, so the wrapper DOES bind the provider it declares - the fault is exactly and only the everyday path that bypasses the wrapper (BUG-849 stands, and its mechanism limb is now a reading rather than a hypothesis). The durable monitor belongs with T-157 (census the harness homes a decision names)
rather than in a second home for the counter.

## BUG-851 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the door's rc 2 folded a STORAGE class into "identity is unresolved", so accepting the marker class opened the ingest door without either reading naming the item that drove the refusal

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (the T-173 acceptance, D-3043). Found by the forensic audit OF that acceptance — the audit asked what the acceptance would change BEYOND the class, and the answer was the door itself.

SYMPTOM: `scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py --gate` printed "REFUSED at the door: identity is unresolved, so a run
would mint a corroboration claim its own evidence contradicts (task T-129/T-131)" while the ONLY owner-owed item was
the 459-stem ingest-site MARKER class — a class the same gate documents as "a DIFFERENT defect class than the
whitespace debt", whose remedy is a WRITE, and whose names the door's own `_key()` strips before any comparison
(MEASURED 2026-10-15, BUG-799). Both readings were correct about the COUNT and silent about the DRIVER.

ROOT CAUSE: one tri-state rc carried two unlike facts — "identity is unresolved" (an epistemic state about the
corpus) and "a counted class is declared owner_owed" (a scheduling state about a remedy). Because the marker class
was the LAST owner-owed item, accepting it (owner word 2026-10-16, T-173) flipped the ingest reading to rc 0 in one
line of config, and the sentence printed above the flip would have described the new state just as confidently as
the old. Nothing in either reading could have said which item moved.

REMEDY (landed with the acceptance, D-3043): an accepted class is declared PER CLASS and is still COUNTED and
PRINTED with its count, its word and its row; the reader prints one line per counted class DERIVED from the report
instead of a literal (the literal said "ingest-site markers 459 (OWNER-OWED, T-173)" and could not have said
anything else, whichever way the register moved). MEASURED after: the marker class appears under
`accepted_debt.classes` with its word and row, `--gate` reads rc 0, 0 delta candidates are pending (so the opening
is operationally neutral today), and the refusal that remains is genuine identity ambiguity.

CONTROL: `an_accepted_class_is_counted_printed_and_not_an_rc_2_trigger`, whose fixture is measured in BOTH
directions — it OWES the class while the disposition is `owner_owed` and stops owing it while accepted, so the
control cannot pass by counting nothing (20/20 controls green).

ACKNOWLEDGED LIMIT: the door's rc is still ONE number. What changed is that the reading names its driver per class,
so a future acceptance cannot move the door silently.

## BUG-850 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py, pipeline/parallel.py and pipeline/subagent_fanout.py each BIND a client binding by hand, so the ONE declared home is not the only home

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (T-175/D-3046). MEASURED 2026-10-16 by `scripts/check_agent_surface.py` (19/19 known-answer controls when it was found; 21/21 after the class is measured), the rail T-169 landed.

FIX (three sites, each the remedy its own row named - and no row was DELETED to make a number look good):
SITE 1 MOVED - `agent/adapters/goose/apply_provider_flip.py`, because a file whose whole subject is ONE named
client's configuration home is that client's mechanism, and the surface's own rule puts it under `adapter.roots`;
the register row comes off because its hits are now INSIDE a declared root, which is where the rail says a binding
BELONGS. SITE 2 DECLARED - `config/agent_context.yaml#worker_env.strip` names the client knobs a pipeline worker
must not inherit, each with its reason, read by ONE reader (`pipeline/harness_env.py#worker_strip`) in the PARENT
and passed to each worker as initargs; MEASURED in a real two-worker pool - a parent holding both names in a
sentinel value sees them ABSENT in every pooled worker and untouched in the parent. SITE 3 DECLARED -
`config/agent_surface.yaml#adapter.provider_bindings.goose.client_bin` plus `#adapter.executor` (declared ONCE,
because the wrapper is harness-agnostic); the fanout's `agent` mode now invokes the declared executor with the
declared binary and writes neither into generated shell. MEASURED AFTER: the live register declares FIVE sites,
NO owed row, and the rail reads rc 0 where it read rc 2 with three debts.

SYMPTOM: `config/agent_surface.yaml` declares ONE binding home (`config/agent_context.yaml`) and the engine's own
integration module, and the first live reading of the new rail found three code sites that do the binding by hand:
`pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py` joins the client's home path itself (with a config-env override) although
`config/agent_context.yaml#homes.harness_config` declares that home; `pipeline/parallel.py` pops two client knobs by
their literal names although `config/agent_context.yaml#ratified.knobs` declares them; `pipeline/subagent_fanout.py`
writes the client's BINARY PATH into a generated shell script. Each is invisible to every existing rail: they are not
portable artifacts (nothing scans code for a binding), and they are not a second DECLARATION (nothing compared a
constructed path with the declared home).

ROOT CAUSE: C21/C25 were enforced for INFRASTRUCTURE and for the AGENT INTERFACE, and the CLIENT-SIDE couplings
accumulated where no rail looked - the same shape as BUG-845 one layer down. A declaration with no reader is a
comment (D-3034), and the first three sites the reader found were all second homes for facts the repo already owns.

REMEDY (T-175): each site resolves its name, home or binary from the declared home rather than restating it, and the
register SHRINKS (ceiling 8 -> 5, shrink-only, D-3023). Until then the rail reports them LOUDLY with the row named.

ACKNOWLEDGED LIMIT (narrowed 2026-10-16 by D-3046, not closed): `scripts/check_governance_faces.py` and
`scripts/check_agent_surface.py` are declared `control_fixture`, because a known-answer control must CONTAIN the shape
it proves the rail detects. The class is now MEASURED - its shape must sit in CODE, never in a docstring - so a
CITATION can no longer hide there; what remains is that a fixture and a real binding look alike in bytes, which is
why the ceiling is shrink-only and why a `control_fixture` row is a claim a reader must be able to check by hand.

## BUG-852 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the binding register's CLASS was ASSERTED and never measured, so a row whose remedy had already landed kept the ladder reading LOUD and the count of owed sites was a promise rather than a reading

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (T-175/D-3046; `scripts/check_agent_surface.py` 21/21 known-answer controls, two of them new).

FILE / LINES: `scripts/check_agent_surface.py` (`site_faults`/`binding_hits`) reading `config/agent_surface.yaml#adapter.binding_sites.sites` → the row for `pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py`.

SYMPTOM (read, not inferred): `python3 scripts/check_agent_surface.py` printed THREE `OWED` lines and rc 2, among them
`OWED pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py (row T-175) — it CONSTRUCTS the client home (Path.home()/.config/... with a
GOOSE_CONFIG override)` — while the file had stopped constructing anything one act earlier (T-174: the home is RESOLVED
from `config/agent_context.yaml#homes.harness_config`). The rail was RESTATING the register, so a discharged site kept a
whole ladder line loud and the honest number of owed sites (two) could not be read off the ladder.

ROOT CAUSE: the register declares a CLASS per site, and the rail used that class as the disposition (`owed` ⇒ loud)
without ever testing it against the file. MEASURED with the instrument that now exists: of that file's SIX shape hits,
THREE sit inside the module docstring (prose) and three are code, so the row's claim had become FALSE while the shape
itself was still present — exactly the state the existing "no longer carries a declared shape" fault cannot catch.

FIX (MEASURED, both directions): comments and triple-quoted blocks are BLANKED (line numbers preserved, so a hit is
tested against the same line in code); a site declared `prose_citation` must hold EVERY shape it carries in prose, and a
site of any other DECLARED class must hold at least one in CODE. Both directions are controlled:
`a_site_declared_owed_whose_shape_is_only_PROSE_is_a_fault_D3046` and
`a_site_declared_a_citation_whose_CODE_carries_the_shape_is_a_fault_D3046`. WHICH classes quote is itself declared
(`rules.quoting_classes`), so the rail hardcodes no vocabulary (C12). The three owed rows were then remedied for real
(T-175: one MOVE into the adapter root, two declarations) and the live reading is rc 0 with NO owed site.

ACKNOWLEDGED LIMIT: `control_fixture` remains the one class that could hide a binding — its shape must now be in CODE, so
the residue is narrower (a fixture and a real binding genuinely look alike in bytes) but it is not gone. The shrink-only
ceiling is what keeps that from being a free pass.

## BUG-853 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the default client's binding home named a launch form the engine does not serve: `omlx launch goose` is absent from the engine's own integration list, so the adapter's wiring doc described an invocation that cannot run

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (T-175/D-3046; the doc is corrected in place and the form that EXISTS is declared).

FILE / LINES: `agent/adapters/goose/wiring.md:3-4` (the claim) and its "the client's own wiring module" table row.

SYMPTOM: the adapter home said the wiring "is the engine's own module ... `omlx launch goose` runs it". MEASURED
2026-10-16: `omlx launch list` prints NINE integrations — claude, codex, codex_app, opencode, openclaw, hermes, pi,
copilot, dsh — and `omlx launch --help` accepts exactly those; **goose is not among them**. The engine WIRES CLIENT TOOLS;
goose is the client this repository runs BY DEFAULT and no engine integration for it exists.

ROOT CAUSE: a plausible sentence written from the shape of the neighbouring tools and never executed. It also EXPLAINS
the third hand-bound coupling (BUG-850 site 3): with no engine integration to call, the fanout wrote the client's binary
path into generated shell by hand — the coupling existed because the declared alternative did not.

`config/agent_surface.yaml#adapter` declares the two facts that exist — `executor` (the wrapper that binds the ratified

## BUG-855 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the routing-debt fault named NO item: the list it is about was built by comparing the SINGULAR item class with the PLURAL ceiling token, so a 223-item worklist read as "some debt somewhere"

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (found by this act's forensic audit; `scripts/resolve_route.py --selftest` gains one control).

FILE / LINES: `scripts/resolve_route.py:398` — `grown = [i.id for i, c, _ in rows if i.cls == cls ...]`, inside `for cls in ("tasks", "bugs")`.

SYMPTOM (read, not inferred): `python3 scripts/resolve_route.py --check` read rc 1 with *"(vi) ROUTING DEBT GREW:
223 open bugs resolve to no declared capability, against a declared ceiling of 222 (SHRINK-ONLY ...). Declare the
route, or disposition the item - never raise the ceiling. Now unrouted: "* — and then NOTHING. `Item.cls` is the
SINGULAR class token ("bug"/"task") while the loop token is the PLURAL ceiling key ("bugs"/"tasks"), so the
comprehension matched no row: the ONE fault whose entire purpose is to name the items named none of them. It was
found by hand, while attributing this session's debt growth to a new bug — the reader had to bisect a 223-id
population because the rail would not print it.

ROOT CAUSE: a plural/singular mismatch between two vocabularies that live in the same function. The `debt` dict
builds the same comparison correctly (`i.cls == "bug"`), which is exactly why the fault FIRED with the right count
and the right ceiling and still could not say WHICH items produced them.

FIX + CONTROL: the loop derives the singular (`cls[:-1]`). The new control asserts the IDS are printed — never that
the fault fires — because a fault that names nothing is what passed the old control:
`debt_grew_names_the_bugs_it_is_about` (a synthetic world with two unrouted BUGS against a ceiling of one, both ids
required in the sentence). MEASURED AFTER: the live check prints `Now unrouted: BUG-099, BUG-151, BUG-159, ...`.

## BUG-856 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the route graph owned ITSELF nowhere, so a finding about `config/capability_registry.yaml` could never route and joined the unrouted worklist by construction

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (found while routing this act's own bug; `config/capability_registry.yaml` gains the `route_graph` capability).

FILE / LINES: `config/capability_registry.yaml` (the capabilities list) and the join in `scripts/resolve_route.py`.

SYMPTOM (MEASURED 2026-10-16, by listing every capability's `owns`): NO capability owned `scripts/resolve_route.py`
or `config/capability_registry.yaml` — the two artifacts whose whole subject IS routing were the only ones the graph
could not route. A finding about the route graph therefore lands in the unrouted population (223 of 225 open bugs
that day) BY CONSTRUCTION, and the register's own reason for that population ("a bug routes only when its title
names a declared capability's artifact") becomes a closed loop: the artifact that would have to be named is owned by
nobody.

ROOT CAUSE: the registry enumerated the pipeline's subsystems and never itself. A graph whose own reader is not a
node has an edge it cannot draw — and the consequence is measurable: the census that reports the unrouted debt
cannot report the debt of the thing that reports it.

FIX: a `route_graph` capability (kind script, entrypoint `python3 scripts/resolve_route.py --check`, check `--selftest`,
owns both paths) whose receipt is a COMPOSED pointer into its own registry —
`config/capability_registry.yaml#routing_debt.measured` — because what this capability leaves behind is exactly the
shrink-only debt reading it maintains and refuses to raise, not a separate artifact. MEASURED AFTER: a finding
titled with the registry's own path ROUTES, and the open-bug debt is back at the declared ceiling of 222.

## BUG-857 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-16) — governance/buglog.md could be APPENDED TO and never QUERIED: no artifact computed which findings share a shape, so a later reader re-derived history by reading a 1.6 MB log, and 26 closed findings left nothing anyone can find (remedy: config/bug_recall.yaml)

**Status:** OPEN (remedy: D-3047 and the rail it declares, LANDED). MEASURED 2026-10-16.

SYMPTOM: the register is the repository's memory of what went wrong, and it could answer only two questions — how many findings exist, and what state each is in (the census's own 620 ids, 224 open / 396 closed). It could not answer the three a LATER reader asks: which findings are CHRONIC, which CLOSED findings left no TRACE, and which findings are NEIGHBOURS of a given one. MEASURED, read-only, before any repair: (a) 26 closed findings name no artifact, no ruling and no control — a fix a later reader cannot open, cannot re-run and cannot watch go red; (b) 10 OPEN findings carry three or more heading events, i.e. they have been re-characterised at least twice without being closed, and BUG-712 carries TWELVE while BUG-736/737/748/749 carry five each — the register's own census face already counted this (`events`) and NOTHING read it; (c) 111 cited references resolve against NOTHING (D-3034's currency, in the register); (d) 79 references are cited by more than twenty findings, which is the measure of how much of the register is common substrate rather than signal.

ROOT CAUSE: knowledge was recorded where it was FORMED (a log entry, a hand-maintained recall map) rather than where it is USED (a derived reading). BUG-846 measured the same failure from the other side — verdicts living in a document rather than a register — and `governance/CONTEXT_INDEX.md` calls itself the RECALL MAP while being a document that can drift from the register it summarises by construction. The consequence is not missing data: it is missing RECALL, so the same defect family is re-derived by each new reader (BUG-852 was BUG-492's shape rediscovered; BUG-856 was D-3034's shape rediscovered) and a closed finding with no trace can be reintroduced silently.

REMEDY: D-3047 — the register's recall is DERIVED from the register and its declared homes. One reader (scripts/check_bug_recall.py, 20/20 known-answer controls, READ-ONLY, no LLM, no embedding, no writes) plus one declared home (config/bug_recall.yaml) fold the register through the parser that already owns the fold (D-2646, never a second implementation) and produce three CEILINGED readings plus the RETRIEVE step:

FIX MEASURED AFTER (2026-10-16): `python3 scripts/check_bug_recall.py` reads 620 findings and reports untraced_closed 26 / chronic_open 10 / unresolved_reference 111, each against a declared shrink-only ceiling set from its own measurement plus one slot; `--recall BUG-850` names 13 neighbours ranked by strength (the strongest being BUG-815 at 100% and BUG-852 at 100%, with the ruling home's D-3046 beside it), the three rulings the finding cites that RESOLVE, and the capability that owns each artifact it names — a reading that took one command and previously took an archaeology session. The relation is deliberately narrow: a reference cited by more than twenty findings is EXCLUDED as common substrate (79 of them, COUNTED in the output), a neighbour must share at least two rare references (23 findings dropped for thinness on the BUG-850 query, COUNTED), and a finding related only by MENTIONING a sibling is not a neighbour at all (the class rule trace_sufficiency already declares). THE HONEST LIMIT: `unresolved_reference` mixes a stale repository path with a path that belongs to a home OUTSIDE the repository (a citation written without its `~/` prefix, e.g. ~/.config/goose/config.yaml), so that class is a worklist of citations to LOOK AT and not a verdict on each one.

## BUG-858 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-16) — governance/buglog.md carries NO entry for BUG-492, the most-cited rule in this repository: 128 files cite it (53 lines of the justfile alone) and the census folds straight from BUG-491 to BUG-493

**Status:** OPEN (remedy: promote the register's own text into a heading, or re-point the citations — T-178). FOUND 2026-10-16 by scripts/check_bug_recall.py's FIRST live run, through the `finding` trace class.

SYMPTOM: `BUG-492` is cited 128 times across the repository — 92 files under scripts/, 14 under config/, 14 under governance/, 7 under pipeline/ and 53 separate mentions inside `justfile` — always as the standing rule "a control nothing runs is a comment". MEASURED: the register has NO HEADING for it anywhere (zero lines matching a heading at any hash depth), so the census's own fold skips it (BUG-491 → BUG-493) and the id is not an id the register can resolve. A reader who follows one of the 128 citations arrives at nothing, and the rule that most of this repository's rails are justified BY cannot be read in the register that justifies it. Its content does exist, but as prose INSIDE other entries (58 mention lines in the register itself, e.g. the guard_call_sites finding recorded within another bug's body).

ROOT CAUSE: D-3034's own distinction, at the register level — a value that MENTIONS a thing declares nothing, and only a RESOLUTION confers identity. A heading resolves an id; 58 mentions do not. The id therefore entered the repository's working vocabulary (rails, justfile comments, docstrings) without ever entering the register, and no rail compared the two populations because nothing read a citation's resolvability.

REMEDY (T-178): either PROMOTE the register's own recorded text into a `## BUG-492` heading — preserving the original wording and noting the promotion, never re-writing history (C12/D-2642) — or RE-POINT the 128 citations to the entry that actually carries the rule. The first is preferred: it makes 128 citations resolve in one act. Whichever is chosen, the act must be measured by the same reading that found it: `python3 scripts/check_bug_recall.py` must stop reporting a `finding:BUG-492` that resolves against nothing, and the census must carry the id.

## BUG-859 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — justfile and config/task_register.yaml TAUGHT a command whose path stopped existing when agent/adapters/goose/apply_provider_flip.py MOVED: the owner ran it and got No such file or directory (remedy: config/capability_registry.yaml#lanes)

**Status:** FIXED (2026-10-16). FOUND by the owner's own report ("your manual command doesn't work"), then MEASURED.

SYMPTOM: the ladder's own comment beside the harness-homes rail, and T-174's gate text, both told a human to run the writer at its PRE-T-175 path under `pipeline/`. MEASURED 2026-10-16: `ls pipeline/apply_provider_flip.py` → No such file or directory, while the file itself is alive at `agent/adapters/goose/apply_provider_flip.py` (21031 B, mode 644) and `agent/adapters/goose/wiring.md` had carried the CORRECT path since T-175. So the instruction a human was handed and the file the repository runs had diverged, and the divergence was invisible because NOTHING read the two together: 14 sites named the old path (justfile comments, a session handoff, task rows, an earlier decision record) and none of them is a reader.

ROOT CAUSE: a manual command is a CLAIM about a path, and it was living in comments, handoffs and prose — three homes that no rail compares with the file system. T-164/BUG-837 had already declared the fix for this class (an OPERATOR LANE: an entry point a human runs, declared in `config/capability_registry.yaml#lanes` and CHECKED against the recipe), and the writer had never been declared as one. A path that moves while the prose stays is not a documentation problem: it is a dangling reference in the one place a human is told to look.

FIX MEASURED AFTER (2026-10-16): `config/capability_registry.yaml#lanes` declares `provider-flip` (recipe `provider-flip`, cmd `python3 agent/adapters/goose/apply_provider_flip.py --dry-run`, produces reading, capability `harness_adapter`), the recipe exists in `justfile` with that exact command, and `scripts/resolve_route.py --check` now REFUSES a lane whose recipe or command is absent (rc 0 live). The `--dry-run` form is declared rather than implied: the owner's command now states, in its own bytes, that it writes nothing. The stale path in the ladder comment was corrected IN PLACE (a live claim in a rail, not a record); the pre-T-175 path is preserved in this entry and in D-3044/D-3046 as the history it is.

## BUG-860 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — scripts/normalise_corpus_names.py BUILT A GLOB from a filename, so a name beginning with `*` made the reference census CRASH instead of counting: two live library rows could not be planned at all (remedy: glob.escape)

**Status:** FIXED (2026-10-16). FOUND by feeding the shared reader a population it had never seen.

SYMPTOM: MEASURED 2026-10-16, running the new T-176 planner over the owner's library: `ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component`, raised from `_stage_surface`'s `root.rglob(f"*{stem}*")`. The stem in question is `*Nina_N_rgaard,_Beatrix_Busse,_Roc_o_Montoro]_Ke(z-lib.org)`, and a second live row (`*[Rob_Carter,_Philip_B._Meggs,...`) fails the same way: a leading `*` closes the pattern early and the glob parser sees `**` as a path component.

ROOT CAUSE: the stem is DATA and the pattern is CODE, and the reader concatenated them into one string. The corpus population this reader was first written for happened to contain no glob metacharacter, so the defect was invisible for one act — the same shape as BUG-798 (a filename-only census read a false green) one level down: there the population was measured wrongly, here it CRASHED, and a reader that crashes on the row it was asked about cannot refuse it, which is precisely the fail-closed duty it carries.

FIX MEASURED AFTER: `glob.escape(stem)` — the name is a name again. The two rows now reach the planner's refusal vocabulary instead of raising, and the whole library (1254 defective names) plans in 42 s.

## BUG-861 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the 11 known-answer controls of scripts/census_source_names.py ran in NO ladder line for a full act: a control nothing runs is a comment (BUG-492, in its smallest possible form)

**Status:** FIXED (2026-10-16). FOUND while wiring the rename plan into the ladder.

SYMPTOM: `scripts/census_source_names.py` shipped in D-3045 with 5 known-answer controls and a `--selftest`; MEASURED 2026-10-16: `grep -n census_source_names justfile config/rail_registry.yaml` returned NOTHING. The controls were real, the reader was real, and the ladder that exists to run controls ran none of them — so the only thing standing between the census's five claims and a silent regression was that nobody had edited it yet.

ROOT CAUSE: the act that landed the reader also declared it an AUDIT (correctly — its live reading walks the owner's Dropbox, and a rail that walks Dropbox on every `just health` would be a tax), and then let the audit-ness leak over the controls. The distinction the ladder needs is not audit vs rail: it is between a LIVE READING (which costs an owner's filesystem) and its CONTROLS (which run on synthetic fixtures in a temp dir in under a second).

FIX MEASURED AFTER: `justfile` carries `python3 scripts/census_source_names.py --selftest || exit 1` and `python3 scripts/plan_source_rename.py --selftest || exit 1`, each declared as a `fatal` guard in `config/rail_registry.yaml#guards`; the live readings are OPERATOR LANES instead (`source-names`, `arrangement`, `rename-plan`), so what the ladder runs and what a human runs are two declared sets and not one ambiguous one.

## BUG-862 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-16) — scripts/census_source_names.py now measures TWO MATERIALISATIONS of one work and config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml declares them the same work: 929 works live in both homes and 727 differ byte-for-byte in the SAME kind (remedy: D-3048)

**Status:** OPEN (remedy: D-3048's arrangement reading, LANDED read-only; the disposition is the owner's). MEASURED 2026-10-16.

SYMPTOM: MEASURED by `python3 scripts/census_source_names.py --arrangement` (READ-ONLY, 11/11 known-answer controls): the owner's library holds 2530 files and the pipeline's corpus home holds 940; through the DOOR'S OWN comparison key, 929 works exist in BOTH; of those, 103 agree byte-for-byte and **727 disagree while being the same kind of file** (an .md against an .md). A further 99 works exist in both homes in two CONTAINERS (an .epub and the .md converted from it) — those can never be byte-equal and are NOT drift, which is why the reader counts them separately. 21 works in the library and 1 in the corpus exist as TWO files of the SAME kind.

ROOT CAUSE: the repository never declared which home is the AUTHORITY for an ingested work's bytes, so both homes were maintained, and a "copy" that nobody compares is two files the day after it is made. Nothing was wrong on the day of the copy: that is exactly why nothing detected anything. This is BUG-780's shape (530 rows, one text under two names) moved one layer out — from the corpus to the corpus AND the reading view — and it is the reason T-176 refuses to materialise a THIRD copy for a topic.

REMEDY (D-3048): the corpus home is the ONE bytes home (it is the tree S0 reads and the only tree the S0.5 cache stamps); the library is the owner's READING surface; and the arrangement is a VIEW that is GENERATED or not a view at all. The drift is now a READING with a shrink-only ceiling (727, measured, never raised) at rc 2 — loud and owner-owed, never fatal — and the disposition (retire the second materialisation, or keep it as a declared view with a re-derivation receipt) is the owner's word, registered as T-179.


## BUG-863 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the operator LANES whose declared contract is rc 2 were printed by just(1) as a FAILED COMMAND, so the owner read a working reading as a broken one

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (remedy: the tri-state guard on the recipes, the same form the ladder already used).

FILE / LINES: `justfile` — the recipes `source-names`, `arrangement`, `rename-plan` (added 2026-10-16 with D-3048).

SYMPTOM (MEASURED, not inferred): `just source-names` printed the whole reading and then `error: Recipe source-names failed on line 599 with exit code 2`, and the shell saw rc 2. The reader was RIGHT: rc 2 is its DECLARED contract (name debt is OWNER-OWED, loud, never fatal — BUG-457). The recipe was wrong: a plain line makes just(1) propagate rc 2 as a failure, so the owner is told a working reading is a broken command. This is the SECOND hand-off command to fail in the owner's hands this session, and the two failures are the same shape one layer apart: BUG-859 was a stale PATH in the hand-off, this is a stale GUARD on it.

ROOT CAUSE: the tri-state contract was declared in the READERS and in the ladder comments, and the LADDER already wrote the correct form for `scripts/check_harness_homes.py` (`|| [ $? -eq 2 ]`), but the operator recipes were added later as plain lines. Nothing CHECKED them: `scripts/resolve_route.py` verifies that a lane's command still EXISTS in its recipe, and it says (correctly) that a command the LADDER runs is a guard's business — so a lane's own rc contract had no reader at all. The class is BUG-462: the reader printed "owner-owed" and the shell printed "failed".

FIX + MEASURED AFTER: all four lanes carry `|| [ $? -eq 2 ]` with a comment naming why (`just source-names`, `just arrangement`, `just placement`, `just rename-plan` now read rc 0 and print their readings). THE FIX WAS ITSELF CAUGHT BY A RAIL: the new ladder line `--brief` was first declared `tri_state` in `config/rail_registry.yaml#guards` and the rail read it `fatal`, because `guard_of()` reads the LADDER'S OWN TEXT and the comment said "instead of || exit 1" — a comment that DESCRIBES the wrong guard IS the wrong guard as far as the reader is concerned. Re-worded, `check_rail_registry` reads rc 0.

## BUG-864 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-16) — scripts/census_source_names.py is the ONE reader that makes an abandoned GUI placement rule visible: Hazel owns a PLACEMENT rule for a home no declaration covers, and the three destinations its rules name do not exist on disk

**Status:** OPEN (remedy: D-3049's placement declaration + reading; the owner lane is to check the rules in Hazel's own UI). MEASURED 2026-10-16.

FILE / EVIDENCE: `/Applications/Hazel.app`; `~/Library/Application Support/Hazel/` holds three `*.hazelrules` stores (one 27,510 B, modified 2026-03-14) plus `.hazeldb` files last written 2026-10-15 14:12; `file` reports the rule stores as `data` and `plutil -p` CANNOT parse them (NSKeyedArchiver), so the rules are neither diffable nor readable as text.

SYMPTOM: decoding the largest store's strings shows a `HazelMoveAction` and the destinations `~/Downloads/00_INBOX`, `~/Downloads/ebook` (rules named "ebook epub+mobi sorting", "ebook pdf sorting") and `~/Downloads/docs` — and MEASURED the same day, NONE of those three directories EXISTS. A rule whose destination is gone cannot complete; and a BOOK arriving in Downloads can be moved by a rule the repository cannot read, out of a home the repository does not declare. The library reading cannot see it: Downloads is neither a declared root nor a declared pen.

ROOT CAUSE: this machine's placement policy has TWO homes — the declaration in `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml` and a binary rule store owned by a GUI app — and nothing compares them. One of them is not text, so no diff, no review and no receipt can ever mention it (C12's defect with a GUI). The owner's own Downloads triage is not wrong in KIND (an arrival pen is a good idea); it is wrong in HOME and in SILENCE.

REMEDY (D-3049): the placement declaration records Hazel as REFUSED as a decider (`placement.refusals.no_second_policy_home`) and the reading counts DECLARED pens instead. Two owner-lane steps remain: (a) open Hazel and either retarget those rules at a DECLARED pen or disable the actions; (b) if Downloads is to stay an arrival pen, declare it as a pen row so the census counts it — a pen that is declared is a queue, a pen that is not is a silence.

## BUG-865 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — scripts/census_source_names.py printed a CLEAN verdict about a tree it had only looked at the top of: the placement reading was BLIND below the declared axis, and the FLOW between an arrival and a stamped work was declared NOWHERE

MEASURED AFTER: `--selftest` 18/18; `--brief` reads `below the declared axis 2738 file(s) in 24 name(s), undeclared below: none || flow: 5 transition(s), 0 unresolved`.
