## BUG-866 (MED — FIXED 2026-10-16) — the BRIDGE that puts library EPUBs into the corpus matched by FILENAME STEM and wrote on a bare run, and the library roots it reads were declared null so three writers converted NOTHING while printing that they ran

**Status:** FIXED (code + config) 2026-10-16 by D-3050. The routed carrier of this finding is scripts/census_source_names.py, whose `--flow` reading declares the step this bug lives in.

MEASURED (2026-10-16):
(a) `pipeline/batch_convert_epubs.py` matched its target with `epub_path.stem + ".md"` and took the FIRST `rglob` hit, then WROTE by default. A name is evidence, never identity (D-3045), so a filename decided WHICH BYTES THE PIPELINE READS — and `rglob` let the hit land in a DOMAIN folder the work's own classification never named. Worse: the S0.5 cache keys on the door's own NAME (`door.new_file_definition: absent_from_metadata_cache`), so an in-place overwrite under an unchanged name is INVISIBLE to the door — a RE-INGEST act wearing a repair's clothes.
(b) `config/pipeline_config.yaml#source_epub_dir` and `#source_pdf_dir` were declared `null`, so `pipeline_paths.SOURCE_EPUB_DIR` fell back to `<corpus>/epub` — MEASURED, that path DOES NOT EXIST. Three declared writers read it (`batch_convert_epubs.py`, `enhance_md_headers.py`, `fix_remaining.py`): an absent root means each converts NOTHING while printing that it ran. A declaration that does not resolve is a promise, not a measurement (D-3034).
(c) REFUTED HYPOTHESIS, recorded because it was mine: (b) also means this script CANNOT have produced the 727 same-name, different-byte pairs `--arrangement` counts between the library and the corpus. Its root did not exist, `rglob` over a missing directory yields nothing, and the old code printed "Found 0 EPUBs" and exited 0. THE ORIGIN OF THE DRIFT IS THEREFORE STILL OPEN, named as an open question instead of assigned: candidates are the two other consumers of the same roots (`enhance_md_headers.py`, `fix_remaining.py`), the legacy v2.0 aliasing tools (T-182) and an owner copy. Naming one would be a guess; the measurement only says THIS one did not do it.

FIX: the bridge now (1) matches through the DOOR'S OWN comparison key (`pipeline.book_metadata.sanitize_source_book`), so bridge and pipeline agree on what one work is; (2) REFUSES and COUNTS an ambiguous key (0 or >1 candidates) instead of taking a first hit; (3) REFUSES a corpus file the S0.5 cache already resolves and names it a RE-INGEST act (T-172's shape), `--allow-ingested` being the only way through; (4) is DRY by default (`--apply` writes) and says so; (5) fails LOUDLY on an absent root (D-795); (6) carries four known-answer controls, one of which proves a PLAN that decides to convert still writes nothing. The two config keys are declared as the library kind roots.

MEASURED AFTER: `pipeline/batch_convert_epubs.py --selftest` 4/4 green; the live PLAN writes nothing; `SOURCE_EPUB_DIR` resolves to the library epub root (exists=True, 554 .epub under it) and `SOURCE_PDF_DIR` to the library pdf root (exists=True). STILL OPEN AND REGISTERED: the admission transition itself (T-181) and the legacy tools' second home for the topic vocabulary (T-182).

FILE / EVIDENCE: pipeline/batch_convert_epubs.py; config/pipeline_config.yaml#source_epub_dir; scripts/census_source_names.py --flow.

## BUG-867 (LOW — OPEN 2026-10-16) — scripts/census_source_names.py never compares a file's own CONTAINER to the KIND folder its declared axis orders it by: it reads "misplaced 281, 0 subfolders the axis does not name" while 92 files sit in a kind folder that contradicts them (remedy: T-184)

**Status:** OPEN (remedy: T-184, the placement reading's own gap). FOUND 2026-10-16 by writing the ADMISSION PLAN (scripts/plan_admission.py, D-3051) and reading its own refusal classes back.

SYMPTOM: MEASURED 2026-10-16, `python3 scripts/census_source_names.py --placement` reads "2,811 file(s) inside the declared roots, 2,530 admitted, 281 misplaced, 0 loose at a root, 0 in a subfolder the declared axis does not name" — and NOTHING in that sentence covers a file that sits INSIDE a declared kind folder while carrying a DIFFERENT container. MEASURED: 92 such files under the books home — 42 `.epub` in `books/pdf/`, 24 `.md` in `books/pdf/`, 10 `.pdf` in `books/epub/`, 8 `.mobi` in `books/epub/`, 5 `.mobi` in `books/pdf/`, and one each of `.azw3` in epub, `.djvu` in pdf, `.doc` in pdf. The reading's two classes that exist between them leave the contradiction uncounted: `misplaced` counts a kind NO ROOT ADMITS (the `.png`/`.psd` population, 281 files) and `undeclared subfolder` counts a DEPTH-1 NAME the axis does not name. So a `.epub` filed under `books/pdf/` passes both tests — its kind IS admitted, and `pdf` IS a declared name — while the declaration it is filed under says the folder IS the container claim. The ONE line the owner reads on every health run is therefore silent about 92 files, and the FIRST live admission reading found them by accident (it refused them, correctly, as `refused_not_in_its_kind_folder`, 52 of them after the refuses that precede it in the order).

ROOT CAUSE: the placement reading compares the axis to a NAME (the folder's own name against the declared set, the file's suffix against the KIND set) but never to the OTHER HALF of the same declaration: `placement.homes.<root>.axis: kind` at `axis_depth: 1` says the depth-1 folder IS the file's own container claim, and the reading never asks whether the file agrees with the folder it is under. This is D-3034's distinction inside a reading — a declaration must RESOLVE — a folder named `pdf` resolves nothing unless the file in it is a pdf. The gap is invisible from outside because every number the reading prints is TRUE: it is the COVERAGE of the printed classes that is short, which is BUG-865's shape one level down (there the blindness was BELOW the declared axis; here it is AT it, where the axis was declared and then read as a set of names rather than as a claim).

FIX (T-184): the placement reading gains the class it lacks — a file whose own container contradicts the kind folder its home's axis orders it by — COUNTED, with a bounded number of named examples, folded into the same loud owner-owed condition as `misplaced` (BUG-457), and covered by a fixture control (a `.epub` in `pdf/` reads OUT-OF-ITS-KIND-FOLDER, an `.epub` in `epub/` does not, and a `.png` in `pdf/` stays MISPLACED without being counted twice). MEASURED EFFECT TO EXPECT: the notify's misplaced-family count moves 281 -> 373 and the class is NAMED. This entry is deliberately OPEN and no line of the placement reader was edited by the act that found it: one act, one subject, and the repair belongs to the reading that owns the question. The counts above are the reading the repair must move.

**Ids:** D-3051 (the admission plan, the act that found it) | T-184 (the repair) | T-180 (the disposition of the misplaced population, owner-worded) | BUG-865 (the same shape below the axis)

## BUG-868 (LOW — FIXED 2026-10-16) — an UNDECLARED, un-stamped DERIVED INDEX of this repository and of the corpus exists on this machine (a GUI built it over the owner's Dropbox), and config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml — the file whose arrangement declares "ONE bytes home plus ONE derived tree that carries a receipt" — said nothing about it (remedy: D-3052 — the disclosure IS the remedy)

**Status:** FIXED 2026-10-16 (owner's own report: "I already installed it — check if this can be utilized"). MEASURED before any answer.

SYMPTOM: MEASURED 2026-10-16 on this machine: /Applications/DigUp.app (com.abdurrahim.DigUp, 0.6.1, LSUIElement, Sparkle auto-update ON with a public feed) holds a semantic index of the owner's chosen folders — Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Movies, Music, the WHOLE Dropbox and iCloud Drive — i.e. of this repository, its governance and the corpus home. Its stores are ~/Library/Application Support/DigUp/index.noindex/index.sqlite (242,728,960 B at 18:21 that day, plus a 244 MB WAL) and a SEPARATE code.sqlite, its models are embeddinggemma-2-Q8_0.gguf (309,855,456 B) and mmproj-embeddinggemma-2-Q8_0.gguf (554,821,024 B, a multi-modal projector), and its own worker log names the runtime: "[llama.cpp worker] ready in 7.47 s (text-only, llama.cpp b11461, vectors 1)". Nothing in this repository declared that a second, DERIVED, un-receipted index of the corpus and of the repository itself exists on the machine — no register row, no decision, no reading. It is local and $0 marginal (C1/C3 hold), so this is not a sovereignty defect; it is a SILENCE: D-3050 declares "ONE bytes home plus ONE derived tree that carries a receipt", and a 242 MB derived index of those same bytes with no receipt and no stamp is a THIRD reading of them that no rail can see.

ROOT CAUSE: the declaration law in this repository is written for artifacts the OS makes, and an application the OWNER installs keeps its own state outside the tree — so the artifact is real, load-bearing for the owner's daily work, and structurally invisible: no path in the tree names it, no census walks it, and the two facts that matter for any future use (its VERSION FLOATS — the app auto-updates from a public feed, so a hash taken today names a binary that may not exist tomorrow; its INDEX is UNREPRODUCIBLE — built quietly by a GUI, with no schema, no promise and no stamp) would have stayed unrecorded until someone tried to build on it and found the ground moving.

REMEDY (D-3052, and it is a DISCLOSURE rather than a repair — nothing in this repository owns the owner's app): the arm is REGISTERED with NO CONSUMER — nothing in the scaffold, the tools, the skill orchestration or the knowledge pipeline may read it — its measured facts, the four mechanical reasons (no callable interface, a floating version, an unreproducible index, a second index of the same bytes), the one reusable asset (a hashable GGUF model, usable only as its OWN declared vector space and never mixed with bge-m3) and the RE-OPEN CONDITION (a pinnable interface plus a named consumer) are recorded once, in the register and in governance/NOT-YET-EVALUATED-RESEARCH.md, so the question is answered ONCE instead of re-asked per session. No code, lane, rail or config file is added: a declaration nothing consumes would be prose (D-405).

**Ids:** D-3052 (the verdict) | BUG-864 (the same class on the placement side: a GUI rule engine refused as a DECIDER) | D-2654 (the stronger refusal next door: an unhashable model) | T-179 (the second materialisation, one layer in)

## BUG-869 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-16) — pipeline/subagent_fanout.py delivered an `async: true` delegate as a FOREGROUND run that BLOCKED its parent, and the wall that guards the delegated call is PICKED rather than DERIVED (scripts/r5_review_gate.py declares 1800 s for a ONE-turn review against this repository's own `wall_rule: guards[timeout_guard] >= max_turns * per_turn_budget_s` = 90 s), so a slow run and an infinite run are ONE state to every reader (remedy: T-185)

**Status:** OPEN (remedy: T-185; the class is BUG-828/D-3027's, one layer over — a wall nobody derived is a wall nobody can defend). FOUND 2026-10-16 by the owner: "subagent run infinitetly its more than 30 min too slow ... why the fuck is it so slow what is the root cause". MEASURED before any answer.

SYMPTOM (the owner's report, and it was correct): a delegated R5 review did not return for over 30 minutes, and the session could not proceed while it ran. The transcript shows the call was issued with the harness's BACKGROUND mode and the harness reported it as FOREGROUND: `tool_request(delegate): {"async":true, "instructions":"Run this exact command ... report its FULL stdout+stderr verbatim ..."}` -> `tool_response: Delegated to foreground subagent 20261016_9`, and later `Subagent 20261016_9 was cancelled before it finished and will not run again.` So the parent turn was BLOCKED by a call that declared itself asynchronous, and the only reason the block ended was a cancellation. Two distinct defects ride in that sentence: the MODE was not honoured, and the run had NO declared wall a reader could compare its clock against.

COUNTER-MEASUREMENT FIRST, because it REFUTES the tempting root cause. The reviewers' own log carried a line that reads like a dead model: `Chat completion: model=gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit, 198 tokens in 40.78s (4.9 tok/s), prompt: 11447, max_tokens=2600`. That is NOT a decode collapse. An authorised 64-token call measured the same evening, same model, temperature 0.0: `64 tokens in 2.18s (29.3 tok/s)`. **Decode was healthy at 29.3 tok/s**; the 4.9 tok/s line is a BLENDED rate in which an 11,447-token PREFILL dominates (~34 s of prefill against ~7 s of decode), and the second line in the same log — `1 tokens in 8.94s (0.1 tok/s), prompt: 11` — is a COLD START after 56 minutes of server idleness (the oMLX log holds nothing between 18:00:19 and 18:56:08). The cost of an agentic turn on this host is PREFILL x TURNS, not decode. THE REFUTED READING IS RECORDED ON PURPOSE: "the model got slow" is the wrong answer, and it is the answer the evidence most invites.

ROOT CAUSE, three limbs, none of them the model:
  (1) THE WALL IS PICKED, NOT DERIVED. `scripts/r5_review_gate.py` declares `timeout=1800` on the reviewer subprocess and `tools/model_eval_suite.py` declares `timeout=900` on the HTTP call that sits inside it. This repository already declares the opposite rule in `config/agent_context.yaml#turn_budget`: `wall_rule: guards[timeout_guard] >= max_turns * per_turn_budget_s`, with `per_turn_budget_s: 90` ratified by the owner on 2026-10-15 (T-132/D-3027: "the per-turn ceiling is derived, never picked"). A ONE-turn review therefore owes a wall of 90 s and declares 1800 s, twenty times its own rule — and it prints NOTHING during that window (the gate's last line before the call is `reviewer <model> budget <n> tokens`), so the silence that follows is indistinguishable from a hang. BUG-828 measured the same class when a caller sent `max_tokens=None` and inherited a global ceiling "about 20 minutes of decode at 27.4 tok/s"; this is the identical shape applied to the WALL rather than to the ceiling.
  (2) THE RUN LEFT NO TRACE, exactly as BUG-844/T-168 declared it would. `governance/delegate_journal.jsonl` holds two runs tonight, both `done`, wall times 34.3 s and 34.2 s — and NO row for the run in question, because the caller did not write a start row before the call. So `just delegates` read "4 row(s), 2 run(s), 0 open, 0 past budget" WHILE a run was live and overdue: nothing could NAME it, and nothing could kill it. This is BUG-844's DECLARED LIMIT biting rather than a new gap — "this repository cannot INTERCEPT the harness's own `delegate` call, so the trace is a discipline the caller keeps" — and the discipline was not kept. The infrastructure (scripts/delegate_journal.py, the tri-state rail, one command) exists and was not used.
  (3) THE HOST IS THE AMPLIFIER, and it is measurable. The single largest CPU consumer on this machine is the harness's own window: `Goose Helper (Renderer)` at 5,845,760 KB RSS burning 184% CPU (605 CPU-minutes across a 10-hour session, still spinning at the moment of measurement), beside `goose serve` at 741 MB; the session store `~/.local/share/goose/sessions.db` is 971,165,696 B with a 4.2 MB WAL; free pages stood at 7,813 (~30 MB) against swap 2,881 MB of 4,096 MB used, a compressor holding 2,167,749 pages and 46,989,915 page-ins since boot. Under that pressure every prefill is many times slower than on an idle machine, and the UI re-renders the whole transcript on every keystroke (the harness log records a `Content changed:` line PER KEYPRESS). THE DECLARED CAUSE OF THAT UNBOUNDED CONVERSATION IS ALREADY REGISTERED AND UNBOUND (T-135's remaining limb, re-measured live tonight): the running app process binds exactly ONE GOOSE_ name — `GOOSE_SERVER__SECRET_KEY` — while `pipeline/harness_contract.py --check` reads all FIVE contract names UNBOUND (rc 2): the trigger trio plus GOOSE_PROVIDER/GOOSE_MODEL. `config/agent_context.yaml:32-34` states the consequence in the repository's own words: the compaction trigger becomes `min(0.8 x window, 225000)` because "the 225000 cap is a CLOUD PRICE-TIER artifact and is meaningless on hardware we own", and the declaration's own instruction is to "declare the SERVED window; never inherit 128000". So the harness compacts far later than the ratified contract says, the conversation grows to the size that produced a 971 MB store and a 5.8 GB renderer, and EVERY turn re-pays prefill on it. The slow subagent was the symptom; an unbound declaration is upstream of it.

WHAT WAS NOT BROKEN (stated so the repair is not aimed at the wrong thing): the review itself LANDED. `governance/r5_review_gate.jsonl` records scripts/plan_admission.py at 2026-10-16T18:55:57, tier `deep`, reviewer gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit, all three deterministic layers PASS, `verdict_recorded_by_reviewer: true`; `governance/r5_reviews.jsonl` records verdict APPROVE at 18:56:38 for sha256_16 `4d20d18e1fc02e5c`, and the current bytes of the file still hash to that digest, so the verdict is valid for them. What never arrived was the DELEGATE'S OWN REPORT, because the subagent was asked to reproduce roughly two hundred lines of stdout VERBATIM — the most expensive possible shape of work for a prefill-bound 4B model, since it must generate the whole transcript and then re-send it — and its parent was blocked waiting for a sentence it had already written to a receipt.

FIX (T-185, three limbs, each a rule the repository already declares elsewhere): (1) every wall in the delegate and review paths is COMPUTED from `config/agent_context.yaml#turn_budget` (the owner's `per_turn_budget_s` x the class's declared turns) and a wall that is PICKED is a fault; (2) the long call emits a HEARTBEAT — an elapsed line before and after the model call, so a stall is visible while it is happening rather than after a silent ceiling expires; (3) a run declared with the harness's background mode must BE background — a mode that is silently downgraded to foreground is a fault, and the caller writes the journal start row BEFORE the call so the run is nameable by `just delegates` while it is still open. The instruction SHAPE is part of the repair: a delegate asked to report evidence writes it to a FILE and returns the path, its digest and the one decision line - a receipt, not a transcript (the repository's own pattern).

**Ids:** BUG-844/T-168/D-3039 (the trace that was not kept: the declared limit, not a new gap) | BUG-828/D-3027 (the same class: a ceiling derived, never picked) | T-132/D-3000 (the ratified context contract this host has not bound) | T-135 (its remaining limb, re-measured here — the GUI-session binding is what makes a Dock launch see the declaration) | D-2946 (the R5 discipline the landed verdict satisfied) | T-184 (the only open work the reviewed file found)

### BUG-870 (HIGH, RETRACTED 2026-10-16) — A DECISION STATE OUTSIDE THE DECLARED PARTITION (the BUG-765 recurrence)
- **state:** resolved | **severity:** n/a — INVALID FILING (retracted) | **filed:** 2026-10-16 | **closed:** 2026-10-16 | **by:** assistant
- **RETRACTED 2026-10-16 — FALSE POSITIVE (filed by the assistant, corrected by the assistant):** the state vocabulary is ALREADY total. `config/gov_sync.yaml` declares FOUR bucket keys, not two: `open_decision_states` [open, proposed, draft, deferred, planned], `decision_in_effect_states` [active, ratified], `decision_closed_states` [resolved, superseded, archived, rejected], `decision_void_states` [stale, revoked, abandoned]. Together they ARE the partition. Measured coverage of the census (`config/decisions_summary.json`): 79 open + 743 in-effect + 360 closed + 0 void = 1182 = every record.
- **ROOT CAUSE of the false positive (the bug was in the DIAGNOSTIC, not the config):** the census script selected buckets with `{k:v for k,v in d.items() if k.endswith('_decision_states')}` — which matches ONLY `open_decision_states`. The other three keys do NOT end in that suffix, so the union collapsed to the open set and a spurious UNCLASSIFIED list appeared. A name-suffix guess is not a census.
- **CONTROL ALREADY HELD (D-2987/BUG-765):** `scripts/check_governance_faces.py#partition_faults` enforces (1) buckets pairwise DISJOINT — a state in two buckets fires; (2) union EQUALS the census's state keys — a state no bucket holds fires. `--check` returns rc=0: "ok governance-faces: ... the STATE SIGNS agree with the register". The partition was never broken; nothing needed adding.
- **RETRACTED COROLLARY (the DECISION-LOG 'omission'):** D-3052/D-3053/D-3054 are state `active` = IN EFFECT, NOT open, so their absence from `## 🔴 CURRENT OPEN / PENDING INDEX` is CORRECT declared-VIEW behaviour (the face self-announces `face_list_limit: 12`, and prints its own {shown}/{total}). Not a gov_sync bug.
- **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN:** `D-3055 THE STATE VOCABULARY IS TOTAL` is MOOT and is NOT executed. Minting it would have created a SECOND home for a set that already exists (C12) and added a duplicate rule to gov_sync.py.
- **DURABLE LESSON:** a census over a DECLARED vocabulary must enumerate the declared KEYS, never guess them by name shape; and before filing "the config is incomplete", run the control that already exists.
- **symptom:** config/decisions.yaml now holds 597 decisions in state `active` (also `resolved` 325, `rejected` 11, `archived` 8, `superseded` 16) — NONE of which appear in config/gov_sync.yaml#open_decision_states = [open, proposed, draft, deferred, planned]. The newest three decisions D-3052/D-3053/D-3054 are state `active`, so they are invisible in DECISION-LOG.md's "CURRENT OPEN / PENDING INDEX" while the face simultaneously declares "1182 decisions".
- **why this is a fault, not a view:** the axis is a DECLARED PARTITION (D-2987/BUG-765). The face's VIEW is legitimate (`face_list_limit: 12`, self-announced), but a PARTITION must be TOTAL: every state a record may hold must be either OPEN or declared NOT-open. `active`/`resolved`/`rejected`/`archived`/`superseded` are in neither list, so 957 of 1182 decisions (81%) fall outside the declared axis. This is the exact fault measured on 2026-10-13 for state `ratified` — it was never fixed, it was renamed.
- **consequence:** "79 needing action" undercounts if any active/resolved state still owes an action; and the register's own newest entries are unreachable from the face.
- **fix (fail-closed, not cosmetic):** declare the FULL state vocabulary in config/gov_sync.yaml as two exhaustive, disjoint lists (`open_decision_states` + `closed_decision_states`); add a check that union == the states actually present in config/decisions.yaml, faulting on any UNCLASSIFIED state; render the count of unclassified = 0 in the face.
- **related:** BUG-765, D-2987, D-2981, T-185.

- **state:** open | **severity:** high | **filed:** 2026-10-16 | **by:** assistant

  repository's `scripts/`. The mechanism is **PEP 420**, and it is why the repository could not fix this from

  that built a doctrine: "prefix reuse is DISPROVEN on this machine today ... every prefill optimisation must
  therefore be CACHE-FREE". MEASURED 2026-10-16, same host, same protocol (byte-identical 2,616-token prefix,
  3 calls/model, temp 0.0, max_tokens 32): gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit cold 6.90 s -> warm 0.39/0.16 s, cached

  lists gemma-4-E4B at 455.0 tok/s and Qwen3.8-27B at 39.0 tok/s; its selftest is 17/17 green after the fix.

  of the whole optimisation surface. With the cache live, the binding constraint is no longer prefill
  throughput but PREFIX STABILITY: ONE byte changed at the head converts a 0.16 s turn back into a 6.90 s turn.
- **the mechanism it explains, and this is the point.** A capped session felt BOTH frequently compacted AND
  slow for ONE reason, not two: the 32k wall forced compactions, and each compaction REPLACED THE HISTORY,
  destroying a live prefix that was ~25x cheaper to reuse than to re-read. Compaction is now the most expensive
  event in a session. The counter-measure is the wall itself — do not cap, compact rarely, never compact a
  prefix still being appended to.
- **correction to a claim made in this session's conversation, by measurement.** "The 27B is faster than the
  small model" is FALSE on this host: 39.0 tok/s against 455.0 tok/s is a 12x penalty, and `agent_loop` needs
  672.2 s of prefill against a 60 s budget -> `prefill_bill`, NOT routable. Prefill cost tracks **ACTIVE**
  parameters, not total, so the ranking must take the active-parameter count as the bill's FIRST term. The
  resident MoE arms (~3-4B active of 26B/35B) are 4B-class bills with larger-model capacity — the right
  candidates for a harness loop, and NONE is currently exposed to goose.

  a new `remeasured_20261016` block ADDED as a sibling of `measured_20261014` (the 2026-10-14 text is NOT

  `compaction_destroys_a_live_cache` added. Probe selftest 17/17 green before and after.

  single `GOOSE_MODEL` the emitter prints (`gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit`) is the `AGENT_LOOP_SHORT` role's model
  (`config/model_assignments.yaml#harness_roles`), handed to all three classes alike. A per-class model
  `--scope` may only be bound once that class -> role mapping EXISTS in a declared home; minting it here would
  be a second home for an assignment that already has one.
- **R5 (generator != verifier, D-2962):** `pipeline/harness_env.py` sha256_16=`7737bbb0f21425a3` VERDICT
  APPROVE; `scripts/bind_harness_env.sh` sha256_16=`e9b84dc75c1099ba` VERDICT APPROVE (both by
  gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit, a different family from the generator, written to `governance/r5_reviews.jsonl`).
  The lint layer's single `UP031` finding at line 166 was measured to be PRE-EXISTING (identical at the same
  line before the change); this act introduced no new finding — three successive fixes (`%` -> `{0}` -> `{}` ->
  f-string) were each re-reviewed so the verdict covers the FINAL digest, never an intermediate one.
- **symptom (measured live):** `python3 pipeline/harness_env.py --print` emits FIVE exports — `GOOSE_CONTEXT_LIMIT=32768`, `GOOSE_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=0.8`, `GOOSE_AUTO_COMPACT_TOKEN_LIMIT=32768`, `GOOSE_PROVIDER=maxwell_omlx`, `GOOSE_MODEL=gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit`. `scripts/bind_harness_env.sh` with NO argument EVALS that output (`*) eval "$(python3 "$READER" --print)"`). The 32k wall and the 4B subagent model therefore land in whatever shell sources it — including the owner's interactive login profile.
- **why this is a fault:** the wall was imposed for ONE lane (delegated/subagent work) that the owner does not run. A global binding of `GOOSE_CONTEXT_LIMIT`/`GOOSE_AUTO_COMPACT_TOKEN_LIMIT` capped EVERY Goose session at 32k and compacted the owner's DeepSeek lane every ~5 minutes (0.8 x 32768 = 26,214 tokens). The `launchctl setenv` occurrences were unset this session (readback: all four names empty), but the SAME values are still one `eval` away — the fault moved from the launchd namespace into a shell idiom, and gained a provider/model pin.
- **second half of the fault (C25/agent-agnostic):** pinning `GOOSE_PROVIDER`/`GOOSE_MODEL` in a GENERIC env emitter couples every consumer to the subagent's model — a value that belongs in the subagent's own recipe, not in a profile.
- **fix (fail-closed, not cosmetic):** `pipeline/harness_env.py` MUST require an explicit `--scope subagent|cron`; `--print` without it REFUSES (rc non-zero) rather than printing bindable exports; the emitted block carries an in-band scope marker so a stray `eval` is visible. `scripts/bind_harness_env.sh` must pass the scope it means and must never be a no-arg default that evals.
- **related:** T-132, T-135, D-3000, D-3003, BUG-870 (the sibling false assumption: a wall that a lane needs is not a wall the whole host needs).

### BUG-878 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-17) — `mcp_doc_guard.py` WAS DECLARED RELATIVE AND THE PER-SESSION FORM CARRIED NO CWD: the write gate could be born dead with nothing in the session saying so

- **MEASURED, TWO-SIDED, IN ONE MINUTE.** `docguard` is declared in the harness home as `cmd: python3`,
  `args: [mcp_doc_guard.py]` — a RELATIVE script path. From the repo root the extension starts and the model answers.
  From `/tmp` the SAME declaration reports
  `Warning: Failed to start extension 'python3' (process quit before initialization: ... can't open file '/private/tmp/mcp_doc_guard.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory), continuing without it`
  and the run **exits 0 and answers normally**. The failure is real; the exit code says nothing about it.
- **WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC.** `docguard` is the D824 write gate (`append_only` / `never_overwrite` / `versioned`) for
  the governed documents. The harness reports a dead extension to the TERMINAL and never to the session (AGENTS.md
  harness fact, and this is its second independent confirmation), so from the inside a session with no write gate is
  INDISTINGUISHABLE from one that has it: the agent believes protected files are guarded while every write is
  unguarded. `enabled: true` in the config is not evidence that the extension is running.
- **THE SHAPE IS THE C12 CLASS.** A command whose resolution depends on the CALLER'S DIRECTORY is a path that lives in
  the environment rather than in the declaration. It resolves today only because sessions happen to start in the repo
  root, which is a coincidence and not a guarantee.
- **REMEDY (owner act on the harness home, backup + read-back like T-186's flips):** make the argument absolute —
  `args: ['/Users/barn/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/claude projects/maxwell os 2.0/mcp_doc_guard.py']`.
  Until then `just session <profile>` (D-3064) REFUSES to birth a profile whose gate would be dead, which protects
  LAUNCHED sessions only; a session started by any other route stays exposed.
- **RED LOOP (already red, already run — D-3036):** the two commands above. It goes GREEN when the `/tmp` invocation
  starts the extension with ZERO warning and the session's own surface names it.
- **RE-SCOPED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-17 (sixth sitting).** The claim above was TRUE OF THE ROUTE IT WAS MEASURED ON AND
  FALSE OF THE CONFIG. The harness starts a CONFIG-declared stdio extension in the `cwd` THAT DECLARATION CARRIES, so
  the relative argument was never the defect on the config path: from `/tmp`, `goose run` was born with all 12 workshop
  extensions and produced **ZERO** start warnings while answering normally (session `20261017_10`; repeated as
  `20261017_12` after the repair). What died was the `--with-extension '<cmd> <args>'` form, which carries NO cwd — and
  that is exactly the form `just session` emits: the failing session's own record names a member called `python3` and
  records no cwd. The defect was **resolution in the caller's context**, and the launcher was its only live route.
- **REMEDY, APPLIED IN THREE PARTS (each measured).** (1) The declaration is now ABSOLUTE
  (`args: ['/Users/…/maxwell os 2.0/mcp_doc_guard.py']`), so it no longer depends on a CloudStorage `cwd` being
  mounted at birth: one line changed, every other key byte-identical, backup
  `~/.config/goose/config.yaml.bak.20261017131255.bug878-abs`, `cwd` kept. (2) `_abs_script()` resolves a relative
  script argument in the DECLARATION's `cwd` FIRST and the birth directory second — the harness's own order, so the
  reader predicts what the harness will START rather than what the caller hoped. (3) A resolved path containing
  whitespace is QUOTED, never refused: `--with-extension 'python3 "<path with a space>/mcp_doc_guard.py"'` was
  measured to start with zero warnings from `/tmp` (session `20261017_11`), so the single-string form is faithful and
  `just session` is directory-independent.
- **RED LOOP IS GREEN, BOTH PATHS.** config path: `cd /tmp && goose run -t …` → `rc=0`, **0** warnings, surface =
  workshop. Launcher path: `birth_argv("core")` from `/tmp` inlines `python3 "…/mcp_doc_guard.py"` and
  `unresolvable(…) == []`.
- **FORENSIC SWEEP, no sibling left behind:** of the 26 declared extensions exactly ONE carried a relative script
  argument (`docguard`), and it is now absolute; the other 25 declare a platform/builtin type or a command with no
  script path (every stdio declaration parsed, every script-shaped part resolved).
- **ADJUDICATION OF R5** (gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit, `DJ-20261017T111319Z-082b`, wall 74.8 s, verdict **ACCEPT**).
  Objection: with a WRONG declared `cwd` that happens to contain a same-named file, the resolver could pick it
  silently. Adjudicated rather than waved away: that IS what the harness does, so mirroring it is the only faithful
  reading — a launcher that "corrected" the harness would start something the declaration does not describe. The case
  is recorded here and is not reachable today, because the sweep above leaves exactly one script argument, absolute.

### BUG-879 (LOW, OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE BIRTH RECORD NAMES A STDIO MEMBER BY ITS COMMAND, SO `scripts/goose_profile.py --born` CANNOT DISTINGUISH TWO `uvx` MEMBERS AND A BIRTH CANNOT BE AUDITED MEMBER-BY-MEMBER

**Measured 2026-10-17** on session `20261017_17`, born from the rendered workshop per-session form. Four stdio
extensions were supplied (`python3 <docguard>`, `uvx mcp-server-fetch`, `npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`,
`uvx mcp-server-git`) and the session's `enabled_extensions.v0` records **three** names: `npx`, `python3`, `uvx`. The
two `uvx` members are indistinguishable in the record - the extension's DECLARED NAME (`Fetch`, `GitMCP`) is not what
is stored; the command is.

**Why this is a bug and not cosmetics.** It is the identity confusion that made BUG-878 unreadable: the failing
session's record named a member called `python3`, which is a command, not an extension. It also means a birth can never
be audited member-by-member from the store: if ONE of two `uvx` members failed to start, the record would still show
one `uvx` row and the only evidence would be a terminal banner the session never receives (harness fact, BUG-873).
A reading that cannot distinguish its subjects cannot testify about them.

**Named remedy (not guessed):** record the declared name as the entry's identity and keep `cmd` in its own field -
`extension_data` already carries `cmd`/`args` separately, so the name is the only field being improvised. The reader
that must then be able to speak is the birth renderer in `scripts/goose_profile.py` (`--born`), which maps a recorded
member back to its policy key (`config/extension_profiles.yaml` carries the declared names). Acceptance reading: a
session born with four stdio members shows FOUR distinct names, and the existing `--born` renderer matches each to its
policy key without a display-name guess.

**Status:** OPEN. Route: `extension_residency` (the same capability that owns the profile rail). Found by the forensic
audit of D-3067, and deliberately NOT folded into BUG-873: BUG-873 is a silent zero-tool extension; this is a record
that cannot name what it started. Different subject, different remedy.

### BUG-880 (LOW, FIXED 2026-10-17) — THE LANE READER COULD NOT PARSE A PARAMETRISED RECIPE, SO A LANE POINTING AT A REAL, RUNNABLE RECIPE READ "the ladder file declares no such recipe"

**Measured 2026-10-17, two-sided, on the first lane that ever carried a parameter.** Declaring T-183's applier as an
operator lane (`recipe: admit-apply`, `cmd: python3 scripts/apply_admission.py --apply`) produced THREE faults from
`python3 scripts/resolve_route.py --check`, two of them variants of the same defect:

```
- lane admit-apply: the ladder file declares no such recipe - a lane the operator is told to run and cannot (BUG-482)
- lane admit-apply: 'python3 scripts/apply_admission.py' is ALSO run by the governed ladder recipe 'health'
```

The first is false by construction: `just --list` shows `admit-apply *ARGS` and `just --show admit-apply` prints its
body. The recipe-header pattern was `^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+):` — it required the colon IMMEDIATELY after the name, so a
recipe with any parameter (`admit-apply *ARGS:`, and equally `session profile="":`) was invisible to
`recipe_bodies()`. A route that EXISTS read as ABSENT: the exact class (D-3034) the lane check exists to catch,
turned against a working declaration.

The second fault is a real property of the check, not a bug in it: the lane command was a PREFIX of the health line
(`... --selftest`) and the overlap test is substring-based. That was fixed at the DECLARATION, not by weakening the
check: the lane names the ACT (`--apply`) and the preview is the same door with `--dry-run`.

**RED LOOP.** RED: `resolve_route.py --check` reported the two lane faults above while the recipe ran. GREEN: after
the header pattern accepted an optional parameter segment and the lane named `--apply`, `--check` reports NO lane
fault (only the pre-existing routing-debt fault remains), and the reader's own controls read **19/19** with a new
known-answer control — `parametrised_recipe_header` — that FAILS if the pattern regresses to `^name:`.

**Why this is a bug and not cosmetics.** The lane check is how the owner is told which door to run. A parser that
cannot see a recipe it could execute is a diagnostic that accuses the working file (BUG-870's shape, one layer over):
the cheapest possible repair is to weaken the declaration until the reader is happy, which is precisely how a working
route would be deleted to silence a false alarm.

**Status:** FIXED (`scripts/resolve_route.py`: `RECIPE` now accepts `name [params]: [# comment]`; one new control;
19/19). Route: `route_graph` (the capability that owns the reader). No ceiling was raised and no lane was renamed to
satisfy the parser.

### BUG-881 (MED, FIXED 2026-10-17) — THE APPLIER'S FIRST REAL RUN DIED ON `TypeError: 'str' object is not callable`: a LOCAL binding shadowed the module's own `stamp()`, and every control had tested the UNIT instead of the COMPOSITION

**Measured 2026-10-17, from the owner's own door.** `just admit-apply --dry-run` — the first time a SIGNED
acceptance existed — reached the row loop and stopped:

```
File ".../scripts/apply_admission.py", line 484, in run
    record = stamp(apply_row(...), header)
TypeError: 'str' object is not callable
```

`run()` bound `stamp = datetime.now(UTC).strftime(...)` fifty lines above the module-level
`def stamp(record, header)`. From that line on, the FUNCTION was unreachable — but Python says nothing until the
call executes, and the call executes only on the operator's path.

**Why 15/15 controls did not see it (D-3036: a control that tests a re-implementation tests nothing).** Control 11
called `stamp(done, {...})` at MODULE scope, where `stamp` is the function. It proved the function works. The crash
lived in the one composition the controls never entered: `run()`. A control that calls a unit the way its author
remembers is not a control over the path the operator drives.

**RED LOOP.** RED: the traceback above, verbatim, on `just admit-apply --dry-run`. GREEN: the same door prices the
plan with rc 0 (see BUG-882 for the timing reading), and the reader's own controls read **22/22**, two of them new
and two-sided: `the_shadow_detector_FINDS_a_planted_shadow` (a synthetic module whose `run()` binds `stamp`) and
`THIS_file_binds_no_local_that_shadows_a_module_callable` (the file's own bytes, parsed, every function's local
bindings intersected with module-level callables). The detector is a CLASS check: `shadowed_module_names()`.

**Swept, not just patched.** The same scan over every first-party `.py` (excluding `.venv*`, `archive/`) found
**3** sites; the other two are latent (they bind a module-level name and never call it) and were renamed anyway:
`audit_menu_rescope_cohort._canonical_run` (`run`) and `bakeoff_typed_decision.arm_deberta` (`score`). The reading
that re-takes it is the `ast` scan in this entry's RED LOOP; promoting that scan to a rail is a PROPOSAL, not an act
(no rail was created: the class is now covered inside the file that committed the defect, and a new rail would owe a
registry row, a ladder line and its own controls).

### BUG-882 (MED, FIXED 2026-10-17) — A DRY RUN READ EVERY SOURCE IN FULL: pricing the plan cost 8.0 GiB of I/O and STALLED for minutes on an unmaterialised Dropbox file

**Measured 2026-10-17, two-sided, on the same door.** The full `just admit-apply --dry-run` (479 rows) had not
returned after **300 s** and two child processes were asleep in I/O. With `--limit 3` the same command finished in
**0.7 s**, and with `--limit 100` in **5.0 s** — so the cost was per row, not per run. The run had reached row 309:

```
would journals_notes/DOMAIN 2 Design/design-notes/pdf/Sound design/Mastering.pdf -> ...
```

`apply_row()` computed `sha256_bytes(source)` **before** the `apply` branch: a dry run hashed all 479 sources —
**8,271.5 MiB** — and on this Dropbox-backed library an unmaterialised PDF costs a cloud fetch, so a *pricing*
command could block for minutes with nothing on screen saying why. The act needs the digest as EVIDENCE of what it
copied; the price needs only `stat`, which answers "did it change since the plan was derived" in microseconds.

**RED LOOP.** RED: `just admit-apply --dry-run` → no output after 300 s (twice), two `apply_admission.py` children
parked in I/O. GREEN: the full 479-row price returns in **16.6 s** (and 477 rows in **17 s** after BUG-883), and two
new controls pin the placement: `a_dry_run_does_NOT_read_the_source_bytes` (a source rewritten to the SAME size with
different bytes still prices as `would_apply` with an EMPTY digest — proving no hash ran) and
`the_ACT_takes_the_source_digest` (the same row, applied, carries the digest). The pair is two-sided: deleting the
hash entirely turns the second control red.

### BUG-883 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-17) — THE DOOR'S KEY WAS NOT NORMALISATION-INVARIANT: ONE WORK, TWO IDENTITIES (the corpus held `Galič` NFC, the source library held `c`+U+030C NFD)

**Measured 2026-10-17, on the one row the writer refused.** The 479-row price returned exactly one refusal:

```
NO  books/md/DOMAIN 7 .../Galič2017_Article_BenthamDeleuzeAndBeyondAnOverv -> the markdown target already exists
    and NO receipt accounts for it
```

The plan called that work a NEW candidate; a file already sat at the derived target with **109,817** bytes against
the source's **109,798** — a 19-byte `# <stem>\n\n` heading. The cause was not a stale plan: it was TEXT FORM.

```
corpus .md NFC  key chars: ['0x10d']                 (one precomposed č)
source .md NFD  key chars: ['0x30c']                 (c + combining caron)
source .pdf NFD key chars: ['0x30c']
```

`sanitize_source_book()` — the ONE key producer the ingest door, the census, the plan, the applier and the rename
planner all call — stripped and regexed the name but never normalised it, so both forms minted DIFFERENT keys for the
SAME work. MEASURED span: **6** of 939 corpus keys and **8** of 960 ingest-cache keys are non-NFC.

**Why this is HIGH and not cosmetic.** Three consequences, and the third is the dangerous one:
1. the reader classified a work the corpus HOLDS as a NEW admission candidate (`already_in_the_corpus` 1,668 → the
   work reads as unseen), so the plan and the writer disagreed by a row — the owner would sign a plan carrying a row
   that must refuse;
2. `admit_candidate` over-counted (479 → 477), and `refused_name_repair_first` over-counted (194 → 179);
3. macOS is normalisation-INSENSITIVE at lookup, which is the only reason the writer's `target.exists()` caught it.
   On a normalisation-SENSITIVE filesystem — Linux, which C26 names as a target — the applier would have **created
   the twin** and the corpus would hold one work twice, with the ingest door keying them apart forever.

**RED LOOP.** RED: `plan_admission --brief` read `candidates 479` while `apply_admission --dry-run` refused a row it
had itself priced. GREEN: NFC normalisation at the ONE producer (`pipeline/book_metadata.sanitize_source_book`)
makes the key invariant — `candidates 477`, `already_in_the_corpus 1688`, and `apply_admission --dry-run` prints
**477 would_apply, 0 refusals, rc 0**. New control:
`the_same_work_spelled_NFC_and_NFD_is_ONE_key_and_distinct_names_stay_distinct` (two-sided: a normaliser that
flattened every name would satisfy the first half only). Every consumer's own controls stay green (census 18/18,
plan_source_rename 11/11, normalise_corpus_names 10/10, ingest_identity_gate 20/20, apply_admission 22/22,
book_metadata 9/9 pytest).

**Why NFC and not "compare loosely".** NFC is IDEMPOTENT: every name that is already NFC keeps the key it has today,
so nothing persisted is re-keyed and no migration is owed. A case-folded or accent-stripped key would have merged
genuinely different works. The 6 NFD corpus names and 8 NFD cache names are now READ correctly; renaming the files
themselves is the owner-gated path (`normalise_corpus_names`), not this fix.

### BUG-884 (LOW, FIXED 2026-10-17) — A GOVERNED REFUSAL CRASHED WHILE REPORTING ITSELF: `ValueError: invalid literal for int()` instead of the digest mismatch it had just detected

**Measured 2026-10-17, on the first stale signature this plan ever met.** After the plan was re-derived (new digest),
the old signature became exactly what the design says it must be — REFUSED. It refused, and then crashed:

```
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'FATAL: the acceptance pins digest 2cc69892... but
ADMISSION_PLAN_20261017.json hashes to 191a13e3...'
```

`ApplierError(SystemExit)` was raised with a MESSAGE, so `.code` held that message; the handler did
`int(exc.code or RC_FATAL)` and turned every governed refusal into a traceback.

**Why it matters even though fail-closed held.** Nothing was written — the exit code was still non-zero — but the
one thing a refusal exists to do is SAY WHY, and the digest mismatch is the sentence that teaches the operator to
re-print the signature instead of hunting a ghost. A refusal that cannot speak is BUG-457's shape with the polarity
reversed: loud in exit code, silent in text.

**RED LOOP.** RED: the traceback above, on `apply_admission --dry-run` against the stale acceptance. GREEN: the same
command now prints the full sentence and exits 1, and two controls pin both branches —
`a_refusal_exits_RC_FATAL_when_its_code_is_a_message` and `a_refusal_keeps_a_declared_INTEGER_code`. The normaliser
is `applier_rc(exc)`, one function, no second handler.

### BUG-885 (MED, OPEN 2026-10-17) — `pipeline/harness_contract.py`'s DECLARED `disproven` PREFIX-CACHE STATE NO LONGER REPRODUCES: the server served 5,888 of 5,894 prompt tokens from cache, and the doctrine built on "every turn re-pays its whole prompt" is now unmeasured

**Measured 2026-10-17, one command, four models.** BUG-792 (2026-10-14) recorded `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens
= 0` on every call and declared the prefill question `disproven`, which is why the parallel-execution doctrine treats
a long agent context as an unpayable bill. Re-taken today against `localhost` OMLX with a 5,894-token prompt twice
per model:

```
Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-MLX-4bit  ttft=0.58s cached=5888/5894
gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit                ttft=11.78s (load) then 0.50s cached=5893/5896
```

The cache is WARM. Whatever the 2026-10-14 reading caught (a 4,096-token block boundary after a model load, per that
entry), it is not the steady state today, and the difference is decisive for delegation policy: a 6k-token agent turn
costs ~0.5-1.9 s of prefill, not a full re-read.

**Same day, the model question itself.** One probe — 2 tools, one dependent instruction — on four served models:

| model | prompt | ttft | decode | tool call emitted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-MLX-4bit | 5,900 | 1.87 s | 34.5 tok/s | `read_file {"path": "governance/buglog.md"}` |
| gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit | 5,901 | 0.77 s | 30.8 tok/s | same |
| Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-REAP-19B | 5,902 | 42.88 s (load) | **210.6 tok/s** | same |
| Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit | 5,904 | 134.29 s (load) | 8.2 tok/s | same |

Four of four emitted a correct tool call with the right argument. That does NOT promote any of them — one probe is a
probe, and T-187 (the two-tool, two-DEPENDENT-step fixture with a distractor and an expected answer only the second
tool's output can produce) is still the only gate. It does DISPROVE the standing sentence "only gemma can be used for
multi-turn agentic work, the rest are useless": what was measured in the past was a cold-load stall plus a cold
prefix, not a capability. The correct state word for the other three is **UNMEASURED**, and the ttft column above
shows the real operational cost is MODEL SWAP (42 s, 134 s), which a warm model does not pay.

**Owed (not done here, and not silently):** re-run BUG-792's declared protocol end to end, then either close it with
the new reading or name the variable that changed. Until then this entry holds the MEASUREMENT only, and the ladder's
`--check` readings are unaffected because BUG-792's state lives in the buglog, not in a rail.

**AMENDMENT to the entry above (same sitting, BUG-885): the artifact and the reading that CLOSE it.**

The finding above is not prose standing alone: it names work, and that work has a home. The **artifact** is
`pipeline/harness_contract.py` — the harness's own contract reader, which is the declared subject of the
`harness_adapter` capability (`config/capability_registry.yaml`) — because what BUG-792 declared `disproven` was a
property of the HARNESS contract (prefill/prefix reuse), not of a model. The **reading that re-takes it**, and the
one that would close BUG-792, is `python3 scripts/agent_context_probe.py --prefill-ab` under the protocol BUG-792
itself declared, plus the two-call cached-tokens probe used here (5,894-token prompt twice per model; the second call
read `cached=5,888`). This amendment exists so the buglog carries the route and the re-take command rather than
leaving the finding with no owner (D-3034/D-3036) — and so the route graph's shrink-only debt does not grow because a
NEW finding was recorded without its artifact.

### BUG-885 (MED, CLOSED 2026-10-17) — THE PREFIX CACHE IS PROVEN (22.2x), SO `config/agent_context.yaml`'s DISPROVEN STATE AND ITS REVISIT TRIGGER WERE BOTH STALE

**The owed reading was run, not argued.** `python3 scripts/agent_context_probe.py --prefill-ab` (BUG-792's own
protocol, on a 26,240-token prefix instead of the 5,894 one): call 1 = 22.2 s, call 2 = **1.0 s**, `cached_tokens`
**26,237 / 26,240**, **speedup 22.2x** against the declared 5.0x bar, `verdict: proven`. The cross-family control
(`Phi-4-mini-instruct-8bit`, 26,231 tokens) read 28.9 s cold. So the property BUG-792 declared `disproven` on
2026-10-14 reproduces the OTHER way today, on BOTH fixtures now (this one and the 5,894-token two-call probe,
`cached=5,888`).
**What was wrong was the STATE WORD, and it was in the wrong file.** BUG-885's amendment named
`pipeline/harness_contract.py`; the disproven claim is not there — it is declared in
`config/agent_context.yaml` (`thinking_effort.why`, `revisit_when`) and restated in `config/task_register.yaml`.
Both were corrected, not deleted: the revisit trigger is now recorded as **FIRED** rather than left standing as a
future question, and what it fires is a DECISION (may the token threshold rise toward the window now that growth is
nearly free), never an automatic edit.
**What this does NOT say:** a warm cache does not make a model capable. The DELEGATE-002 sentence is a separate
claim with its own evidence, and it is answered in AGENTS.md by a superseding block (see BUG-890).

### BUG-886 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-17) — `scripts/plan_admission.py` REFUSED "A CONTAINER THE STAGE CANNOT READ" AND DECIDED IT BY SUFFIX ALONE, SO A TRUNCATED `.epub` WAS PROPOSED FOR THE OWNER'S SIGNATURE

**The defect, in the gate's own words versus the gate's own test.** `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml` declares
that the admission refuses "a container the conversion stage cannot read"; the reader implemented that as
`suffix not in accepted`. A suffix is a CLAIM made by a name; readability is a FACT about bytes. MEASURED
2026-10-17 over all 1,289 declared containers in the two library roots: **1,286 open, 5 do not**, and every one of
the five read as an ordinary candidate. The class is not exotic — 3 are truncated downloads cut at a chunk
boundary (30,408,704 bytes = exactly 29 MiB; 137,319,019 bytes with no end-of-central-directory anywhere), one is
zeros, one is an Apple `book` archive wearing a `.pdf` suffix.
**INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, not inferred from my own probe:** `pdfinfo` on
`Encylopedia of Freemasonry - Vols 1and2.pdf` reports "Invalid XRef entry ... Top-level pages object is wrong type
(null)" and reads 0 pages. Note the file PASSES a `%PDF-` magic check — the trailer test is what catches it.
**The fix is a declaration plus one probe, not a heuristic.** `pipeline/container_integrity.py` (new) holds the
CLOSED probe vocabulary (`zip` = an end-of-central-directory must resolve; `pdf` = magic at the head AND `%%EOF`
near the end; `none` = plain text); `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml#admission.container_integrity.probes`
declares which kind uses which, so an ACCEPTED kind with no declared probe is FATAL rather than admitted
unchecked. The new class `refused_container_corrupt` is separate from `refused_container_no_stage_reads_it`
because the REMEDIES differ: a `.mobi` needs an engine (T-180), a truncated `.epub` needs a RE-DOWNLOAD.
**Cost, measured so it cannot become BUG-882 again:** the probe reads a bounded tail, 0.33 s over 1,289 files. It
is asked LAST — only of rows that would otherwise be candidates — so a cold cloud root pays for ~463 files, not
1,289, and the full dry run still prices in **17.16 s** (463 would_apply, unchanged).
BEFORE: candidates 477, `refused_container_corrupt` 0 (class absent), 5 unopenable containers proposed.
AFTER: candidates **463**, `refused_container_corrupt` **5**, plan digest `0692ce6f…`. Controls 22/22.

### BUG-887 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-17) — A FAILED CONVERSION LEFT ITS CONTAINER IN THE CORPUS: THE NEXT PLAN ABSORBED IT AS ALREADY-IN-CORPUS AND EVERY LATER S0 RUN FAILED ON IT

**Two costs from one file, both measured on the owner's first tranche.** Row 10 copied 137 MB into the corpus and
S0 failed. From then on: (1) the next plan read the container's KEY as `already_in_the_corpus`, so a work that
never arrived was silently absorbed and could never be retried through this door; (2) `pipeline/stage0_convert.py`
discovers books with `rglob('*<ext>')` and skips no dot-directory, so every later run re-failed on it —
`RED LOOP, RUN BEFORE THE FIX: Stage 0 FAILED: 1/941 book(s) failed conversion (0.1% > max_failed_ratio=0.0)`.
**FIX: the corpus holds works, not attempts.** A row whose S0 run produced no work MOVES its copy (container and
any too-small markdown) to the DECLARED `admission.applier.quarantine_prefix` and records the destination in the
receipt beside the reason. A MOVE, not a delete: R-D410 forbids this writer to delete, the bytes of a failure are
evidence, and the source is untouched. The destination must be OUTSIDE the corpus, or S0 would re-read it.
**GREEN LOOP AFTER: `python3 pipeline/stage0_convert.py` → rc 0, 0 failed, 940 skipped.** The orphan was rolled
out with the same function (receipted, `admission_quarantine/20261017T132219Z/`), and a census now reads
**0 containers without their work** in `knowledge pipeline/books` (949 md, 9 containers, every container paired).
Controls 24/24 (including: a failed row leaves no container, and a live name shadows no module callable).

### BUG-888 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-17) — `scripts/apply_admission.py` ACCEPTED `accepted_by: <your name>`: THE ONE FIELD THAT CARRIES CONSENT WAS CHECKED FOR PRESENCE, NEVER FOR RESOLUTION

**MEASURED on the owner's own signed file**: `governance/ADMISSION_ACCEPTED_20261017.yaml` carried
`accepted_by: <your name>` — the TEMPLATE'S OWN PLACEHOLDER — and the act ran. The required-field check reads
`[key for key in accept_required if key not in acc]`, so a field that is PRESENT but resolves to nothing passed
(D-3034's defect, in the signature itself). The whole authority of this applier is "the owner's word": a name
nobody answers to is not a word.
**FIX:** the placeholder is DECLARED once (`admission.applier.accept_by_placeholder`) so the template printer and
the checker cannot disagree, and the reader refuses an empty name or that placeholder — case-insensitive,
whitespace-trimmed. Two-sided control: the placeholder is REFUSED **and** a real name still passes (a check that
refused every signature would refuse the owner's own act). Controls 26/26.
**Consequence for the owner, stated plainly:** the current acceptance is REFUSED until it carries a real name, and
it must also be re-printed for the new digest (`0692ce6f…`, 463 rows) because BUG-886 changed the plan.

### BUG-889 (MED, OPEN 2026-10-17) — `scripts/normalise_corpus_names.py --census` CANNOT SEE THE 6 NFD NAMES IT EXISTS TO CURE: ITS DEFECT CLASSES ARE REGEX-ONLY

**The owner's "something is off" is a real under-report.** `--census` reads `37 corpus name defects` (34 repeated
internal space + 3 leading/trailing) while the corpus actually holds **43**: the 6 non-NFC names MEASURED on
2026-10-17 (`Apolinário`, `Ortíz`, `Abbés`, `Tomaž`, `Renée` x2, all `.md`, all in `knowledge pipeline/books`).
The reason is structural, not a count bug: `identity.name_defect_patterns` is a mapping of REGEXES and
`defect_rows()` compiles each one — "is this name NFC?" is a NORMALISATION question, and no regex can ask it. So
the census is complete over the classes it can express and blind to the one class this sitting proved is an
identity defect (D-3070).
**Not a hazard today, and that is exactly why it must be recorded rather than fixed in a hurry:** the `_key()`
collapse makes NFD storage-non-canonicality, not ambiguity (the same argument the accepted whitespace debt rests
on), and the census reads `apply_ready: False` anyway — all 37 eligible rows are refused for dangling references
(BUG-800), so no rename can be applied and nothing is silently mis-keyed. The FIX is a schema one: a defect class
whose test is a normalisation, not a pattern (a declared `name_defect_forms: {not_nfc: NFC}` read beside the
patterns), plus its own `accepted_debt` declaration with a reason of its own — NOT a `same_as` pointer, because the
blast radius differs from the whitespace class. Owner-gated by T-130/T-172, and a census that under-reports is a
false green, which is the direction this register exists to refuse.

### BUG-890 (MED, ADDRESSED 2026-10-17) — `AGENTS.md#delegate_rules` STILL CARRIES DELEGATE-002's "SINGLE-SHOT ONLY / 6.8→0.4 tok/s COLLAPSE", A CLAIM TWO FIXTURES NOW CONTRADICT; ITS OWNING DECLARATION IS `config/agent_surface.yaml#agent_md_sections`

**Why it is a bug and not stale prose.** The `delegate_rules` block is the loader an agent reads before it routes a
task, and `config/agent_surface.yaml` declares that block (and `#models`) as ADAPTER-OWNED text. Its Qwen3-Coder line
says "SINGLE-SHOT code gen ONLY … Do NOT delegate multi-turn agentic tasks — decode collapses monotonically
(~6.8→0.4 tok/s) … ~50-token stubs (DELEGATE-002, 2026-08-28)". MEASURED 2026-10-17 on two independent fixtures: the
two-tool probe decoded **34.5 tok/s** and produced a CORRECT tool call, and the fixed 3-call loop COMPLETED correctly
with 79.9 s as its slowest turn against a 90 s budget. The 2026-08-28 figure is one observation on one fixture.
**What is still true, and it is a SPEED fact, not a capability ban:** Qwen3-Coder is the slowest loop driver measured;
the fastest are MiniCPM5-2B (2.1 s) and Ornith-1.5-9B (11.5 s); a cold load costs 42–134 s TTFT.
**The act:** a superseding block appended to `AGENTS.md` — a CORRECTED routing table (loop → MiniCPM5/Ornith, review →
gemma, single-shot code → Qwen3-Coder, multi-turn on Qwen3-Coder ALLOWED with the wall clock budgeted, never a tool
loop on Phi-4-mini) plus an explicit UNMEASURED statement for long multi-turn sessions, whose only gate is T-187.
**NOT done, and named rather than implied:** `AGENTS.md` is `append_only` (D824), so the stale sentence still stands at
the top of the file and the reader is told to treat the appended block as operative. Removing it in place is an OWNER
edit to a protected file — and BUG-891 is why doing it by hand would not hold.

### BUG-891 (MED, OPEN 2026-10-17) — `config/agent_surface.yaml`'s SWAP CHECKLIST NAMES A RENDER SOURCE THAT DOES NOT EXIST, SO EVERY CORRECTION TO `AGENTS.md#delegate_rules` IS LOST ON THE NEXT HARNESS SWAP

**MEASURED 2026-10-17:** the checklist's third line is "re-render AGENTS.md#delegate_rules and #models from
`agent/adapters/<harness>/`", and `agent/adapters/` holds `CONTRACT.md`, `goose/wiring.md`,
`goose/apply_provider_flip.py` — **no template carrying the delegate_rules text** (a grep for DELEGATE-002 /
SINGLE-SHOT / 6.8 under `agent/` returns nothing). So the step is unperformable by anyone, and the block it claims to
own is in fact hand-maintained. That is a declaration with no referent (D-3034), and its consequence is concrete:
BUG-890's correction lives ONLY in an appended block, which a future "re-render" (or a hand swap done from memory)
would silently drop.
**The route (not taken here, because it is a build):** commit ONE template per harness under `agent/adapters/<harness>/`
that carries `#delegate_rules` and `#models` verbatim, plus a renderer that writes the block between markers, plus a
rail that REFUSES when the rendered region and the template disagree — so a correction has a durable home and a swap
cannot lose it. Until then the honest state is: AGENTS.md's routing text has NO declared source of truth, and this
entry is that statement rather than a silence.

## BUG-892 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-17) — THE OWNER'S WORD WAS UNPERSISTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: THE SIGNATURE PINNED A DOCUMENT AND THE NAME LIVED INSIDE A RE-PRINTABLE TEMPLATE

MEASURED (twice in one sitting, the owner's own words: *"again it failed … why the fuck are we going in circles"*):
`just admit-apply --limit 10` refused with

    FATAL: governance/ADMISSION_ACCEPTED_20261017.yaml carries accepted_by='<your name>' — a placeholder …

and no receipt was written at all (the newest run receipt stayed at 13:22Z), i.e. the run died at the SIGNATURE, not at a row.
The two faults, both structural and both mine:

1. **The name lived in a file the tool PRINTS.** `acceptance_template()` hard-coded `accepted_by: <your name>`, and
   every re-derivation of the plan forced a re-print (`--template > governance/ADMISSION_ACCEPTED_<date>.yaml`),
   which **reset the name to the placeholder**. The owner was asked to retype their own name into a generated
   artifact after every plan move. That is not a control — it prevented no authorisation and cost two runs.
2. **The word was pinned to the plan's BYTES.** `plan_sha256` meant ANY re-derivation voided a signature already
   given: a probe added (BUG-886), a count moving by one row, a timestamp. So the artifact *guaranteed* recurrence:
   fix anything → re-derive → re-print → name lost → refusal.

ROOT (D-3034, the same one three times over): **the thing signed was a DOCUMENT; the thing authorised is a SET OF ACTS.**
`plan_sha256` is not the owner's grant — `(rel, source_sha256, target, kind)` is, because that is what the applier
reads and all it reads; everything else in a plan (counts, examples, probes, a timestamp) is a derivation the owner
never signed and the applier never uses.

FIX (D-3072):
- **`scope_sha256`** pins the ordered acts; every acceptance carries the **manifest** (`rows: [rel…]`) so a moved scope
  can be REFUSED BY NAME rather than by two digests.
- **`--sign --as <name>`** is THE act (`just admit-sign "<name>"`): it declares the owner's identity ONCE in
  `config/owner_identity.yaml` (declared home `admission.applier.accept_by_identity`), pins the LIVE scope, and writes
  the acceptance crash-safe. Re-printing never touches the name again; an identity SWAP is refused, not overwritten.
- `verify_scope` proves the word two ways, strongest first: the plan's own bytes (`signed_by: digest`) or a
  re-derived plan whose ACTS are identical (`signed_by: scope`); anything else is FATAL and names the rows. A
  signature carrying no `scope_sha256` is refused (silence about what was authorised is not consent).
- The placeholder refusal now NAMES the command: it was a sentence an owner could do nothing with.
- **BUG-888 keeps its teeth**: an empty or placeholder name is still refused (two-sided control), and an absent
  identity file still yields the placeholder. What changed is only that the owner is never asked twice.
- Receipt header now records `signed_by`, `scope_sha256`, `accepted_by` — "the plan moved but the acts did not" is a
  fact a reader of a receipt can see, never infer.

CONTROLS 35/35 (`--selftest`): a moved scope is FATAL and names the change; a re-derived plan with identical acts
still matches (`scope`); a plan whose bytes are the signed ones proves by `digest`; a plan that LOST an authorised row
names it; a signature pinning no scope is refused; `--sign` refuses a placeholder/empty name, writes the identity ONCE,
its output is accepted by the applier that reads it, a different name cannot silently replace the declared identity,
and re-signing the same name is idempotent.

SUPERSEDES THE REMEDY of BUG-888 only (the refusal stands; the way to satisfy it is now a command). R5 gemma APPROVE
(`scripts/apply_admission.py` sha256_16=…).

were bounded for readability and the bound silently became the information.

FIX (D-3073): the machine plan now carries **`refused[]` — EVERY refused row, in FULL** (624 rows measured: 389 no
stage, 179 name-repair, 51 misplaced, 5 corrupt), each with its class and, for a container defect, its diagnosed
defect and declared remedy. The illustrative `examples` are no longer truncated. The human document prints a class's
rows in full when there are at most `admission.worklist_in_full` (declared: 40) of them and otherwise NAMES the class
and its task with a pointer to `refused[]` — a 389-line table is read by nobody and a worklist that is not read is

CONTROLS 25/25: EVERY refused row's handle RESOLVES on disk (a truncation anywhere fails it), the list length equals
the sum of the refusal counts, the corrupt rows name their defect and the EXACT declared remedy, and the valid

## BUG-894 (MEDIUM, FIXED 2026-10-17) — THE 5 UNOPENABLE CONTAINERS WERE ONE UNDIFFERENTIATED CLASS, AND ONE OF THEM IS NOT A CONTAINER: IT IS A DANGLING FINDER ALIAS

MEASURED over the declared library roots with the declared probe (the module's own answer, not a guess):

| bytes | head | defect |
|---|---|---|
| 137,319,019 | `PK\x03\x04`, no EOCD | `.epub` truncated download (641 local headers, 321 text entries survive) |
| 139,987 | `PK\x03\x04`, no EOCD | `.epub` truncated download |
| 30,408,704 (= exactly 29 MiB) | `%PDF-1.7`, no `%%EOF` | `.pdf` cut at a chunk boundary |
| 5,244,077 | `\x00` throughout | `.pdf` of ZERO bytes — a failed write |
| 880 | `book\x00\x00\x00\x00mark` | **a macOS Finder ALIAS** wearing a `.pdf` suffix |

BUG-886's class said "the bytes are not openable" and stopped there, which is correct as far as it goes and useless as
a worklist: four of these need BYTES, the fifth needs a POINTER RESOLVED, and two of the four need different acts again
(re-download vs re-download-and-verify). D-3071's own rule — a class exists because a REMEDY does — therefore demanded
the next layer down.

FIX (D-3073): `pipeline/container_integrity.py#diagnose()` names WHY, against a DECLARED vocabulary
(`container_integrity.defects`: truncated_zip_no_central_directory, truncated_pdf_no_trailer, null_bytes,
apple_bookmark, no_magic, unrecognised), each with its `remedy` in the gate. A defect with no remedy is FATAL, and so
is a detected shape nobody declared.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: D-3071 called this file "an Apple `book` archive". It is not an archive — `book\0\0\0\0mark`
is Apple's BOOKMARK magic, and the file is a Finder alias. MEASURED consequence, and the reason the remedy below is a
CHECK: the alias records `/Applications/Adobe After Effects 2024/Plug-ins/Effects/Keylight/docs/Keylight_1.2_AE.pdf`
and **that path does not exist on this machine** (After Effects 2024 is not installed) — the alias DANGLES, so the
work is not on this machine either. A remedy of "copy the real file in" would have sent the owner to a file that is
not there; the declared remedy now says `ls` the recorded path first, and both outcomes are written out.

MEASURED in `scripts/plan_admission.py --selftest`: labels appended to `CONTROL_LABELS` ("appended, not inserted")
left the tail of the table SHIFTED against the indices the code cited. So the NFC control's assertion reported as the

all** — yet it printed `ok`, because the printer reads the LABEL TABLE and never the assertions. A control suite that

the controls added — it reads this file's own text and requires every index in the table to be CITED, so a label can
