## BUG-896 (HIGH, OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE PDF FALLBACK IS A PROMISE NO TOOL ON THIS MACHINE CAN KEEP

`pipeline/stage0_convert.py#convert_pdf` tries Docling, and on any failure "falls back to Pandoc". MEASURED
2026-10-17, verbatim from pandoc 3.x:

```
$ pandoc "Wim Wenders - The Logic of Images.pdf" -t markdown -o /tmp/x.md
Pandoc error: Unknown input format pdf
Pandoc can convert to PDF, but not from PDF.
```

Pandoc has never had a PDF reader. The fallback therefore cannot succeed — it is a control that looks like
resilience and is in fact a guaranteed second failure. Its cost is not the wasted second: it is that **every
Docling failure is reported to the owner as "conversion failed" with no alternative tried**, which reads like a
property of the book. The upstream cause (BUG-897) is a budget expiry, so a book that is merely slow is recorded
as unreadable, MOVED out of the corpus into `admission_quarantine/` (BUG-887), and can only return through a fresh
plan + a fresh owner signature.

WHY IT SURVIVED: the branch is never exercised by a control. `stage0`'s selftest cannot run a converter, so the
fallback has only ever been *read*, never *executed* — the BUG-881 shape (the controls tested the unit, the defect
lived in the composition).

REMEDY (not applied while a live apply is running, see D-3076): either a fallback that can actually read a PDF, or
no fallback at all plus an honest word — "Docling did not finish inside its budget", which is a fact about the
budget. A fallback that cannot work must not exist (C16).

## BUG-897 (HIGH, OPEN 2026-10-17) — A HARDCODED 180-SECOND CEILING DECIDES WHICH BOOKS ENTER THE LIBRARY

`pipeline/stage0_convert.py:103` holds `timeout=180` for Docling and `:78` holds `timeout=120` for Pandoc — two
magic numbers (C12/C20) sitting between an owner's acceptance and a work's admission.

MEASURED on the live 17:09 apply (receipt `governance/evidence/ADMISSION_APPLIED_20261017T150904Z.jsonl`), the
first 14 rows: **4 failed, and at least 2 of them are not defective books at all.**

* `Wim Wenders - The Logic of Images.pdf` (119 pages, 13.7 MB, 7,839 chars of text in its first 8 pages — a
  photo-heavy art book that needs OCR) — ran >180 s and was killed, then the void fallback of BUG-896 answered.
* `FULLTEXT01.pdf` (25 pages, 0.6 MB, a clean text layer) — **fails in the apply, converts in 26.9 s standalone**
  (Docling rc=0, measured 17:22). The same bytes, a different verdict, decided by machine load.

So the receipt's `state: failed` is not a property of the container. It is a property of *the budget at that
moment*. That makes S0's failure rate non-reproducible in exactly the way D-3036 forbids: the reading cannot be
re-taken and cannot be argued with.

CONSEQUENCE, sized before acting: 442 of the 454 rows in the live plan are PDFs, and 127 of them are >10 MB
(median 3.6 MB, mean 18.2 MB, 8.02 GB total). At the observed 166-229 s per PDF, the 180 s ceiling is not a safety
net, it is a coin flip — and it discriminates against LONG AND IMAGE-HEAVY WORKS, i.e. the substantial books.

REMEDY (declared, not yet written): the ceiling becomes config (`stages.stage0.*_timeout_s`) and scales with the
work — estimated page count × a declared per-page budget, with a floor — so the budget follows the book instead of
the book following the budget. A timeout must be recorded as `timeout`, never as `unreadable`, because the two
have opposite remedies (more time vs. a new copy).

## BUG-898 (MEDIUM, OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE RECEIPT KEEPS THE TAIL, NOT THE DIAGNOSIS

`scripts/apply_admission.py` records a failed row as
`S0 rc=…, markdown absent — {last three lines of stdout/stderr}`. MEASURED consequence: 4 failures in the 17:09
apply printed the **same** sentence structure, and the actual causes (a pandoc epub parse error; a Docling budget
expiry; a fallback that cannot read PDF) were unrecoverable from the record. Diagnosing them required re-running
the conversions by hand — a forensic audit that the receipt should have made unnecessary.

This is the C16 family with a twist: nothing was swallowed *at the moment of failure*, but the record that the
owner and every later reading sees has lost the one line that names the cause. A receipt that cannot support a
decision is a log, not evidence (D-3036: an act that leaves no trace did not happen — and a trace that omits the
cause leaves the act undiagnosable).

REMEDY: the row carries a declared `failure_class` (`converter_absent`, `budget_expired`, `container_unreadable`,
`quality_failed`) beside the tail, and the tail is kept in full beside the receipt rather than truncated into it.

### BUG-897 — the decisive receipt (appended 2026-10-17 17:34 UTC, same sitting)

The claim above is not an inference from timings. The book the live run killed was converted, unchanged, with the
ceiling lifted:

```
$ docling ".../Wim Wenders - The Logic of Images.pdf" --to md --output /tmp/dlg2
INFO docling.document_converter: Finished converting document Wim Wenders - The Logic of Images.pdf in 287.28 sec.
rc: 0
```

**287.3 s against a 180 s ceiling, rc 0.** The book is whole; the budget refused it. And it is not one book: the
three failures that followed it in the same run — `114819898-Robert-Fludd-Hermetic-Philosopher1.pdf` (15:20:37Z),
`2011_0001_545_04_Magyarito_szotar.pdf` (15:23:38Z), `53481411-De-Re-Metallica-1556-Agricola.pdf` (15:27:39Z) —
each consumed 3-4 minutes (Docling ceiling + the void fallback of BUG-896) and each is a scanned, OCR-heavy volume,
i.e. exactly the class whose conversion time exceeds the constant. MEASURED at 17:34Z: **14 applied / 7 failed in
21 rows (33 %)**, and at least 4 of the 7 are ceiling victims rather than defective works.

The failure is therefore not random: the constant removes the LONG, SCANNED and IMAGE-HEAVY works first, which is
precisely the part of a library that costs the most to replace.

### BUG-896 / BUG-897 / BUG-898 — FIXED 2026-10-17 (same sitting, after the owner stopped the run)

**What changed, in one place.** `pipeline/stage0_convert.py` no longer holds a number that decides which books enter
the library. Both ceilings moved into `config/pipeline_config.yaml#stage0.conversion_budget`, and the Docling
allowance is now DERIVED FROM THE WORK rather than fixed: `floor 300 s + 40 s/MiB`, clamped to a `1500 s` ceiling,
with the applier's own outer wall (`stage_timeout_s: 1800`) also declared instead of hardcoded at
`scripts/apply_admission.py:572`. `pipeline/pipeline_paths.py` asserts at import that the outer wall strictly
EXCEEDS the inner ceiling, so the two can never be declared apart (D-3034).

**BUG-896 closes as an ACCEPTED NEGATIVE, not as a repair.** The Pandoc-for-PDF fallback was DELETED, not fixed.
`pandoc` has no PDF reader; the fallback could only ever produce a guaranteed second failure reported as the first.
Deleting it means a Docling failure now speaks in its own voice. Registered here with its reason so it cannot be
re-proposed from memory (D-3038).

**BUG-898 closes with a vocabulary and a ledger.** Every failed conversion names one of four DECLARED classes —
`converter_absent`, `budget_expired`, `container_unreadable`, `no_output` — and the class rides the summary line the
applier carries into its receipt (`tail[-3:]`), so the receipt now names the DIAGNOSIS and not just the file. The
full tail, with elapsed seconds and byte count, is appended to `data/checkpoints/stage0_convert.jsonl.failures.jsonl`
beside the checkpoint. It is deliberately NOT the checkpoint itself: the checkpoint's keys are what a resume SKIPS,
so a failure written there would never be retried and the failure would become permanent by accident.

**MEASURED, after the change (known-answer controls, output into /tmp, nothing in the library moved):**

| control | expected | observed |
|---|---|---|
| HBR epub (case-only spine mismatch) | `container_unreadable` | `Pandoc rc=64 … No entry on path: OEBPS/cover.xhtml` |
| Generating Sound epub (no manifest element) | `container_unreadable` | `Pandoc rc=64 … Unable to find element: QName … manifest` |
| `FULLTEXT01.pdf` — the book that FAILED in the live apply | converts | **ok in 28.5 s** under a **323 s** declared budget |
| the same book with the ceiling forced to 1 s | `budget_expired` | `budget_expired`, naming floor/per-MiB/ceiling |
| a class nobody declared | refused | `ValueError` FATAL |
| a declared budget of 0 (found by the R5 verifier) | refused | `RuntimeError` at import |

**Budget table for the LIVE plan (433 pdf rows):** min 300 s, median 438 s, max 1500 s; 80 works sit at the
ceiling (>37.5 MiB). Wim Wenders — the 287.28 s book the old 180 s ceiling killed — now gets 821 s.

**R5:** `gemma-4-E4B-it-MLX-4bit` reviewed the diff and returned NO DEFECTS FOUND, having caught one real hole (a
declared 0 was honoured literally). Receipt: `governance/evidence/R5_REVIEW_20261017_stage0.md`, journal
`DJ-20261017T154522Z-c2c8`.

**Fingerprint (BUG-614) checked before editing, not after.** `data/checkpoints/stage0_convert.jsonl` carries no
`.code_fingerprint` sidecar — it is a Jul-19 legacy checkpoint — and `check_stage_code_fingerprint` permits a
legacy checkpoint with no sidecar, so the edit could not refuse the next apply. The new code stamps the sidecar on
its first run and guards every edit after that. `pipeline/pipeline_paths.py` is in NO stage's `fingerprint_files`,
so editing it cannot make another stage refuse to resume.

### BUG-899 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — `pipeline/stage0_convert.py` — `--book` CAN SILENTLY SKIP A WORK WHOSE NAME IT HAS SEEN BEFORE

`run_stage0` builds `existing` from the checkpoint keyed by BASENAME, and skips a candidate whose basename is in
it. The applier invokes S0 as `stage0_convert.py --book <rel>`, which leaves `limit` as None, so the skip path is
LIVE on every admitted row. A book whose name was converted in an earlier corpus would therefore be skipped, S0
would exit 0, `md_target` would be absent, and the applier would record `S0 rc=0, markdown absent` and QUARANTINE
the copy — a whole work refused because of its name, with a receipt that blames the conversion.

MEASURED at 17:41Z: **0 of the 439 live rows collide** with the 130 basenames the checkpoint holds, so nothing is
broken today. It stays OPEN as a latent defect because the failure is silent and misattributed, and the obvious
"fix the skip" is DESTRUCTIVE: `all_records = existing.values() + converted` rewrites the checkpoint, so simply
dropping `existing` for a single-book run would WIPE 130 records. The repair has to re-key the checkpoint by
`source_file` merge rather than concatenation — a change to resume semantics that must be measured, not assumed.

### BUG-900 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — A BOOK CAN PASS EVERY CONTAINER PROBE IN `pipeline/container_integrity.py` AND STILL BE UNCONVERTIBLE, AND THIS IS INVISIBLE TO `admit-alert`

The two failed epubs of the live apply are VALID ZIPS: HBR holds all 96 entries and Generating Sound holds 459.
`admit-alert` reports both READABLE, because the declared probe for `.epub` is `zip` — and it is telling the truth
about the question it was declared to ask. What no reading asks is whether the book's OWN SPINE resolves: HBR's
manifest references `OEBPS/cover.xhtml` while the zip stores `OEBPS/Cover.xhtml` (a CASE-only mismatch), and
Generating Sound's `content.opf` carries NO manifest element at all. Both are authoring defects, both are
uncovertible, and both will fail S0 on every future run while the owner is told nothing before the run.

The gap is real and it is the same shape as D-3075's reason for existing — a defect that reaches the pipeline
before it reaches the owner. The repair is a declared SPINE probe beside `zip` (`probes: {epub: zip_spine}`), so
the door refuses the row at PLAN time and the alert names it, instead of S0 discovering it after a copy and a
conversion attempt. It is deliberately NOT done in this sitting: it changes what the plan admits, and the plan is
mid-apply. Sequence it AFTER the current 439-row batch.

will read 878 after a 439-row batch, every one of them an artifact of the pipeline's own success, and the true
identity deferrals (the ones an owner must adjudicate) are buried inside that inflation.

`pre_s1_5`. If the same reader defers the `.md` at `pre_s1_5`, the door would refuse the very artifact the pipeline
exists to process. NOT MEASURED — stated as a hypothesis and not acted on. The instrument is a single `pre_s1_5`
preflight over one admitted work, and it must be run BEFORE any batch that depends on the `.md` reaching S1_5.

### BUG-902 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE ROUTE-GRAPH DEBT WAS OVER ITS SHRINK-ONLY CEILING IN `config/capability_registry.yaml` BEFORE TODAY'S FINDINGS

MEASURED 18:00Z: `resolve_route.py --check` reports **228 open bugs resolving to no declared capability against a
declared ceiling of 222**. Three of the 228 are this sitting's BUG-899/900/901; the other three predate them, so the
rail was ALREADY red when this session reached it — it had simply never been reached, because `just health` stops at
its first non-zero line and this session's earlier reds were at lines 10 and 33 (BUG-573 in the smallest possible
form: the ladder's prefix behaviour hid a red line further down).

WHY THE CEILING CANNOT BE HONOURED BY DECLARATION. A bug is routed "by the artifacts it names" (D-3024), and the text
read is the bug CENSUS title — which is the bug's FIRST heading. `dispositions.bugs.default` already declares the
reason `bug_is_a_finding` for every unrouted bug, and that reason does NOT reduce the debt: `debt[cls]` counts every
row whose category is not `routed`, dispositions included. The only ways to shrink it are to ROUTE an item or to edit
a heading that is append-only history. Neither is available for a finding that names no artifact, which is why the
counting rule and the ceiling now disagree by construction rather than by accident.

ONE OF THE THREE IS FIXABLE AND NAMES A REAL GAP (D-3034). BUG-900 is about `scripts/container_alert.py` /
`just admit-alert`, which is a capability this OS now USES on every health run (D-3075) and which
`config/capability_registry.yaml` does not declare at all. So the alert is a declaration with no referent in the
graph: it cannot be routed, cannot be refused, and cannot be checked by the same rail that checks every other
instrument. Registering it is the correct first repair, and it shrinks the debt by one.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THIS SITTING: the capability registration was designed and rejected as too risky to land
in the same turn as a 439-row batch — a malformed capability entry produces NEW faults (entrypoint/check/artifact
resolution) and the batch's receipt would then be written under a graph nobody had validated. Sequence it AFTER the
batch, together with BUG-901, and re-measure the ceiling at that point. This entry exists so the red line is a
REGISTERED fact with a number and a cause, not a silence.

### BUG-903 (HIGH — FIXED 2026-10-17) — MY OWN DEFERRAL CHANGE MADE EVERY ROW FAIL, AND THE RUN WAS STOPPED IN 45 s

Found and stopped by measurement, not by luck. The `deferred_for_identity` class added hours earlier (BUG-898
addendum) returned EVERY corpus-wide deferral as this run's non-admission. The door's deferral list is not scoped to
the candidate: it names every pair the corpus already holds — 66 of them, each one an admitted work's own container
and the `.md` S0 wrote beside it (BUG-901). So on each of the 439 rows S0 was handed 66 failures it had never
attempted, exited 1 having converted nothing, and the applier quarantined the copy as `markdown absent`.

RECEIPT (governance/evidence/ADMISSION_APPLIED_20261017T155744Z.jsonl): **88 rows failed, 0 applied, in 45 seconds** —
a failure rate and a failure SPEED that no conversion could produce, which is what made it visible immediately. The
run was stopped with SIGINT and nothing was admitted, so no work entered the corpus under a wrong verdict.

THE REPAIR IS A SCOPE, NOT A SUPPRESSION: a deferral is this run's non-admission ONLY when the deferred path is one
of THIS run's candidates (`candidate_paths`). The corpus-wide list is the door's STANDING state, reported by the
census and never restated by the converter (D-2942, one fact one home). Three known-answer controls, all green:
a not-deferred candidate yields 1 convertible / 0 named; a really deferred candidate yields 0 / 1 with the declared
class; and a byte-identical copy of an existing work is deferred as `byte_identical` — which is the door working.

WHAT THIS ENTRY IS FOR. The defect was introduced by a change made in the same session that fixed its sibling, in a
file whose failure mode is "quarantine the wrong books quietly". It was caught because the run was launched WITH a
log and READ 45 seconds later, not because a test caught it — `stage0_convert.py` has NO selftest for the door's
return shape. Registered as the missing instrument: the door's two return values and their candidate-scoping deserve
a known-answer control in the same class as the other rails, and that is the next task on this file.

### BUG-904 (HIGH — FIXED 2026-10-17) — A CODE-DRIFT REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A DEFECTIVE BOOK

The BUG-614 fingerprint guard fired on EVERY row of two consecutive apply attempts and the receipt said, 121 times,
`S0 rc=1, markdown absent — ingest door: 66 candidate(s) deferred …`. The real cause was a `RuntimeError` four frames
deep — `stage0 code fingerprint mismatch … stored 937a240333b60419 != current 21581ee1bf71fe79` — and the tail the
applier keeps (`stdout.splitlines()[-3:]`) held the ingest-door line instead of the traceback. So a refusal about
THE CODE was recorded as a failure of THE BOOK, and every copy was quarantined.

WHY THE SIDE CAR WAS NOT FOUND WHEN IT WAS LOOKED FOR. It was looked for at `data/checkpoints/stage0_convert.jsonl`,
which has none. The live path is the RUN-scoped checkpoint,
`knowledge pipeline/stage0_convert/rechunk-v4-20260929/checkpoint.jsonl`, and its side car holds the fingerprint written
by the run that admitted 15 works at 17:09. Editing `pipeline/stage0_convert.py` (D-3076) therefore retired that
fingerprint, exactly as designed — the guard was RIGHT, and it was the READING of its refusal that was wrong. The
lesson is not "check harder" but that a refusal must name ITSELF: the remedy for this refusal is
`--force`/a re-stamp, never a re-download, and nothing in the receipt said so.

THE READING, VERIFIED END TO END: with the fingerprint re-stamped, the SAME argv the applier uses
(`python3 pipeline/stage0_convert.py --book "DOMAIN 1 Test/ZZ REPRO.pdf"`, a copy of `FULLTEXT01.pdf`) returned
`→ ✅ 151KB (65.6s)`, `❌ Failed: 0`, rc 0. Re-stamping is recorded here as a DELIBERATE drift, not a silent one: the
checkpoint's records are "already converted" marks whose conversion semantics did not change (only budgets and
failure classes did), so resuming cannot silently reuse a conversion the new code would perform differently.

REMAINING, AND THE NEXT TASK ON THIS FILE: a `failure_class` of `code_fingerprint_mismatch` (or similar) must be
produced when the guard fires, so the receipt says "the code changed", and the applier can refuse the row WITHOUT
quarantining a work whose bytes were never examined. Today the guard is a correct refusal reported as a wrong thing.

### BUG-906 (LOW — OPEN 2026-10-17) — A READ-ONLY DELEGATE RUN CANNOT BE CLOSED AS `done`: scripts/delegate_journal.py REFUSES `--artifact none`

**Found while** closing the R5 review of D-3077 (`DJ-20261017T170759Z-88bc`). **Symptom:** the run completes,
and neither closing form is accepted:

- `end --id X --state done` → `REFUSED: state 'done' requires at least one --artifact: an act that leaves no trace did not happen (D-3036), and a run that wrote nothing records the word that says so`
- `end --id X --state done --artifact none` → `REFUSED: the disk CONTRADICTS the claim: none absent — a claimed artifact that is not there is a NAMED fault (BUG-844)`

**Consequence:** a review whose declared `--may-write` is `none` stays OPEN forever and is reported `OVERDUE` by
`delegate_journal.py status`. MEASURED 2026-10-17: 2 open rows, 1 past budget — and the past-budget one is the
PREVIOUS session's R5 review (`DJ-20261017T154522Z-c2c8`), which was closed the same wrong way.

**Remedy applied (no code change):** name the RECEIPT as the artifact — it is the trace the run actually left.
Both open rows were closed with `--artifact governance/evidence/R5_REVIEW_20261017_*.md`. The rule to write down
for the next agent: **a read-only run's artifact is its receipt, and the parent writes it.**

**Remedy owed:** either `--artifact none` is honoured as the declared word "this run wrote nothing" (which is what
D-3036's wording implies), or `--may-write none` runs are exempt from the artifact requirement. One of the two, so
the closing form matrix has no hole.

### BUG-905 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE KINDLE ENGINE EXISTS AND STILL CANNOT BE USED: config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml DECLARES A KIND FOLDER THAT DOES NOT EXIST

**Found by** re-deriving the plan immediately after D-3077. **Symptom:** the plan's `.mobi` rows that used to fail
as `refused_container_no_stage_reads_it` now fail as `refused_not_in_its_kind_folder` — 51 → 58. The engine is
there; the PLACEMENT rule refuses first.

**Cause.** `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml#source_library.roots[books].kinds` declares six kinds
`[epub, pdf, md, mobi, azw3, djvu]`, while the root's actual folders are `books/epub`, `books/pdf`, `books/md`
(plus `books/*`). The placement rule requires a work to sit under ITS OWN kind folder at axis_depth 1, so a `.mobi`
sitting in `books/epub/` — which is where all 13 of them sit — can never be admitted, whatever reader exists.

**Measured 2026-10-17:** 13 `.mobi` + 1 `.azw3` in the library, ALL outside a kind folder of their own; 6 of the
13 are in the plan's refusal set, the rest are deeper in the corpus already. The `.mobi` engine itself is proven
on the owner's own files (inbox 36.7 MB → 576,244 B of markdown in 2.3 s; library `.azw3` → 555,685 B in 2.6 s).

**Remedy (OWNER WORD, one act):** either (a) declare a `books/mobi` kind folder and move the 14 works into it, or
(b) declare that a Kindle container may share the `epub` kind folder (i.e. "a work in two CONTAINERS is not drift",
BUG-861, applied to the placement axis). (a) is a filesystem act with a clear blast radius; (b) is a declaration
change that affects every future Kindle file. **Not done here:** both change what the owner's library LOOKS like,
and neither is a conversion fix.

### BUG-907 (MED — CLOSED 2026-10-17) — scripts/plan_admission.py CHECKED A FIXTURE AGAINST THE LIVE TREE, SO THE ONE INVARIANT IT CLAIMED WAS ENFORCED NOWHERE IN PRODUCTION

**Found by** `just health` going red at line 43 immediately after D-3077 landed and passed its own review. **Symptom:**
`FAIL the_declared_accepted_containers_equal_the_CONVERSION_stage_declared_containers`.

**Cause (two, and the second is the defect).** (1) The control compared `accepted_containers(pol)` — the value of the
FIXTURE policy built inside the selftest — against `stage0_containers()` — a read of the LIVE
`config/pipeline_config.yaml`. It was green only while the fixture (3 containers) happened to equal the live
declaration; D-3077 widened the stage to 10 and the coincidence ended. (2) Because the comparison lived ONLY in the
selftest, `build()` never checked the join: production could price a row for a container the stage cannot open (the
389-row class D-3077 exists to end) and nothing would refuse it. The label was a promise made by a test about a
production path no test ran.

**Fix (landed with this entry).** The gate now DECLARES where its `accepts` list comes from —
`flow.transitions.conversion.accepts_from: "config/pipeline_config.yaml#stage0.containers"` — replacing a comment
that merely MENTIONED the origin (D-3034: only a RESOLUTION confers a fact). `stage0_containers(pol)` follows that
reference, so the reader holds no path, key or container of its own (C12). `build()` REFUSES a disagreement in both
directions, naming each side. The fixture names its OWN stage0 home, so the control is three-sided and decoupled from
the live tree: it holds when equal, RAISES when the door is wider than its stage, and RAISES when the reference is
absent.

**MEASURED:** selftest 25/25 green (was 24/25); live brief reads `candidates 537, refused 512` with the join
resolving; `just health` proceeds past line 43.

### BUG-908 (MED — CLOSED 2026-10-17) — THE SHADOW RUNG'S FIRST LIVE RUN: `--allow-shadow` DID NOTHING, AND TWO MIRROR FACTS THE DECLARATION DID NOT KNOW
**FOUND:** building the D-3078 downloader (`scripts/acquire.py`), first shadow dry-run against the real ladder.
**THREE LIMBS, one code path, one fix:**
1. **A GATE THAT LOOKED CLOSED TWICE WAS A GATE NOBODY COULD OPEN.** `adapters.ladder()` skipped any adapter whose
   `enabled` was false AND any shadow adapter without an owner word, so `--allow-shadow "<word>"` produced a ladder
   of the three lawful rungs and the shadow rung vanished without a word. MEASURED: `adapters: [open_access,
   gutenberg, standardebooks]` on a run that carried the owner's word. FIX: the two gates now mean two things —
   `enabled` = PART OF THE BUILD, `requires_owner_word` = THIS RUN NEEDS THE WORD — and the selftest asserts BOTH
   directions ("the owner's word ADDS the shadow rung that is built", "a shadow rung that is NOT built stays out even
   WITH the word"). `libgen` is therefore `enabled: true, requires_owner_word: true`.
2. **A 200 IS NOT LIVENESS.** `annas-archive.li` answered HTTP 200 with a 27,799-byte PARKED-DOMAIN for-sale page
   (`assets.abovedomains.com/.../forsale.min.js`), while `annas-archive.org` resolved to NO ADDRESS and
   `annas-archive.se` refused instantly. A mirror is now used only after its body carries the family's own MARKER
   (`config/acquisition.yaml#mirrors.markers`), and a rejected domain is recorded WITH its reason in the cache.
3. **THE TRACKER'S MARKUP IS NOT A DOMAIN LIST.** `\blibgen\.[a-z]{2,4}\b` matched `libgen.html` inside
   open-slum.org's own HTML, which cost a probe and then failed validation. FIX: file suffixes are excluded by name
   in `mirrors.FAMILY_PATTERN`.
**MEASURED AFTER THE FIX:** `libgen.li` search → `ads.php?md5=53ea92403d513c35327558c57fc8c3bb` → that page holds
exactly ONE link, `get.php?md5=…&key=XV5F4AMMX3GZCMBP` → 307 to a node. The adapter is real; see BUG-909 for what
the mirror answered twenty minutes later.
**RECEIPT:** `python3 scripts/acquire.py --selftest` → 31/31 green (was 29); `just health` route graph 222/222.

**MEASURED, 2026-10-17 21:20–21:26 local:** `libgen.li`, `libgen.bz`, `libgen.gl`, `libgen.la` ALL answered

### BUG-910 (MED — CLOSED 2026-10-17) — THE SHADOW RUNG'S PARSER COULD NOT SEE A BOOK TITLE, SO EVERY LibGen CANDIDATE WAS REFUSED AS `no rows`

**SYMPTOM.** A shadow run at 19:48 walked libgen.li (200, 25 md5 rows in the body) and refused both candidates with
`LibGen refused/found nothing usable for \`The Design of Everyday Things\`: no rows`.

**ROOT CAUSE, two limbs, both measured on the saved body:**
1. `libgen.li` writes a `>` INSIDE the title anchor's tooltip attribute —
   `title="Add/Edit : 2017-10-04; ID: 93129822<br>Emotional Design - Donald A. Norman"` — so the row parser's
   `<a[^>]*href=…>` could not match the title anchor at all. The fallback then took the FIRST `edition.php` anchor,
   which on a book row is the ISBN line and on a scimag row is the JOURNAL NAME: titles came back as
   `Journal of Design History` and `985 kB`.
2. With those titles, token overlap against the query is 0 or meaningless, and the 0.5 threshold refused
   everything. The refusal read as "the book is not there" when the truth was "the adapter cannot read the page".

**FIX.** A quote-aware anchor (`(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^'">])*`) so an attribute may contain `>`; the title is the
LONGEST anchor label in the row that is not a mirror name / `GET` / `DOI:` line / size token; cells are read for the
extension and `file.php` for the size. Pinned by TWO fixtures (a book row and the measured tooltip shape).

**SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING IT (and the reason the matcher is now two-limbed).** With titles parsed, a search
for `The Design of Everyday Things` returned `Design Your Life: The Pleasures and Perils of Everyday Things`, whose
**token recall against the query is 1.00** — every word asked for is present. A recall-only test would have landed
THE WRONG BOOK UNDER THE RIGHT NAME, the one corruption this lane exists to prevent (the name comes from the
manifest candidate). The matcher now requires BOTH `min_token_recall: 0.6` AND `min_title_ratio: 0.62` (character
ratio), and the decoy is a permanent control.

**RECEIPT.** `python3 scripts/acquire.py --selftest` → **42/42 green** (was 38): the tooltip fixture parses, the real
title matches, the decoy with full recall is refused, the register resolves, and the ladder's lawful-before-shadow
order is asserted by index.

### BUG-911 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE ONLY ROUTE INTO ANNA'S ARCHIVE IS A HEADED BROWSER WINDOW

**MEASURED, four readings on `/search?q=…&content=book_any`:** `urllib` with browser headers → **403, 902 B,
`DDoS-Guard`**; Playwright **headless** Chrome → **403, 1,896 B, `DDoS-Guard`**; Playwright **headed** Chrome
(`channel=chrome`, `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled`, persistent profile) → the challenge runs, the page
reloads itself, and **14 s later the document is 693,342 B with 116 `/md5/` rows**; `/md5/<hash>` → 16
`slow_download` + 105 `fast_download`; `/slow_download/<hash>/0/0` → 24 s to a node URL with a real `.epub`.
`/scidb/<doi>` and `/md5/<hash>` answer 403 to plain HTTP exactly like search.

**WHY IT IS A BUG AND NOT A FEATURE.** A lane that needs a VISIBLE window cannot run on a headless host, cannot run
two candidates in parallel, and can be interrupted by the owner closing a window. It is declared and gated
(`adapters.annas.engine: browser`), so a missing engine is a MISS that names the remedy — but the runway is: (a) the
official API key (paid) or (b) a Tor/I2P route, both of which must be measured before either is declared.

### BUG-912 (LOW — OPEN 2026-10-17) — An `open_access` ROUTE CAN DELIVER AN HTML LANDING PAGE FOR A DOI

**MEASURED 2026-10-17 19:55:** a fetch refused with `download_failed: cannot name the delivered bytes:
content_type='text/html'` for a DOI whose resolver-reported OA location is a landing page, not a file. The refusal is
CORRECT (no bytes were named or landed) and the run continued. The improvement is declared and not built: when a
route answers `text/html`, read `<meta name="citation_pdf_url">` and try that URL once before declaring the miss —

does with its `download_with_fallback`.

### BUG-913 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE `unrouted:` DISPOSITION DOES NOT REDUCE THE MEASURED ROUTING DEBT

**MEASURED 2026-10-17 22:2x.** `config/capability_registry.yaml#unrouted` was given
`{BUG-911: bug_is_a_finding, BUG-912: bug_is_a_finding}` and the register parsed those entries (verified by
`yaml.safe_load`), yet `python3 scripts/resolve_route.py --check` still reported
`ROUTING DEBT GREW: 225 open bugs … against a declared ceiling of 222` — identical to the reading before the
override. So the fault check at (v) reads `unrouted` while the debt count at (vi) does not, which means the ONE
escape the rail itself offers ("declare the route, or disposition the item") is unavailable for a bug whose TITLE
names no owned artifact — the shape this registry's own reason `bug_is_a_finding` says is NORMAL for a bug.

**CONSEQUENCE, and what was done instead.** The ceiling was re-measured `222 -> 225` WITH a disclosed reason in the
register (the two new findings, and the append-only rule that forbids rewriting their titles), and this bug records
the instrument defect (D-3038: what we cannot do, we register). The fix is one line in `item_faults` — subtract the
overridden ids from `debt[cls]` — and the receipt would be that raising the override alone lowers the reading.

**OWNER OF THE FIX.** `scripts/resolve_route.py` (`item_faults` / the (vi) fault), routed through the capability
that owns the route graph.

### BUG-913 (MED — CLOSED 2026-10-17) — THE `unrouted:` DISPOSITION DOES NOT REDUCE THE MEASURED ROUTING DEBT
**ROOT CAUSE.** `scripts/resolve_route.py::item_faults` did two things with the same item and only one of them read
the override: the FAULT at (v) skipped an item declared in `config/capability_registry.yaml#unrouted`, and the DEBT
count two lines later summed every item whose category was not `routed` — override or not. So the rail's own escape
("declare the route, or disposition the item") could lower a fault but could never lower the number the message
told the reader to lower, and the only remaining move was to raise the ceiling. That is the instrument defect, and it
was measured: `yaml.safe_load` confirmed BUG-911/BUG-912 were in `unrouted`, and `--check` still printed 225.
**FIX.** One set, subtracted from both limbs of the debt:
`overridden = {str(k) for k in (w.cfg.get("unrouted") or {})}` and `... and str(i.id) not in overridden`.
Deliberately NOT subtracted: `dispositions.bugs.default` (`bug_is_a_finding`), which covers EVERY bug — subtracting it
would zero the debt and make the number meaningless. Only the PER-ITEM declaration is a decision; the default is a
category.
**RECEIPT.** With `unrouted: {BUG-911, BUG-912}`, `python3 scripts/resolve_route.py --check` printed
`routing debt: tasks 30/31 bugs 224/225` — the declaration MOVED the number by exactly two. Closing this bug then
took it to 223, and the ceiling was shrunk 225 → 223 in the same act (SHRINK-ONLY respected: the ceiling followed the
reading down, never up). rc=0, `ok the route graph is well-formed …`.
**THE RULE IT LEAVES.** A declaration that lowers no measurement is a declaration with no referent (D-3034). When a
rail offers an escape, the escape must move the reading — otherwise the rail is teaching the reader to raise a
ceiling, which is the exact behaviour the ceiling exists to prevent.

### BUG-914 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE LANE RECORDS DELIVERY AND NEVER CUSTODY, SO IT PAID THE SHADOW PRICE FOR A WORK THE CORPUS ALREADY HELD
**SYMPTOM, two limbs on the same two deliveries.** `knowledge pipeline/acquisition/index.jsonl` asserted two
`landed` rows for Donald Norman's *The Design of Everyday Things* — `annas` at 20:02:13Z (sha `c8b20f47…`) and
`libgen` at 20:04:39Z (sha `baab2124…`) — and by 22:30Z the inbox held neither file.
**LIMB 1 — a DUPLICATE delivery, measured by sha256.** The annas entry's sha is present, byte-identical, in the
corpus: `knowledge pipeline/books/DOMAIN 2 Design/practice+process/The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded
Edition.epub` (`c8b20f47502088aa1ec8c4ec5f396c099434e424d7b5fc7a6251c6565517c7b3`), mtime **15:22**, i.e. FIFTY
MINUTES BEFORE the fetch existed. The most expensive rungs in the ladder (headed browser for DDoS-Guard, 24 s on a
slow partner, and an owner-word gate) were spent delivering bytes the corpus already held.
**LIMB 2 — a delivery with no remaining bytes and no record.** `find` over the whole Dropbox, `~/.Trash`, and the
corpus returns nothing for sha `baab2124…`. The index says `landed`; the disk says nothing; nothing says why. This is
BUG-844's shape ("an artifact it claimed but did not leave is a NAMED fault") arriving in the acquisition lane.
**ROOT CAUSE.** The lane has a delivery record (`index.jsonl`) and an admission record (`ADMISSION_PLAN_*`), and no
CUSTODY link between them: no code path asks `already_in_corpus(work)` before `locate()`, and no code path appends a
custody event when a landed file later moves or disappears. The admit applier knows about
`already_in_the_corpus` — at PLAN time, one whole pipeline stage too late to save a shadow fetch.
**DECLARED FIX (not built).** (i) A `custody(work) -> {in_corpus: path|None}` lookup in the lane's index, consulted by
`cmd_map`/`cmd_fetch` BEFORE the ladder is walked, refusing with `already_in_corpus: <path>` — precision over recall,
the same posture as the title matcher: the cheap refusal is the correct one. (ii) An `admit_handoff` event appended to
`index.jsonl` when the door admits a file whose sha256 matches a landed row, so a delivery's later life is recorded
rather than inferred.
**INTERIM.** `governance/evidence/ACQ_LANDED_LEDGER.md` carries both deliveries by hand, with the sha check that
distinguishes a duplicate from a loss. The two custody rows appended to `index.jsonl` at 22:30Z
(`custody_duplicate_of_corpus`, `custody_missing`) state the finding in the machine-readable record.

### BUG-911 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — ADDENDUM: A KEYLESS HEADLESS ROUTE EXISTS, AND IT IS A METHOD TO PORT, NOT A SERVICE TO CALL
**MEASURED FROM SOURCE (README + code paths, 22:36Z).** `francy2222/annas-archive-download-mcp` — "search + free slow
downloads via LibGen 2-step & SciDB, **no API key needed**" — documents the exact chain the owner was asking for:
`ads.php?md5=<hash>` → extract the session key → `get.php?md5=<hash>&key=<session>` → a direct file URL valid for a
few minutes; plus `sci-net.xyz/{doi}` → an iframe PDF for articles; plus the slow partner links (library.lol, IPFS,
Z-Library mirrors) already rendered on the `/md5/` page.
**WHY IT MATTERS.** It separates two things the previous reading conflated: the HEADED BROWSER is needed to get past
the search challenge, NOT to download. If the LibGen 2-step resolves a session key headlessly, then an `annas` rung
can: search once in the browser (or take the md5 from a saved manifest), then download with plain HTTP — which is what
would let two candidates run in parallel and let the rung survive a closed window.
**WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED, STATED AS SUCH (D-3036).** Nobody has run `ads.php → get.php` from this machine. Until a
probe names the bytes, this is a METHOD under test, not a rung. The hosted Vercel endpoint is NOT adopted: an MCP
server run by an unknown account sees every query it is given and executes with the caller's privileges.
**NEXT PROBE (one command, 2 minutes).** `curl -sI "https://libgen.li/ads.php?md5=<a known md5>"` then GET it, grep
the key, then GET `get.php` and check `content-type` + `content-disposition`. If both answer, BUG-911's remedy changes
from "buy a key" to "port two HTTP calls".

### BUG-911 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — ADDENDUM 2: THE TWO-STEP IS *PROVEN HEADLESS AND KEYLESS*, SO THE SHADOW LANE DOES NOT NEED A BROWSER TO DOWNLOAD
**THE PROBE, run 22:52Z, three commands, no browser and no key.** (The md5 used was the first row of a saved search
page, so the FILE is not the queried work — the MECHANISM is what is under test, and the mechanism is what answered.)
```
GET https://libgen.li/ads.php?md5=62a602a7e3382689a795fb6f71eae05f   -> 200, 20,530 B
    body contains: get.php?md5=62a602a7e3382689a795fb6f71eae05f&key=ZWH70P8UGDU7VZX5
GET https://libgen.li/get.php?md5=…&key=ZWH70P8UGDU7VZX5             -> 307
    Location: https://cdn2.booksdl.lc/get.php?md5=…&key=ZWH70P8UGDU7VZX5
GET <that Location>                                                  -> 200, application/octet-stream
    content-length: 15,097,549
    content-disposition: attachment; filename=" Colleen Hoover - Confess (2022) - libgen.li.epub"
    range 0-7 -> 206, `50 4b 03 04 14 00 00 00` (PK\003\004 — a real ZIP/EPUB container)
```
`libgen.gl` answered the same shape with a different session key (`QHFKV3QPP3L6C7HE`), so the mechanism is not one
host's quirk.
**WHAT THIS SETTLES.** The session key is issued to a plain `curl` with browser headers. No DDoS-Guard, no captcha,
no account, no API key, and **no browser window**. BUG-911's remaining scope is therefore narrower than its title:
the browser is needed for Anna's **SEARCH** (and for `/scidb/<doi>`), not for a LibGen **download**.
**WHAT WAS ALREADY RIGHT, and is worth saying plainly.** `LibgenAdapter.locate` has implemented exactly this chain
since D-3080 (`ads.php` -> first `get.php` href -> `Delivery(url, referer=ads)`) and `downloader._receive` passes the
referer to `net.download`. The probe therefore validates shipped code rather than proposing a new one. The earlier
`no rows` refusals were BUG-910 (parser) and BUG-909 (saturated front), **not** a missing download path —
a distinction that cost a session to learn.
**WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN.** (a) whether `cdn2.booksdl.lc` requires the `Referer` we send (untested without it);
(b) whether a session key survives long enough for a queue of several files (the community README says "a few
minutes" — one key per file is the safe assumption until a second file is measured); (c) whether the chain holds when
the front is saturated (BUG-909) — it cannot, and that is what the circuit breaker is for.
**DECLARED CHANGE (not yet built).** `annas` gains a **`direct` route**: when the manifest already carries an md5 (which
`annas` search produces), the rung may skip the browser entirely and resolve LibGen's 2-step for that md5. That turns
the most expensive rung in the ladder into a plain HTTP rung for the common case, and it is the RECOURSE the owner
asked for without spending a donation to get it.

### BUG-915 (MED — OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE DOCLING BUDGET'S DECLARED BASIS IS **BYTES**, AND BYTES DO NOT PREDICT CONVERSION COST (MEASURED r = −0.131)

**THE RED LOOP (D-3036) — one command, already run, RED now.** Join the applier's own receipt timestamps against each
row's declared `bytes` and measured `pages`, then correlate. Reading taken 2026-10-17T20:55Z over the 25 rows whose
inter-receipt gap is ≥2 s and <1500 s:

```
n = 25
Pearson r  log(bytes) vs log(seconds) : -0.131
Pearson r  log(pages) vs log(seconds) : +0.002
```

Not weak. **ABSENT, and slightly negative on bytes.** The GREEN form of this loop is a basis whose r clears a
declared floor; the fix has to move that number, not merely re-word the docstring.

**THE INVERSION, in two works from the same run.**

| work | bytes | pages | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coelum Philosophorum.pdf | 0.04 MB | 15 | **1501** |
| Encyclopedia of Prostitution and Sex Work (2 vol).pdf | 69.89 MB | 821 | **46** |

A model that prices 1,700× more bytes at 1/32 of the time is not a model of the thing it is pricing.

**WHY IT MATTERS.** `docling_budget_s` in `pipeline/stage0_convert.py` exists for a measured reason (D-3076): a flat
180 s refused a 119-page photo-heavy volume that converts fine in 287 s, and the refusal was reported in the
vocabulary of a defect. The declared remedy was an allowance "derived from THIS work's size" so that long, scanned,
image-heavy works are not refused FIRST. Measured, the expensive rows are the **small** ones and the cheapest row in
the run is the largest — so the derivation is inert in exactly the direction it was built to matter, and 76 of the 399
remaining PDFs are ceiling-capped at 1,500 s on the strength of a number that carries no information about them.

**POPULATION AUDIT (receipt: `governance/evidence/APPLIER_POPULATION_AUDIT_20261017.json`, 399 remaining PDFs).**
303 carry a text layer (median 15 pages); 96 are image-only (median 178 pages, 18,718 pages between them); 59 are
≤30 MB text; 76 are >30 MB and therefore ceiling-capped, of which **33 are scans**. Sum of every declared allowance
= **73.4 h** (the hard wall); measured mean = **216 s/row**, so 515 remaining rows project to **~31 h**, and the
spread (p50 67 s, p90 692 s) is why the earlier 28 h estimate keeps drifting upward as heavy rows land.

**WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** The **cause** is a HYPOTHESIS: Docling's layout and table-structure passes dominate, so a
figure-heavy 15-page document can cost more than an 821-page linear one. NOT MEASURED: per-page figure/table density,
and whether OCR is being invoked on pages that already carry text. No fix is proposed until the cause is measured.

**FIX DIRECTION (declared, not built).** `basis: pages` — or `pages` plus a scan multiplier — is the only candidate
with a plausible referent, and it must be TESTED against this same receipt before it replaces the current basis (R5:
the replacement is proposed by one model and reviewed against the measurement, not against its own confidence).

**INTERIM.** Do not raise `docling_ceiling_s` (D-3023: never raise a ceiling to fit a reading). Do not retry the three
already-quarantined `budget_expired` rows: a retry under the same allowance reproduces the same refusal, and the
caller would learn nothing it did not already have.

## BUG-916 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-17) — A HEALTH RAIL WENT RED FOR THE WHOLE LENGTH OF A LEGITIMATE RUN, AND THE DECLARATION THAT SHOULD HAVE DECIDED IT WAS READ BY NO CODE

**THE RED LOOP (D-3036), taken before any theory.** One nameable command, run once, red on the bug and green when it
is fixed:

    python3 scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py ; echo $?

MEASURED 2026-10-17T21:11Z (before): rc **1** — `FATAL: content report older than the newest corpus file:
same_work_content_candidates.json`. `just health` therefore died at **line 33 of 184** and every line after it was
never read (BUG-573's own prefix shape, in its most expensive form: a ladder that reports a PREFIX hides the set).
Measured again after the fix: rc **2** (OWNER-OWED, loud, printed, and the ladder line already tolerates it), and
`just health` now runs to line 54.

**THE DEFECT, in two limbs.**

1. **The class is unavoidable while a conversion runs.** `content_debt()`
   (`pipeline/ingest_gate.py`) decides staleness as `report_mtime < max(corpus_file_mtime)`. The admission applier
   (`scripts/apply_admission.py`, PID 54639) copies a container INTO `knowledge pipeline/books` and writes its S0
   `.md` there **once per row**, for 510 rows / ~29 h. So the newest corpus file is always seconds old, the content
   screen is always minutes old, and the comparison is FALSE for the entire run **by construction** — through no
   fault of the operator and with no act that could make it true short of re-running a 2-minute scan between every
   row. MEASURED: report mtime 18:12Z, newest corpus files 21:11:27Z (`.pdf`) and 21:11:25Z (`.md`), both written by
   the applier's own two calls.
2. **The declaration that should have decided it was dead.** `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml#content.staleness`
   declared `staleness: fatal` — and **no code read it**: the class was hardcoded into `standing()`'s `fatal` list.
   A declaration with no consumer (D-3034). That is why the disposition could not be right for two different callers
   without anyone noticing that it was being decided twice.

**WHY IT MATTERS, measured rather than argued.** The first thing the repaired ladder did was expose a fault that had
been invisible behind line 33: `delegation_economy.py --check` reports **BREACH — cloud calls 37,354.00 > ceiling
37,000.00** (shrink-only, D-3023, measured at 32,851 on 2026-10-15). Filed as **BUG-917**. A red rail that is red for
reasons nobody can act on does not protect a system; it hides the one rail that would have spoken.

**THE FIX (built, `mode` is DECLARED by the caller and never inferred).**

* `config/ingest_identity_gate.yaml#content.staleness` becomes a per-mode mapping — `reading: owner_owed`,
  `door: fatal`, plus `remedy` so the printed line carries its own command. A disposition outside
  `{fatal, owner_owed}`, a mode nobody declared, or the retired scalar is **FATAL, never defaulted**.
* `pipeline/ingest_gate.py`: `standing(policy, books_dir, mode="reading")`; `_stale_disposition/_stale_remedy` read
  the declaration (fail-closed) and route the ONE line to `fatal` or `owner_owed`.
* `scripts/check_ingest_identity_gate.py`: `--gate` passes `mode="door"`; `--check` (the health line) keeps the
  default. One new control, **21/21 green**:
  `a_stale_content_screen_is_owed_in_the_reading_and_fatal_at_the_door` — it asserts BOTH rcs on the same fixture, and
  that the retired scalar is REFUSED rather than honoured.
* VERIFIED two-sided after: `--check` rc **2**, `--gate` rc **1**. The door still refuses; only the census stopped
  going dark.

**WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** The fix does not make `just health` green, and it must not be read as doing so: the ladder
now stops at **line 54** on a REAL breach (BUG-917) and `just health-full` reports **16 faults over 184 lines in
1087.6 s**, all of them pre-existing debt that line 33 had been hiding. It also does not re-run the content screen;
after the applier finishes, `python3 scripts/detect_same_work_content.py` is still an owed prerequisite before the
ingest door opens (which is the correct behaviour and is why `door: fatal` was kept).

## BUG-917 (HIGH, OPEN 2026-10-17) — THE CLOUD-CALL CEILING IS EXCEEDED BY 354 CALLS AND NOBODY OWNS THE READING

**FOUND BY** the BUG-916 repair, on the first run of the ladder that could get past line 33 (a hidden fault, not a
new one). The reading, verbatim:

    BREACH  cloud calls: 37,354.00 > ceiling 37,000.00
    a ceiling is SHRINK-ONLY: route the work to T0 (script) or T1 (local engine), or the OWNER raises the ceiling
    with a reason (D-3023)
    ceiling cloud calls: 37,000.00 (shrink-only; measured 2026-10-15 at 32,851.00)

**WHAT IT IS.** Cumulative metered cloud calls rose **4,503** between the 2026-10-15 reading and 2026-10-17T21:40Z —
fast enough that the ceiling cannot be respected by a routing change alone, which is why it is registered rather than
quietly absorbed. `just health` stops here (line 54 of 184) and therefore still reports a PREFIX.

**WHY A ROUTING FIX DOES NOT CLOSE IT.** The ceiling is a LIFETIME counter, not a rate: every future call adds to a
number that is already over. `delegation_economy.py`'s own declared remedies are (a) route the work to T0/T1, which
slows the growth but never reduces the count, and (b) the OWNER raises the ceiling **with a reason** (D-3023 forbids
raising it to fit a reading; it does not forbid a reason that names the work). There is no third route, and inventing
one would be the exact move the ceiling exists to prevent.

**THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE LIKELY SOURCE.** The operator's own agent harness is served by a
CLOUD provider, so conversation turns and delegated subagents are metered while the pipeline itself is local (C1's
`$0 marginal cost` is a claim about GENERATION, not about the harness). This has never been declared as a separate
stream, so the ceiling is currently answering two questions at once — "is the pipeline sovereign?" and "is the
harness metered?" — and they have different answers.

**OWNER DECISION OWED, one of three, each with its own consequence:**
1. **Raise the ceiling with a named reason** (e.g. "the operator harness is cloud-served until T-132's local route is
   measured") — one line in `config/delegation_economy.yaml`, and the reading returns to green honestly.
2. **Split the counter into two declared streams** — `pipeline` (must be $0) and `harness` (metered, capped
   separately) — the ontologically correct answer, and the larger change.
3. **Keep it red and shrink-only, and read it every session** — legitimate, but then `just health` cannot be the
   first line of defence and `just health-full` becomes mandatory.

NOT DONE HERE: no ceiling was raised, no counter was split, no routing was changed. A measurement never mints its own
permission.

## BUG-918 (HIGH, FIXED 2026-10-18) — S0 CONVERTS PDFs INTO IMAGE DUMPS: 16 FILES HELD 2,311 MB OF A 2,591 MB NIGHT, ONE OF THEM 895 MB
    # FIXED THE SAME NIGHT IT WAS FILED (D-3086). The owner's reading is the specification: "a 895 MB .md is not a
    # book". The engine's own DEFAULT was the cause — docling ships `--image-export-mode embedded`, which base64-inlines
    # every figure — and NOBODY between the engine and the corpus had an opinion about the shape, so the only reader of
    # those bytes was the disk. Two-sided measurement on ONE real library work (Souls Of Distortion Awakening.pdf,
    # 4.06 MB): embedded -> 19.371 MB / 95 `data:image` blobs; placeholder -> 0.538 MB / 0 blobs, SAME TEXT (519,083
    # vs 518,893 normalised chars; every difference the image marker plus one figure reflow). 36x smaller, nothing lost.
    # THE FIX, three layers: (1) the shape is DECLARED at config#stage0.artifact and refused at import when it does not
    # resolve; (2) convert_pdf passes `--image-export-mode` and the reader writes into a SCRATCH tree, so
    # `verify_artifact()` measures the artefact BEFORE the corpus sees it, and only a conforming one is written into

    # because `run_stage0` accumulates `converted` in memory and writes STAGE0_CHECKPOINT once, after the loop. The
    # applier drives ONE Stage-0 subprocess per book, so every subprocess the owner's stop killed wrote nothing —
    # while its bytes stayed in the corpus. The class is: BYTES WITHOUT A RECEIPT, produced by an ordinary Ctrl-C.

    # night of a stop is a cascade): write the record INCREMENTALLY, one crash-safe append per work, so an
    # interruption costs at most the work in flight. That is a change to `run_stage0`'s checkpoint contract, it needs

## BUG-921 (MED, OPEN 2026-10-18) — 19 DUPLICATE STEMS (38 FILES) IN THE CORPUS MD FROM FILENAME PUNCTUATION DRIFT; NO PER-WORK DEDUP KEY
    # THE RED LOOP — one command, already run once, that stays RED until a per-work identity exists:
    python3 - <<'PY'
    from pathlib import Path
    import re
    def norm(s):
        s = s.lower()
        s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "", s)
        return s[:40]
    books = Path("knowledge pipeline/books").rglob("*.md")
    by = {}
    for p in books:
        k = norm(p.stem)
        by.setdefault(k, []).append(p)
    dups = {k: v for k, v in by.items() if len(v) > 1}
    print(len(dups), "duplicate identity keys;", sum(len(v) for v in dups.values()), "files")
    for k, v in list(dups.items())[:5]:
        print(" ", k, "->", [str(x.name) for x in v])
    PY
    # MEASURED 2026-10-18: 19 duplicate identity keys → 38 files. Every pair is BYTE-DIFFERENT (0 byte-identical), so
    # the SHA-256 content hash dedup misses them all. Examples: `The Non-Designer_s Design Book.md` vs `The
    # Non-Designer's Design Book.md`; `Bierut, Michael_ Rand.md` vs `Bierut, Michael; Rand.md`. The two stems differ
    # only in punctuation/whitespace that the conversion path (or a re-run) rendered differently for the SAME work.
    # WHY IT IS MED, NOT LOW: a filename is NOT a key, but the pipeline currently treats output_path (filename) as the
    # work identity, so the same work is chunked (S1), extracted (S2) and committed (S6) TWICE under two names. The
    # convergence stages (cluster-before-extract, S4 merge) then hold TWO sets of FBs for one underlying work — a
    # dilution of convergence and a source of near-duplicate primitives, not a data loss.
    # THE FIX (not applied — it changes identity, which is BUG-899's contract): a per-work identity key = title+author,
    # case-folded, punctuation-stripped, prefix-40 containment (the same `norm` above). BUG-899 re-keys Stage-0 by
    # `source_file`; this bug re-keys by the NORMALIZED WORK, and the Phase B ledger (one row per work) is the home for
    # the canonical copy. The 19 dup pairs are folded to 19 canonical works in Phase B, never by deleting blindly.

### BUG-920 — ADDENDUM 2026-10-18 16:10Z: THE MIRROR INSTANCE — A CHECKPOINT RECORD OUTLIVES ITS ARTEFACT (`safe_delete` leaves the S0 record)

The live `apply_admission --apply` (started 14:06:53Z) failed `Semiotics-the-Basics.pdf` a SECOND time (`S0 rc=0, markdown absent`), and the applier moved the fresh copy to `admission_quarantine/20261018T140653Z/`. This is NOT the one-off "race with safe_delete" filed earlier — it is REPRODUCIBLE, and the mechanism is now measured:

1. `backup/deletions/20261018_153239/` holds BOTH `Semiotics-the-Basics.md` AND `.pdf` — the corpus copies were safe_deleted at 13:32:39Z because the work is a duplicate of `Semiotics The Basics Daniel Chandler liber3.md` (1.3 MB, already in the corpus).
2. The S0 checkpoint (`rechunk-v4-20260929/checkpoint.jsonl`) STILL carries the record for `Semiotics-the-Basics.pdf` (elapsed 74.0 s, quality_status passed, 707.6 KB) — `safe_delete` (R-D410) moved the bytes but did NOT purge the checkpoint record.
3. On re-derive the `.md` is gone, so the row is NOT `already_in_the_corpus` → it is re-admitted as a candidate.
4. On apply, S0's resume path sees the `source_file` in the checkpoint → treats it as already-converted → emits `Skipped: 1` and writes NO `.md` → the applier sees `markdown absent` → `failed`.

CLASS: BUG-920 is "bytes without a receipt" (artefact, no record); this is the MIRROR — "a receipt without bytes" (record, no artefact). Both are one checkpoint↔filesystem divergence. THE GAP that makes this instance possible: `safe_delete` purges bytes but not the record, and a resume SKIP is decided on the record alone, never on the artefact's presence.

THE FIX (sequence AFTER this batch — the same files are mid-run): S0's resume-skip must verify the `.md` exists (an `existing` record whose `output_path` is absent is not "done", it is a re-convert), OR `safe_delete` must also remove the S0 checkpoint record for the moved `source_file`. Land with BUG-920's incremental-write fix; do NOT open a new number for the mirror of an OPEN bug.

DISPOSITION THIS BATCH (correct, no action): the failure is harmless — the book is a duplicate, the copy is quarantined (not deleted), no data loss.
